items.title: How Well Do Prior-Data Fitted Networks Amortize Bayesian Inference?
items.abstract: Prior-data fitted networks (PFNs) are trained to approximate the Bayesian posterior predictive distribution (PPD) of a synthetic prior, yet results about the approximation quality are surprisingly thin. Taking an empirical risk minimization perspective, we decompose the deployment error of PFNs into prior, context, and amortization error, and measure the latter against a reference PPD under a realistic prior. Results show that PFNs generally recover the targeted PPD very well. Nevertheless, we find that parts of the residual amortization error persist, especially in \textit{rare} settings under the prior pretraining distribution, even when scaling the model size, which manifests in disagreement between independently pretrained PFNs and leaves uncertainty about the predictor at inference time. As a remedy, we study multiple types of Bayesian model averages and find that these can consistently reduce this uncertainty and improve predictions up to full-size TabICLv2 models.
items.authors: Manuel H\"ulskamp, Julius Kobialka, Emanuel Sommer, Thomas Nagler, David R\"ugamer

items.title: Shortcut Learning in Geospatial Foundation Model Embeddings for Cross-Disaster Damage Assessment
items.abstract: Geospatial foundation models can support disaster damage assessment, but high accuracy on familiar disasters may hide shortcut learning: prediction from event or scene characteristics rather than evidence that transfers to a new disaster. We study embeddings from TerraMind, Prithvi-EO-2.0, DOFA, and DINOv3 on the multi-disaster datasets xView2 and BRIGHT. Holding out an entire disaster, instead of randomly splitting image tiles, reduces mean balanced accuracy from 0.807 to 0.638 on xView2 and from 0.818 to 0.568 on BRIGHT. Four sets of tests examine what information supports prediction: event and acquisition context, before/after image inputs, building count, and correct image pairing. Pre-event images remain predictive, and a classifier given only the annotated number of buildings reaches balanced accuracy of 0.629 and 0.653. Combining before/after features performs best on average on xView2, but does not improve over pre-only features on BRIGHT. Shuffling image pairs within the same disaster and damage class causes modest losses. Motivated by these findings, we test whether feature transformations learned only from training disasters improve generalization to unseen disasters. These transformations improve performance, with supervised contrastive learning performing best on xView2 and PCA on BRIGHT. Our results highlight the importance of evaluation on unseen domains for assessing model robustness and show that simple feature-level transformations can improve generalization. Code and experiments can be found at https://github.com/alishibli97/gfm-shortcut-learning.
items.authors: Ali Shibli, Andrea Nascetti, Yifang Ban

items.title: From Pixels to Privacy-Sensitive Features: An Information-Theoretic Framework for Reconstruction Bounds
items.abstract: What can an adversary recover from a model trained with DP-SGD? Its $(\varepsilon,\delta)$ guarantee does not answer this question directly. We derive a distortion bound that can be computed before training and applies even to an adversary who observes the parameter trajectory during training, knows every other training record and the population distribution from which the training records are drawn. The analyst may choose the representation in which error is measured, allowing the bound to target the aspects of reconstruction that are privacy-sensitive in a given application. Our information-theoretic framework separates two contributions: the information about a record revealed by training, measured through conditional mutual information, and the uncertainty already present in the data distribution, measured through source entropy. Rate-distortion theory combines them into a lower bound on the expected error of every reconstruction attack. For DP-SGD, the leakage bound depends only on the sampling rates and noise multipliers, while the source entropy is lower-bounded from a sample with finite-sample confidence. An orthogonal block construction keeps the resulting bound informative for high-dimensional images. We instantiate the framework in pixel space and in LPIPS feature space, obtaining, to our knowledge, the first lower bound on reconstruction distortion measured directly by LPIPS. On a range of image datasets the bounds establish non-trivial unavoidable expected reconstruction error within heuristically recommended privacy-budget ranges and beyond. Experiments compare the bounds with strong reconstruction attacks and identify the principal sources of the remaining slack.
items.authors: Henry Bourne, Robert F. Allison

items.title: Geometry-Aware Multi-Objective Optimization: Norm-Constrained Oracles with Entropic Weight Updates
items.abstract: Multiple-gradient descent is typically formulated in Euclidean geometry, whereas matrix-aware optimizers use directions induced by other norms. We analyze a single-loop multi-objective method combining a norm-constrained linear minimization oracle with entropic updates of task weights. For any finite-dimensional norm pair, we establish an $O(T^{-1/2})$ ergodic stationarity rate in the deterministic setting, deriving the required trajectory gradient bound from smoothness and lower-boundedness in the unregularized case. With stochastic gradients and a bounded-gradient assumption, one persistent blended-gradient momentum buffer yields an $O(T^{-1/4})$ rate whose leading term has no explicit dependence on the number of tasks. We also establish static regret for the inner weighting objective on arbitrary bounded gradient sequences and, with entropy regularization and a weight floor, iteration-wise inner-gap control after burn-in while retaining ergodic stationarity, conditional on a trajectory gradient bound. The optimal blended gradient can be nonunique in spectral and sign geometries, motivating a selection-independent inner gap. Our analysis extends the spectral construction studied by concurrent MOON to general norms. Experiments compare the method with existing multi-task optimizers and examine its oracle, weighting, and momentum choices.
items.authors: El Mahdi Chayti, Alireza Mirrokni, Martin Jaggi

items.title: Optimal Algorithms for Nonsmooth Nonconvex Stochastic Optimization with Constraints
items.abstract: We present new algorithms for stochastic optimization problems in which the objective is neither smooth nor convex, subject to a convex constraint set. Our algorithms return a $(\delta,\varepsilon)$-Goldstein stationary point, as recently defined for constrained problems by Liu et al. (2024), with improved complexities, and are the first to achieve optimal convergence rates for this task in several settings. In particular, we design projection-based and projection-free algorithms that achieve a $\widetilde O(\delta^{-1}\varepsilon^{-3})$ rate using stochastic gradients, which we show to be optimal, and a $\widetilde O(d\delta^{-1}\varepsilon^{-3})$ rate using zeroth-order queries, which is also optimal in its dependence on the dimension $d$ and improves over prior work. Notably, our lower bound is given in terms of the Frank-Wolfe gap and holds even for smooth problems, which is of independent interest. These results show that in nonconvex stochastic optimization, the convergence rate is degraded neither by the presence of constraints nor by nonsmoothness. Our analysis is based on a reduction to online linear optimization, extending a related technique from unconstrained optimization.
items.authors: Gon Buzaglo, Guy Kornowski

items.title: Adaptive Variance Reduction without Knowing Oracle Smoothness
items.abstract: Variance reduction improves the convergence rate of stochastic non-convex optimization under the average smoothness condition. Existing adaptive variance reduction methods are especially designed for average smoothness and do not adapt to standard smoothness. In this paper, we study how one algorithm can adapt to these two settings and the noiseless setting without knowing the smoothness constants or the variance bound. Given the gradient budget $T$, we develop a two-phase method. The first phase compares two independent gradients and switches to normalized momentum when their difference exceeds a threshold. This phase provides both a candidate with standard smooth and noiseless guarantees and also ensures a bounded expected function gap for the second variance reduction phase. The resulting rates are $O(T^{-1/3})$ under average smoothness, $O(T^{-1/4})$ under standard smoothness, and $O(T^{-1/2})$ without noise. When $T$ is unknown, we propose a method with two paths that attain the corresponding rates with logarithmic factors in the stochastic settings. Here, we use a variance reduction path to deal with average smoothness and employ the AdaGrad-Norm for standard smoothness and noiseless setting. Neither method restarts from the initial point or requires a growing number of oracle calls in each round.
items.authors: Wei Jiang, Yibo Wang, Zechao Li

items.title: Constrained Probabilistic Numerics: Gaussian Process Solvers for Linear PDEs under Linear Inequality Constraints
items.abstract: Gaussian process solvers for linear partial differential equations (PDEs) return posteriors rather than point estimates, but they condition only on equality information: the PDE residual, boundary data, and measurements. Many solutions of interest also obey inequality constraints, including nonnegativity, monotonicity, and absence of arbitrage, which equality conditioning cannot enforce. We prove that conditioning a Gaussian process prior jointly on linear equality observations and a finite-dimensional inequality event is equivalent to conditioning sequentially in terms of Borel measures on the solution space. The physics-informed posterior is therefore a valid prior for the inequality update at virtual points. The combined law is non-Gaussian yet computable through truncated-Gaussian moments, and neither the PDE conditioning nor the inequality update requires modification. We evaluated the construction on a Poisson benchmark, option-price surfaces, and air-quality fields. Under incomplete boundary data, a monotonicity constraint lowered the error of a two-dimensional Poisson reconstruction by $63\%$. On a real S&P 500 option chain thinned to $20$ retained quotes, no-arbitrage constraints reduced held-out extrapolation error by $22\%$ and cut the calendar-arbitrage rate from $10\%$ to $1\%$. On four real air-quality snapshots, nonnegativity reduced a Gaussian moment-based sub-zero-tail proxy by $74\%$ at the sparsest monitor count. Changes in mean accuracy and constraint diagnostics differed across data regimes. The probability of the noisy virtual constraint event under the equality posterior measures agreement with the specified bounds before the update. The construction turns admissibility from a post-processing step into conditioning information for probabilistic PDE solvers.
items.authors: Boyuan Deng, Kshitiz Upadhyay, Michael Shields

items.title: Diversity-Aware Ensemble of Quantum-Classical Models via Combinatorial Fusion
items.abstract: Variational quantum circuits (VQCs) are highly sensitive to circuit architecture, yet most quantum machine learning pipelines select a single best design and discard the remaining candidates. This paper addresses whether the structural diversity across quantum circuit search spaces can be used to produce stronger predictions through model fusion. We apply Combinatorial Fusion Analysis (CFA), a model fusion framework that selects and combines multiple scoring systems using rank-score function (RSF) and cognitive diversity (CD), to a pool of 29 architecturally diverse classical models and quantum circuits. Using a diversity-aware model selection method, we identify subsets of maximally diverse models and combine them with both score and rank combination. Experiments on four binary classification benchmarks covering different domains demonstrate that CFA-based hybrid classical-quantum fusion consistently outperform the best individual model on every dataset considered with improvements up to 6.03% in accuracy. When comparing with relevant literatures, the CFA framework further achieves superior performance across all four datasets.
items.authors: Jingyan Xu, Yuanhong Wu, Samuel Yen-Chi Chen, Sean Patten, Christina Schweikert, D. Frank Hsu

items.title: Dream to Remember: Continual Steering of Generalist Robot Policies with World Models
items.abstract: Generalist robot policies are trained with imitation learning and are bounded by the quality and coverage of their demonstrations. Reinforcement learning can improve and extend them, either by fine-tuning the policy weights or by training a small module to steer the input noise of a frozen generative policy. When tasks arrive sequentially, both approaches suffer from catastrophic forgetting. Fine-tuning on a task degrades prior tasks, and steering only shifts forgetting to the shared steering module. We propose Dream to Remember (D2R), which continually steers a frozen generalist policy toward new tasks, while retaining its earlier skills. As the steering module learns a new task, a frozen pretrained world model rehearses prior tasks through imagined rollouts, anchoring the module to its earlier behavior without a replay buffer or new data. When the world model is faithful enough, D2R learns the new task entirely in imagination. Otherwise, it learns the task in the environment while using the world model only to rehearse prior tasks. On CALVIN, D2R improves eight tasks in sequence entirely in imagination, raising average success from 63.7% to 74.8%, while LoRA fine-tuning on the same sequence drops it to 11.7%. With a frozen off-the-shelf generalist policy and world model, $\pi_0$ and A2World, D2R learns unseen LIBERO-90 tasks in the environment while keeping $\pi_0$'s performance on the LIBERO suites it was fine-tuned on, even though the world model is not accurate enough for policy optimization. Finally, on a real Franka robot, D2R improves three tasks in sequence entirely in imagination while retaining the earlier improvements.
items.authors: Bahey Tharwat, Iman Nematollahi, Marvin Alles, Xingyuan Zhang, Akshay L Chandra, Abhinav Valada

items.title: Finite-Sample Guarantees for Fully Discrete Conditional Diffusion Models
items.abstract: We establish finite-sample guarantees for conditional diffusion models learned from data and implemented with finitely many denoising steps. Our approach aligns the score-training objective with the sampling grid, allowing statistical estimation and numerical discretization errors to be analyzed together. Under a smooth conditional density model, we derive high-probability bounds on the generated distribution's error and quantify the required number of score evaluations. For every smoothness index $\beta>0$, a suitable grid yields averaged conditional Kullback--Leibler (KL) divergence $\widetilde O_p(n^{-2\beta/(d_x+d_y+2\beta)})$ relative to the original target with or without early stopping. Both the full and early-stopped samplers attain average target total-variation (TV) error $\widetilde O_p(n^{-\beta/(d_x+d_y+2\beta)})$. Here $n$ is the sample size, $d_x,d_y$ are the data and conditioning dimensions, and errors are averaged over the conditioning variable. The total-variation bound matches the rate established in existing conditional distribution-estimation theory, up to logarithmic factors.
items.authors: Qiuyun Zhu

items.title: Hitting-Time Bounds for Asynchronous Q-Learning
items.abstract: We study the last iterate of standard asynchronous Q-learning from a single trajectory of a finite Markov decision process. The trajectory follows a fixed behavior policy whose state--action chain is irreducible and may be periodic. For discount factor $\gamma$, write $H=(1-\gamma)^{-1}$, and let $\mu_{\min}$ be the minimum stationary state--action probability and $\mathfrak h_\star$ the largest expected hitting time of the reverse state--action chain. We prove that zero-initialized Q-learning with a constant step size achieves sup-norm error at most $\varepsilon$ with high probability using $\widetilde{O}(H^4/(\mu_{\min}\varepsilon^2)+\mathfrak h_\star)$ transitions, for $0<\varepsilon\le1$. The statistical term retains the quartic effective-horizon dependence of standard Q-learning, while initialization cost is additive in $\mathfrak h_\star$. For aperiodic behavior chains, a comparison with mixing time yields a transient term $\widetilde{O}(t_{\mathrm{mix}}/\mu_{\min})$. An empirical state--action count rule selects a constant step size for a subsequent training run and attains the same rate without prior knowledge of model parameters, target accuracy, or confidence level. The output is the last training iterate, with both stages included in the sample count. The proof uses two deterministic Bellman envelopes to separate statistical error from fixed-policy initialization error and adapts reverse-time hitting-cost compensation from TD learning to state--action propagation. An exploration lower bound holds for arbitrary predictable step sizes. Together with the existing statistical lower bound and its extension to pilot-selected constant steps, it yields matching mean-square rates up to logarithmic factors on the stated large-sample parameter classes.
items.authors: Yang Peng

items.title: DyssomniaNN: Multi-Scale Spiking Neural Modeling of Human Sleep Disorders and Perceived Restedness
items.abstract: Clinical sleep medicine repeatedly documents profound divergences between objective sleep duration and subjective daytime impairment, notably exemplified by sleep state misperception in paradoxical insomnia and boundary instability in narcolepsy type 1. Here, we present DyssomniaNN: a multi-scale biophysical computational framework coupling Borb\'ely's two-process regulation of sleep homeostasis and circadian drive with Saper's hypothalamic reciprocal flip-flop circuit and a recurrent corticothalamic leaky integrate-and-fire spiking neural network. We formalize five clinical cohorts across an identical 72-hour photoperiod: healthy control, circadian rhythm sleep-wake disorder (delayed-phase), chronic insomnia, paradoxical insomnia, and narcolepsy type 1. The synthetic local field potential converges closely with empirical human electroencephalography spectra from the PhysioNet Sleep-EDF database across all canonical frequency bands (spectral mean absolute error of 0.33--0.35). Furthermore, we introduce the Well-Rested Index to quantify restorative efficacy. Simulations reveal that sleep duration fails to predict restorative recovery: paradoxical insomnia achieves normal total sleep time (21.15 h) yet yields low restoration (37.6%) from unsuppressed cortical beta-band intrusion, whereas hypocretin deficiency in narcolepsy produces severe nocturnal fragmentation (781 min of wake after sleep onset) and 35 sleep-onset rapid eye movement periods. DyssomniaNN provides an in silico platform for mechanistic sleep research and virtual neuropharmacology.
items.authors: Daniel Szelogowski

items.title: Goal-Oriented Bundle Management and Flow Control for Deep-Space Communications via Reinforcement Learning
items.abstract: Deep-space communications operate under intermittent connectivity, long propagation delays, and relay storage constraints. In such networks, the Bundle Protocol enables store-carry-forward communication, requiring relay nodes to manage limited storage and scarce contact opportunities. Relay-side scheduling and dropping decisions are inherently goal-oriented: transmission resources should be allocated to bundles most valuable to downstream mission objectives. Conventional schedulers, such as FIFO, do not explicitly optimize task utility and may provide unfair service across heterogeneous planetary sources. This paper presents a closed-loop modeling and learning framework for relay-side bundle and flow management in a contact-driven deep-space network, where lunar and Martian updates are forwarded through a shared-buffer relay to Earth. We quantify destination-side information freshness using excess age $\Delta_i^e(t)=[\Delta_i(t)-d_i(t)]^+$, where $\Delta_i(t)$ denotes the Age of Information of source $i$ and $d_i(t)$ is a source-dependent delay baseline. Based on this metric, we define a goal-oriented loss that supports source-dependent nonlinear penalties, allowing prioritization according to mission relevance. We formulate relay control as a constrained semi-Markov decision process (CSMDP) and solve it using masked Lagrangian Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO). Feasibility-aware action masking restricts transmissions to bundles that can complete within the remaining contact window. DTNSim simulations indicate improved age-based utility and inter-flow fairness compared with baseline schedulers. The proposed framework jointly optimizes relay-side bundle scheduling, dropping, and flow control under contact-driven dynamics with explicit fairness considerations across heterogeneous sources.
items.authors: Sajjad Baghaeea, Aimin Lib, Shanmugarajan Balasubramanian, Elif Uysal

items.title: Constructive Bounds for the Topological Expressivity of Neural Networks
items.abstract: The expressivity of a neural network $\Phi$ describes the class of functions that a network can express. The term topological expressivity refers to a family of measures particularly suited to understand binary classification and is often formulated in terms of the Betti numbers of a decision boundary $\beta (\Phi^{-1}(0))$. Despite its popularity, this measure is not as useful for regression and other problems that do not involve a decision boundary. Instead, we propose to study topological expressivity in terms of the Betti numbers of the output of a neural network $\beta(\Phi(X))$. We formally prove that a ReLU network with architecture $(d,\sum\limits_{k=1}^{d } \beta_k(3k+2),\sum\limits_{k=1}^{d}\beta_k(k+1))$ can express spaces homotopy equivalent to wedge sums of spheres with arbitrary Betti numbers. This gives upper bounds for any arbitrary connected ($\beta_0=1$) sequence of Betti numbers, but by constructing spaces homotopy equivalent to products of $N$ spheres of dimension $d_1,...,d_N$ we achieve much better bounds $(\sum\limits_{n=1} d_n, 3\sum\limits_{n=1}\limits^N d_n + 2N, \sum\limits_{n=1}\limits^N d_n + N) $ for Betti numbers given by $\prod_n (1+x^{d_n})$. Finally we conjecture a much stronger tight bound which gives the architectural bound $(d,d+1,d+1)$ for a space homeomorphic to the sphere.
items.authors: Kosio Beshkov

items.title: Linearized Wasserstein dimensionality reduction with approximation guarantees
items.abstract: We introduce LOT Wassmap, a computationally feasible algorithm to uncover low-dimensional structures in the Wasserstein space. The algorithm is motivated by the observation that many datasets are naturally interpreted as probability measures rather than points in $\mathbb{R}^n$, and that finding low-dimensional descriptions of such datasets requires manifold learning algorithms in the Wasserstein space. Most available algorithms are based on computing the pairwise Wasserstein distance matrix, which can be computationally challenging for large datasets in high dimensions. Our algorithm leverages approximation schemes such as Sinkhorn distances and linearized optimal transport to speed-up computations, and in particular, avoids computing a pairwise distance matrix. We provide guarantees on the embedding quality under such approximations, including when explicit descriptions of the probability measures are not available and one must deal with finite samples instead. Experiments demonstrate that LOT Wassmap attains correct embeddings and that the quality improves with increased sample size. We also show how LOT Wassmap significantly reduces the computational cost when compared to algorithms that depend on pairwise distance computations.
items.authors: Alexander Cloninger, Keaton Hamm, Varun Khurana, Caroline Moosm\"uller

items.title: TernaryLLM: Ternarized Large Language Model
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have achieved remarkable performance on Natural Language Processing (NLP) tasks, but they are hindered by high computational costs and memory requirements. Ternarization, an extreme form of quantization, offers a solution by reducing memory usage and enabling energy-efficient floating-point additions. However, applying ternarization to LLMs faces challenges stemming from outliers in both weights and activations. In this work, observing asymmetric outliers and non-zero means in weights, we introduce Dual Learnable Ternarization (DLT), which enables both scales and shifts to be learnable. We also propose Outlier-Friendly Feature Knowledge Distillation (OFF) to recover the information lost in extremely low-bit quantization. The proposed OFF can incorporate semantic information and is insensitive to outliers. At the core of OFF is maximizing the mutual information between features in ternarized and floating-point models using cosine similarity. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our TernaryLLM surpasses previous low-bit quantization methods on the standard text generation and zero-shot benchmarks for different LLM families. Specifically, for one of the most powerful open-source models, LLaMA-3, our approach (W1.58A16) outperforms the previous state-of-the-art method (W2A16) by 5.8 in terms of perplexity on C4 and by 8.2% in terms of average accuracy on zero-shot tasks.
items.authors: Tianqi Chen, Zhe Li, Weixiang Xu, Zeyu Zhu, Dong Li, Lu Tian, Emad Barsoum, Peisong Wang, Jian Cheng

items.title: Instance-Level Difficulty: A Missing Perspective in Machine Unlearning
items.abstract: Current research on deep machine unlearning primarily focuses on improving or evaluating the overall effectiveness of unlearning methods while overlooking the varying difficulty of unlearning individual training samples. As a result, the broader feasibility of machine unlearning remains under-explored. This paper studies the cruxes that make machine unlearning difficult through a thorough instance-level unlearning performance analysis over various unlearning algorithms and datasets. In particular, we summarize four factors that make unlearning a data point difficult, and we empirically show that these factors are independent of a specific unlearning algorithm but only relevant to the target model and its training data. Given these findings, we argue that machine unlearning research should pay attention to the instance-level difficulty of unlearning.
items.authors: Hammad Rizwan, Mahtab Sarvmaili, Hassan Sajjad, Ga Wu

items.title: Deep End-to-End Survival Analysis with Temporal Consistency
items.abstract: In this study, we present a novel Survival Analysis algorithm designed to efficiently handle large-scale longitudinal data. Our approach draws inspiration from Reinforcement Learning principles, particularly the Deep Q-Network paradigm, extending Temporal Learning concepts to Survival Regression. A central argument in our method relies on temporal consistency, a recursive consistency condition between survival predictions made at consecutive states. Our framework introduces a delayed target network that decouples the generation of temporally consistent training targets from model updates, providing a more stable training signal while enabling mini-batch optimization and end-to-end training. Additionally, it supports arbitrarily complex architectures, enabling the modeling of intricate temporal dependencies. Through numerous experiments we provide empirical evidence demonstrating our framework's ability to exploit temporal consistency across datasets of varying sizes. Moreover, our algorithm outperforms benchmarks on datasets with long sequences, demonstrating its ability to capture long-term patterns. Finally, ablation studies show that the degree of target delay has a substantial effect on predictive performance and training variability. Across two distinct survival model families, delayed target updates consistently improve over the same-timescale baseline.
items.authors: Mariana Vargas Vieyra, Pascal Frossard

items.title: Bandits with Anytime Knapsacks
items.abstract: We consider bandits with anytime knapsacks (BwAK), a novel version of the BwK problem where there is an \textit{anytime} cost constraint instead of a total cost budget. This problem setting introduces additional complexities as it mandates adherence to the constraint throughout the decision-making process. We propose SUAK (Strategic Under-utilization for Anytime Knapsacks), an algorithm that utilizes upper confidence bounds to identify the optimal mixture of arms while maintaining a balance between exploration and exploitation. SUAK is an adaptive algorithm that strategically utilizes the available budget in each round in the decision-making process and skips a round when it is possible to violate the anytime cost constraint. In particular, SUAK slightly under-utilizes the available cost budget to reduce the need for skipping rounds. We show that SUAK attains the same problem-dependent regret upper bound of $ O(K \log T)$ established in prior work under the simpler BwK framework, where $K$ denotes the number of arms, and $T$ denotes the time horizon. We also establish an instance-dependent lower bound showing that the $O(K\log T)$ dependence is unavoidable. Finally, we show via extensive simulations that SUAK achieves considerably higher rewards than naive adaptations of BwK algorithms that do not optimize learning under anytime cost constraints.
items.authors: Eray Can Elumar, Cem Tekin, Osman Yagan

items.title: Disentangling Total-Variance and Signal-to-Noise-Ratio Improves Diffusion Models
items.abstract: Diffusion models have been widely adopted as a powerful generative framework across numerous scientific domains, yet their inherently iterative sampling process remains a significant computational bottleneck. While this is typically mitigated by reducing the number of reverse diffusion steps, sample quality becomes highly sensitive to the chosen noise schedule, i.e. the manner in which noise is introduced and the signal is reduced at each step. Although prior work has improved on the original variance-preserving and variance-exploding schedules, these approaches passively adjust the total variance, without direct independent control over it. In this work, we propose a novel total-variance/signal-to-noise-ratio disentangled (TV/SNR) framework, where TV and SNR can be controlled independently. Our approach reveals that schedules with exponentially exploding TV can be consistently improved by adopting a constant TV schedule while preserving the underlying SNR schedule. Furthermore, we demonstrate that generalizing the SNR schedule of optimal transport flow matching significantly enhances generation efficiency. Crucially, these gains remain consistent across various reverse diffusion solvers and reduce the search space to two independent and interpretable parameters, enabling fast and robust sampling for complex scientific applications, such as molecular structure generation.
items.authors: Khaled Kahouli, Winfried Ripken, Stefan Gugler, Oliver T. Unke, Klaus-Robert M\"{u}ller, Shinichi Nakajima

items.title: EmbodiTTA: Resource-Efficient Test-Time Adaptation for Embodied Visual Systems
items.abstract: Continual Test-time adaptation (CTTA) continuously adapts the deployed model on every incoming batch of data. While achieving optimal accuracy, existing CTTA approaches present poor real-world applicability on resource-constrained edge devices, due to the substantial memory overhead and energy consumption. In this work, we first introduce a novel paradigm -- on-demand TTA -- which triggers adaptation only when a significant domain shift is detected. Then, we present OD-TTA, an on-demand TTA framework for accurate and efficient adaptation on edge devices. OD-TTA comprises three innovative techniques: 1) a lightweight domain shift detection mechanism to activate TTA only when it is needed, drastically reducing the overall computation overhead, 2) a source domain selection module that chooses an appropriate source model for adaptation, ensuring high and robust accuracy, 3) a decoupled Batch Normalization (BN) update scheme to enable memory-efficient adaptation with small batch sizes. Extensive experiments show that OD-TTA achieves comparable and even better performance while reducing the energy and computation overhead remarkably, making TTA a practical reality.
items.authors: Xiao Ma, Young D. Kwon, Dong Ma

items.title: Optimizable Model Averaging for Ensembling Heterogeneous Model Outputs
items.abstract: Foundation model ensembles can improve accuracy and robustness, but full fine-tuning and parameter-space merging are often expensive or impossible when candidate models have different architectures. We propose Optimizable Model Averaging (OMA), a black-box approach that learns nonnegative model-combination weights, one scalar coefficient per model, to average the candidate models' predictive probabilities, leaving all model parameters frozen, by minimizing regularized predictive entropy. A central challenge is that minimizing predictive entropy can favour confidently incorrect models: increased confidence need not imply improved accuracy or calibration. We therefore examine regularization as a mechanism for controlling adaptation and empirically evaluate its effect on calibration, observing lower expected calibration error in selected configurations, alongside better performance-calibration trade-offs than model output averaging. As foundation models continue to advance, these approaches will enable the incorporation of future, potentially much better models to improve performance on challenging text and image classification tasks.
items.authors: Mijung Park

items.title: User Trajectory Prediction Unifying Global and Local Temporal Information
items.abstract: Trajectory prediction is essential for formulating proactive strategies that anticipate user mobility and support advance preparation. Therefore, how to reduce the forecasting error in user trajectory prediction within an acceptable inference time arises as an interesting issue. However, trajectory data contains both global and local temporal information, complicating the extraction of the complete temporal pattern. Moreover, user behavior occurs over different time scales, increasing the difficulty of capturing behavioral patterns. To address these challenges, a trajectory prediction model based on multilayer perceptron (MLP), multi-scale convolutional neural network (MSCNN), and cross-attention (CA) is proposed. Specifically, MLP is used to extract the global temporal information of each feature. In parallel, MSCNN is employed to extract the local temporal information by modeling interactions among features within a local temporal range. Convolutional kernels with different sizes are used in MSCNN to capture temporal information at multiple resolutions, enhancing the model's adaptability to different behavioral patterns. Finally, CA is applied to fuse the global and local temporal information. Experimental results show that our model reduces mean squared error (MSE) by 5.04% and mean absolute error (MAE) by 4.35% compared with ModernTCN in 12-step prediction, while maintaining similar inference time.
items.authors: Wei Hao, Bin Chong, Ronghua Ji, Chen Hou

items.title: Multidimensional Bayesian Active Machine Learning of Working Memory Task Performance
items.abstract: While adaptive experimental design has outgrown one-dimensional, staircase-based adaptations, most cognitive experiments still control a single factor and summarize performance with a scalar. In contrast, we validate here a Bayesian, two-axis, active-classification approach in an immersive virtual testing environment, using a 5-by-5 spatial working-memory reconstruction task as an application domain. Two variables are controlled: spatial load L (number of occupied tiles) and feature-binding load K (number of distinct colors) of items. Stimulus acquisition is guided by posterior uncertainty of a nonparametric Gaussian Process (GP) probabilistic classifier, which outputs a surface over (L, K) rather than a single threshold or maximum span value. In a young adult population, we compare GP-driven Adaptive Mode (AM) with a traditional adaptive staircase Classic Mode (CM), which varies L only at K = 3. Parity between the methods is achieved for this cohort, with an intraclass correlation coefficient of 0.755 at K = 3. As a secondary exploratory result, AM reveals individual differences in interactions between spatial load and feature binding. AM estimates converge more quickly than other sampling strategies, demonstrating that only about 30 samples are required for accurate fitting of the full model.
items.authors: Dom CP Marticorena, Chris Wissmann, Zeyu Lu, Dennis L Barbour

items.title: Mixture of Many Zero-Compute Experts: A High-Rate Quantization Theory Perspective
items.abstract: This paper uses classical high-rate quantization theory to provide new insights into mixture-of-experts (MoE) models for regression tasks. Our MoE is defined by a segmentation of the input space to regions, each with a single-parameter expert that acts as a constant predictor with zero-compute at inference. Motivated by high-rate quantization theory assumptions, we assume that the number of experts is sufficiently large to make their input-space regions very small. This lets us study the approximation error of our MoE model class: (i) for one-dimensional inputs, we formulate the test error and its minimizing segmentation and experts; (ii) for multidimensional inputs, we formulate an upper bound for the test error and study its minimization. Moreover, we consider the learning of the expert parameters from a training dataset, given an input-space segmentation, and formulate their statistical learning properties. This leads us to theoretically and empirically show how the tradeoff between approximation and estimation errors in MoE learning depends on the number of experts.
items.authors: Yehuda Dar

items.title: Bayesian dynamic scheduling of multipurpose batch processes under incomplete look-ahead information
items.abstract: Multipurpose batch processes become increasingly popular in manufacturing industries since they adapt to low-volume, high-value products and shifting demands. These processes often operate in a dynamic environment, which faces disturbances such as processing delays and demand changes. To minimise long-term cost and system nervousness (i.e., disruptive changes to schedules), schedulers must design rescheduling strategies to address such disturbances effectively. Existing methods often assume complete look-ahead information over the scheduling horizon. This assumption contrasts with realistic situations where schedulers can only access incomplete look-ahead information. Sticking with existing methods may lead to suboptimal long-term costs and high-level system nervousness. In this work we propose a Bayesian dynamic scheduling method. Our method relies on learning a Bayesian Network from the probability distribution of disturbances. Specifically, the Bayesian Network represents how likely each operation will be impacted by disturbances. During the online execution, when new disturbances become observed, this method updates the posterior distribution and therefore guides the rescheduling strategy. We compare our method with the existing periodic rescheduling strategy (which generates new schedules from scratch at fixed intervals) on four benchmark problems. Computational results show that our method achieves statistically better long-term costs and system nervousness. In the theoretical aspect, we prove that if disturbances are mutually independent, the impact-quantifying variables inherently satisfy the independence assumptions required by Bayesian Networks. As an implication, practitioners can extend the method to other scheduling problems (such as job shop scheduling and continuous processes), given that they define the problem-specific dependencies between operations.
items.authors: Taicheng Zheng, Dan Li, Jie Li

items.title: Beyond Prediction-Set Size: Quantifying Conformal Uncertainty through Credal Geometry
items.abstract: Prediction-set size offers a coarse summary of conformal uncertainty. We develop a richer perspective through the geometry of credal sets: families of probability distributions compatible with conformal prediction (CP) regions. We establish this representation for split CP, extending a correspondence recently identified for full CP. Building on this representation, we derive analytical characterisations and exact algorithms for several widely used credal uncertainty measures, reducing potentially exponential computations to linear time after sorting the conformal p-values. We further unify several of these measures with classical conformal summaries by integrating set-size penalties based on Tsallis entropies across error levels. We also prove an impossibility theorem: for common split-conformal regression constructions, uncertainty summaries of the induced credal sets cannot distinguish between inputs. Classification experiments on selective prediction and distribution-shift detection show that these summaries often recover useful ranking information lost by prediction-set size at a fixed error level, enabling finer-grained uncertainty assessment. These results establish credal geometry as a principled framework for quantifying conformal uncertainty and understanding its limitations.
items.authors: Siu Lun Chau, Soroush H. Zargarbashi, Yusuf Sale, Michele Caprio

items.title: ERIS: Enhancing the Privacy-Utility-Scalability Trade-Off in Federated Learning via Federated Shard Aggregation
items.abstract: Scaling Federated Learning (FL) to billion-parameter models forces a challenging trade-off between privacy, scalability, and model utility. Existing solutions often tackle these challenges in isolation, sacrificing accuracy, relying on costly cryptographic tools, or introducing communication and optimization inefficiencies that affect convergence. We introduce ERIS, an FL framework centered on Federated Shard Aggregation (FSA), a novel mechanism that partitions each client update into non-overlapping shards whose aggregation is distributed across multiple client-side aggregators. FSA removes the central aggregation bottleneck, limits the information visible to any single observer, and preserves the centralized FL update after reassembly. ERIS can further readily integrate Distributed Shifted Compression (DSC) to reduce transmitted payloads and exposed coordinates. We prove that ERIS preserves convergence under standard assumptions and bounds mutual information leakage by the observable fraction of each update, decreasing with the number of client-side aggregators, and with the compression level when DSC is enabled. Experiments across image and text tasks, including large language models, show that ERIS achieves FedAvg-level utility while substantially reducing communication bottlenecks and improving robustness to membership inference and reconstruction attacks, without relying on heavy cryptography or utility-degrading perturbations.
items.authors: Dario Fenoglio, Pasquale Polverino, Akash Dhasade, Jacopo Quizi, Martin Gjoreski, Marc Langheinrich

items.title: Federated Learning of Nonlinear Temporal Dynamics with Graph Attention-based Cross-Client Interpretability
items.abstract: Networks of modern industrial systems are increasingly monitored by distributed sensors, where each system comprises multiple subsystems that generate high-dimensional time-series. These subsystems are often interdependent, making it important to understand how temporal patterns observed at one subsystem relate to those observed across others. This problem is particularly challenging in decentralized settings where raw measurements cannot be shared, and client observations are heterogeneous. Moreover, in practice, each subsystem (client) operates a fixed, proprietary model that cannot be modified or retrained, limiting the applicability of existing approaches. Separately, nonlinear dynamics make cross-client temporal interdependencies difficult to characterize, as they are embedded implicitly within nonlinear state-transition functions. This paper presents a vertical federated learning framework for learning one-step-ahead cross-client temporal interdependencies under these constraints. Each client maps high-dimensional local observations to low-dimensional latent states using a nonlinear state-space model, while a Graph Attention Network (GAT)-based central server learns a state-transition model over the communicated states. Given a candidate graph skeleton, the server learns state-dependent attention coefficients that capture cross-client interactions. We analytically relate the GAT attention coefficients to the Jacobian of the learned state-transition model, yielding a first-order characterization of cross-client interdependencies. We further establish bounded closeness of the learned dynamics and Jacobians to a corresponding centralized oracle. Synthetic experiments validate the theoretical results on controlled systems with known graph skeletons. Experiments on real-world datasets with unknown graph skeletons demonstrate superior federated root cause analysis over baselines.
items.authors: Ayse Tursucular, Ayush Mohanty, Nazal Mohamed, Nagi Gebraeel

items.title: Bridge Matching Sampler: Scalable Sampling via Generalized Fixed-Point Diffusion Matching
items.abstract: Sampling from unnormalized densities using diffusion models has emerged as a powerful paradigm. However, while recent approaches that use least-squares `matching' objectives have improved scalability, they often necessitate significant trade-offs, such as restricting prior distributions or relying on unstable optimization schemes. By generalizing these methods as special forms of fixed-point iterations rooted in Nelson's relation, we develop a new method that addresses these limitations, called Bridge Matching Sampler (BMS). Our approach enables learning a stochastic transport map between arbitrary prior and target distributions with a single, scalable, and stable objective. Furthermore, we introduce a damped variant of this iteration that incorporates a regularization term to mitigate mode collapse and further stabilize training. Empirically, we demonstrate that our method enables sampling at unprecedented scales while preserving mode diversity, achieving state-of-the-art results on complex synthetic densities and high-dimensional molecular benchmarks.
items.authors: Denis Blessing, Lorenz Richter, Julius Berner, Egor Malitskiy, Gerhard Neumann

items.title: Differentiable Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Predicting Cellular Responses to Gene Perturbation
items.abstract: Predicting transcriptional responses to genetic perturbations is fundamental to functional genomics and therapeutic discovery. Recent deep learning models have shown promise in single-cell perturbation response prediction, but they typically generate each response in isolation, without explicitly leveraging related perturbations. We introduce PT-RAG (Perturbation-aware Two-stage Retrieval-Augmented Generation), a plug-in retrieval-and-conditioning module for generative cellular perturbation response. PT-RAG augments an existing perturbation-response backbone with learned access to related perturbation contexts. The key challenge is that relevance is not fixed in this setting: functionally related genes may elicit different effects across cell types. PT-RAG addresses this with a two-stage retrieval mechanism: GenePT-based semantic retrieval first identifies K candidate perturbations, after which a differentiable Gumbel-Softmax selector adaptively selects retrieved contexts conditioned on the control cell state, the query perturbation, and each candidate perturbation. We evaluate PT-RAG on two backbones, a STATE-style generator used as a frozen random reservoir and a fully trained scGPT, across cross-cell-type and cross-perturbation generalization tasks. PT-RAG consistently improves distributional similarity and often overall predictive quality; for example, on scGPT cross-cell-type results, the 2-Wasserstein distance drops by 5.9% relative to scGPT alone. The code to reproduce our experiments is available at https://github.com/difra100/PT-RAG_NIPS.
items.authors: Andrea Giuseppe Di Francesco, Andrea Rubbi, Rishabh Jain, Pietro Li\`o
items.title_zh: 可微分检索增强生成模型预测细胞对基因扰动的响应
items.summary_zh: 预测基因扰动的转录响应是功能基因组学和治疗发现的基础。近期深度学习模型在单细胞扰动响应预测中展现出潜力，但通常独立生成每个响应，未能显著利用相关扰动。我们提出了PT-RAG（扰动感知两阶段检索增强生成），这是一个用于生成细胞扰动响应的插件检索与条件模块。PT-RAG通过学习相关扰动上下文来增强现有的扰动响应模型。关键挑战在于相关性在此设置中并非固定：功能相关基因在不同细胞类型中可能产生不同效果。PT-RAG通过两阶段检索机制解决此问题：基于GenePT的语义检索首先识别K个候选扰动，随后可微分的Gumbel-Softmax选择器根据控制细胞状态、查询扰动及每个候选扰动自适应选择检索上下文。我们在两个基础模型上评估PT-RAG，结果显示其在分布相似性和预测质量上均有显著提升。

items.title: Weight Clustering Reveals the Importance of Relative Rank in Large Language Models
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) contain billions of parameters, but many exact weight values are not essential. We apply scalar $K$-means clustering to pretrained models, replacing each weight matrix with only 16--64 shared values. For Llama~3.1-8B-Instruct and SmolLM2-135M, this preserves strong accuracy without retraining, providing a simple way to compress LLMs on disk. Fine-tuning only the cluster centroids further recovers 30--40\% of the remaining accuracy loss. Using clustering as an analysis tool, we then keep the cluster assignments fixed and perturb only the shared values, to study which of their properties matter most. We find that preserving their \emph{relative rank} (which connections are stronger or weaker than others) is more important than preserving their exact magnitudes. Breaking this ordering greatly increases perplexity, while changing the values but keeping the ordering causes little loss in many middle and late layers. However, rank preservation alone is not sufficient. Model performance also depends on maintaining the variance of the reconstructed weights, while early layers remain more sensitive; perturbing the cluster assignments themselves shows that their spatial geometry is also load-bearing. We observe the same behavior across four LLMs from two architecture families. These results suggest that the ordering of weights, together with their overall variance, plays a central role in LLM compression and robustness.
items.authors: Borja Aizpurua, Sukhbinder Singh, Rom\'an Or\'us

items.title: Koopman-Based Nonlinear Identification and Model Predictive Control of a Turbofan Engine
items.abstract: This paper investigates Koopman operator-based approaches for multivariable control of a two-spool turbofan engine. A physics-based component-level model is developed to generate training data and validate the controllers. A meta-heuristic extended dynamic mode decomposition is adapted, with a cost function designed to accurately capture both spool-speed dynamics and the engine pressure ratio (EPR), enabling the construction of a single Koopman model that can be reused across multiple control strategies. Using the identified time-varying Koopman model, an adaptive Koopman-based model predictive controller (AKMPC) with a disturbance observer is developed and compared with a Koopman-based feedback linearization controller (K-FBLC) and its integrator-augmented version (K-FBLC-I). The Koopman representation further enables nonlinear GTE output limiters, such as rotor-acceleration and turbine-inlet-temperature limits, to be expressed as linear constraints in the AKMPC. The controllers are evaluated for two control configurations of spool speeds and EPR, under both sea-level and varying flight conditions. The results demonstrate that the proposed identification approach enables accurate predictions of both spool speeds and EPR, allowing the Koopman model to be reused flexibly across different control formulations. While all strategies achieve comparable performance in sea-level conditions, the AKMPC demonstrates improved performance under varying flight conditions due to its ability to capture nonlinear dynamics, handle constraints, and compensate for model mismatch. Moreover, the EPR control strategy improves the thrust response. The study highlights the applicability of Koopman-based control and the advantages of the AKMPC framework for robust turbofan engine control.
items.authors: David Grasev

items.title: Approximating Uniform Random Rotations by Two-Stage Structured Hadamard Rotations in High Dimensions
items.abstract: Uniform random rotations are useful in fast Johnson--Lindenstrauss embeddings, kernel approximation, communication-efficient learning, and recent AI compression pipelines, but are computationally expensive to generate and apply in high dimensions. A practical alternative repeats Walsh--Hadamard transforms with random sign diagonals. Applying this structured rotation twice has shown empirical benefits, but supporting theory remains limited. We study the approximation quality of the two-stage structured Hadamard rotation. Here $d$ is the dimension of the rotated vector. On the positive side, we prove explicit, nonasymptotic upper bounds of order $\sqrt{\log d/d}$ in both Kolmogorov and Wasserstein-1 distance for corresponding coordinates scaled by $\sqrt d$, uniformly over unit inputs and coordinates. For the input $u=e_1$, both distances also have lower bounds of order $d^{-1/2}$ at every coordinate. On the negative side, we prove an explicit lower bound on the Wasserstein-1 distance between the full vector distributions, showing a substantial discrepancy that does not vanish as $d$ grows for the input $u=e_1$. For the same input, we also prove a matching asymptotic upper bound, showing that the lower-bound scale is sharp. Taken together, the results identify a separation between one-dimensional marginal behavior, where approximation improves with dimension, and the full-vector law, where a nonvanishing Wasserstein-1 discrepancy remains. The marginal bounds control coordinate threshold probabilities and expected scalar Lipschitz losses, including expected averages over coordinates. They do not establish joint-coordinate approximation, and the full-vector separation does not imply failure of a particular algorithm. Connecting these distributional results to performance guarantees for specific algorithms remains open.
items.authors: Tomer Zilca, Gal Mendelson

items.title: Training Non-Differentiable Networks via Optimal Transport
items.abstract: Hard thresholds, quantization, and discrete routing can produce training losses with flat regions and jumps, where ordinary gradients vanish or are undefined. We introduce PolyStep, a forward-only optimizer that evaluates rotated polytope probes and moves parameter blocks along weighted averages of the probe directions. We derive the weights from one-sided entropic transport and use its uncoupled softmax solution in our primary experiments. Our analysis explains when variation among probe costs produces motion and when that motion decreases the loss. On a regular simplex, nonconstant costs always give a nonzero direction. For monotone ridge losses, the softmax update cannot increase the loss at any positive temperature; a perturbation bound gives sufficient conditions for descent near curved jumps. For bounded measurable losses, we randomize the probe radii and identify an exact smoothing whose gradient equals the expected linear cost-weighted direction up to scale. This identity yields a stationarity bound for an idealized fixed-temperature variant: under regularity and sampling assumptions stronger than those met by our trained configurations, the bound has an $O(T^{-1/2})$ term and a persistent bias floor. We evaluate the practical method on networks with hard operations, discrete optimization, and policy search. On MNIST with hard-threshold spiking neurons, PolyStep reaches $93.0 \pm 0.2\%$, compared with $79.6 \pm 5.2\%$ for the best-tuned gradient-free baseline at matched evaluations. These gains come with a query cost proportional to the search dimension per fresh step, which limits the number of updates available at a fixed budget.
items.authors: An T. Le

items.title: Playing the network backward: A Game Theoretic Attribution Framework
items.abstract: Attribution methods explain which input features drive a model's prediction, making them central to model debugging and mechanistic interpretability. Yet backward attribution methods, including gradients, LRP, and transformer-specific rules, lack a shared framework in which to compare the underlying backward calculations. We introduce such a framework by recasting backward attribution as a two-player game on an extended network graph, building on Gaubert and Vlassopoulos' ReLU Net Game. Gradients and the full alpha-beta-LRP family arise as integrals over game trajectories under specific equilibria, so attribution maps become projections of trajectory distributions rather than the primary object. Desired explanation properties, such as localisation focus, robustness to input noise, or stable attention routing, can be specified as game-theoretic concepts, including policy regularization, risk aversion, and extended action sets, and translate directly into novel adaptations of the well-known backward rules. On ViT-B/16, one such selected adaptation of alpha-beta-LRP outperforms prior transformer-specific backward methods across all considered localisation metrics.
items.authors: Jakob Paul Zimmermann, Jim Berend, Georg Loho, Sebastian Lapuschkin, Wojciech Samek

items.title: Constrained Triple-Head Price Optimization (C3PO) Network for Discrete-Choice Models
items.abstract: We propose a Constrained Triple-Head Price Optimization (C3PO) network for real-time bi-level decision making in discrete-choice environments. In these settings, a seller selects product or service offerings to achieve business objectives, while heterogeneous users make personalized acceptance or rejection decisions based on their preferences, ultimately determining seller outcomes. Existing approaches that fine-tune pre-trained tabular foundation models on synthetic data are limited by their imitation-learning paradigm and inability to enforce common pricing rules, including cross-product and global constraints. C3PO addresses these limitations through a novel transformer-based architecture that jointly integrates price imitation learning, multi-task revenue prediction, and in-context elasticity learning to generate robust pricing recommendations across domains without retraining. A lightweight differentiable constraint layer enables generated prices to satisfy business constraints while optimizing the revenue objective. We demonstrate strong out-of-distribution performance on simulated, synthetic, and real-world datasets. Across simulated benchmarks where the calibrated MNL model is misspecified relative to the ground-truth choice model, C3PO improves expected revenue by 1.4 to 7.9 percentage points over a calibrated MNL baseline. The constraint layer reduces average absolute constraint violations by more than 50\%. We further deploy the model in real-world applications, including healthcare tender pricing and airline ancillary pricing, where C3PO improves directional pricing effectiveness, measured by price-increase and price-decrease recall, by 18--34 percentage points depending on the baselines considered, including calibrated MNL, classical optimization, and off-the-shelf tabular foundation-models.
items.authors: Shivaram Subramanian, Zhengliang Xue, Markus Ettl, Yingdong Lu, Jayant Kalagnanam

items.title: Reinforcement learning for inverse silhouette design and rapid laser cutting of compact parallelogram quad kirigami prototypes
items.abstract: Kirigami is an increasingly useful fabrication method to produce shape-programmable metamaterial structures. However, inverse design remains difficult because deployment is nonlinear, and feasible cut layouts must satisfy discrete compatibility rules, avoid overlap, and map one target shape to valid designs. We present RL-Kirigami, an inverse design framework that combines optimal-transport conditional flow matching (OT-CFM) with reinforcement learning to generate compatible ratio fields for compact reconfigurable parallelogram quad kirigami. A marching decoder enforces global geometric compatibility, and Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) aligns the generator with nondifferentiable rewards for silhouette matching, feasibility, and ratio-field regularity. Across procedurally generated target shape instances, a single sample from the pretrained OT-CFM prior reached $94.2\%~\mathrm{sIoU}$ and outperformed solver baselines while reducing forward simulator evaluations from hundreds to $1$. GRPO improved accuracy to $94.91\%~\mathrm{sIoU}$ and, with regularity included, reduced $\mathrm{TV}(\mathbf{x})$ from $0.95$ to $0.81$ while maintaining $94.83\%~\mathrm{sIoU}$. Generated layouts were exported to DXF and laser cut in $50~\mu\mathrm{m}$ polymeric sheets to produce deployable prototypes in $8.0\pm 1.0$ minutes per part. These results support a manufacturing-aware inverse design workflow for deployable kirigami metamaterials under geometric feasibility constraints. Code is available at https://github.com/milad1378yz/RL-Kirigami.
items.authors: Milad Yazdani, Shahriar Shalileh, Dena Shahriari

items.title: Model Capacity Determines Grokking through Competing Memorisation and Generalisation Speeds
items.abstract: Existing accounts of grokking explain the phenomena in terms of mechanistic frameworks such as circuit efficiency or lazy-to-rich transitions. However, despite a known dependence between grokking and model size, how model capacity shapes grokking remains an open question. We give an information-theoretic account of this relationship on the task of modular arithmetic, showing that grokking does not immediately occur when a model becomes large enough to memorise the training set, but rather emerges as the outcome of a competition between two measurable timescales: a memorisation speed $T_{\text{mem}}(P)$ and a generalisation speed $T_{\text{gen}}(P)$, both of which are functions of model parameter count $P$. Adapting the information capacity framework of Morris et al. (2025), we estimate $T_{\text{mem}}(P)$ on random-label data of equivalent complexity and $T_{\text{gen}}(P)$ on the modular task itself, and show that grokking emerges close to the parameter scale where these timescales intersect. The framework also suggests an empirical model for predicting memorisation speed given model capacity and dataset complexity, recovering the previously reported empirical observation that larger models memorise faster. Overall, we motivate the formalisation of different learning timescales as important abstractions to study when explaining how model capacity shapes grokking on algorithmic tasks.
items.authors: Yiding Song, Hanming Ye

items.title: On the Approximation Complexity of Matrix Product Operator (MPO) Born Machines
items.abstract: Matrix product operator Born machines (MPO-BMs) are tractable tensor-network models for probabilistic modeling, yet their approximation capabilities remain poorly understood in theory. In this paper, we characterize these capabilities from both negative and positive perspectives. As a negative result, we prove that constructing a polynomial-bond MPO-BM approximation to an arbitrary continuous target with bounded KL error is NP-hard. On the positive side, for score-based variational inference, we prove that targets satisfying a log-Sobolev inequality admit polynomial-bond MPO-BM approximations with provable KL guarantees when the loss-induced Hamiltonian is local and has a constant spectral gap. Furthermore, under the same conditions, we construct local importance-sampling estimators and prove that polynomially many local score queries suffice to preserve the KL guarantees.
items.authors: Chao Li, Zerui Tao, Yuchen Cong, Jian Xu, Qibin Zhao

items.title: Bayesian Nonparametric Mixed-Effect ODEs with Gaussian Processes
items.abstract: Dynamical modelling in pharmacometrics, systems biology, and epidemiology often involves subjects with related but distinct dynamics, observed through temporally sparse and irregular measurements. Classical nonlinear mixed-effects ODE models represent this heterogeneity but rely on parametric vector fields, making them vulnerable to structural misspecification. Existing nonparametric ODE methods typically assume shared dynamics rather than an explicit mixed-effect hierarchy. We propose MEGPODE, a Bayesian nonparametric mixed-effect ODE model that decomposes each subject's vector field into a shared population component and a subject-specific deviation, both endowed with Gaussian process priors. To avoid repeated ODE solves during training, we represent latent trajectories with state-space GP priors and penalize discrepancies between their derivatives and the vector fields on a finite time grid. A single variational objective enables approximate joint inference over trajectories and vector fields, accounting for state uncertainty and dependence between population and subject-specific dynamics. Across heterogeneous oscillatory and biomedical ODE benchmarks, MEGPODE improves population-field recovery and subject-level trajectory prediction relative to strong baselines.
items.authors: Julien Martinelli, Maksim Sinelnikov, Harri L\"ahdesm\"aki, Quentin Clairon, M\'elanie Prague

items.title: Quadratic Characterizations for Reachability Analysis of Neural Networks
items.abstract: Quadratic constraints (QCs) are widely used to characterize nonlinearities and uncertainties, but generic analytical characterizations can be conservative on bounded domains. This paper develops a framework for constructing verified quadratic characterizations of scalar relations in the two-dimensional real plane. Candidate quadratic inequalities are locally generated by solving convex quadratic programs using samples from the relation and exterior sample points. They are then verified globally using sum-of-squares certificates over an exact semialgebraic description or, in the case of nonpolynomial relations, over relaxed polynomial descriptions. The resulting verified constraints define a sound overapproximation of the scalar relations over the considered domains. These constraints are directly compatible with existing analysis frameworks based on QCs and pointwise integral quadratic constraints (IQCs) for static nonlinearities and uncertainties, and they can also be embedded in QC-based semidefinite programs for reachability and safety analysis of feedforward neural networks. For smooth activations such as $\tanh$, the method yields domain-dependent quadratic characterizations that constitute an alternative to generic sector- or slope-based descriptions. For ReLU networks, we give methods to reduce conservatism in QC-based reachability analysis of feedforward networks by exploiting dependencies between neurons and tighter local bounds. Numerical examples demonstrate improved reachability results for smooth activations, reduced conservatism for ReLU networks, and applicability beyond neural networks through an example involving saturation.
items.authors: Elias Khalife, Mazen Farhood, Pierre-Loic Garoche

items.title: SURF: Steering the Scalarization Weight to Uniformly Traverse the Pareto Front
items.abstract: Scalarization is widely used in multi-objective optimization owing to its simplicity and scalability. In many applications, the goal is to generate solutions that represent diverse user preferences, ideally with uniform coverage of the Pareto front (PF). However, uniformly sampling scalarization weights usually induces non-uniform coverage of the PF. We explain this mismatch through the geometry of the scalarization path. As the weight varies, the corresponding solutions traverse the PF at a generally nonuniform speed. Integrating this speed gives cumulative arc length. After normalization by the total length, it defines a cumulative distribution function (CDF) on weights whose inverse selects points at equal arc-length intervals. Building on this insight, we propose SURF (Sampling Uniformly along the Pareto Front). For structured problems, including bi-objective bandits, we derive analytical expressions for this CDF map and the resulting PF-aware weight sampling rule. For general problems, SURF alternates between CDF reconstruction and weight sampling. Theoretically, we show that under provable conditions for bi-objective LS, SURF's CDF reconstruction error converges linearly to an $O(N^{-2})$ discretization floor. Empirically, experiments on bandits, multi-objective-gymnasium, and multi-objective LLM alignment demonstrate that SURF efficiently achieves more uniform PF coverage than baselines.
items.authors: Liuyuan Jiang, Chentong Huang, Lisha Chen

items.title: Do Deep Ensembles Actually Capture Uncertainty in Graph Neural Networks?
items.abstract: While deep ensembles are widely considered to be the default method for uncertainty quantification in deep learning, their effectiveness for graph-structured data is often simply assumed based on successes in domains like computer vision. We investigate standard deep ensembles specifically for message-passing graph neural networks. Benchmarking across eight datasets representing varied tasks and complexities, we reveal that ensembles provide only marginal improvement over a single model. These marginal gains stem primarily from averaging out optimization noise in point predictions rather than from meaningfully better uncertainty estimates. Through an aleatoric-epistemic decomposition, we identify epistemic collapse: independently trained networks consistently converge to overly similar predictions. Because disagreement is the fundamental mechanism through which ensembles capture epistemic uncertainty, this lack of diversity neutralizes their key advantage. Towards explaining this phenomenon, we derive a bound on epistemic variance in terms of the graph topology and Dirichlet energy budget, linking epistemic collapse to the smoothing bias of message passing. Our results suggest that deep ensemble success does not seamlessly transfer to graph machine learning.
items.authors: Pedro C. Vieira, Viacheslav Borovitskiy, Pedro Ribeiro

items.title: A Unified Benchmark for Dynamic Medical Treatment Reinforcement Learning
items.abstract: Medical treatment recommendation poses several challenges to reinforcement learning (RL): patient physiology evolves in continuous time, measurements and interventions are performed at irregular intervals, and treatment effects vary substantially across individuals. Existing RL formulations and simulated environments, however, are based on discrete-time MDPs with fixed decision intervals. Thus, it remains difficult to evaluate whether RL methods can handle time-interval-dependent disease progression, personalized treatment response, and safety between consecutive measurement points. To address this gap, we introduce MedGym, a benchmark environment for dynamic treatment recommendation. MedGym models longitudinal patient evolution in a continuous-time framework and constructs a configurable medical RL benchmark from clinical data by using Physics-Informed Neural Networks. The resulting benchmark enables direct comparison between discrete-time and continuous-time methods under irregular treatment timing and patient-specific dynamics. Furthermore, MedGym supports evaluation from clinically important perspectives, such as personalization and trajectory-level safety. By providing a standardized and configurable benchmark for continuous-time dynamic treatment, MedGym enables more realistic and informative evaluation of medical RL methods.
items.authors: Yuepeng Wang, Ken Kawano, Yoshihiko Fujisawa, Yongqi Zhou, Akifumi Wachi, Mehrshad Sadria, Lei Zhou, Richard Weiss, Katsuki Fujisawa, Ying Chen, Xin Liu, Kyoung-Sook Kim, Xiao Hu, Sebastien Gros, Xun Shen

items.title: Learning Transfers: Kan Extensions of Topological Invariants of Learned Representations
items.abstract: When a learned representation is reused for a new task, which of its structure should survive? A task is a small category, a change of task is a functor $J$, and the invariants of a trained representation form a functor $F$. The left Kan extension $\operatorname{Lan}_JF$ is the invariant that the source and the change of task force on the target: by its universal property, every comparison of the source with an observed target invariant factors through it. The transfer discrepancy is the largest distance, over the target objects, between this extension and the observed invariant. For persistent homology the extension is a cokernel over comma categories, and a functorial version of the discrepancy, which also compares the maps between target objects, is $1$-Lipschitz under interleavings. On finite samples the discrepancy is a bottleneck distance, computed without approximation. For data glued from two pieces whose exclusive parts lie farther apart than the filtration scale, a Mayer-Vietoris sequence identifies what extending homology loses, while extending chains loses nothing. For a merge of labelled point clouds, the degree-zero discrepancy vanishes if and only if some $1$-Lipschitz classifier has a margin above the filtration scale at every sample point. In experiments on sampled manifolds, trained encoders and pretrained image models, every exact prediction holds on every sample. The discrepancy of truncated invariants recovers a hidden merge of separated parts far above chance and tells the intended target of a merge from a permuted control, but across pretrained models it does not track the accuracy of a linear probe.
items.authors: Luciano Melodia

items.title: Urban Power Grid Topology and Hierarchy Identification from Open Data
items.abstract: Understanding the complex topology and hierarchy of urban power grid is crucial for energy prognosis, power flow management, and system resilience analysis. However, detailed grid information remains largely proprietary. This information, nevertheless, is crucial especially for analyzing the last-mile distribution networks connecting individual buildings. This paper addresses this challenge by developing an open-data-driven framework to identify urban power grid topology, from high-voltage transmission down to individual building connections. We integrate public infrastructure data (power-lines, substations, transformers, poles) to map the high and medium-voltage grid skeleton. We then leverage geospatial machine learning on OpenStreetMap building data to cluster loads of building energy demand. Upon the clustering, we develop the physical topology of the final distribution lines linking the clustered buildings and low-voltage distribution grids. Our derived grid topology incorporates physical and geographical constraints like voltage level and road networks, thus leading to reasonable topology and hierarchy of grid networks. We apply the developed framework to the districts of Alna in Oslo, Norway, and Waiheke Island in New Zealand, and we reconstruct the complete grid topology that connects all the buildings, power lines, and electricity infrastructure assets. With the developed framework, we provide a critical tool that facilitates power system analysis, e.g., power flow optimization, cascading failure simulation, and grid resilience against the penetration of distributed renewable generation. This work also opens the opportunity to build energy digital twins that fuse power assets and grid topology, geographic constraints, and fine-grained power demand profiles.
items.authors: Shiliang Zhang, Sabita Maharjan, Alexey Vinel, Shui Yu

items.title: VLA-FAIL: Efficient Task Failure Detection for Finetuned Vision-Language-Action Models
items.abstract: Vision-language-action models (VLAs) achieve state-of-the-art performance on many robotic manipulation tasks, yet they can still behave unpredictably in out-of-distribution scenarios. Runtime failure detection is therefore essential for the safe real-world deployment of VLAs.However, existing task failure detectors require computationally expensive action sampling, are based on architectural assumptions that limit their applicability to VLAs, or need access to failure rollouts. We propose VLA-FAIL, a lightweight and broadly applicable failure detection framework for VLAs that combines two novel failure detectors with minimal overhead, without requiring failure data. The first, last-layer Mahalanobis distance (LLMD), detects out-of-distribution states by measuring token-wise deviations in last-layer features relative to the training data. The second, action chunk consistency (ACC), exploits the temporal overlap induced by receding-horizon control and detects failures when consecutive action chunks become inconsistent. To capture the trade-off between detection accuracy and detection latency, we introduce \textsc{AUCPDT}, a threshold-independent metric that jointly evaluates precision, recall, and detection time. Through extensive real-world and simulation experiments, we demonstrate that LLMD and ACC capture complementary failure modes whose combination enables reliable and early failure detection across diverse tasks, frequently outperforming significantly more expensive baseline methods. Project page: https://vla-fail.github.io/vla-fail-2026
items.authors: Florian Seligmann, Emiliyan Gospodinov, Enes Ulas Dincer, Gerhard Neumann

items.title: FlowAWR: Online Adaptive Flow Reinforcement via Advantage-Weighted Rectification
items.abstract: Aligning generative flow models on continuous spaces via online reinforcement learning is constrained by intractable trajectory likelihoods. Existing density-approximated policy gradient methods rely on stochastic SDE samplers to construct tractable transition kernels, which introduce training-inference inconsistencies and necessitates Classifier-Free Guidance (CFG). While implicit frameworks such as DiffusionNFT directly optimize forward-process velocity fields, its heuristic fixed-magnitude corrections prevent optimization strength from relative intra-group quality. We propose \textit{Flow Advantage-Weighted Rectification} (\textbf{FlowAWR}), a paradigm that recasts continuous generative policy optimization as supervised regression toward a theoretically optimal velocity field. Starting from the optimal policy of a KL-constrained reward maximization, FlowAWR derives the optimal velocity field that admits a magnitude-aware, advantage-weighted rectification form, yielding SDE-free optimization and CFG-free generation. In comparative evaluations on SD3.5-Medium, FlowAWR achieves improved alignment performance alongside a 2$\times$ to 5$\times$ convergence acceleration over DiffusionNFT (e.g., reaching a 24.12 PickScore in 1.2k steps, versus 23.82 in 2.0k steps for DiffusionNFT and 23.50 in $>$4k steps for FlowGRPO). Under multi-reward constraints, FlowAWR sustains generation quality, satisfying structural rules while maintaining stable out-of-domain performance. Code at \href{https://github.com/Fuzm7/FlowAWR}{FlowAWR}.
items.authors: Zheming Fu, Ruizhe He, Wei Shang, Xiaoxiao Ma, Lianrui Mu, Lei Wang, Chang Liu, Siming Fu
