To prevent current ``embarrassment of over-prediction'', we propose necessary conditions for next-generation AI that should be automatically enforced before claiming any new materials.
items.authors: Daniel E Widdowson, Tatiana V Kurlina, Olga D Anosova, Vitaliy A Kurlin

items.title: Surface scalar plasmons on curved interfaces: a venue for analogue gravity
items.abstract: We investigate whether the geometry of a curved conductor--dielectric interface can modify the effective mass and propagation of scalar surface plasmons (SSPs). In the hydrodynamic limit, we describe SSPs as density perturbations in a semiclassical jellium electron gas. Using a thin--layer dimensional reduction procedure, we derive a massive Klein--Gordon equation for SSPs on the curved interface with a geometric potential. We find that under specific conditions, the geometric potential allows SSP propagation with a vanishing effective mass. We then apply the formalism to a well known analogue black hole configuration, determining the corresponding quasinormal mode frequencies. Our results show that interface curvature provides a geometric handle on plasmon propagation and localization, suggesting new possibilities for plasmon transport and analogue gravity experiments with surface plasmons.
items.authors: Matheus E. Pereira

items.title: Enhanced Coulomb pseudopotentials in high-pressure hydrides from first principles
items.abstract: In the Eliashberg theory of superconductivity, Coulomb interactions oppose the phonon-mediated attraction and suppress the superconducting critical temperature $T_{\mathrm{c}}$. However, most first-principles predictions continue to treat this repulsion with an empirical Coulomb pseudopotential $\mu^*_{\text{ME}}$ in the range 0.1-0.15. Here we present first-principles calculations of the Coulomb parameter $\mu$ and pseudopotential $\mu^*_{\text{ME}}$ in superconducting hydrides across a range of pressures. The screened Coulomb interaction is evaluated at the random phase approximation level with the Mantel code. We demonstrate that several hydride systems, including H$_3$S, YSbH$_6$ and Mg$_2$IrH$_6$, have strong Coulomb repulsions driven by a large density of states at the Fermi energy, $N_{\mathrm{F}}$. For Mg$_2$IrH$_6$ we obtain $\mu=0.62$ and $\mu^*_{\text{ME}}\approx0.39$, leading to a 40 K suppression in $T_{\mathrm{c}}$ relative to a standard $\mu^*_{\text{ME}}=0.16$. Our obtained $\mu^*_{\text{ME}}$ is far above the conventional range and, accounting for the energy dependence of the density of states, resolves the factor-of-two discrepancy between $T_{\mathrm{c}}$ estimates of previous studies. Across all systems and pressures studied, we find that $\mu$ closely tracks $N_{\mathrm{F}}$, suggesting that commonly used $\mu^*_{\text{ME}}$ values lead to overestimated $T_{\mathrm{c}}$ in materials where the density of states at the Fermi energy is large.
items.authors: Kieran Bozier, Chris J. Pickard

items.title: Ground-State Phase Diagram of the Effective Model with Antiferromagnetic Nearest-Neighbor and Ferromagnetic Next-Nearest-Neighbor Interactions in 1/1 Periodic Approximants to Icosahedral Quasicrystals
items.abstract: By performing complete enumeration of all configurations of magnetic moments, we have determined the ground-state phase diagram of the effective model with antiferromagnetic nearest-neighbor interactions $J_1$ and ferromagnetic next-nearest-neighbor interactions $J_2$ on the 1/1 periodic approximant to icosahedral quasicrystal. Depending on the ratio of $J_2/J_1$ and the magnetic anisotropy arising from the crystalline electric field, various non-collinear ferrimagnetic orders and antiferromagnetic orders are shown to be stabilized, whose magnetic space groups are identified as $R\bar{3}$, $C2'/m'$, $Pm'm'2$ and $I_{\rm P}m'\bar{3}'$. We have revealed the topological as well as magnetic property of each ground state with degeneracy, which is useful to understand experimental observations of magnetic structures and domains in the rare-earth-based 1/1 approximants.
items.authors: Shinji Watanabe

items.title: Alter-excitons in Altermagnets: Symmetry, Splitting and Dispersion
items.abstract: Magnetism provides a fertile platform for discovering emergent quantum phenomena governed by symmetry. Recent developments of spin-space-group (SSG) theory have revealed altermagnets as a distinct class of nonrelativistic collinear magnets with unconventional spin-dependent electronic structures. Here, we demonstrate that altermagnetic symmetry imposes fundamentally different constraints on electronic and excitonic excitations. Although the quasiparticle and two-body Hamiltonians possess identical SSG symmetries, we find that symmetry-protected degeneracies present in the electronic band structure can be intrinsically lifted in the exciton spectrum at specific momenta. This splitting arises solely from the many-body nature of excitons and does not require spin-orbit coupling or noncollinear magnetic order. Combining symmetry analysis with many-body perturbation theory, we predict a novel class of spin-split excitonic quasiparticles, termed alter-excitons, and reveal their characteristic dispersions in altermagnetic systems. Our results establish excitons as a sensitive probe of hidden spin-space symmetries and uncover a new route toward symmetry-engineered many-body phenomena in collinear magnets.
items.authors: Yuanfan Xiong, Liangyu Wang, Xuan Wu, Wei Hu, Jinlong Yang

items.title: Electron- and hole-doped superconductivity in two-dimensional electride ZrX$_2$ (X = Cl, Br, I)
items.abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) superconducting systems have recently emerged as a frontier in condensed matter physics, driven by their unique physical properties and potential applications. Using first-principles calculations, we show that monolayer ZrX$_2$ (X = Cl, Br, I), which is a family of 2D semiconducting electrides, hosts phonon-mediated superconductivity under both electron and hole dopings. Electron doping in ZrX$_{2}$ can achieve high superconducting transition temperatures at very low concentrations, with ZrBr$_2$ reaching $T_c = 30.0$ K at 0.01 \textit{e}/f.u., followed by ZrCl$_2$ (22.5 K at 0.05 \textit{e}/f.u.) and ZrI$_2$ (18.1 K at 0.01 \textit{e}/f.u.), for which the high $T_c$ originates from the flat conduction band minimum, with Van Hove singularities nearby enhancing the density of states. In contrast, hole doping requires higher concentrations (0.2--0.25 \textit{h}/f.u.) to activate superconductivity, yielding $T_c \sim 2$ K, and approaches a magnetic instability at elevated doping levels. By comparing with InSe and LaBr$_2$, we identify the spatial location and orbital character of excess electrons as key factors determining the strength of hole-doped superconductivity and the nature of competing orders. These findings establish monolayer ZrX$_2$ as a platform for bipolar superconductivity in a 2D electride and provide insights into flat-band engineering for high-$T_c$ superconductors.
items.authors: Tian-Xin Liu, Xin-Yang Li, Zuo-Wei Yin, Jing Jiang, Ben-Chao Gong, Wei Fan, Xiao-Le Qiu, Kai Liu

items.title: Orbital transfer reveals material-selective structure in Rydberg excitons
items.abstract: Rydberg excitons in atomically thin semiconductors offer a sensitive view of dielectric screening and electronic structure. As their spectra become increasingly well resolved, a central question is how much material information an effective Hamiltonian can predict beyond the states used to determine it. Using the 1s, 2p and 2s levels to determine a scalar Rytova-Keldysh Hamiltonian, we test its transfer to the excluded 3p state. The transfer deviations have opposite signs: the observed 3p lies 7.38 meV below the prediction in MoSe2 and 5.58 meV above it in WS2; the opposite signs persist across the complete reported +/-2-sigma peak-error boxes. In a separate high-field-calibrated benchmark, RK removes 66.8% of the orbital error of a pure two-dimensional Coulomb reference, making the remaining state-selective deviations particularly informative. After separating gap and common-scale contributions, the residuals reveal distinct material-dependent orbital patterns and constrain simple multichannel descriptions. For WS2, the measured 2p/3p curvatures yield a parameter-fixed prediction, Q4p=+4.08 meV, for a future same-platform measurement. Together these results show how a well-performing spectral model can be tested for transferable physical information, with the next unmeasured state providing an independent experimental check.
items.authors: Mengli Wang, Peng Chen, Wenqi Xue, Haonan Xia, Hong Zhang, Benniu Zhang

items.title: X-ray absorption spectroscopic studies of oxygen-deficient double perovskite oxide NdBaCo$_2$O$_{5+\delta}$ ($\delta \sim 0.65$)
items.abstract: The degree of oxygen vacancy in A-site-doped layered double perovskite oxides can lead to anion vacancy ordering, which subsequently results in distinct superstructures. We have studied oxygen deficient double perovskite oxide, NdBaCo$2$O$_{5+\delta}$ ($\delta \sim$ 0.65), utilising X-ray absorption near edge structure (XANES) spectroscopy complemented by multiple scattering and first-principles calculations based on density functional theory (DFT+U). The present results establish a direct correlation between oxygen-vacancy distribution, magnetic inhomogeneity, and charge transport in layered cobaltates. Our investigations on the Co K, Ba, and Nd $L_{\mathrm{III}}$ edges suggest that the near-edge spectra, based on the number and shape of the spectral features, indicate the value of $\delta$ for the compound under study lies closer to 0.75. The analysis of the Ba $L_{\mathrm{III}}$ edge spectrum confirms the +2 oxidation state for Ba ions. The Co K-edge near-edge spectra suggest the possibility of oxygen vacancies arising at the basal sites in addition to the apical sites. This is counterintuitive to the common understanding that oxygen vacancies usually occur at the apical sites, i.e., in the lanthanide (Nd) layer in these compounds. Such a distribution of oxygen vacancies naturally explains the Griffith phase and the conduction mechanism of variable range hopping observed in the compound. The vacancy distribution, when at the optimum level, can also bring about easier oxygen ion mobility and a more sensitive and faster oxygen sensor. We believe that our results will help in tailoring oxygen-ion mobility and enhancing oxygen-sensing performance.
items.authors: Himanshu Pant, S. Khalid, R. Bindu

items.title: Controlling the Atomic Reconstruction in Twisted MoSe$_2$/WSe$_2$ with a Monolayer hBN Spacer
items.abstract: Twisted van der Waals heterobilayers are a promising material platform for studying collective exciton many-body phenomena, but near-aligned structures often exhibit a local, anisotropic atomic reconstruction that compromises lateral homogeneity. The present study describes how atomic-scale rearrangement in adjacent regions of hBN-encapsulated, near-aligned MoSe$_2$/WSe$_2$ heterobilayers is controlled by the presence of a mono- or bilayer hBN spacer between the two monolayers. High-angle annular dark-field STEM directly resolves the atomic alignment in both layers and shows that the spacer suppresses the reconstruction and strongly increases the structural uniformity of the heterobilayers. 4D-STEM quantitatively maps local rotation, dilation, and heterostrain, revealing that the separated regions remain consistent with rigid moir\'e superlattice simulations, whereas without the spacer the structural parameters have two to three times broader distributions. By suppressing reconstruction, ultrathin hBN spacers therefore provide an effective route to enhance lattice homogeneity in MoSe$_2$/WSe$_2$ heterobilayers targeting collective excitonic and optoelectronic phenomena.
items.authors: Johannes Figueiredo, Kaiyuan Chen, Aubrey Penn, Mirco Troue, Sebastian Loy, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Frances M. Ross, Julian Klein, Alexander W. Holleitner

items.title: Aubry-Andr\'e transition in photonic time quasicrystals
items.abstract: In one dimension, Anderson localization by a disordered potential sets in at any strength, whereas localization by a quasiperiodic potential in the Aubry-Andr\'e model occurs through a transition at a critical strength. Disordered photonic time crystals exhibit a temporal counterpart of this Anderson localization, in which light, instead of decaying in space, stops propagating and grows in time. Whether a counterpart of the Aubry-Andr\'e transition exists in photonic time quasicrystals remains an open question. Here we show that it does, and that the transition occurs at mobility edges in momentum rather than in energy. These edges arise even under impulsive modulation, where the field obeys the self-dual almost-Mathieu equation exactly, and for general analytic modulations Avila's global theory reveals the condition under which they form. The Aubry-Andr\'e transition thus extends from spatial lattices to the time domain, where it sorts light by wave number into components that propagate and components that stop and grow.
items.authors: Shuhang Chen, Qi Zhu

items.title: Giant geometric nonlinear transport in inhomogeneously strained Bi$_2$Se$_3$ single crystalline slabs
items.abstract: Electrical transport in non-centrosymmetric materials exhibits a nonlinear conductivity tensor component that generates second-harmonic voltages in response to applied electric fields. Harnessing this effect is essential for developing zero-threshold electromagnetic energy harvesters and broadband frequency upconverters, both of which require maximizing the nonlinear responsivity. Here, we demonstrate that inhomogeneously strained macroscopic slabs of the topological insulator Bi$_2$Se$_3$ achieve a record-high nonlinear responsivity of $10^4\,\mu$m/V: a six orders of magnitude boost compared to its thin-film counterparts. We attribute this giant enhancement to a classical geometric nonlinear transport effect, which is driven by complex strain gradients within the bulk material. Notably, a similar geometric mechanism known as geometric nonlinear Hall was previously observed only in microscale-patterned structures. Our findings establish macroscopic strain engineering as a powerful route to enhance nonlinear transport, with immediate relevance to a broad class of layered systems, including transition metal dichalcogenides and moir\'e heterostructures.
items.authors: Igor Veremchuk, Pavlo Makushko, Anita Guarino, Muhammad Waqee Ur Rehman, Rosalba Tatiana Fittipaldi, Tobias Kosub, Alexej Pashkin, Fabian Ganss, Oleg A. Petrenko, Proloy T. Das, Rui Xu, Rhonald Burgos Atencia, Debottam Mandal, Antonio Vecchione, Carmine Ortix, Denys Makarov

items.title: Electric-Field Driven Nuclear Dynamics of Liquids and Solids from a Multi-Valued Machine-Learned Dipolar Model
items.abstract: The driving of vibrational motion by external electric fields is a topic of continued interest, due to the possibility of assessing new or metastable material phases with desirable properties. Here, we combine ab initio molecular dynamics within the electric-dipole approximation with machine-learning neural networks (NNs) to develop a general, efficient and accurate method to perform electric-field-driven nuclear dynamics for molecules, solids, and liquids. We train equivariant and autodifferentiable NNs for the interatomic potential and the dipole, modifying the model infrastructure to account for the multi-valued nature of the latter in periodic systems. We showcase the method by addressing property modifications induced by electric field interactions in a polar liquid and a polar solid from nanosecond-long molecular dynamics simulations with quantum-mechanical accuracy. For liquid water, we present a calculation of the dielectric function in the GHz to THz range and the electrofreezing transition, showing that nuclear quantum effects enhance this phenomenon. For the ferroelectric perovskite LiNbO$_3$, we simulate the ferroelectric to paraelectric phase transition and the non-equilibrium dynamics of driven phonon modes related to the polarization switching mechanisms, showing that a full polarization switch is not achieved in the simulations.
items.authors: Elia Stocco, Christian Carbogno, Mariana Rossi

items.title: Deterministic domain selection of antiferromagnets via magnetic fields
items.abstract: Antiferromagnets (AFMs) hold promise for applications in digital logic. However, switching AFM domains is challenging, as magnetic fields do not couple to the bulk antiferromagnetic order parameter. Here we show that magnetic-field-driven switching of AFM domains can in many cases be enabled by a generic reduction of magnetic exchange at surfaces. We use statistical mechanics and Monte Carlo simulations to demonstrate that an inequivalence in magnetic exchange between top and bottom surface moments, combined with the enhanced magnetic susceptibility of surface spins, can enable deterministic selection of antiferromagnetic domains depending on the magnetic-field ramping direction. We further show that this mechanism provides a natural interpretation for experimental observations of hysteresis in magneto-optical response of the van der Waals AFM $\mathrm{MnBi_2Te_4}$. Our findings highlight the critical role of surface spins in responses of antiferromagnets to magnetic fields. Furthermore, our results suggest that antiferromagnetic domain selection via purely magnetic means may be a more common and experimentally accessible phenomenon than previously assumed.
items.authors: Sophie F. Weber, Veronika Sunko

items.title: Complex surface patterning in homo- and heteroepitaxial contexts: (simultaneous) step bunching and step meandering
items.abstract: We confront a meso-scale continuum model, archetypical for the heteroepitaxial context, with an atomistic Vicinal Cellular Automaton (VicCA), built as a homoepitaxial counterpart, to show that in (2+1)D complex surface instabilities are fundamental growth phenomena rather than context-specific artifacts. Our approach is to first construct a Ginzburg-Landau-type model, designed to extend the previously (1+1)D Tersoff-type models to (2+1)D. We complement the continuum approach with a discrete one - the VicCA, in which we use a novel version of the potential landscape for the diffusing particles - a double-well potential located at each step edge. Importantly, this framework also captures both step bunching and step meandering. While these behaviors are rarely treated together in earlier approaches, they naturally coexist in real materials. Thus we establish a cross-context correspondence at the level of obtained morphologies and morphology diagrams and, additionally, a multiscale perspective on the governing parameters, bridging the gap between the mesoscale and atomistic modeling.
items.authors: Vassil Ivanov, Vesselin Tonchev, Marta A. Chabowska, Hristina Popova, Magdalena A. Za{\l}uska-Kotur

items.title: First-Principles Study of Fe Adsorption and Its Effects on the Mechanical and Electrical Properties of Monolayer and Bilayer Biphenylene Networks
items.abstract: BPN is a 2D carbon allotrope that exhibits promising potential for applications across a wide range of fields. In this work, we systematically investigated the adsorption characteristics of Fe atoms on monolayer and bilayer BPN using first-principles calculations. Structural optimization and adsorption energy analysis reveal that, for monolayer BPN, the adsorption strength gradually enhances with increasing Fe coverage, indicating a strengthening of Fe-substrate interactions. An Fe/C ratio of 50% corresponds approximately to completion of the first Fe adsorption layer on the BPN surface. For bilayer BPN, the energetically preferred adsorption site for Fe atom is located at the center of the interlayer four-membered ring, with an average adsorption energy of -4.3 eV. Mechanical properties are further evaluated for pristine and Fe-decorated BPN. The results demonstrate that monolayer and bilayer BPN possess relatively high in-plane Young's and shear moduli, indicative of excellent in-plane mechanical stability. For monolayer BPN, Fe adsorption has only a limited effect on the in-plane mechanical response at low coverages, whereas a noticeable enhancement in stiffness emerges at higher Fe loadings. In contrast, the out-of-plane mechanical response of bilayer BPN is significantly affected by Fe incorporation. The effective out-of-plane elastic constant C33 of pristine bilayer BPN is calculated to be 24.59 GPa, indicating relatively weak interlayer interactions and facile deformation along the out-of-plane direction. Notably, this property can be substantially enhanced by interlayer Fe adsorption, with C33 increasing dramatically to 515.63 GPa upon an Fe/C ratio of 25 %. The transport calculations reveal pronounced anisotropy in the conductivity normalized by the relaxation time {\sigma} / {\tau}, with markedly different values along the two in-plane crystallographic directions.
items.authors: Xiao-Ke Zhang, Zheng-Zhe Lin

items.title: HPHT growth of centimeter-sized cubic boron nitride crystals
items.abstract: Single crystals of cubic boron nitride (cBN) exceeding 10 mm in size were grown by the high-pressure high-temperature (HPHT) temperature-gradient method using a Ni-Cr-based solvent catalyst. Compared with the previously reported maximum crystal size of approximately 3 mm, this improvement was achieved by maintaining a stable precursor flux during one week of growth at a source temperature of 1950 {\deg}C. In contrast to diamonds, which were grown with the same HPHT cell and showed nearly isometric shapes, the cBN crystals had elongated shapes. We attribute this cBN morphology to a localized growth near the BN source due to the relatively low effective diffusivity of boron and nitrogen species in the metallic solvent.
items.authors: Andrey Katrusha, Weihua Peng, Jianguo Peng, Konstantin Iakoubovskii

items.title: Efficient simulation of second-order phase transitions in quantum anharmonic materials
items.abstract: When a crystal undergoes a second-order structural phase transition, such as in ferroelectrics, Peierls, and charge-density waves, the diverging fluctuations of the order parameter lead to the break- down of the standard phonon quasiparticle picture. Simulating these highly anharmonic regimes is notoriously challenging, as methods such as molecular dynamics suffer from a critical slowdown near the transition point, while the harmonic approximation fails dramatically at saddle points of the energy landscape stabilized by quantum or thermal ionic fluctuations. This work introduces a new approach, based on the variational free-energy principle, to predict critical long-range behavior and dynamical spectra in strongly anharmonic systems, even when quantum ionic fluctuations dominate. The proposed framework builds upon the stochastic self- consistent harmonic approximation but reduces its computational scaling with the number of atoms, N, from O(N^6) to O(N^2) and the memory requirement from O(N^4) to O(N). We benchmark the method on the prototypical lead-free metal-halide perovskite CsSnI3, a promising candidate for photovoltaic engineering, simulating its phase stability and Raman spectrum near the phase transition, where the breakdown of the quasiparticle picture becomes evident. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the method by computing the full free-energy Hessian and the critical temperature in a supercell with 1080 atoms. Such simulations would have required tens of thousands of years with the legacy approach; it is now feasible in a few hours on consumer hardware.
items.authors: Andrea Baldanza, Lorenzo Monacelli

items.title: Pressure induced structural transitions, coordination crossover, and optoelectronic response in divalent metavanadate CaV$_2$O$_6$
items.abstract: High-pressure synchrotron X-ray diffraction, Raman spectroscopy, photoluminescence (PL), and UV-Vis absorption measurements were carried out on the divalent metavanadate CaV$_2$O$_6$ up to 31 GPa at room temperature. Ambient CaV$_2$O$_6$ crystallizes in a centrosymmetric pseudo-brannerite monoclinic structure ($C2/m$), where vanadium atoms reside in fivefold-coordinated VO$_5$ trigonal bipyramids. Under hydrostatic compression, the system undergoes a structural phase transition starting at $\sim$1 GPa to a lower-symmetry, non-centrosymmetric monoclinic phase ($C2$), which becomes the single stable phase above 5.2 GPa. This transition involves an increase in vanadium coordination from VO$_5$ bipyramids to edge-sharing distorted VO$_6$ octahedra. High-pressure Raman scattering corroborates the structural phase boundaries, exhibiting mode softening ($\gamma_3 = -0.42$, $\gamma_9 = -0.46$) within the mixed-phase regime (1.0 - 4.4 GPa) and sharp anomalies in mode frequencies and linewidths across 5.2 GPa. The optical measurements show complete PL quenching near 1 GPa due to non-radiative recombination pathways introduced by local polyhedral distortions, alongside a non-monotonic evolution of the indirect optical band gap. Above 20 GPa, an anomaly in polyhedral distortion and internal strain drives an isosymmetric structural modification within the $C2$ phase, marked by an alteration in bulk compressibility and stabilization of the optical gap. Comparative high-pressure band-gap measurements on the sister compound MgV$_2$O$_6$ validate the explicit coupling between cation coordination changes and optoelectronic response in divalent metavanadates.
items.authors: Bhagyashri Giri, Asish Kumar Mishra, Bidisha Mukherjee, Debabrata Samanta, Nico Giordano, Goutam Dev Mukherjee

items.title: Specialized machine learning force fields for materials dynamics
items.abstract: Machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) are transforming atomistic simulations by accessing unprecedented length and time scales. While pretrained equivariant graph neural networks achieve robust zero-shot performance for near-equilibrium properties across broad chemical spaces, their translation to complex materials dynamics remains fundamentally challenged by out-of-distribution reactive states, representation biases, and computational scaling limits. In this Review, we examine how physics-driven specialization extends the applicability of MLIPs to complex dynamical systems. We systematically evaluate the structural trade-offs in MLIP design: the undersampling of highly strained configurations, the prohibitive computational overhead of high-order message-passing architectures, and the necessity of nonlocal interactions for open and field-coupled systems. Through four demanding application contexts - electrified interfaces, compositionally fluctuating open systems, multiphase evolution, and large-scale fracture - we establish a framework for observable-specific validation. Highlighting the complementary roles of universal foundation models and task-specific potentials, we emphasize that targeted adaptations must be rigorously benchmarked against intended observables. We conclude with a roadmap for developing physically consistent, hardware-aware force fields that seamlessly connect electronic-structure accuracy to macroscopic materials phenomena.
items.authors: Yue Wu, Haoyu Wan, Yuan Tian, Deng Pan, Mingwei Chen

items.title: Quantum Theory of Exciton Magnetic Moment: Interaction and Topological Effects
items.abstract: Combining magnetometry with optical spectroscopy has uncovered novel quantum phenomena and is emerging as a powerful probe of quantum materials. However, the theory of the magnetic response of excitons, correlated electron-hole pairs in insulators, remains incomplete due to insufficient treatment of electron-hole interactions and quantum geometric effects. In biased bilayer graphene, for instance, theoretical predictions of valley g-factors for p-excitons deviate from experiment by nearly an order of magnitude. Here, we develop a quantum theory of the exciton orbital magnetic moment, based on first-order perturbation theory within the GW plus Bethe-Salpeter Equation approach and a rigorous treatment of the position operator in the response of exciton states to a magnetic field. Our formalism reveals three distinct contributions that go beyond the heuristic approaches used in the literature: a Berry-phase-corrected single-particle electron and hole moment difference, a term from envelope-function winding linked to electron-hole relative motion, and a center-of-mass correction from exciton band quantum geometry, with the latter two being completely new effects not considered in previous studies. Our ab initio calculations yield results in excellent agreement with experiment, establishing the importance of interaction and quantum geometric effects in the magnetic response of excitons.
items.authors: Gurjyot Sethi, Jiawei Ruan, Fang Zhang, Weichen Tang, Chen Hu, Mit Naik, Steven G. Louie

items.title: Anomalous Edge Contrast in Magnetic Force Imaging of 2D Topological Insulators
items.abstract: Magnetic force imaging (MFM) of 2D topological insulators, such as crystalline plates of Bi2Te3 and Bi2Se3, reveals anomalously large contrast around the plate edges even under ambient imaging conditions. And while there are several known contrast mechanisms in MFM, these cannot easily explain the magnitude of contrast observe for such systems. In this work we use multi-parameter magnetic force phase imaging together with a simple analytical model to suggest that the observed magnetic edge-features can be associated with two sources: a pseudo-Faraday effect in the conductive edge channels of the topological system and magnetic scattering in those channels caused by the proximal, localized field of the tip. These results suggest novel MFM contrast mechanisms unique to topological systems and point to the utility of multi-parameter MFM techniques in studies of topological-material-based circuit elements.
items.authors: Timothy W. Carlson, Motahhare Mirhosseini, Allison Swyt, Gabriel Marcus, Daniel Lazega, Scott McGuire, Lindsey J. Gray, Anthony Walsh, Swathi Kadaba, Maria Kolesnik-Gray, C. C. Dun, Vojislav Krstic, D. L. Carroll

items.title: Guidelines for band gap opening in graphene superlattices with periodic {\pi}-vacancy distribution
items.abstract: Periodic $\pi$-vacancies in graphene superlattices (GSLs) provide a symmetry-based route to band-gap opening in graphene by modifying the $\pi$-band dispersion. However, the symmetry conditions that determine whether a vacancy motif can open a band gap remain unclear. Here, we investigate periodic $\pi$-vacancy GSLs using a nearest-neighbor tight-binding model with one $p_z$ orbital per carbon site to identify the symmetry requirements for gap opening. $\pi$-vacancies, representing functionalized, substituted, or missing carbon sites, are modeled as site deletions in the $\pi$ basis, with all hopping matrix elements to and from the deleted sites set to zero. We focus on $\pi$-vacancy motifs with $C_2$ and $C_3$ point-group symmetry. A $3n \times 3n$ GSL, where $n=1,2,3,\ldots$ is the integer scaling factor multiplying the honeycomb primitive-cell vectors, folds $K$ and $K'$ to $\Gamma$ and can therefore open a band gap. For $C_3$-type vacancies, the Dirac cones remain pinned at high-symmetry points and thus stay at $\Gamma$ in folded $3n$ GSLs. In contrast, $C_2$-type vacancies that reduce the global point group of the GSL to $D_{2h}$ by preserving a pair of perpendicular mirror symmetries, $\sigma_v \perp \sigma_d$, can also constrain the Dirac cones to $\Gamma$. When the $\sigma_v$ and $\sigma_d$ mirror planes are absent, the cones are allowed to shift away from $\Gamma$ to $(\pm \Delta q,\pm \Delta q)$ in the $3n$ superlattice.
items.authors: Diyan Unmu Dzujah, Hongde Yu, Thomas Heine

items.title: Frustration induced dimensional reduction and coexistence of long and short-range magnetic order in NdCl$_{3}$
items.abstract: The phenomenon of frustration greatly enriches the accessible physics of quantum magnets. With this in mind we study the magnetism of \NC using a combination of bulk properties measurements and neutron scattering techniques. The low-temperature heat capacity reveals two magnetic transitions at $T_{N1}$ = 270 mK and $T_{N2}$ = 180 mK. However, much of the magnetic entropy is released above $T_{N1}$, manifesting as a broad peak centered at $T^{*} \approx$ 450 mK. A similar broad peak is observed in the magnetic susceptibility, which possesses a clear anisotropy; this data can be well fit using a 1-dimensional XXZ model, yielding an antiferromagnetic nearest-neighbor exchange $J_{NN}$ = -0.962(2) K and exchange anisotropy close to the Ising limit. Single crystal elastic neutron scattering reveals highly anisotropic magnetic diffuse scattering above $T_{N1}$, confirming that quasi-one-dimensional, short-range, antiferromagnetic order is the origin of the broad peak in the heat capacity and magnetic susceptibility. Magnetic Bragg peaks characterized by a $\vec{k}$ = ($0$ $0$ $\frac{1}{2}$) propagation vector emerge below $T_{N1}$. Interestingly, the magnetic diffuse scattering persists for $T_{N2} < T < T_{N1}$, indicating a regime of coexisting short and long-range order. The magnetic Bragg peaks exhibit an additional increase in intensity below $T_{N2}$ with no change in $\vec{k}$. Concomitantly, the diffuse scattering disappears indicating the attainment of full long-range order. While the precise nature of the ordered magnetic ground state remains unresolved, the observed magnetic scattering indicates predominate $c$-axis moments with a small $ab$-plane component. We propose that the quasi-one-dimensional behavior and the coexistence of short and long-range order are driven by frustration of exchange interactions with significant anisotropy.
items.authors: Eli Zoghlin, Matthew B. Stone, Vasile O. Garlea, Matthias D. Frontzek, Andrew D. Christianson, Andrew F. May

items.title: Evaluating LLMs for Translating Legacy Fortran Atmospheric Physics to GPU-Accelerated JAX
items.abstract: Legacy Fortran physics packages in atmospheric models such as CESM, WRF, and E3SM pose a barrier to GPU modernization, while manual porting requires accelerator-programming expertise. We present LAFT (LLM-Assisted Fortran Translation), an agentic framework for converting Fortran atmospheric physics parameterizations into GPU-accelerated JAX while preserving numerical agreement with the Fortran reference. LAFT coordinates source-code analysis, translation, repair, runtime validation, and performance profiling. It combines a deterministic front end for metadata extraction and bridge generation, structured translation prompts, numerical validation, and profiling-guided feedback to identify inefficient execution patterns. The bridge handles array-layout conversion separately from scientific computation. We evaluate LAFT using the Kessler warm-rain microphysics scheme and four LLMs: Claude, GPT, Gemini, and Qwen. All four validated translations reproduce the Fortran reference outputs to near floating-point precision for the evaluated case, but their GPU performance differs substantially with execution design. The Gemini-generated implementation achieves up to a 357-fold speedup over serial Fortran in cached execution at 1,000,000 atmospheric columns, excluding compilation and host-device transfers. The results demonstrate that numerical agreement alone does not ensure efficient GPU execution and motivate combining numerical validation with hardware-aware performance analysis. LAFT provides a practical workflow for modernizing legacy atmospheric physics code through LLM-assisted translation, deterministic interface generation, automated validation and repair, and reproducible profiling.
items.authors: Iris Linck, John Dennis, John Schreck, Karen Stengel, David John Gagne II

items.title: Parametric wave spectrum models for prediction of Stokes drift profiles
items.abstract: In this report, 15 variants of nine parametric models for non-directional ocean wave spectra are reviewed. They are compared against observation-based spectra created by taking spectra measured by moored buoys, binning by wind speed, and averaging. Surface Stokes drift (SSD) and Stokes drift profiles are computed using the model and observation-based spectra, and these are compared. This 'parametric wave model' strategy for estimating Stokes drift is contrasted with other methods for estimating Stokes drift, such as using spectra from a dynamical wave model. Advantages and shortcomings are reviewed. One practical application for Stokes drift profiles is in ocean circulation modeling. Here, the information is used to compute wave-enhanced mixing ('Langmuir turbulence'). We present examples of such cases, in the context of a global ocean model, tested in two modes (coupled and uncoupled) and with two types of forcing (Stokes drift approximated using wind speed and Stokes drift computed using a full ocean wave model). A more comprehensive review of the uncoupled tests with the full ocean wave model can be found in a separate report, Fan et al. (2026). We evaluate simple Stokes drift models that use wind speed and/or wind stress but do not require a dynamical wave model. We find some are sufficiently accurate for routine prediction of SSD. A subset of these models can also predict Stokes drift profiles (via parametric spectra), but none are accurate in this role. The SSD values computed from a very large drifting buoy dataset are compared with the total drift calculated using positional change of the same buoys. The SSD is roughly 25% of the total drift, consistent with expectations based on 'rules of thumb'. However, the scatter is large, indicating that such rules have predictive skill only in the mean sense.
items.authors: W. Erick Rogers, Yalin Fan, Luis Zamudio, Elizabeth M. Douglass

items.title: Morphology-based retrieval of local wave parameters and phase shifts in satellite-observed atmospheric disturbances
items.abstract: Currently available methods for processing atmospheric wave disturbances are often based on integral wavelet transform techniques, which efficiently estimate spectral data but are fundamentally limited by the uncertainty principle. To address this limitation, this work proposes a novel morphological approach based on partitioning spatial disturbance profiles into separate, well-defined wave segments. By focusing exclusively on the local waveform morphology of a central half-wave and its two adjacent out-of-phase counterparts, and taking the modified Morlet wavelet as a primary example of a model wave packet, we successfully reconstruct the complete set of local wave parameters directly from the amplitudes and positions of these three dominant half-waves. Consequently, the theory demonstrates good agreement with observations, confirming the high accuracy of the proposed waveform morphology approach in reconstructing the localized structure of atmospheric disturbances. When applied to evaluating the phase shift between different wave field components, the method reveals that this shift is a weighted combination of the classical monochromatic phase difference and a morphological one determined by the internal symmetry of the underlying wave packets. Although the classical factor yields the dominant contribution, the symmetry-related factor provides a moderate correction to it. The applicability and accuracy of the approach are verified using observational data gathered over several orbits of the low-Earth-orbit satellite Dynamic Explorer 2 as it passed over Earth's polar caps. The obtained results confirm that the observed disturbances correspond to medium-scale acoustic-gravity waves propagating at a small angle to the horizontal plane, demonstrating the broader methodological potential of the proposed technique for analyzing a wide range of wave phenomena.
items.authors: Yuriy Klymenko, Alla Fedorenko, Evgen Kryuchkov, Oleg Cheremnykh

items.title: The Hydrological Cycle and Circulation of Tidally-Locked Planets with a Finite Moisture Inventory
items.abstract: Tidally-locked planets express a range of climate regimes distinct from those found in our solar system. Their atmospheres are often dominated by planetary-wide overturning circulations and super- rotating jets. In this paper we explore the hydrological cycle of such planets and how it might depend on the total inventory of condensate. To this end we use a set of idealised GCM simulations to probe the response of the hydrological cycle to the surface moisture budget in their atmospheres. We find that for low moisture inventories the climate quickly develops a barren day side and a moist night side where the moisture is trapped, as might be expected. For higher moisture inventories the drying of the day side is significantly delayed by the development of a substellar lake just east of the substellar point, which is sustained by the presence of a local thunderstorm-like convective system that persists even after the lake disappears. The timescales for the lake to disappear are millennia, suggesting that even a weak transfer of moisture through surface processes could maintain a moist day side. We also find that adjusting the threshold at which the evaporative rate becomes constrained by the remaining surface liquid depth modifies the longevity of the lake and surrounding day side conditions. These findings have implications for understanding a diverse range of planetary climates and habitability, given the distribution of moisture and presence of a substellar lake.
items.authors: Daniel A. Williams, Geoffrey K. Vallis, Stephen I. Thomson, William J. M. Seviour

items.title: Unifying spherical convolutions through lifting
items.abstract: We develop a unified description of convolution on the sphere by lifting to the rotation group. A number of definitions of spherical convolution have been proposed, differing in whether the kernel is axisymmetric or directional, whether the output is on the sphere or the rotation group, whether the signals carry spin, and in their computational cost. No unified treatment exists. Regarding the sphere as the homogeneous space $S^2 \cong \text{SO(3)}/\text{SO(2)}$, we lift a spin $s$ field to the rotation group, convolve on $\text{SO(3)}$, and project back to the sphere through the adjoint of the lift for a potentially different spin $s'$. We recover every rotation-equivariant convolution considered previously through constraints on the kernel, spin choices and inclusion or omission of the lift and projection. For maps between fields of fixed input and output spin, we prove that directional kernels, output on the sphere and equivariance cannot be achieved simultaneously. We make explicit that spin fields are sections of associated line bundles, linking the physics and bundle literatures, and express the spin rotation phase as the character of the twist of the section. We present harmonic-space algorithms for the exact and efficient computation of lifted spherical convolutions of band-limited fields by appealing to sampling theorems on the sphere and rotation group. All operators are implemented in the open-source s2conv code, and numerical experiments confirm the reductions and the equivariance of the operators to machine precision. Finally, we illustrate the operators on fields measured on the Earth and on the celestial sky.
items.authors: J. D. McEwen

items.title: Where should the null live? Surrogate tests for clustering of threshold-derived air-quality indices, with application to PM2.5 exceedances in Chile
items.abstract: Air-quality and climate monitoring routinely convert native-resolution measurements into exceedance counts before testing whether high values cluster in time. A surrogate null can be imposed on the derived index or on the native series and then propagated through the same thresholding and aggregation. We show that the two placements can encode different scientific hypotheses and lead to opposite conclusions. In 31 Chilean PM2.5 monitoring stations (2018--2025), weekly clustering of days above the 50 ug m^-3 national 24-hour standard was significant at all stations under an index-level IAAFT null but at only two under a daily native-resolution null; a native generative null with seasonal marginals and short-memory Gaussian-copula dependence agreed with the native surrogate at 30 of 31 stations. Across thresholds spanning the WHO guideline (15 ug m^-3) to the Chilean episode-alert level (80 ug m^-3), index-only rejections increased from 8 of 31 to all eligible stations as monthly event probabilities became more seasonally concentrated, and equalizing monthly event probabilities at the 50 ug m^-3 level reduced index-only decisions from 29 to five. We formalize the issue as null transport through a lossy observation map: an exact aggregate-level equivalent of a native null exists if and only if the randomization kernel is lumpable with respect to that map. A within-fiber diagnostic, which perturbs native amplitudes while keeping the observed index exactly fixed, shows that this condition fails in the monitoring data: the native null distribution moved by a median of 18 times its Monte Carlo variability. Weekly clustering of PM2.5 exceedances in Chile is therefore fully compatible with seasonality plus short-memory daily persistence, and index-level surrogate rejections should not be read as evidence about daily concentration dynamics.
items.authors: Mauricio Herrera-Mar\'in

items.title: Is the Number of Foreshocks Underestimated? The Role of Declustering Symmetry
items.abstract: The physical origin of foreshocks remains one of the major unresolved problems in statistical seismology. In bottom-up (BU) triggering models, foreshocks are interpreted as ordinary earthquakes that stochastically trigger a larger event through cascading interactions, as in the Epidemic-Type Aftershock Sequence (ETAS) model. In contrast, top-down (TD) models interpret foreshocks as manifestations of a preparatory process preceding the mainshock. This ambiguity has important implications not only for earthquake forecasting, but also for declustering itself, since the inferred number of foreshocks may depend on the assumed physical mechanism governing seismicity. Here we investigate the detectability of foreshocks using synthetic catalogues representing two limiting physical scenarios: purely bottom-up triggering and mixed preparatory-triggering dynamics. These cases are implemented through the ETAS and ETAFS models, respectively. We compare the classical nearest-neighbor (NN) declustering metric with a reverse nearest-neighbor metric (rNN) introduced here. While the standard NN metric scales the correlation metric to the magnitude of the earlier event, rNN scales it with the magnitude of the later event. We show that rNN is mathematically equivalent to applying the standard nearest-neighbor metric to the time-reversed catalog, establishing a direct symmetry between the two approaches. Our simulations reveal [...]
items.authors: Herbian Hokky Prabowo, Eugenio Lippiello, Sebastian Hainzl, Giuseppe Petrillo

items.title: Is Earthquake Replenishment Sufficient for Unbiased b-Value Estimation?
items.abstract: Short-term aftershock incompleteness biases Gutenberg-Richter b-value estimates because many small earthquakes remain undetected immediately after large events. Two strategies address this problem. Earthquake replenishment reconstructs missing events to restore a more complete catalog, whereas robust positive-difference estimators infer the b-value directly from incomplete observations. Whether these approaches provide equivalent information on the magnitude distribution remains open. We address this issue using synthetic aftershock sequences generated with the Epidemic-Type Aftershock Sequence (ETAS) model and degraded through a time- and magnitude-dependent incompleteness model. Incomplete catalogs are replenished using AutoBETA, and b is estimated using the standard maximum-likelihood, b-more-positive, and b-more-incomplete estimators. Replenishment reconstructs the overall structure of the missing-event population and substantially improves conventional maximum-likelihood estimates, although small residual biases remain. By contrast, both positive-difference estimators recover the imposed b-value directly from incomplete synthetic catalogs. Applications to the Ridgecrest, Landers, and Hector Mine sequences show that b-more-incomplete is less sensitive to replenishment than b-more-positive. Ten independent replenishment seeds indicate that seedto-seed variability is small relative to differences among estimators. Replenishment and robust b-value estimation therefore address different aspects of catalog incompleteness: replenishment provides a more complete aftershock representation, whereas robust estimators are preferable when accurate b-value estimation is the primary objective.
items.authors: Herbian Hokky Prabowo, Giuseppe Petrillo

items.title: Differences among preparatory processes preceding major earthquakes in Kamchatka, 2014-2025, including the MW 8.8 event
items.abstract: Earthquake preparation involves progressive damage accumulation, strain localization, and changes in the organization of seismicity. We investigate preparatory processes preceding seven episodes of major earthquakes in the Kuril - Kamchatka subduction zone during 2014 - 2025, including the 29 July 2025 MW 8.8 Kamchatka megathrust earthquake. We track damage evolution using the seismic regularity coefficient dc and seismic strain dynamics coefficient SSD, defined for seismic series. Before 2022, each episode of strong seismicity was preceded by a pronounced dc minimum, commonly accompanied by an SSD minimum, followed by an increase in dc toward a maximum near the strong event or event group. After 2022, dc minima became shallower and were superimposed on a sustained upward trend. We interpret this transition as evidence that the metrics recorded two superimposed processes. The cycles before 2022 reflect complete strain-localization histories on southern or more distant structures that did not contribute to the segment ruptured in 2025. In contrast, the upward dc trend from 2022, with only shallow minima preceding Episodes 6 and 7, marks coupled behavior within the eventual main rupture segment, also influenced by stress transfer from southern source regions.
items.authors: Stanislaw Lasocki, Beata Orlecka-Sikora, Mateusz Olszewski

items.title: Density Functional Theory of Dion-Jacobson Double Perovskite Halides
items.abstract: First-principles density functional theory was used to study six (four unreported) hybrid layered double perovskites of the Dion-Jacobson A2MM ′′′ X8 family. All 6 compounds consist of organic diamines that bridge rock-saltordered inorganic octahedra, with Ag+ as the M ′ site and Bi+3/Sb+3 as the M′′′ site. Both aliphatic (1,3-diaminopropane [PDA], 1,4-diaminobutane [BDA], 1,8-diaminooctane [ODA]) and aromatic (para-phenylenediamine [PPDA]) spac-ers are investigated, revealing how composition affects the band gap character and magnitude. Formation energy analysis using the DFT-D3 method reveals negative formation energies with respect to relevant precursors. Furthermore, calculations using the complex dielectric function reveal key optical properties, including absorption coefficients, refractive indices, and complex permittivity.
items.authors: Sarang Srikanth, Neshwanth Kumar Tene, Srinagesh Kumar Potluri, Adam Malofsky, Micheal Annis

items.title: Building the Data Foundations for the Design and Discovery of Transition Metal Complexes
items.abstract: The unique chemistry of transition metal complexes (TMCs) enables several advanced technologies in diverse fields including renewable energies, medicine, and catalysis. Machine learning methods can accelerate their rational design but are bounded by limited dataset sizes, restricted chemical scopes, and insufficient quality. This Perspective surveys the current landscape of TMC datasets and investigates how they seek to address these challenges. The analysis focuses on the data curation processes as well as the scope of the properties provided, and their level of theory. Furthermore, the applications and methodological advancements enabled by TMC datasets are reviewed, including the generative design of metal ligands and the evolutionary optimization of TMCs. The Perspective concludes by outlining future directions, with particular emphasis on extending data to broader chemical scopes including non-equilibrium geometries, establishing community-wide data formats and benchmarks, and developing strategies to effectively integrate heterogeneous data sources.
items.authors: Hannes Kneiding, Bastian Bjerkem Skjelstad, Luca Cibinel, Lucı́a Morán-González, Ainara Nova, David Balcells

items.title: Detection and Characterization of the Cosmological Neutrino Background by EPR Spectroscopy on Molecular Hydrino with Implications for Telecommunications
items.abstract: A hydrino atom, H(1/p) solved using a Maxwellian electrodynamics and relativistic mechanics, is atomic hydrogen with state energy En = -13.598/n2 eV, in which n = 1/p, and p is limited by the energy in the electric field of the proton to 126 whereafter the proton and electron decay. Electron transitions to hydrino states involve an initial non-radiative energy transfer to a catalyst that serves as an energy hole or sink of a quantized amount of energy, 2mE1 (m is integer) to be transferred to a catalyst such as HOH, a free or nascent water molecule. Furthermore, hydrino atoms can react to form the corresponding diatomic molecule referred to as molecular hydrino H2(1/p). In contrast to molecular hydrogen (H2), the molecular hydrino (H2(1/p)) is paramagnetic with S = ½ comprising a paired and unpaired electron in the same MO wherein the lower energy state central field is provided by photons akin to gluons in nucleons in addition to the field of the protons. Due to its unique structure, H2(1/p)) interacts with the neutrinos in the energy range of the cosmological neutrino background (𝐶𝜈𝐵) as confirmed by the neutrino mediated observations of predicted fine structure, predicted high magnetic field Paschen Beck effect, large downfield shifts, temporal changes of EPR spectra due to accumulated changes in fine structure state populations, extraordinary broadened signals, zero order absorption occurring in the perpendicular and parallel modes, and the observation of magnetic dipole-dipole interactions of H2(1/4)-H2 dimer requiring intramolecular angular momentum transfer from a neutrino excited fine structure state in H2(1/4) as well as unique temperature and matrix dependences of the EPR signals. EPR was used to detect and characterize the 𝐶𝜈𝐵 for the first time. The isotropic and parallel propagation nature of 𝐶𝜈𝐵 can be exploited for line of site telecommunications requiring no transmission power to transmit signals in any direction unattenuated and undispersed through any physical barrier, including the Earth.
items.authors: Wilfred R. Hagen, Randell L. Mills

items.title: Size-Controlled HgTe Nanocrystals Achieve Near-Unity Shortwave Infrared Emission
items.abstract: The near-infrared (NIR, 700-1000 nm) and short-wave infrared (SWIR, 1000-2000 nm) regions of light are privileged for optoelectronic applications due to the decreased scattering and diminished autofluorescence arising from the few natural chromophores which absorb or emit in these windows. We demonstrate a two-stage, size-resolved synthesis of spherical HgTe quantum dots (QDs) with narrowband photoluminescence tunable across the NIR and SWIR which combine exceptionally high photoluminescence quantum yields (QY 80%), low polydispersity ( 10%), and stability in air. Using this synthetic control, we determine the size-dependent bandgap and molar extinction coefficients of HgTe under extreme confinement, and show conclusively that separating nucleation from growth — via a fast injection followed by a slow one — suppresses Ostwald ripening. Post-synthetic incubation with zinc salts further improves optical stability, pushing QY to near unity across the SWIR, including at telecom-relevant wavelengths. We then formulate water-soluble HgTe QD micelles as contrast agents for in vivo mouse imaging in the SWIR, achieving 100 frame/s video-rate imaging above 1400 nm with contrast and temporal resolution that substantially exceed those of indocyanine green. Together, these results establish that even without a protective shell, HgTe QDs offer a near-optimal, air-stable platform for optoelectronic applications at telecom-relevant wavelengths .
items.authors: Belle Coffey, Eric Lin, Lorenzo Spollero, Skylar Whitley, Caleb Tuot-Pike, Sohan Jadhav

items.title: Zr-MOF/Quinone Multicatalysis Enables Programmable Aerobic Synthesis of Benzimidazoles
items.abstract: Selectivity control in aerobic oxidation reactions containing several oxidizable functional groups remains challenging. Herein, we show that the chemoselectivity of a Zr-MOF/quinone 2 multicatalytic platform can be controlled through modulation of the organic redox co-catalyst. In contrast to previously reported Zr-MOF-808/(hydro)quinone combinations that promote direct oxidation of anilines or thiols, Zr-MOF-808/1,8-dichloroanthraquinone unlocks a different reaction pathway to selectively oxidize primary alcohols in the presence of aromatic diamines and aminothiophenols. This pathway enables the one-pot synthesis of 2-substituted benzimidazoles and benzothiazoles under atmospheric air. Mechanistic experiments support coupled catalytic cycles in which Lewis-acidic Zr sites facilitate quinone-mediated alcohol oxidation, while the MOF/semiquinone interface regenerates the oxidized mediator using oxygen. This method furnishes a highly sustainable synthesis of 31 benzimidazole and benzothiazole products, permitting recovery and reuse of both catalytic components.
items.authors: Juan Camilo Arango-Daza, Spandan Hati, Sakarn Khamkaeo, Yuttapoom Puttisong, Miguel A. Rivero-Crespo

items.title: Density Functional Theory Bond Dissociation Energies of Model Compounds Relevant to LDL Oxidation: Bis-Allylic C–H, Phenolic O–H and Hydroperoxide O–H Bonds
items.abstract: Background : Oxidative modification of low-density lipoprotein (LDL) contributes to atherogenesis, with polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) as its main chemical target. Vitamin E is an effective chainbreaking antioxidant in vitro, yet large clinical trials showed no cardiovascular benefit. We calculated bond dissociation energies (BDEs) of model compounds to quantify the underlying thermodynamics. Methods : Density functional theory calculations (PySCF; B3LYP/6-311+G(d,p)//B3LYP/6-31G*, scaled zero-point energy, 0K) were performed for butane, 1,4-pentadiene, phenol, catechol and methyl hydroperoxide. Vitamin E was not calculated at the relaxed level; published values were used. A truncated tocopherol model (5,7,8-trimethylchroman-6-ol) was run at screening level only (B3LYP/6-31+G*, unrelaxed geometries, no zero-point correction), with phenol at the same level. Results : The bis-allylic C–H bond of 1,4-pentadiene (68.2 kcal/mol) was 28.3 below that of butane (96.5). Catechol O–H (73.4) was 8.4 below phenol (81.8). The hydroperoxide model (79.6) fell 2.2 below phenol, opposite to the approximate literature order; the cause was not investigated. In screening calculations the tocopherol model was 9.0 below phenol. Published values place α-tocopherol O–H at about 77 to 78 kcal/mol, about 10 below phenol, the same direction as our screening gap. Computed values were 1.7 to 8.6 kcal/mol below approximate literature values, so gaps and ordering, not absolute values, are interpreted. Conclusions : The calculations quantify the thermodynamic basis for PUFA vulnerability and for the stronger hydrogen donation of polyphenol-type O–H bonds. They do not by themselves show donation to peroxyl radicals. Bond energies cannot explain the clinical trial results; kinetics, LDL localization and tocopherol-mediated peroxidation must be considered. No clinical outcomes or biomarkers were computed.
items.authors: Yadlapalli Anirudh

items.title: Process and Systems Modeling of Hydrothermal Liquefaction for Fuels and Bioproducts from Wet Organic Wastes
items.abstract: Hydrothermal liquefaction (HTL) can convert wet organic waste into fuels and bioproducts, but variation in feedstocks and operating conditions can propagate from product yields to system performance and deployment. This study linked machine learning based HTL yield prediction with process simulation, techno-economic analysis (TEA), life cycle assessment (LCA), uncertainty analysis, and surrogate modeling. A literature data set of 402 experiments was used to predict biocrude, aqueous, gas, and solids yields, with 71.8% of predictions within ±5 wt% of experimental values. The predicted yields reproduced 77.1% of internal rate of return (IRR) and 83.2% of GWP 100 estimates within ±5% and ±10 kg CO 2 e/kg, respectively, and were integrated into two deployment configurations (centralized and decentralized HTL) and two product pathways (biobinder/biofuel and sustainable aviation fuel [SAF]). Process and system scale analyses showed that operating conditions strongly affecting HTL performance could have weaker or competing economic effects due to tradeoffs among product yields, water handling, energy requirements, and capital costs. Across representative feedstocks, decentralized biobinder systems achieved median IRRs up to 35.8%, compared with up to 8.0% for decentralized SAF systems. Feedstock price, followed by biocrude quality, and biocrude yield emerged as the leading economic drivers. Monte Carlo filtering identified waste tipping fee thresholds $25.1–196.7 per wet metric tonne for achieving the 10% IRR target. These results show that existing tipping fee structure can support HTL deployment in some cases, while higher tipping fees or additional financial incentives can expand viability and enable higher investment returns.
items.authors: Ali Ahmad, Rohit Bhagat, Kevin Warren, Saketnath Pabba, Yalin Li

items.title: Electrochemical Capture of Microplastics via Reversible Metal Deposition in Aqueous Solutions
items.abstract: Microplastics are persistent aqueous contaminants for which effective removal strategies remain needed. Here, we investigate electrochemical deposition as a means of capturing suspended polystyrene (PS) particles. The purpose of this study is to understand the plausibility of electrochemical deposition as a means for removing microplastics from aqueous systems. The central hypothesis guiding this work is that ramified solid metallic deposits created during electrodeposition can mechanically capture plastic particles suspended in the liquid phase. PS particles of 200 nm and 250 μm were evaluated in ZnSO4 electrolyte under applied potentials from 0 to −4 V, with surfactant conditions also examined. Electrochemical treatment resulted in visibly reduced turbidity, suggesting a decrease in suspended particle concentration. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) showed particles attached to or incorporated within deposited zinc. Particle capture was not observed at 0 V but was evident under active zinc deposition at −2 V, supporting the role of electrodeposited zinc in particle capture. The observed particle–electrode interactions differed with particle size: larger particles were partially embedded within rough, dendritic zinc deposits, whereas nanoscale particles were densely distributed across the deposited structure. These observations demonstrate the ability of electrodeposition to facilitate particle capture through distinct particle–deposit interactions and support its potential as a tunable approach for investigating microplastic capture in aqueous systems.
items.authors: Casey Mari Apurado, Amaris Sacalxot-Berrios, Kent J. X. Zheng

items.title: Removal of Cu(II) and a PET Glitter Microplastic Surrogate by Alginate, Alginate–Opuntia, and Chitosan-Treated Alginate–Opuntia Beads
items.abstract: The use of alginate-only beads, alginate–Opuntia (AO) beads, and chitosan-treated AO beads for the removal of Cu(II) and a PET glitter (a microplastic surrogate) from water has been investigated. Each bead type was made from the previous one by the addition of one component. Batch experiments were carried out in water containing glitter, Cu(II), or both, and AO beads soaked in dilute acetic acid without chitosan served as a control for the acid. The removal of Cu(II) in copper-only water was 45.71 ± 1.97%, 59.44 ± 2.28%, and 84.19 ± 2.65% for the alginate-only, AO, and chitosan-treated beads, respectively (mean ± SD, n = 12, 6 h, 140 rpm). Opuntia increased the Cu(II) removal by 13.72 percentage points and chitosan by a further 24.75 points (paired t-test, p 0.001 for both, and p ≤ 0.0013 for the batch means). In the presence of 2.00 g of glitter, the chitosan-treated beads still removed about 84% of the Cu(II). Meanwhile, the glitter removal increased by about 7 points with Opuntia but changed by less than 0.25 points with chitosan (p = 0.648 and 0.231). No significant difference was found between the acid-soaked and the untreated AO beads. It can be concluded that Opuntia was responsible for the increase in glitter capture and chitosan for most of the increase in Cu(II) removal.
items.authors: Shilo Karakkattu

items.title: De novo Rewriting DNA Identity into Functional RNA via Genetic Information Compiler
items.abstract: Genetic information is expressed through the molecular products encoded by DNA. Synthetic systems can regulate these outputs, but retain the original link between DNA identity and function. Re-engineering this link could assign new functions to existing DNA identities. Here we present a genetic information compiler (GIC) that converts selected double-stranded DNA (dsDNA) identities into user-defined RNA outputs. GIC exploits the nontrivial activity of λ exonuclease to interrogate dsDNA and release predefined activators. These activators restore T7 promoters and drive programmable transcription. This modular architecture enables orthogonal and concurrent routing, logic processing, and control of RNA identity, amplitude, composition and timing. Spatial compartmentalization further reveals activator-mediated information transfer between separated compartments. By programming functional gRNAs as outputs, GIC enables tunable, sequence-dependent, and selective regulation of Cas9, Cas12a and Cas13a. GIC establishes a new programmable information layer in which existing dsDNA identities can be interpreted de novo as user-defined functional RNAs.
items.authors: Linghao Zhang, Qinze Rong, Xueting Wang, Dandan Tian, Shihui Wang, Huiyu Liu

items.title: When Ethylene Meets Sulfur: Direct Synthesis of Minimal Ethylene-Sulfur Copolymers
items.abstract: In inverse vulcanization chemistry, research has predominantly focused on multifunctional unsaturated comonomers to stabilize sulfur-rich structures, whereas the direct copolymerization of elemental sulfur with simple olefins has remained comparatively unexplored. Extending this concept to the simplest olefin, we report Minimal Ethylene-Sulfur Copolymers (MinESC), synthesized through the direct reaction of gaseous ethylene with elemental sulfur via a base-mediated inverse vulcanization approach under mild conditions. These materials are viscoelastic fluids of tunable viscosity reaching exceptionally high values. They exhibit a peculiar sheet-like morphology, polar surfaces, elevated electrical conductivity, and high permittivity, and can be reprocessed into predominantly elastic structures following thermal treatment. Our approach provides a straightforward route to a distinct class of sulfurethylene-derived functional materials and demonstrates that inverse vulcanization chemistry can be extended to the simplest olefin under industrially relevant pressures and temperatures.
items.authors: Jules Henrotte, Francesco Zaccaria, Alessio Mingione, Hatice Mutlu, Anton Ginzburg

items.title: The role of membrane properties and environmental footprint in shaping the cost-climate optimal carbon capture processes
items.abstract: Membrane development for carbon capture is typically guided by CO2 permeability and CO2/N2 selectivity, although these properties alone cannot determine whether a material will deliver economically and environmentally favourable performance at scale. Herein, we develop a multi-criteria optimization framework that integrates a machine-learning surrogate model of a multi-stage membrane process with techno-economic analysis and life cycle assessment. By applying this framework to mixed matrix membranes, we investigate the interplay of membrane properties and membrane-specific inventories in defining process-level costs and environmental indicators. For the capture from flue gases produced by a waste incinerator plant and a cement plant, electricity is mostly driven by CO2/O2 selectivity within the investigated range and is the dominant contributor to process costs and climate change impacts. This makes the climate benefits of membrane-based capture strongly dependent on the electricity supply: high-performance membranes supplied with carbon-intensive electricity can have climate change impacts comparable to or even higher than those of low-performing membranes supplied with low-carbon electricity. Therefore, we show for the first time how the system-level context shapes the properties that must be prioritized and their target values to unlock economic and environmental benefits: membrane synthesis and lifetime have a substantial impact in the presence of clean electricity, whereas increasingly high CO2/O2 and CO2/N2 selectivity are needed in the presence of moderate to high carbon intensity. Overall, with this work, we identify priorities for improvement in membrane production and performance that could only be revealed by jointly considering process-level costs and environmental impacts.
items.authors: Stefania Bempeli, Julian Nohl, Hitesh Sewani, Andre Bardow, Marina Micari

items.title: Commit: Automated Scale-Up Crystallisation DataFactory for model-based pharmaceutical process development: a data-driven, mechanistic and hybrid model case study
items.abstract: In 2025, we introduced the Scale-Up Crystallisation DataFactory, an automated platform for crystallisation experimentation and Bayesian optimisation. However, the initial case study used a relatively simple three-parameter, single-objective optimisation problem. In this Commit paper, we extend the platform to a five-dimensional, multi-objective cooling-antisolvent crystallisation of lovastatin and benchmark data-driven, mechanistic and hybrid optimisation approaches. Sixteen screening experiments were followed by model-guided experiments targeting yield and particle size (D90). Bayesian optimisation produced continued improvements in hypervolume, while mechanistic and hybrid approaches did not improve experimental performance beyond screening. The results demonstrate the value of experimentally benchmarking optimisation strategies for autonomous process development.
items.authors: Thomas Pickles, Cameron J. Brown

items.title: Phosphorus(V) Umpolung Converts Electrophilic Phosphates into Nucleophilic H-Phosphonates
items.abstract: Ubiquitous in chemistry, biology and medicine, phosphate groups form the backbone of DNA and RNA, and their analogues like phosphorothioate antisense oligonucleotides provide frontier therapies for challenging genetic disorders. However, the inherent electrophilicity of phosphorus(V) and thermodynamic stability of native P–OH bonds preclude their direct, latestage conversion into phosphate analogues. Here, we introduce a polarity-reversal (umpolung) strategy for converting electrophilic phosphates into nucleophilic H-phosphonates. This approach proceeds through two stages: P–OH thiolation into a thiophosphate followed by radical P–S cleavage, which generates the P–H bond. This sequence converts diverse phosphate substrates, such as complex drug scaffolds and nucleotides, into H-phosphonates that can undergo further phosphorus functionalization. The thiolation step also enables direct, one-pot conversion of P–OH into P–SH in nucleotides, providing a chemical route to the phosphorothioation of native phosphate backbones associated with bacterial and archaeal DNA defense. Therefore, phosphorus(V) umpolung reverses the polarity of phosphate chemistry, transforming otherwise stable P–OH bonds into synthetically versatile phosphorus functionalities.
items.authors: Petr Oeser, Petr Šimon, Kristýna Kellovská, Matthew Z. Todd, Rafael Navrátil

items.title: Synthesis of Large-area Two-Dimension Metal-Organic Framework Films via Chemical Vapour Deposition
items.abstract: Synthesizing uniform and large-are two-dimensional (2D) metal-organic framework (MOF) films directly on substrates is highly desirable and important for MOF-based electronics, but it still remains great challenge. Here, a simple chemical vapour deposition (CVD) growth strategy with controllable-thickness and large-area capabilities has been developed to directly prepare them on substrates, in which 2,3,6,7,10,11-hexahydroxytriphenylene (HHTP) ligand films pre-deposited on substrates react with copper (II) acetylacetonate (Cu(acac) 2 ) vapor, resulting the structure transformation from small molecule thin film to Cu 3 (HHTP) 2 MOF films. The MOF films have high crystalline quality with uniform surface, large area (4 inches wafer) and controllable thickness (15 nm to 100 nm). And Replacing Cu(acac) 2 with nickel (II) acetylacetonate (Ni(acac) 2 ) and platinum (II) acetylacetonate (Pt(acac) 2 ) as metal ion source, the method can also be used to synthesize uniform Ni 3 (HHTP) 2 and Pt 3 (HHTP) 2 MOF films, suggesting the generic applicability of this method. When employed the Cu 3 (HHTP) 2 MOF films as an active material for optoelectronic devices, it simulates light-stimulated and synaptic memory properties, making it exhibit promising application in artificial biological synapse.
items.authors: Jinzhi Zhang, Runkun Li

items.title: Free induction decay-detected high-field electron spin resonance for accurate monitoring highly polarized spin dynamics
items.authors: Quentin Stern, Hoang M. Le, Martyna Judd, Joshua S. Straub, Songi Han

items.title: A study of the valence shell photoionization dynamics following core level resonant excitation in imidazole
items.abstract: The photoionization and subsequent Auger decay dynamics of core-excited states in imidazole have been investigated at the carbon and nitrogen K-edges using linearly polarized synchrotron radiation. Ion yield measurements in the pre-edge regions were used to locate core-level transitions into either unoccupied valence or Rydberg states, and assignments were made through comparison with simulated spectra obtained using the RASPT2 method. Valence shell photoelectron spectra were recorded at photon energies coinciding with these core-level transitions, using two polarization orientations to allow the photoelectron angular distributions to be determined. The interpretation of these resonantly excited photoelectron spectra was guided by RASPT2 simulations that helped distinguish between participator and spectator contributions. Autoionization strongly affects the photoelectron intensity and angular distributions of the outer valence 1h states. Spectator contributions become evident at binding energies above 15 eV, and some of the intense 2h-1p states are well-described by the calculations, allowing assignments to be proposed. The non-resonantly excited C(KVV) and N(KVV) Auger spectra have been measured and some of the features at high kinetic energies have been assigned.
items.authors: D. M. P. Holland, H. G. McGhee, A. R. Milosavljević, J. D. Bozek, E. Muchová, R. A. Ingle

items.title: UpKast: Method, Model, and Database for Large-Scale Cross-Solvent Determination of pKa Values
items.abstract: The acid dissociation constant, commonly written as p K a , plays a key role in chemistry. However, most p K a measurements have been conducted in only a handful of solvents, resulting in data scarcity for many relevant solvent systems. Herein, we introduce the UpKast-DB, which comprises of p K a estimates for around 3,000 acids and bases in 29 solvents. We constructed UpKast-DB using a quantum-chemical method that integrates solvation free energy calculations with experimental data. Furthermore, we trained a surrogate machine learning model UpKast-ML on the computed values, allowing for rapid and accurate prediction of p K a values beyond the acids and bases presented in UpKast-DB. The quantum-chemical and machine learning methods result in RMSEs of approximately 1 p K a unit relative to experimental values, slightly higher than the typical aleatoric uncertainty of underlying experimental data, but more accurate than many existing experimental measurements (which can have uncertainties up to, and sometimes beyond, 3 p K a units). The data and modeling approaches provide a means of productively augmenting existing p K a data sources, and represent a significant step toward general determination of p K a in any solvent. The dataset and models can be found on Zenodo: doi:10.5281/zenodo.23239570
items.authors: Jonathan Wenyuan Zheng, William H. Green

items.title: Molecular Symmetry Decomposition by Graph Automorphism: Fast, Symmetry-Aware RMSD, Structure Alignment, and Canonical Atom Ranks
items.abstract: The root-mean-square deviation (RMSD) is among the most widely used metrics in computational chemistry. However, computing a chemically meaningful RMSD requires solving a combinatorial “atom mapping” problem: finding the RMSD-minimizing and chemically acceptable correspondence between atoms in two structures. Existing methods force a trade-off. Graph-isomorphism enumeration is exact but can be computationally prohibitive. The faster (cubic scaling with molecular size) Hungarian assignment algorithm disregards the bonding topology and can return chemically invalid mappings and spuriously low RMSD values. We eliminate this trade-off by recasting the assignment problem in the language of graph automorphism, where the bond-preserving permutations form a group whose internal structure (orbits, stabilizers, and product decompositions) mirrors molecular topology. This yields a complete classification of molecular graph symmetry into coupled core and independent peripheral symmetry (falling into exactly two graph-theoretic classes), reducing the search from a product of local symmetries to a sum. The resulting algorithm, snapRMSD, produces assignments that are bond-preserving by construction and recovers the global RMSD minimum under mild conditions satisfied by most molecular structures. We demonstrate that snapRMSD is significantly faster than existing methods, often by orders of magnitude. As a byproduct, the same machinery yields exact canonical atom ranks, a rigorous alternative to the refinement heuristics used since the 1960s.
items.authors: Colton B. Hicks, Todd J. Martinez

items.title: COSMO-RS-Based Theoretical Investigation of Equilibria in Protic Ionic Liquids
items.abstract: Ionic liquids have become an increasingly important field of research. A subgroup, protic ionic liquids, have been shown to be excellent solvents even for poorly soluble materials such as cellulose or polyamides.
