Still, the composition of such liquids, e.g., their ionicity and the nature of formed aggregates, is mostly unknown and experimental attempts to shed light on this have been mostly unsuccessful. Herein, we report the development of the Python-based COSMOPIL program (COnductor-like Screening MOdel for Protic Ionic Liquids) to analyze the composition of protic ionic liquids via theoretical methods based on density functional theory (DFT) and the COSMO-RS (COnductor-like Screening MOdel for Real Solvents) implicit solvation model. The inputs of experimental data such as dielectric constants is not necessary. The COSMO-PIL program demonstrates the influence of acid/base ratios and residual water on the ionic liquid composition and allows the understanding of the reported poor ionicity of those liquids. Most notably, we explain this “ionicity gap” in protic ionic liquids, as even superbases fail to achieve full acid deprotonation, with a polarity mismatch between anion and cation, requiring residual acid as mediator.
items.authors: Kevin Breitwieser, Ilkka Kilpeläinen, Vladimir Aseyev

items.title: Late-Stage Ligand Prioritization by Combining Rapid-Dissociation Filtering with MM/GBSA
items.abstract: Accurate and efficient prediction of binding free energies remains a central challenge in computational chemistry, largely due to the complexity of solvent effects and the trade-off between accuracy and computational cost. Explicit solvent molecular dynamics (MD) simulations provide detailed thermodynamic and kinetic insight, now routinely reaching microsecond timescales, while end-point methods such as MM/GBSA offer high efficiency but are sensitive to model parameters. In particular, the accuracy of MM/GBSA strongly depends on the atomic radii used to define the dielectric boundary within the implicit solvent framework. Here, we introduce an explicit–implicit hybrid workflow for late-stage ligand prioritization that integrates the strengths of both approaches. In this framework, microsecond-scale explicit solvent MD simulations act as a rapid-dissociation filter, flagging weak or unstable binders through spontaneous dissociation within the simulation window. MM/GBSA is then used to rank the remaining candidates. To improve the accuracy of the implicit solvent stage, we employ optimized atomic radii sets (OPTBIND), specifically designed for binding free-energy calculations. On the protein–ligand complexes of Curated32-4 set , a new curated benchmark of 32 complexes including 4 congeneric series, the entropy-free MM/GBSA stage with OPT- BIND 6D achieved Pearson r = 0.82 and Spearman ρ = 0.84, with 100% recovery of the experimental rank ordering across all four congeneric series, while a single-replica consistency test of the rapid-dissociation filter yielded an AUC of 0.88 and retained all 15 sub-micromolar binders. Finally, as a real-world drug design application, we apply the workflow to halogen substitutions in SARS-CoV-2 main protease inhibitors, demonstrating its ability to identify favorable chemical modifications. Notably, the approach prospectively identifies F→Cl and F→I as affinity-enhancing substitutions; the predicted enhancement for the chlorine analog is subsequently confirmed experimentally, while the iodine analog remains a testable prediction, highlighting its predictive power in guiding chemical optimization. Together, these results establish a practical framework for detailed studies of receptor–ligand binding and for late-stage ligand prioritization in drug discovery.
items.authors: Fatemeh Ghafouri-Plate, Timothy W. Johann, Luke H. Elder, Alexey V. Onufriev

items.title: Automated Extraction and FAIRification of Chemical Structures from Scientific Publications
items.abstract: Chemical structures are published predominantly as images, which makes them inaccessible for database indexing, structure-based search and computational reuse. While Optical Chemical Structure Recognition and PDF-extraction tools attempt post-publication recovery, they cannot restore the information lost during image rendering. To address this, we present BChemXtract, an open-source Java library that extracts chemical structures directly from the CDX and CDXML files that authors already submit with their manuscripts. BChemXtract parses the CDX object hierarchy to isolate chemical fragments from graphical annotations and expands abbreviations using a community-curated lookup table. The structures are then converted via the Chemistry Development Kit into standard machine-readable formats. BChemXtract is integrated into the production workflow of the Beilstein Journals, where extracted structures are manually validated before being embedded in article metadata as Schema.org JSON-LD, deposited in PubChem and offered for download. Applied to the 2993 ChemDraw figures and schemes of volume 20 of the Beilstein Journal of Organic Chemistry, it yielded 23,320 structures with InChIs in under two minutes. On a 225-file benchmark corpus, it generated valid InChIs for 98.2% of extracted unique substances, compared with 14.2% for Open Babel, at comparable per-file speed. BChemXtract makes published chemistry FAIR at the point of publication without altering author workflows. It is available under the MIT license together with a web application and the benchmark corpus.
items.authors: Felix Bänsch, Kohulan Rajan, Markus Nietfeld

items.title: Utilization of heuristic approaches and molecular modelling to visualise chemical reactivity in small student groups
items.abstract: According to current psychometric analyses, a vast majority of novices in universities mostly utilize algorithmic mental processes to solve given tasks and tests. Although algorithmic thinking is an essential part of brain functions, experts on didactics call for methods which also develop conceptual thinking in beginners. In this sense, heuristic molecular modelling plays an important role in chemistry education since it inherently employs several conceptual thinking principles. Herein, we present eight different molecular modelling tasks of Diels-Alder reactions to develop understanding of the concept of chemical reactivity in undergraduate students of chemistry. The aim of this study is to provide teachers of chemistry with an example lesson utilizing heuristic education techniques and molecular modelling. The present study was evaluated in a university course on advanced organic chemistry for students in the third year of a chemistry master program. Interviews with the involved students and analyses of the applied pre/post didactical tests show that the proposed lesson has a positive impact on the understanding of basic chemical concepts related with chemical reactivity and Diels-Alder reaction.
items.authors: Rafael Dolezal, Natálie Karásková, Nadezhda V. Maltsevskaya, Karel Kolář

items.title: CP-GFM-SGX: Topology-Aware Cyclic Peptide Generation and Design with Receptor-Conditioned Structural Evaluation and Experimental KRAS Affinity Optimization
items.abstract: Cyclic-peptide discovery requires molecular topology, atomic structure, receptor-associated evidence and computational decisions to remain consistent across a multistage workflow. We present CP-GFM-SGX, an all-atom generative AI model for cyclic-peptide design that integrates a topology-aware generative core with a Unified Evidence State Machine (UESM) to track candidate identity, chemical validity, provenance, typed failures and bounded computation. We evaluated three distinct aspects of the system. In Track A, a frozen five-complex known-ligand benchmark with 100 scheduled poses per complex, the native-free FULL route selected a ligand-backbone pose with root-mean-square deviation (RMSD) below 2 Å in four of five systems; retrospective best-of-100 evaluation found a sub-2-Å pose in all five (median selected RMSD, 1.72 Å). In Track B, matched true-pocket versus shuffled-pocket comparisons favored the specified pocket in all seven main targets (median of target medians, +172.6 Rosetta energy units; weakest margin, +3.9 for MCL-1–9CDT). An exploratory post-protocol assessor admitted 42/42, 42/42 and 40/42 selected top-K slots in the full, condition-masked and post hoc head-to-tail arms, respectively. In Track C, FULL UESM produced the specified protective outcomes for six deterministic synthetic fault fixtures and one additional missing-evidence case; targeted ablations isolated the roles of provenance and failure propagation. In a separate KRAS G12D–GDP experimental-feedback series, synthesis and SPR/BLI testing of cyclic-peptide analogues guided position-2 basic-side-chain selection and dual-basic-group placement, advancing the reported SPR affinity from approximately 60 µM for CRO-748 to approximately 6 µM for 748-R1 and approximately 1 µM for 748-RK. Comparisons using the 31-dimension Structured Capability and Evidence Grid (SCEG-31D) demonstrate that CP-GFM-SGX exhibits certain superiority over other design platforms in multiple aspects. Together, we evaluate a topology-aware generative artificial intelligence workflow for receptor-focused cyclic-peptide design and show, in a KRAS feedback series, how binding measurements guide iterative chemical optimization.
items.authors: Zhiyuan Hu, Russell Dillworth

items.title: Prediction of MOF Adsorption Isotherms and High-Throughput Screening Using a Physics-Informed Membranes Graph Neural Network
items.abstract: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) are prime CO 2 -capture candidates, but grand canonical Monte Carlo (GCMC) screening is costly when full isotherms, not single uptakes, are required; machine learning surrogates rarely resolve the continuous pressure response. We report a physics-informed pressure-aware multi-task graph neural network (PI-MGNN) to predict CO 2 uptake at arbitrary pressure and reconstruct isotherms from structure. From ~130,000 candidates, PCA and K-means select 5,023 representative MOFs, each simulated by GCMC at five pressures spanning 0.1-5.0 MPa, enforcing a continuous pressure response. Crystal graphs are processed by decoupled geometric and electrostatic graph-attention branches with auxiliary supervision, while a Gaussian-expanded pressure query is fused by cross-attention. PI-MGNN attains R 2 = 0.977 and MAE = 0.291 mol kg -1 ; isotherm MAEs are 0.428/0.312/0.330 mol kg -1 for high/medium/low-uptake MOFs, and cross-attention improves accuracy by 6.3%. Attention weights recover the pressure-resolved physics, enabling accurate and interpretable high-throughput screening.
items.authors: Li Linfeng, Xingshuo Fan, Ning Zhang

items.title: Descriptor-Based Regression Analysis Enables the Discovery of Highly Selective Ligands for Palladium-Catalyzed Siloxycyclopropanation
items.abstract: A palladium-catalyzed siloxycyclopropanation of alkenes using acylsilanes as carbene precursors provides a distinctive catalytic approach to structurally diverse cyclopropanes through a siloxycarbene–palladium intermediate. Although the reaction scope and major mechanistic features have been established, the origin of its ligand-dependent diastereoselectivity has remained unclear, limiting the rational development of more selective catalysts. Here, we combine density functional theory (DFT) calculations, molecular parameterization, and statistical modeling to elucidate the steric and electronic factors governing the stereochemical outcome. DFT calculations of a series of NHC ligands and their corresponding siloxycarbene–palladium complexes provided a diverse set of molecular descriptors, which were used to construct a multivariate linear regression (MLR) model against experimental activation energies. The refined model identified complementary descriptors reflecting ligand steric demand, directional steric effects, and metal–ligand electronic interactions as key factors associated with the observed selectivity. MLR-guided virtual screening of 21 NHC ligands identified L24 and L30 as promising candidates for enhanced syn- and anti-selectivity, respectively, and their predicted selectivities were experimentally validated. The newly identified ligands not only improved the selectivity in their respective directions but also enabled a pronounced switch between syn- and anti-selectivity relative to the previously optimized ligand. Furthermore, L24 and L30 exhibited 2 complementary stereocontrol across a range of acylsilanes and alkenes beyond the benchmark reaction. Mechanistic analysis of the corresponding transition states revealed the roles of anisotropic steric environments and ligand-specific electronic interactions in determining the distinct stereochemical preferences of L24 and L30. These findings provide a mechanistic basis for ligand-controlled stereoselectivity in siloxycarbene–palladium cyclopropanation and establish molecular-level ligand features as useful parameters for improving and redirecting stereochemical
items.authors: Vishal Kumar Rawat, Ryoichi Tabata, Tetsuya Inagaki, Yuki Akita, Reiko Hirosawa, Maria Fyta

items.title: A hydrochromic porous aromatic framework for self-reporting, high-capacity atmospheric water harvesting
items.abstract: Atmospheric water harvesting materials are typically optimised for sorption performance alone, despite the practical importance of monitoring sorbent loading. Here, we report a hydrochromic porous aromatic framework that integrates water capture and self-reporting within a single adaptive material. Sulfonation of PAF-1 affords the hydrophilic framework PAF-1-S that adsorbs 0.18 g·g-1 of water at only 10% RH and reaches 1.87 g·g-1 at 90% RH, combining exceptional low-humidity capture with the highest total capacity among the porous sorbents surveyed here. Water adsorption simultaneously induces a reversible, graded colour change, enabling direct visualisation of sorbent loading without external sensing hardware. Spectroscopic analysis indicates that this response arises from hydration-driven acid–base equilibria within the modified framework. Combined with rapid sorption kinetics, low-temperature regeneration and robust cycling stability, these findings establish responsive porous adsorbents as a strategy for intelligent sorption materials.
items.authors: Paul Schweng, Christoph Bendl, Kai C. Hultzsch, Robert T. Woodward

items.title: Solid-phase synthesis and structure-degradation relationships of VHL-recruiting PROTACs for preferential histone deacetylase 6 degradation
items.abstract: This work reports on a series of von Hippel-Lindau (VHL)-recruiting histone deacetylase 6 (HDAC6) PROTACs based on a vorinostat-inspired HDAC inhibitor. Systematic variations of the VHL ligand, the exit vector, and the linker architecture revealed that longer, semi-rigid linkers promoted efficient HDAC6 degradation. Compounds 12-15 emerged as potent HDAC6 degraders, with 15 exhibiting a half-maximal degradation value of 26 nM with 12 showing particularly rapid degradation kinetics. The lead compounds induced pronounced and preferential HDAC6 degradation in MM.1S and FLT3-ITD-positive MV4-11 cells. Notably, 13-15 displayed submicromolar antiproliferative activity in MV4-11 cells and significantly induced apoptosis. Compound 13 was markedly more active than its non-degrading control nc-13, despite nearly identical HDAC1 and HDAC6 inhibitory activities, which underscores the important contribution of targeted HDAC degradation to the antiproliferative activity. Overall, this study supports VHL-mediated targeted degradation as a promising strategy to translate HDAC6 targeting into pronounced antileukemic activity.
items.authors: Martina Miranda, Maria Hanl, Nisha Setia, Sophie Spülbeck, Katrin Nekipelov, Helena Skalski

items.title: Complementary Roles of Iodide-Mediated Pathways and Anion Dynamics in Lithium-Ion Transport in Li3PS4-LiI Glasses
items.abstract: LiI addition enhances lithium-ion transport in sulfide glasses, yet the microscopic mechanisms linking halide incorporation to faster conduction remain unclear. Here, we investigate how LiI promotes Li+ migration in (100−x)Li3PS4–xLiI glasses by resolving changes in local structure, migration energetics, and anion dynamics. A machinelearning potential trained on newly generated ab initio molecular dynamics data and an existing sulfide-electrolyte dataset enables 10 ns simulations of approximately 5000atom glass models at 300 K over a LiI content range of 0–50 mol%. The potential is validated against density functional theory calculations, experimental densities, and X-ray total scattering profiles. Although the PS4 3–units remain intact and their time-averaged inter-unit correlations change little, Li+ diffusivity more than doubles across this composition range, accompanied by increased migration beyond local cage-like regions. To characterize the energetics of these pathways in a disordered environment, we introduce an analysis that combines Voronoi partitioning into P-and I–-centered domains with atomic potentialenergy fluctuations along Li+ trajectories. The resulting statistical local energy-barrier indicators allow comparisons between domain transitions without assigning absolute activation energies. This analysis reveals two complementary effects of LiI addition. Transitions involving I–-centered domains exhibit lower barrier indicators than direct transitions between P-centered domains, identifying favorable I–-mediated migration pathways. LiI addition also lowers the barrier indicators for direct P-to-P transitions, extending its influence beyond pathways that pass through I–-centered domains. Enhanced local translational and rotational dynamics of PS4 3–units accompany this broader reduction, suggesting that anion motion helps facilitate Li+ migration. These findings explain how LiI can enhance transport while largely preserving the average glass structure and highlight the combined roles of local migration pathways and anion dynamics in designing sulfide glass electrolytes.
items.authors: Minami Sakuma, Shoma Kawano, Kazuki Fukuda, Aoto Matsuo, Futoshi Utsuno, Koji Ohara

items.title: Conformational Heterogeneity and Local Electronic Structure in Wild-Type and Arctic Amyloid-Β42
items.abstract: Amyloid-𝛽 42 is a heterogeneous system, widely known as an intrinsically disordered protein, or IDP, sampling a variety of conformations. However, how ensemble redistribution affects the underlying local electronic structure remains less well understood. In this study, classical molecular dynamics simulations are combined with population-aware density functional theory and reduced active-space calculations to compare the LVFFA fragment of the wild-type and Arctic (E22G) variants. Common-space principal component analysis, clustering, and Ramachandran plot analysis depicted distinct trajectory distributions and greater conformational heterogeneity for the E22G trajectory. Population-ranked conformations representing 60.58% of WT and 54.98% of Arctic populations yielded conditional population-weighted B3LYP/def2-SVP HOMO-LUMO separations of 5.81 and 5.95 eV, respectively. The 0.14 eV Arctic–WT shift remained positive across moving-block bootstrap analyses. Fragment expansion altered frontier-orbital ordering, although the spatial character of LVFFA-associated states was preserved. CASCI tested active-space sensitivity, and matched UCCSD-VQE calculations reproduced CAS(4,4) CASCI reference energies for the reduced Hamiltonians. Together, these results demonstrate the importance of population-aware conformational sampling and model-definition sensitivity when relating heterogeneous biomolecular ensembles to quantum-chemical properties.
items.authors: kushal patil

items.title: Mechanistic Classification of Multicatalysis
items.abstract: Multicatalysis combines two or more catalytic functions within a single reaction network and can unlock reactivity, selectivity, and synthetic efficiency that are difficult to achieve with an individual catalyst. Its mechanistic description, however, remains fragmented across partially overlapping terms such as tandem, relay, cooperative, synergistic, double-activation, and bifunctional catalysis, among others. Here, we propose a mechanism-first classification based on the relationship between catalytic functions and, specifically, on the catalytic ‘currency’ exchanged between them. When the currency is substrate-derived, the coupling is classified as tandem, cooperative, or double activation. When the exchanged currency controls catalyst state rather than contributing to the substrate framework (e.g. electrons, cofactors), the relationship is gated or regenerative, distinguished by whether activation is required only once or repeatedly during turnover. Importantly, the classification is additive, so complex reaction networks are represented as combinations of pairwise relationships. Representative reactions illustrate how this framework resolves mechanistic distinctions that are hidden by conventional labels. By linking nomenclature to the elementary connection between catalytic functions, the classification provides a compact language for comparing multicatalytic systems and a basis for more deliberate catalyst and reaction-network design.
items.authors: Miguel A. Rivero-Crespo

items.title: Customizable Approach to Conformer Space Discretization using Torsion Angular Bin Strings (customTABS)
items.abstract: Conformational ensembles of small organic molecules are primarily determined by the rotameric states of their torsional or dihedral angles. The previously introduced concept of torsion angular bin strings (TABS) is a discrete vector representation of a molecule’s dihedral states, which therefore offer a quantitative description of such ensembles. Discretization of the torsional-angle space allows us to count distinct conformational states, giving an estimate of the upper limit of the expected conformational ensemble size (nTABS). In addition to nTABS being used as a qualitative measure of molecular flexibility, TABS itself is a way of grouping conformers of a molecule without picking thresholds. In the initial version of the TABS application, the discretization was based on crystal-structure derived torsion preferences, which may not be fully transferable to the conformational preferences in other environments. Here, we present the extension of the TABS framework to consider observed, system-specific distributions for the discretization of the conformational space. CustomTABS can be used to decompose the given conformational ensemble into the torsional states, which can be useful for clustering, importance ranking of dihedrals, or convergence analysis. We present the algorithmic solutions developed for the customTABS extension and demonstrate their application in clustering molecular dynamics (MD) trajectories and monitoring the convergence of the observed torsional space.
items.authors: Jessica Braun, Enrico Ruijsenaars, Carl Schiebroek, Djahan Lamei, Paul Katzberger, Gregory A. Landrum

items.title: Substituent Effects on Anion Bonding and Disassembly of Hypervalent Iodine Macrocycles
items.abstract: A series of phenylalanine-derived hypervalent iodine-based macrocycles (HIMs) bearing electron donating and withdrawing substituents were prepared. The HIM associations with the anion of tetrabutylammonium chloride (TBA-Cl) were systematically investigated using binding isotherms generated via NMR spectroscopy. The association constants of the resulting I-Cl bond were found to linearly correlate with the electronic substituents via Hammett analysis. Electron-withdrawing substituents strengthened the I–Cl bond and disassembled the macrocycle more readily. In addition, the shifting of HIM carbonyl frequencies obtained by Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy were found to correlate with the binding affinities and provide an alternative predictive methodology to determine HIM disassembly and anion binding affinities.
items.authors: Samsul Arafin, Riya Krishnan, Maximilian S. Kersten, Katherine E. Helme, Sean D. Moran, Kyle N. Plunkett

items.title: Topology-Dependent Glass Formation Behavior in Poly[n]catenane Melts with Variable Ring Size and Chain Length
items.abstract: Poly[n]catenanes consist of cyclic subunits that are connected by mechanical bonds rather than covalent bonds, which gives them internal degrees of freedom and permanent topological constraints that are absent in conventional polymers. How these features affect the glass transition is not known. Here, we employ molecular dynamics simulations of the Kremer–Grest bead–spring model to determine the glass transition temperature, Tg, of poly[n]catenane melts with ring sizes of m = 8–50 beads and chain lengths of n = 5–40 rings. Each melt is compared with a bonded-ring analogue in which the mechanical link between neighboring rings is replaced by a covalent bond. Mechanical interlocking raises Tg by up to 0.44 εk B -1 , nearly a factor of 2, for the smallest rings, whereas the effect vanishes for m ≥ 20. This crossover coincides with the ring size at which the free aperture of a ring, measured in the melt, falls below one bead diameter. The topological contribution to Tg scales as 1 − n end /n with n end ≈ 2.1 for all tightly interlocked chains, indicating that the two singly interlocked terminal rings act as topological chain ends. The Debye–Waller factor, the generalized localization model, and the non-Gaussian parameter show that tight mechanical bonds restrict bead motion at a given temperature, make the relaxation time grow more steeply as the cage tightens, and add a broad, slow, and strongly non-Gaussian component to segmental relaxation. In contrast, the dynamic fragility and the large-scale Gaussian chain statistics are nearly unaffected, and the modest increase of the characteristic ratio cannot account for the rise of Tg. Our work identifies ring size as the primary molecular parameter controlling the glass transition of poly[n]catenanes and shows that it acts through local topological confinement rather than global chain stiffness.
items.authors: Yuxiang Chen, Wei Li, Zhenghao Wu

items.title: Tuning the Anchoring and ORR Activity of Sub-Nano Pt Clusters on HOPG via Ion Implantation and Oxygen Functionalization
items.abstract: Sub-nanometer supported clusters are of interest in catalysis due to nearly complete precious metal atom utilization, generally high catalytic activity, and attractive tunability via size and clustersupport interactions. The stability of such clusters remains a challenge, however. We demonstrate anchoring and stabilization of size-selected Ptn, n = 2 - 10 clusters soft-landed on HOPG, achieved 2 by modifying the HOPG with 100 eV kinetic energy N(𝑛 1, 2) and Ar+ ions, with and without O2 oxidation of the ion-modified surfaces, prior to Ptn soft-landing. Ion modification is found to significantly improve the sticking probability for soft-landed Ptn, implying increased adsorption energies, and O2 exposure prior to cluster deposition increases the sticking probability to ~unity. DFT finds that Ptn bind preferentially to under-coordinated carbon sites created by the ion impacts, rather than to implanted N atoms, and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy and scanning tunneling microscopy both show that the defect-anchored clusters are stable against sintering. There is net electron transfer from the defect-bound clusters to the support, and the local defect structure may undergo significant restructuring due to Pt-C bond formation. To probe the effects of ion-modified HOPG on the chemical properties of the adsorbed Ptn clusters, we tested electrodes prepared by Ptn deposition on ion-modified HOPG for the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR). The ion-modified electrodes showed ORR activity consistent with cluster size being maintained, and O2 modification enhanced both cluster anchoring and ORR activity. Thus, ion modification provides means to stabilize sub-nano cluster electrodes, while oxygen functionalization of the anchoring sites tunes the electrocatalytic activity.
items.authors: Lokesh Saravanan, Yu Wei, José J. Ortiz-Garcia, Zihan Wang, Zdenek Dohnálek, Zbynek Novotny

items.title: Core-to-rim chemical zoning of a Paraíbatype tourmaline from Abulo, Ethiopia: Implications for origin determination
items.abstract: Copper-bearing tourmaline of Paraíba type is now mined at Abulo in southern Ethiopia. We report the core-to-rim characterisation of one colour-zoned crystal attributed to this locality, obtained in Bangkok in June 2026. A sawn slab about 12 mm across and 5 mm thick was e x t e n s i v e l y analysed by electron microprobe (113 points), LA-ICP-MS analysis (45 spots on two traverses and 58 isotopes, totaling 2,565 concentration values with silicon as internal standard and GSE and NIST 610 as external standards), LA-ICP-TOFMS imaging (13,500 measuring spots of 24 µm and 55 isotopes, totalling 729,000 concentration values with silicon as internal standard and GSE and NIST 610 as external standard, about 505,000 of them above limits of detection), Raman spectroscopy (24 spectra) and a screening test by ED-XRF. The crystal is an Al–Li tourmaline of the elbaite series, including elbaite, fluor-elbaite, and elbaite with a liddicoatite component. Fluorine at the W site is 0.385 apfu in the core and exceeds the 0.5 apfu boundary to fluor-elbaite in the zones next to the core (0.51–0.53 apfu); 25 of 111 points lie within 1of that boundary. Ca/(Ca + Na) increases from core to rim but never exceeds σ 0.43. Lithium, measured by LA-ICP-MS, increases from about 7,840 µg/g in the core to about 10,000 µg/g in the outer zones. With this lithium taken zone by zone, boron and H O taken from 2 the formula and the unanalysed trace elements added as oxides, the analytical totals of the microprobe are 99.2 ± 0.5 wt.% over 111points.The trace elements are quantified on this measured matrix, with silicon measured by microprobe as internal standard using GSE and NIST610 as external standards. To our knowledge for the first time, silicon concentrations were measured across a growth profile of this material, in each of the five growth zones of the crystal. Themeasurementsprovide36.3 wt.% SiO2 in the core, 35.2–35.4 wt.% in the dark-blue zone, 35.5–35.8 wt% in the "neon"-blue zone, 35.9 wt% in the pink zone and 36.0 wt% in the yellowbrown zone. The concentrations of the trace elements are significantly zoned. Copper zone averages decrease from 16,200–25,700 µg/g in the core and the dark-blue zones around it to 1,420–1,820 µg/g in the yellow-brown outer zone. The iron concentration d e c r e a s e sfrom 4,130–4,150 µg/g to below detection. The bismuth concentration increases from 26–27 to 1,370 µg/g and the lead concentration from 146–160 to 1,650–1,810 µg/g. I nc o n t r a s t ,Gallium (629–741 µg/g as zone averages) and vanadium (58–158 µg/g at all 45 spots) vary far less. The element ratios used in origin determination therefore change by up to an order of magnitude inside this one crystal. For example, Cu/Ga changes from 2.3 to 41, Pb/Bi from 1.2 to 5.9 Peretti, Oberholzer, Allaz and Günther: Colour-zoned Paraíba-type tourmaline from Ethiopia. Draft of 9 October 2026 2 / 78 and Fe/Mn starts below detection to 1.1 w h i c ha r ecalculated as zone averages. The imaging confirms the element ratios of the spot analyses and separates the elements that are present in the tourmaline's composition from those carried by inclusions, which are detected above the matrix composition of the tourmaline. Of the rare earth elements, only the light rare earths, La to Sm, are present in the tourmaline's composition. Yttrium is also present in the tourmaline, at about 0.6–0.9 µg/g outside the core and lower in the core. The other elements found in the tourmaline include Li, Be, Sn, Ga, Nb, Ta and B, all of which are typically found in LCT pegmatites. Compared with our 2009 reference profiles for Brazil, Mozambique and Nigeria, the crystal from Ethopia has higher vanadium and gallium concentrations and evolves toward bismuth rather than manganese. A high vanadium concentration is independently reported for Ethiopian material by other laboratories, and the vanadium test proposed there holds across the growth zones of this crystal, with the core at the limitofdetection. The gallium difference from Mozambique is small, whereas the published Ethiopian gallium concentration extends to 280 µg/g. Because the comparison is based on a very detailed analysis of five growth zones, the reported observations are very significant and represent more information than the analyses of larger sample sets. Therefore, this information is crucial as origin criteria. Individual analyses of samples could represent mixtures of various growth zones and would not easily be identified withoutknowledgeaboutthegrowth stage. Any discriminant therefore has to be implemented into the growth-stage concentration profiles of this study as reference. A limited Raman data set, placed on the element maps, shows that the framework bands shift with the copper concentration and that the OH bands follow the fluorine and lithium concentrations; these relations are shown for one crystal.
items.authors: A. Peretti, S. J. Oberholzer, J. Allaz, D. Günther

items.title: Pathway Reweighting in DNA Reaction Networks Enables Adaptation to Environmental Pressures
items.abstract: Adaptive biochemical reaction networks must respond to environmental changes while maintaining function, yet synthetic networks typically rely on predefined pathways and stimulus–response relationships. Here, we introduce pathway reweighting as a strategy for adaptivity in DNA strand-displacement reaction networks. We design a splitting network in which two competing pathways connect a shared initial state to a common output. This allows environmental perturbations to redistribute reaction flux between the pathways while preserving overall network function. We showcase environmental sensitivity by integrating pHresponsive i-motif and ATP-binding aptamer motifs that enable selective and proportional adaptation. Combining these pressures demonstrates pathway reweighting under more complex, biologically relevant environmental conditions. Beyond proportional adaptation, we introduce a distinct, history-dependent mechanism based on an enzymatic feed-forward loop. The loop progressively modifies the Input strand, creating delayed pathway reweighting and encoding a memory of prior environmental exposure. A deep-learning reaction-network framework resolves the resulting interconnected dynamics and identifies changes in pathway utilization without requiring complete mechanistic parameterization. Our experimentalnumerical framework enables the rational design of synthetic CRNs whose adaptive behavior emerges from network organization rather than explicit reaction-by-reaction programming.
items.authors: Brigitta Dúzs, Nicolò Alagna, Livia Lehmann, Alexander Haehnel, Susanne Gerber, Andreas Walther

items.title: Photocatalytic CO 2 Conversion Driven by UV Light Above 300 nm Using Ammonia as an Electron Donor
items.abstract: Efficient utilisation of solar UV light ( λ 300 nm) is essential for practical photocatalytic CO 2 conversion. However, in conventional systems using water as an electron donor, slow water oxidation kinetics present a critical bottleneck that severely limits the CO production rate. Here, we demonstrate an efficient CO 2 conversion system that overcomes this kinetic limitation by employing ammonia as an alternative electron donor over Mg-doped SrTiO 3 loaded with Ag and Fe as dualcocatalysts (Ag–Fe/Mg–SrTiO 3 ). Under UV irradiation ( λ 300 nm), the optimised photocatalyst achieved a remarkable CO produc on rate exceeding 200 μmol h −1 . Mechanistic investigations revealed that the Fe cocatalyst played a crucial role in promoting ammonia oxidation, facilitating the rapid consumption of photogenerated holes, and significantly enhancing CO 2 conversion activity. Furthermore, nitrite (NO 2 − ) was successfully quantified as the primary oxidation product of ammonia, yielding a calculated e − / h + balance of approximately 1.2, validating the stoichiometric relationship of the reaction. This study offers a promising strategy for simultaneously achieving the upcycling of CO 2 and effective utilisation of ammonia as both an energy source and an electron donor.
items.authors: Koki Kajiwara, Shoji Iguchi, Shimpei Naniwa, Kentaro Teramura

items.title: Directional Prediction Errors Reveal Systematic Underprediction of Low-Pressure Carbon Dioxide Adsorption in Compact Metal–Organic Frameworks
items.abstract: A prediction residual has both magnitude and sign, yet materials-screening studies usually treat only its magnitude as informative. Here we show that residual sign localizes systematic underprediction of low-pressure carbon dioxide (CO2) adsorption to a compact, low-accessibility region of metalorganic-framework (MOF) descriptor space. We analyze 7,306 MOFs in a topology-held-out test set, keeping related framework topologies out of training. A one-sided 90% calibration defines the expected underprediction tail; critically, that tail is not distributed uniformly across materials space. Strong-underprediction incidence falls from 27.6% to 4.0% across accessible-volume-fraction quintiles and from 26.5% to 2.7% across accessible-surface-area quintiles, while rising from 4.2% to 24.7% with density. Individual discrepancies reach 6.35 mmol g−1. Literature-derived structural annotations of leading Mg-and Ca-containing cases motivate the testable hypothesis that global geometric descriptors can miss favorable first adsorption environments in compact frameworks; they do not establish a distinct microscopic adsorption mechanism. A calibrated lower-bound screen provides a separate practical corollary for conservative candidate prioritization. The central result is not the expected size of a positive-error tail, but its structured location in descriptor space. Retaining residual direction therefore provides a chemically interpretable diagnostic of model failure and identifies the next discriminating calculation or experiment.
items.authors: Mohammadsadegh Salimian Rizi, Angelo Di Bella, Shayan Abaei, Natalia Lydia Papadantonaki, Mehrdad Asgari

items.title: Drug Molecular and Route Similarity-Aware Retrieval-Augmented LLM Generation with Knowledge Graph for Semantic Reasoning
items.abstract: To address the inherent limitations of large language models (LLMs) in chemical synthesis—hallucinations, and low knowledge dense—this study presents a Knowledge Graph–enhanced Retrieval-Augmented Generation framework (KG-RAG-LLM) with a multi-scale calculation of molecular and route similarity. Empirical evaluations demonstrate that KG-RAG-LLM significantly mitigates hallucinations, increasing the proportion of concrete chemical information in generated responses to 39.52%–40.87%, drastically outperforming baseline LLMs and standard literature-based RAG pipelines in response completeness and accuracy. To overcome the inability of traditional 2D linear fingerprints to capture 3D spatial properties and reaction path variations, we further developed a multidimensional molecular and route similarity calculation combining SimHash, core similarity, and FCFP, as an alternative to Route CGR representations coupled with UMAP dimensionality reduction. This formulation accurately distinguishes between subtle and distinct synthetic strategies, demonstrating superior precision over traditional clustering methods for fuzzy retrieval of synthetic routes. Overall, this work provides a reliable, knowledge-dense solution for intelligent retrosynthetic Semantic Reasoning.
items.authors: Jiaxin Lao, Liansuo Zu

items.title: Assessing the Limits of He Isotope Separation Under
items.abstract: Separation of helium isotopes is of interest owing to the critical importance and limited supply of helium-3 (3He). Nanoporous materials offer a viable route for gas-phase isotope separation through either selective adsorption or quantum sieving. Here, to maximize the isotope selectivity of quantum sieving we propose coupling a strongly attracting open-metal site for He adsorption to a surrounding nanopore acting as a confining potential. We demonstrate that upon tightening the pore, the zero-point energy (ZPE) elevates up to a point where 3He detaches while 4He remains bound. Our model shows that 100% isotope-selective adsorption of 4He is achieved when pores of diameter 4.8-5.3 Å are coupled to metal sites with He binding energies of 2-20 kJ/mol. At 20 K, operating pressures between 0.3-30 bar are estimated, which increase to 2-6 kbar at 77 K. Even if the exact pore size for 100% isotope-selective adsorption cannot be realized, our results provide a rational design strategy for materials with unprecedentedly large He isotope separation factors at elevated temperatures.
items.authors: Elvira Gouatieu Dongmo, Felix Moncada, Shubhajit Das, Toshiki Riemer-Wulf, Thomas Heine

items.title: Enhanced Sodium Metal Anode Cycling Stability via an Organometallic Electrolyte Additive
items.abstract: Despite the high theoretical capacity of sodium metal anodes, practical application is limited by the general instability of the solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI) leading to dendritic growth and capacity fade. Here we report that the dimolybdenum paddlewheel complex, Mo2(mea)4 (1, mea = 2-(2-methoxyethoxy)acetate), functions as an effective electrolyte additive for Na metal anodes at millimolar loadings, enabled by self-assembly on the anode surface upon formation of aggregates involving 1 and Na+. In symmetric Na||Na cells, additive 1 was found to increase cycling stability and attenuate overpotential growth and impedance rise over 450 cycles compared to additive-free controls. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy revealed that 1 promotes early formation of an inorganic-rich SEI that also contains intact 1 and its downstream products. Scanning electron microscopy confirmed suppression of morphologies associated with dendrite growth. Full-cell Na||Na3V2(PO4)3 testing demonstrated improved Coulombic efficiency relative to an additive-free control and served to validate cathode compatibility of the additive. This work establishes organometallic complexes as an effective “third class” of Na metal battery additives, complementing purely organic or inorganic systems.
items.authors: S. M. Supundrika Subasinghe, Bhavya N. Vira, A. A. P. R. Perera, Simon G. Gersib, Jordi Cabana, Neal P. Mankad

items.title: Mechanistic basis of μ-opioid receptor allosteric modulation from molecular simulations
items.abstract: The μ-opioid receptor (μOR) is a central mediator of analgesia and opioid-induced adverse effects, yet the molecular basis by which allosteric modulators reshape receptor signaling remains poorly understood. Here, we integrate all-atom molecular dynamics with unbinding kinetics simulations to resolve the mechanistic basis of positive and negative allosteric modulation of μOR. We show that the positive allosteric modulator BMS-986122 enhances signaling not through uniform stabilization of canonical active microswitches, but by selectively remodeling the sodium pocket and, critically, stabilizing the μOR–G protein interface. This stabilization increases interfacial interactions and buried surface area, providing a G protein–dependent mechanism for enhanced efficacy despite increased agonist conformational flexibility and weakened orthosteric contacts. In contrast, the negative allosteric modulator compound 368 broadly enforces inactive-like microswitch conformations while simultaneously stabilizing antagonist binding. Unbinding kinetics simulations reveal that 368 exerts a dominant kinetic effect, restricting naloxone egress pathways and increasing residence time by approximately three orders of magnitude. Together, these results establish a unified framework in which μOR allostery operates through modulation of receptor and ligand conformational dynamics, G protein engagement, and ligand dissociation kinetics. This work provides an atomistic foundation for the rational design of next-generation opioid therapeutics that exploit allosteric mechanisms to enhance efficacy and safety.
items.authors: Liam Kwak, Roberto Garza-López

items.title: Stoichiometric Control in H 2 S-Mediated Nitrite Reduction at a Zn-site: Intercepting SNO 1− , SSNO 1− and HONO Intermediates
items.abstract: Hydrogen sulfide (H 2 S) and nitrite participate in intertwined signaling chemistry, yet the factors governing product selectivity between nitric oxide (NO) and nitroxyl (HNO) and the underlying reaction pathways remain poorly defined. Here, we establish that reduction of a zinc-nitrite complex by H 2 S follows stoichiometry-dependent product selectivity. With 2 equiv of H 2 S, the reaction generates NO and HNO-derived nitrous oxide (N 2 O) trapped in 46.3% ± 2.1% and 19.7% ± 1.5%, yields, respectively. UV-vis and 15 N NMR spectroscopy along with phosphine-based intermediate trapping and DFT studies support a nucleophilic attack pathway involving zinc-bound thionitrite (SNO − ) and perthionitrite (SSNO − ) intermediates. We independently synthesize and crystallographically characterize the zinc-perthionitrite complex, identifying isomers with cis-ĸ 2 -S,O and unprecedented Y-shaped ĸ 2 -S,S coordination modes in the solid-state. In contrast, 5 equiv of H 2 S favors an acidbase pathway involving spectroscopically intercepted nitrous acid (HONO) intermediate and affords NO in 94.6% ± 1.5% yield, with only trace N 2 O. Reaction with hydrosulfide (HS − ) instead, generate a zinc-hydrosulfide-nitrite adduct without nitrite reduction; subsequent protonation produces NO exclusively. Together, these findings establish H 2 S stoichiometry and proton availability as complementary determinants of competing nitrite reduction pathways that control NO versus N 2 O selectivity at a redox-inactive zinc center.
items.authors: Saikat Mishra, Anagha Kuruvayil, Esther Olatunji, Jeffery A. Bertke, Pokhraj Ghosh

items.title: Chromoselective Control for Aminoalkylation of CF3‑Alkenes through Low-Energy Photoredox Catalysis
items.abstract: Recent advances in chromoselective photoredox catalysis have demonstrated that light wavelength can serve as a powerful and orthogonal reaction parameter, enabling divergent reactivity from a single catalytic system. Building on recent advances in the sequential decarboxylative/defluorinative aminoalkylation of trifluoromethyl-substituted alkenes, we report a divergent, wavelength-dependent strategy for the site-selective functionalization of N-arylglycines. High-throughput experimentation (HTE) was used to systematically screen photocatalysts and irradiation wavelengths to identify the most suitable divergent conditions. Interestingly, using [Ru(bpy)3]2+ as photocatalyst, irradiation with blue light promotes efficient difunctionalization of CF3-alkenes with N-arylglycines, affording monofluoroalkenyl-1,5-diamines, while switching the irradiation to red light enables selective monofunctionalization, delivering the corresponding gem-difluoroalkenyl amine intermediates exclusively under otherwise identical conditions, via a spin-forbidden transition pathway. This wavelength-governed switchable reactivity provides a powerful and tunable platform for the controlled radical modification of amino acids, expanding the synthetic utility of visible-light photoredox catalysis in divergent amine synthesis. Mechanistic investigations using photoelectrochemistry and TD-DFT have revealed notably a photo-excitation of intermediates, allowing for the second functionalization to whether happens or not, based on the irradiation wavelength used.
items.authors: Marine Le Stum, Maria Eduarda Candido Thedy, Taline Kerackian, Jean-Christophe Cintrat, Emmanuel Nicolas, Laurence Grimaud

items.title: Solvent Dynamics and Multiconfigurational Treatment Drive the Anomalous Stokes Shift of HINA
items.abstract: The 3-hydroxyisonicotinaldehyde (HINA) anion is one of the smallest known green-emissive fluorophores, yet the origin of its anomalously large Stokes shift (0.87 eV) remains unexplained. Given the well-established influence of the surrounding environment on the photophysical properties of fluorescent dyes, we examine its role in this shift by simulating the anion's absorption and emission spectra with four computational protocols that differ in configurational sampling, solvent treatment, and electronic-structure method. Wigner sampling protocols capture less than half of the experimental Stokes shift, whether the solvent is treated implicitly or explicitly, whereas QM/MM molecular dynamics sampling improves it significantly. Structural analysis associates this improvement with coupling between the first solvation shell and the intramolecular interaction between the aldehyde hydrogen and the hydroxyl oxygen, which is captured by molecular-dynamics sampling but not by the corresponding frozen-solute Wigner-sampling protocol. When combined with RMS-CASPT2, this sampling quantitatively reproduces the experimental spectra and Stokes shift (0.85 versus 0.87 eV), showing that quantitative description of the Stokes shift of HINA requires both solvent-induced conformational dynamics and a multiconfigurational electronic-structure treatment.
items.authors: Carlo Albani, Mario Barbatti, Lea M. Ibele

items.title: Defining the Catalytic Boundaries of N -Nitrosourea-Forming StzF/SznF and Related Metalloenzymes through Genome Mining and Mechanistic Analysis
items.abstract: Enzymatic N–N bond formation is a rare and chemically challenging transformation in natural product biosynthesis. The non-heme iron metalloenzyme SznF catalyzes the formation of the N -nitrosourea pharmacophore of streptozotocin via the coordinated action of a diiron heme-oxygenase-like (HDO) domain and a mononuclear iron cupin domain. Although recent computational studies have advanced mechanistic models for this transformation, the determinants governing substrate specificity within this enzyme family remain poorly understood. Here, we employed a multi-pronged approach combining genome mining, substrate scope screening, protein engineering, structural analysis, and biochemical characterization to define the catalytic boundaries of SznF and related homologs. Genome mining identified a previously uncharacterized homolog displaying higher activity toward the native substrate N ω -methyl-L-arginine than SznF, expanding the known repertoire of N-nitrosourea-forming metalloenzymes. Comprehensive substrate screening further revealed the first non-native substrate accepted by this enzyme family, N ω -propyl-L-arginine, whereas all other modifications in carbon chain length, guanidino substitution, alkylation state, or stereochemistry did not result in detectable turnover. Structure-guided engineering that targeted the binding pocket surrounding the terminal alkyl substituent increased the activity of several variants toward N ω -propyl-L-arginine compared to wildtype SznF. Furthermore, cascade experiments, and nitric oxide supplementation further demonstrate that productive catalysis requires a precise combination of steric, electronic, and geometric features that cannot readily be compensated by alternative substrates. Together, these findings show that the substrate specificity of SznF and related homologs is governed by mechanistic constraints arising from the tightly coupled hydroxylation and rearrangement chemistry underlying N–N bond formation. More broadly, this work defines the catalytic boundaries of enzymatic N -nitrosourea formation while identifying new opportunities for the discovery and engineering of N–N bond-forming metalloenzymes for biocatalytic synthesis of structurally diverse N -nitrosourea derivatives.
items.authors: Charitomeni Angeli, Mohammad Faizan Bhat, Frank J. Dekker, Sandy Schmidt

items.title: Cholesteric Liquid Crystals for Ultratrace PFAS Detection
items.abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent, mobile water contaminants associated with adverse effects on human health and ecosystems. Current analytical methods require specialized instrumentation, complicating their on-site detection at ultratrace concentrations across distributed water infrastructures. Here we integrate fluorophilic partitioning and proton-responsive recognition within a cholesteric liquid crystal (CLC). The fluorinated component promotes selectivity over non-fluorinated structural analogues, whereas the pyridine receptor transduces protonation into changes in helical organization and reflected color. The formulation was confined within monodisperse spherical droplets and processed as a photocurable photonic ink to produce sensing strips with a strong reflection signal readable by portable fiber-optic spectroscopy. The platform detected five PFAS through concentration-dependent blue-shifts, reaching detection limits of 5.9 parts per trillion (ppt) without sample preconcentration and maintaining comparable performance across three water matrices. Coupling molecular recognition to collective supramolecular reorganization establishes CLCs as promising sensing materials for on-site ultratrace PFAS detection.
items.authors: Mauricio Vera-Arévalo, Alberto Concellón

items.title: Characterisation of thermostable CYP116B reductase domains as modular electron transfer units for redox biocatalysis
items.abstract: Electron transfer is a common bottleneck in redox biocatalysis. Here, we report the isolation of five cytochrome P450 reductase (CPR) domains from the thermophilic, self-sufficient CYP116B family. These enzymes have considerable industrial potential because their CPR and haem domains are naturally fused, yet the catalytic properties of the individual components remain poorly understood. EPR and UV–Vis spectroscopy confirmed the canonical FMN and [2Fe–2S] cofactors were present, although occupancy varied (FMN, 30–62%; [2Fe–2S], 10–33%). The isolated CPRs were generally stable, robust and electron-transfer competent, supporting electrochemical NADPH/NADP+ oxidation/reduction and NADPH-driven reduction of ferric cytochrome c. All homologues were more thermostable than the CPR from non-thermophilic CYP116B2, with stability showing an apparent correlation with [2Fe-2S] occupancy. Separating the CPR and haem domains generally reduced the ability to perform hydroxylation on a model substrate (diclofenac). However, isolated AxCPR and AxHAEM formed a productive non-covalent combination with activity comparable to the full-length enzyme (TON 439.38 ± 5.19 versus 416.43 ± 12.11). Given the widespread use of CYP116B CPR domains as surrogate redox partners in P450 catalysis, these findings provide valuable insight into their catalytic performance. Furthermore, the results demonstrate the potential of the isolated CYP116B CPRs as modular electron-transfer units for redox biocatalysis more widely.
items.authors: Kevin Hamdani, Samarth Pratap Singh, Kai Wu, Ting Wang, Clare F. Megarity, Henrik P. H. Wong

items.title: Toward bio-circular, fully organic batteries from non-toxic and bio-derived materials
items.abstract: The development of biodegradable energy storage systems is essential for enabling environmental monitoring devices that can degrade after stable operation. In this work, we present a fully organic, bio-circular battery that uses materials selected using a framework based on their natural occurrence and hazard classification according to the Globally Harmonized System of Classification and Labelling of Chemicals (GHS). We use redox-active organic molecules, aloe-emodin and luteolin, immobilized on activated coconut charcoal, together with an agarose/carboxymethyl cellulose gel polymer electrolyte and current collectors based on graphite flakes, carbon black, and agarose. The resulting battery delivers 0.7 V and stable electrochemical performance, supplying 8.8 mAh/g after 200 cycles, with 73.6% capacity retention and 98% coulombic efficiency. All components are further integrated into a pouch cell with an agarose packaging and beeswax coating. This prototype exhibits a discharge capacity of 7.1 μAh and 77.9% capacity retention over 20 cycles. Under simulated aerobic composting conditions, the pouch cell shows rapid and substantial disintegration, highlighting its potential for environmentally benign end-of-life scenarios. This work establishes a comprehensive design strategy for bio-circular batteries and demonstrates the applicability of bio-derived, GHS-non-toxic, fully organic materials for sustainable energy storage solutions.
items.authors: Veronica F. Michel, Tina Curtins, Oliver von Grünigen, Markus Niederberger

items.title: Next Generation NPK Slow Release Hydrogel Fertilizers: A Critical Review of Material Design, Performance, and Field Translation
items.abstract: Climate variability, water scarcity, declining soil quality, and inefficient fertilizer use are increasing the need for nutrient-delivery systems that support climate-resilient agriculture. Slow-release fertilizer hydrogels (SRFHs) are promising because they can retain water and control nutrient transport. This critical review examines SRFHs within conventional and enhanced-efficiency fertilizer strategies. It covers matrix, coated reservoir, and multilayer systems, along with their preparation methods and functional properties. The available evidence shows that polymer composition, crosslink density, pore structure, particle size, fertilizer loading, and environmental conditions affect swelling, mechanical behavior, and nutrient release. Important environmental factors include soil confinement, pH, ionic strength, and temperature. Kinetic models and response surface methodology can help explain release mechanisms and formulation trade-offs. Moisture-, pH-, and temperature-responsive systems may also support more adaptive nutrient delivery. However, high swelling or prolonged release in deionized water does not demonstrate improved nutrient uptake, crop yield, water-use efficiency, reduced nutrient loss, or environmental safety under field conditions. Translation is limited by inconsistent protocols, inadequate dose-matched controls, few multi-season trials, and limited evidence on degradation, residual materials, batch reproducibility, scale-up, and farm-level value. To address these gaps, this review proposes a target product profile that links crop, soil, and climate conditions with nutrient-specific release, mechanical service life, environmental fate, manufacturability, and economic performance. Model-guided responsive formulations could eventually be combined with sensor- and IoT-enabled monitoring for precision agriculture. However, this remains a prospective rather than field-validated approach. SRFHs should therefore be judged by reproducible and context-specific agronomic and environmental performance rather than maximum laboratory performance alone.
items.authors: Sayem Kawsar, Ahasan Chowdhury Mridul, Khondoker Kabbyo Shariar, Nafisa Islam, Ahasan Chowdhury Mridul

items.title: Case Studies of Homemorphic Isomerization: Interconversion of In/Out Isomers of Bicyclo[6.5.1]tetradecane and Related Bicyclic Hydrocarbons
items.abstract: Homeomorphic isomerization is equivalent to turning a molecule inside out in the same manner as a reversible article of clothing. Manifestations include the interconversion of (a) in,in and out,out isomers, or (b) in,out and out,in isomers of bicyclic molecules, but without inverting the configurations of the bridgehead atoms. In this preprint, this topological process is probed computationally for the title molecules. For the in,in/out,out manifold, the CH 2 tether is able to transit through the CH(CH 2 ) 6 CH tether with a barrier of ~26 kcal/mol, in good agreement with an experimental measurement. The geometries of the ground and transition states are analyzed in detail and the process of isomerization is visualized in animations.
items.authors: Marsel Z. Shafikov, John A. Gladysz

items.title: Spirocyclic Azetidines as Lactam Bioisosteres in Isoindolinones Through Facile C1 Stitching Enabled by Dual Energy- and Electron-Transfer Photocatalysis
items.abstract: Bioisosteric replacement of nitrogen-containing cyclic structures with smaller, more conformationally rigid ring systems such as azetidines and spirocyclic azetidines has emerged as an effective strategy to improve the physicochemical and pharmacokinetic profiles of nitrogen-bearing drug candidates. Despite extensive studies, the use of spirocyclic azetidines as bioisosteres has been limited to simple ring systems and has not been extended to medicinally relevant complex pharmacophores. Herein, we introduce benzo-fused spirocyclic azetidines as three-dimensional bioisosteres of lactam moieties in isoindolinones, significant structural motifs present in 40,000 bioactive compounds. Our synthetic strategy is to “stitch” in one step a broad range of oxadiazoline carbene precursors and substituted 1-azabicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (ABBs), thus accessing structurally diverse spirocyclic azetidines. This reaction is mechanistically novel, merging strain-release activation of ABB with a dual energy-transfer/single-electron-transfer photocatalytic cascade, enabling formal C1-insertion under mild conditions. The physicochemical and metabolic profiling suggests that these spirocyclic azetidine bioisosteres retain key physicochemical properties while improving metabolic stability. Moreover, docking studies indicate conserved recognition with the potential for interaction rewiring at selected targets. Given the ubiquitous presence of lactam and amide-containing motifs in bioactive molecules and drug candidates, this work opens new avenues for drug discovery and clinical development.
items.authors: Zi-An Shen, Mengyang Zhang, Sirui Wu, Yixin Lu

items.title: Advancing Targeted Nanoparticle mRNA Delivery Using Machine Learning
items.authors: Marius Kausas, Valentina Schastlivaia

items.title: Lithium Plating-Induced Fracture of Individual Graphite Platelets Revealed by Operando
items.abstract: Lithium plating is a key barrier to achieving faster charging of lithium-ion batteries; however, fundamental and nanoscale understanding of plating is still being developed, largely due to the dynamic nature of the process. Here, we perform operando electrochemical atomic force microscopy on individual graphite platelets to observe the morphology evolution of plated lithium and graphite electrodes simultaneously. We observe plating-induced fracture of the graphite platelets even in the absence of a porous electrode structure. Unexpectedly, fracture occurs through preferential lithium deposition beneath the particle surface despite lithium-ion transport limitations, pointing to lithium in graphite as the lithium source. Our findings deepen the understanding of the lithium plating process and offer pathways to improvement for fast-charged negative electrodes.
items.authors: Justin A. Rose, Che-Ning Yeh, Swati Narasimhan, Michael L. Li, Henry L. Thaman, Alexander E. Cohen

items.title: NEVPT2 Multiple Spawning Molecular Dynamics Simulations for Uracil
items.abstract: The quasidegenerate n-electron valence state second-order perturbation theory (QD-NEVPT2) for complete active space reference wavefunctions has been implemented in the OpenMolcas package. The implementation utilizes the efficient formulation of Kollmar et al. for the electronic energy, which is extended here to the calculation of analytic derivatives. To demonstrate its utility, the method is applied to classical and non-adiabatic molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of uracil. The non-adiabatic MD simulations describe the ultrafast deactivation of the initially excited bright ππ∗ state through the S 2 /S 1 conical intersection, demonstrating the applicability of the method to photochemical processes. Furthermore, a machine learning-based analysis of the trajectory data extracts key geometrical parameters that are associated with the magnitude of the time-derivative coupling.
items.authors: Yoshio Nishimoto

items.title: Formamidine-Linked Covalent Organic Frameworks
items.abstract: Formamidine has been established as a versatile molecule in agriculture, organic solar cells, and as a ligand in organometallic catalysis. Despite, formamidine-based materials have remained largely unexplored due to challenges in achieving controlled polymerization. In this direction, we introduce a one-pot microwave-assisted diamine-orthoformate condensation strategy to synthesize formamidine-linked conjugated covalent organic frameworks (FOF-2 and FOF-3). Interestingly, the formamidine units of FOFs enable affinity towards urea, and that allowed us to use as metal-free electrocatalysts for the urea oxidation reaction (UOR) in alkaline media. FOF-2 demonstrates an onset potential value of 1.47 V (vs RHE) and a lower overpotential. The ordered microporous conjugated backbone facilitates charge and mass transport in FOFs. These findings demonstrate that metal-free FOFs can serve as a platform for UOR and open new directions toward organic framework-based electrocatalysts for sustainable energy conversion.
items.authors: Om Prakash Swain, Tapan Ping, Bidita Panda, Preeti Bhauriyal, Narayan Deep Singh, B. L. Bhargava

items.title: From Vacuum Geometry to Solution-Phase Electronic Properties and Thermodynamics via Equivariant Neural Networks
items.abstract: We introduce a general framework for predicting solution-phase quantum-mechanical (QM) properties of drug-like molecules directly from gas-phase geometries, without solvent-specific structural optimization or property calculations. Using current equivariant neural network (ENN) architectures, such as MACE and Allegro, we demonstrate that they can also predict extensive and intensive QM properties in implicit water at a high level of theory. Direct-and ∆-learning strategies are employed for this prediction task using the Aquamarine dataset, which provides QM properties for the same molecules in both environments. The developed models are systematically evaluated for scalability to larger molecules, transferability across chemical space, and generalization to out-of-equilibrium configurations. Our results show that, despite substantial differences between gas-and solution-phase conformational ensembles, the models can accurately reconstruct ensemble-averaged solution-phase properties from gas-phase molecular dynamics. We further integrate the learned QM properties into the QUEDsol framework (“QUantum Electronic Descriptors in SOLution”) as electronic descriptors for hydration free-energy prediction. A simple and interpretable quadratic regression model trained on the FreeSolv dataset achieves state-of-the-art performance on the challenging and chemically diverse FlexiSol benchmark, outperforming previously reported QM-and ML-based approaches. These results establish ENNs as a versatile approach for inter-phase molecular property prediction and demonstrate that environment-specific QM descriptors generated from gas-phase geometries can provide transferable inputs for complex thermodynamic modeling.
items.authors: Mathias Hilfiker, Lorenzo D’Amore, Dries Van Rompaey, Marco Klähn, Ola Engkvist, Alexandre Tkatchenko

items.title: Resolving Month-Long Nanostructural Evolution in Degrading Anion Exchange Membranes
items.abstract: Chemical degradation reshapes the hydrated ion-transport channels of anion exchange membranes (AEMs), but conventional aging measurements do not reveal how their nanostructure evolves toward functional failure. Here we resolve this structural evolution using high-resolution kinetic Monte Carlo (kMC) simulations. The simulations are calibrated to reproduce the experimental ion exchange capacity (IEC) and water uptake (WU) over a month degradation of a PPO-TEA membrane. The ionomer-peak position remains essentially unchanged even after 70% cation loss, while the water channels narrow from approximately 0.8 to 0.6 nm and progressively fragment. The hydrated network loses percolation at a critical hydrophilic volume fraction 𝜙!≈ 0.26, close to the threshold (𝜙!≈ 0.25) inferred from experimental conductivity using a percolation power law. Two complementary descriptions, a percolation law and a connected-carrier model, reproduce the normalized conductivity decay without using conductivity to calibrate the degradation kinetics. These results link conductivity failure to the loss of connected transport pathways within a membrane that retains its characteristic phase-separation length scale. The structural predictions are similar for two kinetic models with different dependencies on local hydration. Thus, a persistent ionomer-peak position can conceal substantial deterioration of the ion-transport network. Resolving channel connectivity along the aging trajectory provides a structural measure of membrane durability that complements conventional characterization of phase separation.
items.authors: Shakkira Erimban, Esteban D. Gadea, Ignacio J. Bombau, John J. Karnes, Johanna J. Schwartz, Valeria Molinero

items.title: Rational construction of semi-clathrate-like water networks on engineered ferritin cages
items.abstract: Understanding and controlling the organization of water at molecular interfaces is a longstanding goal in both biological and materials sciences, as it controls the biophysical properties of the surfaces. For example, semi-clathrate waters containing polygonal hydrogen-bonded water clusters found in some antifreeze proteins (AFPs), are thought to play key roles in interacting with ice. Despite this significance, the lack of well-defined design principles makes it difficult to rationally construct such ordered hydration architectures. Here, we report the rational construction of a semiclathrate-like water network in an engineered ferritin cage. We designed a series of alanine (Ala) mutants on the internal surface of the ferritin cage and analyzed the formation of semi-clathratelike water networks using X-ray crystal structure analysis. Our results indicate that the continuous hydrophobic surface formed by the Ala mutation organizes water molecules on its surface, forming semi-clathrate-like water networks. Specific hydrogen-bonding networks involving the main-chain carbonyl group were found to play a key role in initiating the formation of semi-clathrate-like water networks. These findings are significant for organizing water molecules on the protein surface to control biophysical properties.
items.authors: Basudev Maity, Jiaxin Tian, Tadaomi Furuta, Satoshi Yasuda, Takeshi Murata, Takafumi Ueno

items.title: Surface hydroxyls act as key intermediates in the selective oxidative dehydrogenation of 2-propanol on Co3O4
items.abstract: Transition-metal oxides typically catalyze aerobic oxidation reactions with high activity even at low temperatures, but rarely with high selectivity. Owing to the complexity of competing surface processes on such catalysts, the rational design of selective low-temperature catalysts still requires a deeper mechanistic understanding of the active surface and reaction intermediates. In this work, we combine operando modulation-excitation infrared spectroscopy with density functional theory and molecular dynamics to mechanistically investigate 2-propanol oxidation over Co3O4 with a focus on surface hydroxyls, acting as hydrogen acceptors during alcohol adsorption. We identify two chemically distinct hydroxyl populations: linear hydroxyls, which actively participate in acetone formation and can be considered part of the active surface ensemble, and bridged hydroxyls, which behave largely as spectators. Together, these results provide a molecular-level mechanistic picture of alcohol oxidation on Co3O4 and establish the dynamic role of surface hydroxyl species as active players in heterogeneous oxidation catalysis.
items.authors: Pierfrancesco Ticali, Stephane Kenmoe, Hamidreza Hajiyani, Amir Omranpour, Nicolas Cosanne, Hauke Scheele

items.title: Tunable Aza-BODIPY Photocatalysts for Near-Infrared Metallaphotoredox Atom Transfer Radical Polymerization
items.abstract: The merger of photoredox and transition-metal catalysis has significantly advanced radical and redox transformations, yet its reliance on UV or visible light continues to limit applications in optically complex and spatially confined environments. Herein, we introduce a modular family of tetraaryl aza-boron-dipyrromethene (aza-BODIPY) organic photocatalysts (PCs) for near-infrared (NIR) metallaphotoredox atom transfer radical polymerization (ATRP). We systematically modulated peripheral electronics and core bromination, evaluating the dyes through quantum-chemical, electrochemical, and spectroscopic methods. This approach identified the key parameters governing catalytic performance: a delicate interplay between triplet-state accessibility, redox properties, and photostability. The optimized aza-BODIPY dye enables well-controlled ATRP of diverse acrylates and methacrylates at ultralow catalyst loadings, down to 5 ppm PC and 50 ppm copper complex. The system is further translated to open-air aqueous conditions, enabling rapid, high-throughput synthesis of water-soluble polymers in a 96-well plate format. Taking advantage of the enhanced penetration of NIR light, we demonstrate controlled polymerization through challenging physical barriers, including ex vivo tissue. Overall, this work defines design principles for far-red/NIR-absorbing aza-BODIPY PCs and expands the scope of NIR-mediated polymer synthesis to optically turbid, spatially restricted, and aqueous environments.
items.authors: Jakub Piątkowski, Paulina H. Marek-Urban, Martyna Cybularczyk-Cecotka, Magdalena Z. Wiloch-Szyborska, Joanna Jankowska, Yoichi Kobayashi

items.title: Data-Driven Approach to Predicting Durability and Property Retention in Polymer Matrix Composites
items.abstract: Predicting the long-term performance of reinforced polymer composites from short-duration accelerated aging data remains a central challenge in composite durability engineering. This work presents a data-driven kinetic and mechanical-performance characterization of a glass-flake reinforced unsaturated polyester composite exposed to deionized water at 20, 40, 60 and 80 °C for up to 14.5 months, integrating long-term gravimetric sorption, flexural testing, and dynamic mechanical analysis (DMA), including substantial portions of the dataset that have not previously been analyzed or reported. The initial moisture sorption rate constant obeys an Arrhenius relationship across all four temperatures (activation energy Ea = 45.1 kJ/mol, R2 = 0.97), providing a kinetic basis for estimating uptake behavior within the tested temperature range. Extended gravimetric monitoring reveals a two stage hygrothermal response: an initial Fickian-like uptake stage reaching an apparent plateau (4.4-7.5 wt% depending on temperature and replicate), followed by a degradation-associated mass-loss stage, with weight gain at 60 °C falling from a 4.5% plateau to 1.8% after 14.5 months, and markedly greater coupon-to-coupon variability at 80 °C. Flexural modulus and strength retention under wet conditions (22-50% and 28-60% of dry values, respectively) is reported across all four temperatures at 2 and 6 months, alongside DMA glass transition temperature data showing an initial rise with exposure temperature followed by a decrease at 80 °C. No meaningful relationship between initial moisture sorption kinetics and 2-month mechanical retention could be established from the present four temperature-matched averages (Pearson r = 0.43, n = 4; retention is non-monotonic in ln(k)); the 6-month data instead indicate that degradation kinetics and exposure duration, rather than the initial sorption rate, are what track mechanical performance loss. The study does not establish a validated model for predicting mechanical-property retention; rather, it provides a quantitative experimental basis and structured dataset for future data-driven and machine-learning-based durability models of this and structurally similar glass-flake-reinforced polyester and related polymer matrix composite systems.
items.authors: Parastou Kharazmi

items.title: Beyond Bulk Grade: Mineral–Flow Accessibility Controls Pore-Scale Copper Recovery
items.abstract: Mineral dissolution in porous media is driven by fluid flow, solute transport, and geochemical reactions, yet reactive transport models commonly use bulk mineral abundance and specific surface area as proxies for mineral reactivity. This neglects a key constraint: dissolution occurs only where reactants can access minerals through connected fluid-flow pathways. Here, we use pore-scale PFLOTRAN simulations of acid-driven chrysocolla dissolution to isolate the effect of mineral accessibility at fixed initial mineral volume fraction. Across pore-network ensembles and flow–reaction conditions, copper recovery varied substantially (9–21%) despite identical bulk copper content. Recovery depended on the fraction of mineral accessible to connected flow and on mineral proximity to inlet-connected pores, even when cumulative pore volumes flushed during the 48 h acid pulse were nearly identical. In contrast, Péclet and Damköhler numbers characterized transport–reaction regimes but did not uniquely predict copper recovery because they do not encode pore-scale accessibility. An accessibility-weighted pore-volume metric combined with intrinsic dissolution kinetics explained recovery with R2 ≈ 0.95. Thus, our results show that mineral–flow accessibility and reaction kinetics jointly control pore-scale copper recovery and provide a physically interpretable basis for accessibility-aware reactive transport upscaling.
items.authors: Arjun Chakrawal, Maruti Kumar Mudunuru, Sameera Nalin Venkat, Aramy Truong, Christof Meile, Kalyana Nakshatrala

items.title: Beyond Materials Rankings: When Adsorption or Membranes Win for CO2/CH4 Separation
items.abstract: Choosing between adsorption and membranes for carbon dioxide removal from methane is often reduced to a contest between material metrics, even though an industrially meaningful answer emerges from the coupled material, flowsheet, pressure, composition, recovery, and economic context. Here we compare the technologies on a common process boundary, allowing each to select its process-optimal material, equipment size, and membrane architecture while meeting identical methane-product and recovery constraints. The resulting atlas spans 300 ARC–MOF adsorbents, 220 experimental polymers, and 864 matched biogas-and natural-gas-like scenarios. Among 676 mutually feasible cases, adsorption minimizes annualized cost in 73.4% and membranes in 26.6%; choosing the wrong technology incurs a median cost regret of 19.4%. Crucially, the boundary is not a single pressure threshold. Four pressurized-natural-gas slices exhibit clean adsorption–membrane–adsorption re-entry as the optimal material and membrane flowsheet switch with operating conditions. Material and architecture ablations isolate this mechanism. Cost-based choices disagree with energy, methane-loss, and footprint choices in 30.8–46.0% of paired comparisons, while cost and operational-climate choices disagree in 25.4%; joint uncertainty creates an explicit abstention region in 18.3% of boundary-focused cases. The framework converts high-throughput materials screening into conditional, auditable technology-selection rules and a compact agenda for cycle and mixed-gas validation under realistic process conditions and quantified uncertainty ranges.
items.authors: Mehrdad Asgari, Mohammad Sadegh Salimian Rizi, Shayan Abaei, Zeynep Defne Sezen
