items.title: Defining Applicability Domains for Metal–Ligand Selectivity Prediction: Predictive Uncertainty vs. Molecular Similarity
items.abstract: Applicability domains are widely used to determine whether a machine-learning prediction can be trusted, yet they are commonly defined by similarity to the training data rather than by evidence that similarity predicts error. Here, we treat an applicability criterion as a testable claim and evaluate whether it identifies predictions with lower error than an equally sized random subset on a common held-out population. We test 23 criteria on a context-dependent metal–ligand selectivity problem, comparing molecular fingerprints, descriptor-space distances, learned embeddings, training support and predictive uncertainty. At 50% retention, predictive uncertainty reduces mean-of-pairs RMSE by 65%, compared with 32% for the best molecular distance and 18% for the best ligand-only distance. Fingerprint nearest-neighbour and learned-embedding distances provide no useful error ordering, whereas uncertainty remains informative after accounting for training support and predicted magnitude. In a prospective-style selection task, ranking ligands by their standardized predicted margin above a selectivity threshold increases single-ligand success from 0.639±0.035 under random selection to 0.831± 0.059. These results show that, at least for the context-dependent metal-ligand selectivity task studied here, structural similarity to the training data is not, by itself, evidence of predictive reliability in context-dependent molecular prediction. Applicability criteria can instead be treated as empirical hypotheses and tested directly against held-out error before being used to define reliable prediction regions or benchmark difficulty.
items.authors: Ivan Zlobin, Ivan Bespalov, Mark Schneider, Maksim Shandybo, Nikolai Rekut, Alexander Pavlov

items.title: Enabling Optoelectronics in Cu2S/Co9S8 Heteroassembly
items.abstract: Semiconductor heteroassembly can integrate complementary properties through nanoscale interfaces, but structural integration alone does not necessarily yield optoelectronic functionality. Here, we demonstrate an optoelectronically active Cu2S/Co9S8 heteroassembly for photodetection, obtained through higher-temperature nucleation and growth conditions that may promote enhanced crystallization and structural ordering of Co9S8. Structural characterization reveals crystalline Cu2S nanostructures decorated with dense 3–5 nm Co9S8 nanocrystallites, providing extensive interfacial contact. HRTEM, electron diffraction, XRD, and elemental mapping confirm the coexistence and spatial integration of the two phases. Controlled antisolvent processing reduces residual organic content and enables formation of uniform films. A vertical Cu2S/Co9S8/n-Si device exhibits broadband photoresponse with rise and fall times of 2.7 and 2.3 s, respectively. At 2 V bias, the device achieves a responsivity of 1.93 mA W-1 and a shot-noise-limited detectivity of 6.3 × 107 Jones. The bias-dependent response is attributed to field-assisted photocarrier separation and extraction, with the Cu2S/n-Si junction and Cu2S/Co9S8 interfaces influencing carrier transport. These results highlight the combined importance of structural ordering and interfacial architecture in converting nanoscale heteroassembly into functional optoelectronic devices.
items.authors: Biman Jana

items.title: Enhanced Spin-Forbidden Excitation of Ru(II) Polypyridyl Complexes for the Promotion of Red-Light Photocatalysis
items.abstract: Photoredox catalysis, mainly occurring under blue light, has emerged as an indispensable tool in modern organic synthesis. However, some limitations remain, mostly due to the high energy inherent to the irradiation wavelengths used. Red-light excitation of transition-metal photocatalysts is attractive for expanding the synthetic utility of visible-light photochemistry. Here, we report a strategy to enhance spin-forbidden red-light absorption in Ru(II) polypyridyl complexes through ligand tuning. [Ru(Br2-bpy)3](PF6)2 exhibits a substantially intensified spin-forbidden absorption band in the red region, with a molar extinction coefficient approximately 10-fold higher than that of [Ru(bpy)3]2+. The enhanced red-light absorption results in markedly improved photocatalytic activity under 660 nm irradiation in a range of electron- and energy-transfer transformations. Comparison with the parent complex demonstrates that modulation of the spin-forbidden absorption pathway can directly influence red-light photochemical reactivity. These findings support ligand modification as an effective approach for enhancing spin-forbidden excitation and provide a molecular design strategy for redlight-responsive Ru(II) photocatalysts, establishing Ru(II) polypyridyl complexes as an efficient family of photocatalysts activated via a spin-forbidden transition pathway.
items.authors: Yahya Al Ayi, Nathan Grandjean, Benjamin Riss-Yaw, Annamaria Quaranta, Eugénie Romero

items.title: Following Nature’s Lead – Pillar[n]arene Phosphates as Versatile Molecular Hosts
items.abstract: Phosphates are ubiquitous natural recognition motifs. Their charge, hydrogen bonding, variable substitution, and reversible enzymatic installation uniquely enable complex tasks in Biology. However, they are not used extensively in supramolecular systems. Herein, we combine Nature’s modulator with supramolecular rational design, creating rim-functionalised pillar[n]arene phosphates, which act as highaffinity molecular hosts. Using robust phosphoramidite chemistry, we prepared P5Max and P6Max, based on pillar[5]arene and pillar[6]arene cores in four high yielding steps. We developed a high-throughput fluorescence displacement assay enabling us to explore a biologically focused screening panel and so rapidly investigate the recognition properties of our new hosts. P5Max and P6Max bind a series of structurally diverse chemotherapies, neuromuscular blockade agents, anaesthetics and antibiotics, with P6Max proving the more general host. We used functional assays to explore P6Max’s ability to control the biological effect of different drug classes, including highly toxic chemotherapy drugs and antibiotics. The use of high-throughput assays in host-guest systems provides a simple, rapid, and scalable route to translating supramolecular interactions to functional effect.
items.authors: Edvinas Ališauskas, Laia E. Cano, Siu-Chung Chan, Samuel I. Fidler, Ellen M. G. Jamieson, Michael J. O’Sullivan

items.title: A dimension staircase for orientational heat capacity: nature skips the 3/2 rung
items.abstract: The low-temperature orientational heat capacity of an interacting multipole pair is conventionally taken to be two-valued: 3/2 k B for axially symmetric moments and 2 k B otherwise. Here I evaluate it for all 101,666,280 molecular geometries of the OMol25 dataset and show that this is the bottom rung of a staircase: the exponent is a count, not a case split, γ = C v / k B = Σ i 1/ p i , which for two rigid nonlinear molecules is exactly γ = D / 2 and leaves only the rungs 3/2, 2 and 5/2. Of 11,325,000 pairs drawn uniformly from the whole dataset none occupies the 3/2 rung ( P 3.26 x 10 -7 ; structural bound 4.187 x 10 -7 ), and the rest split 12.05% and 87.95% between γ = 2 and 5/2, so nearly the whole molecular world shares one coefficient: 5/2 k B = 20.79 J mol -1 K -1 per mole of pairs. The 3/2 rung is deleted rather than thermally suppressed (a 0.129 Å C-H bending amplitude exceeds the 0.1 Å scale at which a C 3v rotor saturates its axiality defect), so no temperature recovers it.
items.authors: Fuxing Lin

items.title: A Scalable One-Pot Strategy for Porphyrin Metal–Organic Frameworks via In situ Linker Synthesis
items.abstract: Porphyrin metal–organic frameworks (pMOFs) are highly versatile materials for catalysis, energy, and environmental applications, yet their widespread use is limited by the cost and multistep synthesis of porphyrin linkers. Here, we report a one-pot synthetic strategy that integrates porphyrin formation and MOF crystallization, enabling the direct assembly of zirconium-based pMOFs from simple molecular precursors. This approach eliminates the need for linker isolation and purification, significantly reducing synthetic complexity and resource consumption. The method is demonstrated for the benchmark framework PCN-224 and its zinc metalloporphyrin analogue, yielding crystalline, porous materials at multigram scale. Notably, the resulting materials exhibit enhanced mesoporosity, which improves mass transport and enables superior adsorption of large organic dyes, despite lower BET surface areas compared to conventionally synthesized analogues. Importantly, we further demonstrate the generality of this approach by synthesizing USTC-9(Fe), a framework with distinct metal nodes and porphyrin linker geometry. This work establishes a versatile platform for coupling complex linker synthesis with framework assembly, offering a sustainable and scalable route to functional pMOFs and broadening the scope of in situ linker formation in reticular chemistry.
items.authors: Anna Sinelshchikova, Roberto Fernández de Luis, Ibai Bilbao Zulaika, Sofia Castro, Pedro Martins, Stefan Wuttke

items.title: Collective vibrational strong coupling triggers dissociation reaction by overcoming energy threshold
items.abstract: Ground-state reactions under vibrational strong coupling (VSC) have emerged as one of the central topics in polariton chemistry, yet how the energy redistribution under collective VSC translates into chemical reactivity remains an open question. Here we investigate vibrational predissociation in dilute ensembles of water trimers coupled to an optical cavity using full-dimensional cavity quasi-classical trajectory (cav-QCT) simulations with ab initio-quality potential-energy and dipole-moment surfaces. We demonstrate that collective VSC directly induces an otherwise energetically forbidden dissociation of the water trimer through cavity-mediated intermolecular VET. Remarkably, the enhancement of reactivity remains observable with increasing ensemble size despite reduced effective single-molecule light–matter coupling strength. Trajectory analyses identify collective energy transfer as the microscopic mechanism and reveal largely consistent quantum-state distributions of the reaction products. These findings establish a microscopic link between collective polaritonic energy transport and chemical reactivity, and suggest collective VSC as a route toward simultaneously manipulating reactivity and preserving product-state selectivity.
items.authors: Mingliang Ding, Ruitao Ma, Dianfang Chen, Yongchang Han, Dong H. Zhang, Qi Yu

items.title: The Dopant Cage Sets the Phonon Count of Lanthanide Emitters
items.abstract: Multiphonon relaxation decides whether a lanthanide ion emits light or heats its host. Since 1968 it has been predicted from the host’s maximum phonon energy, although the excitation resides on a single ion. First-principles force constants and five decades of relaxation measurements show that the accepting vibration is the stretch of the dopant’s coordination cage, a site property set by local chemistry. Aliovalent substitution stiffens the cage by up to 27%, and across seven halide hosts the cage frequency departs from the host frequency by −21% to +19%. It predicts measured effective phonon frequencies three times more accurately than the host frequency, and in its quanta the seven energy-gap laws share one room-temperature slope. The site-resolved laws map the lattice limits of optical refrigeration from 2 to 6 µm. The phonon count of a lanthanide emitter becomes a site property that chemistry can tune and theory can compute before synthesis.
items.authors: Daqian Bian

items.title: Lipid-Phase Access Does Not Explain P-Glycoprotein Substrate Selection in Matched Pairs
items.abstract: The hydrophobic vacuum cleaner model holds that P-glycoprotein intercepts substrates within the lipid bilayer, which makes lipid-phase access to the transporter a candidate determinant of efflux, but the proposition has never been tested on compounds matched for the properties that otherwise dominate. We simulated nine matched molecular pairs—matched simultaneously on calculated lipophilicity, hydrogen-bond donors, polar surface area and molecular weight, and differing 5.9-to 30.1-fold in measured MDR1-MDCK efflux ratio—in a coarse-grained blood–brain barrier membrane containing human P-glycoprotein, and applied a pre-registered observable: enrichment E of substrate over non-substrate within 3.5 nm of the lateral portal axis. E bears no relation to efflux (ρ = −0.100, p = 0.80, n = 9), and the slope of unity predicted if access governed efflux lies outside the 95% interval [−0.51, +0.79], while five matched replicas put the measurement error at 3.65 times below the pair-to-pair spread, so the null is informative rather than underpowered. Selection is therefore decided after arrival at the transporter rather than during delivery to it.
items.authors: Hayat Ullah, Khwaja Jawad, Khan Ziaullah, Md Ariful Islam Mozumder, Moon-Il Joo, Hee-Cheol Kim

items.title: The Chemical Bond in the Age of Quantum Information: Atoms in Molecules as Entangled Open Systems
items.abstract: The chemical bond is among the oldest ideas in chemistry and still among the least settled: chemists continue to disagree about what a bond is. We argue that the recurring controversies (ionic versus covalent, dative versus shared-electron, hypervalent versus metavalent, whether metal–metal contacts are genuinely collective) are not disputes about the physics but about an unstated reference against which a bond is declared. Removing the reference forces a change of viewpoint: an atom in a molecule is not a fixed piece of electron density but an open quantum system, a mixed state that is a probabilistic superposition over how many electrons it owns. From this vantage the electronnumber fluctuations that the theory of electron distribution functions has long measured acquire a sharp meaning: they are the quantum correlation, the entanglement, shared between the atoms of a molecule. Measured directly between the Bader basins chemists already draw, this entanglement yields a single, reference-free bond order in which the electron pair of Lewis, the resonance of Pauling and the delocalization of Mulliken reappear not as assumptions but as consequences. We outline the open-systems formulation of Quantum Chemical Topology that makes the picture exact, and sketch how the same quantity is the natural readout of molecular quantum computation.
items.authors: D. J. L. Rodrigues, E. Francisco, A. Martín Pendás, Ángel Martín Pendás

items.title: Transformation product bottleneck: Photo-recalcitrance of rotenolone limits the aquatic degradation of rotenone in a temperature-dependent manner
items.abstract: The environmental fate and toxicity of transformation products (TPs) are frequently overlooked. However, in many cases, TPs are functional analogs that exhibit similar, and often greater, toxicity as the parent compound. In cases where the TP is persistent in the environment, the rate of TP degradation can influence the overall environmental fate. Rotenolone (12𝛼-hydroxy-rotenone, ROH) is the primary TP of rotenone (ROT), a pesticide utilized ubiquitously and highly popular in cold regions. Both ROT and ROH are mitochondrial NADH inhibitors, however ROH is more persistent than ROT and remains unregulated. 2 This work investigated the aquatic photochemical pathways and transformation products of ROH, including simulated Subarctic (low-temperature) conditions. Given that ROT degradation is driven by photolysis, we hypothesized that inhibited photochemical activity of ROH accounts for its persistence. Our results suggest ROH persistence is largely attributed to significantly reduced triplet state lifetimes, absorbance, and apparent quantum yields. Temperature was identified as a significant driver of ROH photolysis, accelerating the direct photochemical transformation rate, with half-lives ranging from approximately 115 h (6 °C) to 66 h (19 °C). This suggests that the cool temperatures of Subarctic surface waters further contribute to ROH persistence. Degradation was accelerated in the presence of chromophoric dissolved organic matter (CDOM); Fenton experiments confirmed ROH reacts with hydroxyl radical at near diffusion-limited rates (2.9×1010 ± 1.1×109 M-1 s-1 at 20 °C). Nontarget analysis of ROH photoproducts revealed novel transformation intermediates not previously identified. These were observed to further transform to smaller products, suggesting that ROH photochemical transformation represents the final step in detoxification. Thus, the photochemical recalcitrance of ROH is involved in limiting the detoxification of ROT following aquatic pesticidal use. These results strongly suggest including ROH monitoring during ROT pesticide applications.
items.authors: Brian P. DiMento, Aidan Efird, Stefani Martinez, Lilas Pontvianne, Léa Prajoux, Mohamed Sarakha

items.title: FMS2Lib: A Machine Learning-Ready Tandem Mass Spectral Library for Nontargeted Analysis of Non-conventional PFAS
items.abstract: Nontargeted identification of non-conventional per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), including fluorinated pharmaceuticals and pesticides, remains challenging. Existing machine learning models for nontargeted analysis, primarily trained on tandem mass spectra of nonfluorinated compounds, may not generalize well to non-conventional PFAS because of their distinct mass spectrometric chemistry. Here, we established FMS2Lib, an experimental tandem mass spectral library containing 34,686 fluorinated drug-like compounds (F 1-4 ), to support machine learning-based nontargeted PFAS analysis. We demonstrated that training with FMS2Lib substantially improved the performance of existing models for both molecular formula prediction and structure annotation. We further applied these models to identify PFAS in passive samplers from wastewater effluents and surface waters and in high-throughput laboratory biotransformation experiments, revealing dozens of non-conventional PFAS and their biotransformation products. Collectively, FMS2Lib addresses a major data bottleneck in machine learning-based nontargeted analysis of non-conventional PFAS.
items.authors: Tao Yang, Xiaoyun Wang, Diwen Yang, Elizabeth Xu, Lifei Wang, Sonya M. Kleywegt

items.title: CAN it work? Using hydroxyethyl acrylate or methacrylate to turn epoxy-amine thermosets into covalent adaptable network materials.
items.abstract: Epoxy-amine thermosets can be converted into covalent adaptable networks (CANs) by adding β-aminoester-based curing agents to the formulation. This is achieved by utilizing commercially available di- or trifunctional acrylate monomers, which react with the amine component via an aza-Michael addition. Consequently, this approach is inherently scalable and holds high industrial relevance. In this study, the fundamental applicability of two commodity chemicals—namely 2-hydroxyethyl acrylate (HEA) and 2-hydroxyethyl methacrylate (HEMA)—for this purpose is investigated, aiming to provide an additional handle to mitigate the rapid viscosity increase of the formulations. Using a model epoxy resin consisting of bisphenol A diglycidyl ether (DGEBA) and 1,3-bis(aminomethyl)cyclohexane (BAC), it was demonstrated that a Lewis-base catalyst (1-methylimidazole) is necessary to incorporate the hydroxy groups of HEA and HEMA into the network. Contrary to expectations, this incorporation proceeds predominantly through a condensation reaction that liberates ethylene glycol. Finally, a formulation consisting of 1 equiv. DGEBA, 0.5 equiv. BAC, 1 equiv. HEA, and 0.025 equiv. 1-methylimidazole was found to offer a good compromise, providing both satisfactory reprocessability and a sufficiently high glass transition temperature (74 °C). Compared to a reference formulation made with a trifunctional acrylate monomer, the CAN made with HEA is characterized by a lower glass transition temperature, a similar flow activation energy, a lower storage modulus, and distinctly longer relaxation times. Both acrylate-based CAN materials aged under thermal stress, which resulted in higher storage moduli and glass transition temperatures upon reprocessing. A protocol for characterizing such modulus changes under thermal stress is suggested, consisting of performing repeated frequency sweeps for at least 1 h at temperatures slightly exceeding the maximum temperature of the stress relaxation measurements.
items.authors: Johanna Lang, Christian Slugovc

items.title: Atomic-Scale Insights into the Surface Chemistry, Surface Stability, and Floatability of Spodumene and Montebrasite with Fatty Acid Collectors
items.abstract: Spodumene and montebrasite are minerals that contain significant quantities of lithium and are often found together in phosphate-rich lithium pegmatites. Separating these two minerals by flotation is key to efficient downstream lithium extraction from each. Understanding the crystal and surface properties of both minerals is an important step towards their separation by flotation. We present a systematic study of the surface properties of spodumene and montebrasite, and their interactions with fatty acid collectors, using density functional theory calculations. Our results showed that, for montebrasite, the most dominant surfaces were (110) ≈ (012̅) (102̅) (12̅0) (212̅), with (110) ≈ (012̅) being the most represented (56 %). The Al-terminated (110) surface was the dominant surface on spodumene, accounting for 70 % of the crystal surface area, followed by (111̅) (111) (101̅) (001), consistent with available experimental data. The Wulff equilibrium morphology showed that both minerals are elongated/prismatic, consistent with their naturally occurring crystals, but spodumene is less reactive to flotation reagents than montebrasite. Surface electronic density of states showed that Li and Al states dominate the bottom of the conduction band of spodumene (110) and montebrasite (110) and are available to hybridize with oxygen states of the COO- functional group of fatty acid collectors. Energetics calculations show that both minerals interact with fatty acid collectors via surface Al and Li, but more strongly for montebrasite than spodumene (–18.6 kcal/mol vs +11.05 kcal/mol). Therefore, montebrasite is more floatable with fatty acid collectors than spodumene, making it convenient to separate these two minerals by first recovering montebrasite to the flotation concentrate, resulting in a spodumene-enriched tailings product. Less favorable adsorption energies explain the need to activate/pretreat spodumene before flotation to overcome the energy barrier for fatty-acid adsorption, with spodumene activation by high-density conditioning performed only after montebrasite flotation. This study further demonstrates that the interaction energy of fatty acids with mineral surfaces does not depend on chain length, regardless of mineral type. Our findings open a new direction for efficient lithium production from phosphate-rich lithium pegmatites by generating a montebrasite concentrate while simultaneously upgrading the feed to the spodumene flotation circuit.
items.authors: Espoir M. Murhula, Charlotte E. Gibson, Wennie Wang, Lebogang Babedi, Jing Lian Ng, Suk Gyu Lim

items.title: Application-Specific Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis of Source-Optimized Nanoparticle Textile Formulations: Trade-offs in Washing Durability, Antibacterial Performance, and Laboratory-Scale Raw-Material Cost
items.abstract: Nanoparticle-functionalized textiles offer antibacterial and self-cleaning functions, but their practical suitability is difficult to compare because laundering protocols, reported performance measures, and formulation costs vary across studies. This study develops an application-specific multi-criteria decision-analysis framework using harmonized secondary data from eight source-optimized TiO2-, ZnO-, Ag-, and hybrid-based textile formulations under a school sports-bib scenario. Washing durability and laboratory-scale raw-material cost were evaluated for all eight formulations, while antibacterial performance was included for the six formulations with sufficiently comparable data. Laundering results were converted to a common ten-reference-wash horizon, normalized criterion scores were evaluated across the full feasible weight space, and targeted sensitivity analyses examined uncertainty arising from washing normalization, incomplete Ag laundering conditions, sparse ZnO evidence, and possible cost underestimation. Under baseline conditions, Hybrid ZnO-TiO2 applied by padding-squeezing and Ag deposited through two-step grafting and reduction formed the Pareto frontier in both the two-and three-criterion models. The hybrid formulation was preferred under cost-oriented priorities, whereas the Ag formulation was favored when durability or antibacterial performance received greater weight. This principal decision structure remained stable across the tested uncertainty scenarios. In the Ag-excluded metal-oxide subset, Hybrid Padding-Squeezing remained the budget-sensitive option, while Hybrid In-Situ became more competitive when performance was prioritized. Substantial within-material variation indicated that formulation and deposition route were important sources of practical performance variation within the selected dataset. The framework provides a transparent method for translating heterogeneous published textile data into conditional, application-specific formulation decisions.
items.authors: Yunfei Li

items.title: Photochemical Aminomethylation of C(sp 3 )–H Bonds via Hydrogen Atom Transfer
items.abstract: Direct installation of an aminomethyl group onto aliphatic C–H bonds provides an attractive route to valuable amine-containing building blocks but remains challenging with conventional polar approaches. Here, we report a photochemical aminomethylation of C(sp3)–H bonds enabled by hydrogen atom transfer (HAT). Photoexcited benzophenone directly abstracts hydrogen from αamino, α-oxy, and α-thio C–H bonds, generating carbon-centered radicals that are intercepted by an in situ-formed N-protected formimine. This strategy provides direct access to protected vicinal diamines, amino alcohol derivatives, and related aminomethylated products without requiring prefunctionalization of the C–H donor. Notably, the C–H substrate can be employed as the limiting reagent, while selective radical generation suppresses overfunctionalization. Translation to continuous flow reduces reaction times from 20 h to 3 h, while improving yields for the investigated substrates, and enables scalable synthesis. Subsequent deprotection and functionalization further demonstrate the synthetic utility of the resulting aminomethylated products.
items.authors: Merve Akdeniz, Lorenzo Di Terlizzi, Jonas Djossou, Timothy Noel

items.title: Zwitterionic Acyl Anion Equivalents from Carboxylic Acids via Acylsulfonylhydrazides: A Practical Organocatalytic Umpolung
items.abstract: The development of mild and practical acyl anion equivalents remains a cornerstone challenge in modern organic synthesis, as traditional umpolung strategies often rely on moisture-sensitive reagents, strong bases, or specialized N-heterocyclic carbene catalysts. Here we report that readily available N,N-acylsulfonylhydrazides serve as efficient acyl anion surrogates under operationally simple organocatalytic conditions. Using DMAP as a nucleophilic catalyst, these stable hydrazide precursors readily provide acylation products of a wide range of carbon electrophiles, including aromatic and aliphatic aldehydes, activated ketones, olefins, and imines. Mechanistic investigations, supported by DFT calculations and HRMS analysis, reveal an unconventional pathway wherein DMAP adds to the acyldiazene intermediate, triggering nitrogen extrusion and generating a zwitterionic nucleophile. This dual role of DMAP in enhancing both the stability and nucleophilicity of the reactive species circumvents the hydroxycarbene rearrangement pathway, offering a practical and scalable alternative to existing acyl anion methodologies.
items.authors: Matvey K. Ilyushchenko, Rinat F. Salikov, Yury V. Tomilov

items.title: Direct Mechanochemical Aryl Amination of Polystyrene for Creep Resistant Imine Elastomers
items.abstract: Imine-based covalent adaptable networks (CANs) hold promise for the development of recyclable thermoset materials, but due to low barriers for dynamic exchange, such networks typically suffer from significant material creep. Incorporating linear polymers into imine CANs can improve creep resistance by introducing physical crosslinks, while reactive variants further mitigate through chemical crosslinks. Herein, we directly aminate polystyrene (up to 1.1 mol%) using ball mill grinding mechanochemistry with liquid-assisted grinding for inclusion into dynamic materials. This post-polymerization modification technique allows us to avoid excess solvent while preserving high molar mass. Incorporating aminated PS (aPS) in representative polyimine elastomers enhances creep resistance relative to unmodified PS, while generally maintaining comparable mechanical properties. These findings establish waste PS grafted with low densities of reactive primary amines as an effective additive for improving deformation resistance in polyimines, thus offering a route to give post-consumer plastic waste renewed value.
items.authors: Morgan Skala, Adelle Koenig, Gabriel Soto, Matthew Golder

items.title: A bipartite quantum-acoustic architecture stabilizes multi-exciton solitons at 323 K
items.abstract: A fundamental thermal paradox has constrained the physical viability of quantum coherent Davydov solitons in protein α-helices for over 50 years. At 323 K (0.0278 eV), ambient thermal noise disrupts the localized amide I self-trapping resonance, rapidly scattering multi-quanta excitations into delocalized thermal states on femtosecond timescales. A non-equilibrium, bipartite quantum-acoustic stabilization matrix resolves this long-standing decoherence gap by inducing a transverse acoustic viscoelastic phonon gap, extending exciton coherence lifetimes from 6.5 fs to 42.6 fs—a pre-thermalization window sufficient to outpace non-radiative dissipation and electrostatically prime catalytic interfaces prior to microsecond motor stepping. Utilizing non-Markovian open quantum system simulations, we demonstrate that a highly polarizable variable-dipole linactant at the lipid raft interface induces localized electrodynamic Stark defects, breaking lattice translation symmetry to anchor the wave packet. Sustaining this protective boundary against passive diffusive loss mandates a strict kinetic equilibrium that arrests uncoupled proton leaks, directly coupling the continuous, hydrogen-bonded α-helices of eukaryotic F/V-type rotary c-rings to a hyper-rigid viscoelastic membrane locked in a far-from-equilibrium state. Finally, we present a definitive pathway to bypass thermal decoherence by establishing three physical boundary conditions to translate these biological principles into a predictive blueprint for synthetic quantum-acoustic metamaterials.
items.authors: Doris Loh, Russel J. Reiter

items.title: FoldX interface ΔΔG depends on which structure it starts from, and a learned predictor does not: a cautionary analysis on glutaryl-CoA dehydrogenase
items.abstract: FoldX and related methods are widely used to interpret missense variants, and their sensitivity to the input structure is documented: repair of the coordinates is mandatory, averaging over structural ensembles improves agreement with experiment, and the uncertainty of a FoldX folding ΔΔG has been put at roughly ±3 kcal/mol, with binding stability worse. What has not been asked is whether that uncertainty is spread evenly over a protein. We took 258 ClinVar missense variants in glutaryl-CoA dehydrogenase, a homotetramer, verified every reference residue against the 1SIQ structure and computed ΔΔG for the 124 classified pathogenic. Eighteen variants were then recomputed on three molecular dynamics snapshots of the same complex: six interface variants selected on their monomer-to-tetramer difference, six interface variants drawn at random, and six at least 10 Å from any contact. The displacement between the crystal-based value and the relaxed-frame mean had a median of 1.10, 1.38 and 0.20 kcal/mol in the three groups (random interface against distant, Mann-Whitney p = 0.0130), while frame-to-frame scatter was indistinguishable between them (Kruskal-Wallis p = 0.385). The variation is therefore positional, and it is not explained by noise in the mean. SAAMBE-3D, a learned interface predictor, run on the same eighteen variants and the same four structures, moved by a median of 0.075 kcal/mol at the interface and by nothing at all away from it, so the instability is largely a property of FoldX. It also depends on magnitude: G171R, scored at +22.53 kcal/mol, moved 2.7%, whereas A421V moved from +0.18 kcal/mol, which reads as tolerated, to +4.37 ± 2.22. Along the way we found that ThermoMPNN given a chain selector on a tetramer returns values identical to the isolated monomer at all 7,800 scanned positions. For variant interpretation the consequence is specific: at a subunit interface, in the range where a classification is actually in doubt, a single starting structure does not support a single number.
items.authors: Cumhur Gökhan Ekmekci, Ceren Aleyna Cengiz

items.title: From MOF to polyMOF: Incorporation of Poly(itaconic acid) into a Cu-Ellagate Framework
items.abstract: The incorporation of flexible coordinating polymers into crystalline metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) remains challenging because the conformational freedom of macromolecular ligands can interfere with the development of long-range order. Here, we report IEF-35(Cu), a new Cu–ellagate MOF whose crystal structure was resolved by electron diffraction, and its extension to a polymer-containing framework, PolyIEF-35(Cu), through the incorporation of poly(itaconic acid) (PIA) as a co-ligand. The resulting hybrid retained the characteristic features of the parent framework while displaying pronounced changes in particle morphology and gas sorption. Variation of the ellagic acid (EA) to PIA ratio showed that the crystalline hybrid could be obtained over a relatively broad compositional range. Both materials retained their crystallinity upon heating up to 250 °C and exhibited substantial stability toward the investigated solvents. Finally, biological studies showed cytocompatibility under the investigated conditions and antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus epidermidis .
items.authors: Catalina Biglione, Sergio Carrasco, Álvaro Menendez-Romero, Arianna Melillo, Laura Albentosa-González, Claire Wilson

items.title: 3D DLP Printing of Multi-Responsive Cellulose Derivatives with Tunable Structural Color
items.abstract: Polymer systems exhibiting structural color represent a promising class of materials for 3D printing due to their capability to adapt their properties in response to external stimuli. Hydroxypropyl cellulose (HPC) stands out for its ability to form cholesteric liquid crystalline phases that exhibit vivid structural colors. In this work, we introduce a digital light processing strategy to fabricate complex 3D structures with tunable, stimuli-responsive structural color using methacrylated HPC (HPC-MA). By formulating an aqueous ink system containing 58 to 70 wt% HPC-MA and establishing a pre-print equilibration protocol, cholesteric order is developed and covalently locked into the printed architecture via photopolymerization. The resulting 3D printed structures display bright, iridescent structural colors, tunable within the entire visible spectrum. The thermoresponsive properties of the printed structures are investigated both in a dried and a water-swollen state. Notably, the thermochromic behavior exhibits opposing trends in both environments with increasing temperature inducing a redshift in the dry state but a blueshift in the aqueous state. Finally, we demonstrate the practical utility of this approach in zero-power visual humidity sensing and biomimetic adaptive camouflage. The integration of structural color, stimuli-responsiveness, and 3D geometric freedom opens avenues towards next-generation 4D printing, adaptive materials, and autonomous sensing.
items.authors: Jana L. Lohmann, Lilliana Flórido Martins, Eva Blasco

items.title: Gold nanofibers as scaffolds for neuron differentiation in a 3D microtissue
items.abstract: Engineering neuronal tissues requires biomaterials that provide structural support while actively directing cell fate. Here, high-aspect-ratio gold nanofibers are explored as bioinstructive scaffolds for neuronal organization and differentiation. In a 2.5D paper-based model, the nanofibers guide Neuro-2a cell organization and promote neurite-like extensions through topographical interactions. Building on these findings, a printable composite bioink comprising a gelatin/alginate liquid phase and gelatin microstrands is fabricated. The resulting inks exhibit shear-thinning behavior, rapid structural recovery, and sufficient mechanical stability for extrusion-based 3D bioprinting. Incorporation of SH-SY5Y cells generates viable and proliferative progenitor microtissues, with increasing gelatin microstrand content favoring neuronal-like morphologies. Integration of the gold nanofibers further enhances neuronal differentiation, as supported by cell morphology, immunostaining, and expression of neuronal markers, with differentiation occurring even in the absence of retinoic acid, a common chemical differentiation factor. Spatial separation of the gold nanofibers from the cells reduces this effect, highlighting the importance of direct cell-material interactions. Together, these results establish high-aspect-ratio gold nanofibers provide structural cues capable of promoting neuronal differentiation within 3D bioprinted tissues and provide a strategy for engineering neuron-like microtissues without relying exclusively on chemical differentiation agents.
items.authors: Stefan Stojilkovic, Paula de Dios Andres, Stephany Beyerstedt, Marina Grau Oriols, Malene K. Louw-Christensen, Miguel Alexandre Ramos-Docampo

items.title: Catalytic C–O Bond Cleavage of Vinyl Ethers via Dehydrovinylation and Tandem Tishchenko Coupling
items.abstract: The cleavage of ether C–O bonds by transition-metal complexes has attracted considerable attention, but catalytic cleavage of vinyl ether C(sp²)–O bonds is largely unexplored. Herein we report the dehydrovinylation of alkyl vinyl ethers catalyzed by a pincer-ligated osmium complex. Primary alkyl vinyl ethers undergo C–O bond cleavage to afford ethylene and the corresponding aldehydes, which undergo tandem Tishchenko coupling to yield esters. Secondary alkyl vinyl ethers undergo dehydrovinylation to afford ethylene and ketones. Experimental observations and density functional theory calculations support a mechanism involving insertion of the vinyl ether C=C bond into an Os–H bond, followed by β-alkoxy elimination and β-hydride elimination to form the carbonyl product. These results establish a new mode of catalytic C(sp²)–O bond cleavage and demonstrate its application in a tandem dehydrovinylation–Tishchenko transformation.
items.authors: Ashish Parihar, Soham Chakraborty, Santanu Malakar, Alan S. Goldman

items.title: Diverse Remote Difunctionalization of Enyne-type Propargylic Carbonates: Regio-, Chemo-, and Stereoselective Access to Highly Functionalized Multisubstituted 1,3-Dienes
items.abstract: Herein, we report the first catalytic heterodifunctionalization and homodifunctionalization of readily available 1-substituted enyne-type propargylic derivatives, proceeding via a multicomponent remote C2,C5-addition/substitution pathway. This palladium-catalyzed protocol enables the modular and straightforward assembly of tri-, tetra-, and penta-substituted 1,3-dienes with diverse functional groups from two heteroatom nucleophiles or one heteroatom nucleophile and one carbon nucleophile. The reaction exhibits high chemo-, regio-, and stereoselectivity, accommodates a broad spectrum of O-, N-, S-, and C-nucleophiles, and delivers highly substituted (Z, E)-1,3-dienes with precise stereocontrol. Notably, switching from O- to S-nucleophiles triggers a nucleophile-directed stereodivergence. The synthetic utility is further demonstrated through diverse downstream transformations, efficient synthesis of bioactive molecules, and late-stage functionalization of natural products. Mechanistic studies reveal the involvement of heteroatom-containing pentacoordinate π-allyl palladium and π-alkynyl palladium intermediates in this heterodifunctionalization process.
items.authors: Shan Wang, Ming Jiang, Yifei Zheng, Gengchen Li, Yubin Lin, Long Li

items.title: Direct-Write Printing of Freestanding Prussian Blue Analogue Fibers with Tunable Redox Potentials
items.abstract: Prussian blue (PB) and its analogues (PBAs) are attractive electrode materials for energy storage because of their chemical tunability, open-framework structures, fast ion transport, and rich redox chemistry. Yet, their practical implementation remains limited due to the challenging processability and the discrete set of redox potentials accessible through conventional compositions. Here, a 3D flow-focusing microfluidic strategy is used for directly synthesizing and printing freestanding PB and PBA composite fibers in a single step, coupling particle formation with their integration into an alginate/carbon-nanotube matrix. The method yields continuous, self-supporting fibers incorporating PB and multiple PBAs (Co, Ni, Cu, Zn), which can be directly written into functional electrode architectures and assembled into working energy storage cells. Beyond processability, the platform enables two complementary routes for voltage design: high-entropy PBAs, which access redox responses distinct from those of conventional single-metal PBAs, and spatially encoded fibers in which different PBAs are integrated within one fiber to generate intermediate and deliberately tuned electrochemical behavior. By exploiting the inherent spatial and temporal control afforded by microfluidic flow focusing, the approach establishes a versatile route toward printed, application-tailored PB and PBA electrodes with programmable operating voltages.
items.authors: Anh Tuan Ngo, João Pedro Vale, Maria Pinto, Salvador Pané, Tiago Sotto Mayor, Mario Palacios Corella

items.title: An alternative equation for effective nuclear charge that is applicable to all atoms
items.abstract: Although the advent of ionization energies predated Slater’s rule, there was unawareness of the utilitarian value of the former for the computation of effective nuclear charge (ENC for short) until recently and in this research. The study aimed to derive another equation in which the average ionization energies of hydrogen and any other multielectron atom are independent variables. The objective was to answer the question in the literature that states, "Are Slater’s Rules the Best Approach for Calculating Effective Nuclear Charge for Undergraduates?" (Moore Birnbaum, 2014) and compare the graphical portrayal of chemical periodicity between outcomes using data generated using Slater's rules for some elements and data generated in this research. By exploring theoretical and computational methods and the data in the literature, the study showed that ENC (1.34458-3.32446) for the first 30 elements computed using the 2021 CODATA fine structure constant (FSC, for short) was higher than those (1.34402-3.32309) without it; however, the equation containing the computed FSC using e^2/20hc and other equations gave the same value of ENC. The use of Slater’s result (atomic radii) for the computation of ENC (1.29859-5.06996) and average ionization energy, IE (553.21-2108.13 kJ), gave higher values than other methods. All plots using Slater’s values of ENC and IE versus atomic number (Z) did not show chemical periodicity (greater linearity), unlike the use of other values (less linearity or lower R^2). The use of Slater’s result (atomic radii) for the computation of ENC (1.29859-5.06996) and average ionization energy, IE (553.21-2108.13 kJ), gave higher values than other methods. All plots using Slater’s values of ENC and IE versus Z did not show chemical periodicity (greater linearity), unlike the use of other values (less linearity or lower R^2). The new equation was derived, and with earlier equations, ENC can be accurately computed; they should therefore be part of the school curriculum at all levels without ceasing to teach Slater’s rule, which is not the best approach. A future study should include 30 other elements of the periodic table.
items.authors: Ikechukwu Iloh Udema

items.title: Unleashing AI for preclinical drug development
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping preclinical drug development across target discovery, therapeutic design, synthesis, functional characterization and safety assessment. In this review, we present an integrated view of AI across the preclinical pipeline, beginning with target identification, modality selection and representation learning for molecular, protein, structural, cellular and multimodal data. We then examine major generative modeling paradigms including autoregressive, latent-variable, diffusion, flow-based and guided approaches and their applications across small molecules, peptides, enzymes, antibodies, Tcell receptors and mRNA therapeutics. We discuss how these methods support de novo design, structure- and pocket-conditioned generation, sequence–structure co-design, affinity and activity optimization, developability engineering and synthesis-aware discovery. We further review AI-enabled retrosynthesis, reaction prediction and closed-loop experimental optimization, emphasizing the distinction between computational synthesizability and experimentally executable chemistry. Beyond molecular generation, we organize functional prediction from binding and kinetics through target engagement, pharmacological activity, mechanism of action, pathway response and phenotypic outcome. We also examine singlecell perturbation modeling, organoid-based drug-response prediction, toxicity and off-target assessment, and prospective validation across therapeutic modalities. Across these areas, we highlight the importance of uncertainty estimation, out-of-distribution generalization, reproducibility and experimentally grounded benchmarking. Finally, we discuss how integrating generative AI, mechanistic biology and iterative design–make–test–analyze cycles could transform AI from isolated predictive tools into decision-support systems for preclinical drug development.
items.authors: Himansu Kumar, Yankai Yu, Zhengxiao Yang, Bowen Wang, Xi Hu, Haixia Xu

items.title: Probing Oxygen Transport in β-Cyclodextrin–Cyclohexane Crystal Nanochannels by Luminescence Quenching from Nanoseconds to Seconds
items.abstract: Molecular transport in nanochannels can deviate from normal diffusion and exhibit different regimes depending on the observation timescale. However, resolving them from nanoseconds to seconds remains challenging. Here, oxygen transport in β -cyclodextrin–cyclohexane supramolecular crystals containing solvent-filled nanochannels is probed using room-temperature phosphorescence and fluorescence of aromatic luminophores. Their emission lifetimes, ranging from approximately 50 ns to 15 s, provide intrinsic time windows spanning more than eight orders of magnitude. Comparison of fluorescence and phosphorescence quenching for the same guests provides an internal control for probe identity. The effective bimolecular quenching rate constants decrease by approximately five orders of magnitude. Between approximately 50 ns and 10 ms, the dependence follows a power law, k q ∝ τ 0 -0.8 , followed by a nearly lifetime-independent plateau. The theory of diffusion-controlled reactions relates this dependence to the time-dependent oxygen flux and indicates subdiffusive transport at intermediate times with an effective anomalous exponent of approximately 0.4. A random-barrier model with quenched disorder provides a physical interpretation of this regime and its crossover to normal transport at long times. Thus, molecular excited states with different emission lifetimes enable luminescence quenching to resolve distinct temporal regimes of molecular transport under nanoscale confinement.
items.authors: Denis E. Makhrov, Irina V. Ionova, Alexander A. Korlyukov, Alexander D. Volodin, Georgy A. Yurasik, Mikhail V. Alfimov

items.title: Memory-Augmented Generative Design of Octahedral Co(II) Complexes with Targeted Zero-Field Splitting
items.abstract: The discovery of coordination complexes with targeted magnetic anisotropy remains challenging because the enormous chemical space of ligands and coordination environments makes propertydirected molecular design difficult to achieve by conventional screening. Here, we introduce a memoryaugmented generative framework for the inverse design of octahedral Co(II) complexes with targeted zero-field splitting (ZFS). A chemically curated dataset of ~6000 Co(II) complexes, was used to establish a broad electronic-structure landscape spanning positive and negative ZFS regimes. Building on this chemical space, a generative strategy was developed in which ligand structures are iteratively mutated, recombined, and selected according to their predicted magnetic properties, while an elitememory mechanism preserves high-performing molecular motifs and guides subsequent generations toward increasingly favorable candidates. This enables targeted exploration of ligand combinations and coordination environments associated with large negative ZFS while simultaneously controlling rhombicity. The generated complexes were subjected to independent CASSCF calculations, including spin–orbit coupling, to directly validate their magnetic properties. Notably, the generative framework identified candidates with strongly enhanced axial anisotropy, including a representative complex exhibiting D ≈ −223 cm-1 after ab initio validation. The validated candidates reproduced the targeted ZFS with deviations of approximately 15–18 cm-1. These results establish a generative, memory-guided route from ligand design to electronically validated magnetic complexes, providing a practical strategy for discovering previously unexplored Co(II) molecular magnets and advancing molecular-magnet design from screening toward property-directed generation.
items.authors: Rajanikanta Rana, Aditya Choudhary, Abhijeet Biswas, Subodh Bhalchandra Rawool, Gopalan Rajaraman

items.title: Probing Benzoxazine Dimer Formation Using Methyl-Blocked Derivatives as Mechanistic Probes
items.abstract: The early-stage dimer formation of 1,3-benzoxazine (PH-a) was investigated as a diagnostic system for understanding the ring-opening polymerization (ROP) mechanism using a coupled FAIMS-IRMPD-MS/MS platform. High-field asymmetric waveform ion mobility spectrometry (FAIMS) resolved the protonated PH-a dimer into three distinct populations. A series of methyl-blocked benzoxazine derivatives was used to systematically eliminate individual reactive sites and assign each FAIMS population to a specific reaction route via tandem MS fragmentation patterns and IRMPD action spectroscopy, supported by theoretical vibrational spectra obtained by DFT calculations. Four dimer formation pathways were confirmed: phenolic aromatic substitution at the ortho and para positions, and arylamine aromatic substitution at the ortho and para positions of the aniline ring. Phenoxy- and nitrogen-mediated attack routes were not observed. Each pathway yields dimers in either a closed-ring (CRB) or open-ring (ROP) form, a structural duality with direct implications for the crosslinking topology and network heterogeneity of the resulting polybenzoxazine.
items.authors: Rayan C. Gomes, Francisco W. M. Ribeiro, Thiago C. Correra

items.title: Bio-derived ionic conductive Guar Gum hydrogels as distributed circuit elements for analogue signal processing: the case of Resistor-Capacitor filters
items.abstract: Developing functional electronic materials from renewable resources is a key challenge toward more sustainable electronics. Here, we report on a bio-derived ionic conductive hydrogel based on guar gum and demonstrate its direct integration as a functional circuit element for analogue signal processing. Ionic conductivity is introduced by incorporating sodium chloride into the polysaccharide matrix and systematically tuned through the glycerol and salt contents. Increasing glycerol loading enhances conductivity, while varying NaCl concentration produces a non-monotonic response, with maximum conductivities in the 10-2 S cm-1 range and an optimum salt-loading window. The conductive formulation is subsequently combined with pristine guar gum, used as a dielectric, to fabricate guar gum-based resistor-capacitor elements. Their integration into low-pass and high-pass filters demonstrates frequency-selective operation in the audio range, with cut-off frequencies of 658 and 576 Hz and transition slopes of −17 and +15 dB dec-1, respectively. These results demonstrate that guar gumbased ionic hydrogels can move beyond conventional roles as substrates or electrolytes and directly perform circuit-level functions, providing a simple materials platform for low-frequency analogue electronics.
items.authors: Yeeun Lee, Emilie Jéhanno, Emmanuel Jacques, Anne-Claire Salaün, Fabien Lucas

items.title: Metalsurfer: Fast Generation of Realistic Substrate-Adsorbate Interfaces
items.abstract: Realistic adsorbate–substrate geometries are essential for meaningful electronic-structure calculations at interfaces, yet constructing them remains slow and generally ad hoc for bulky molecules, high coverages, and irregular surfaces. This challenge limits systematic exploration of adsorption configurations across many problems in catalysis, surface chemistry, and materials design. We introduce metalsurfer, a Python package that generates density functional theory (DFT)-ready interface models from simplified molecular input line-entry system (SMILES) strings and a substrate. The workflow combines chemistry-aware, CPU-parallel placement enumeration with TorchSim GPU-batched relaxation under a machine-learned interatomic potential (MLIP), molecular integrity filters, sequential coverage growth, and optional Bayesian acquisition. We demonstrate these capabilities on three chemically distinct systems. For camphor on Cu(111), a ∼1.2 h search recovers neighbors to all eight published weak-adsorption minima and provides a set of plausible basins for refinement. For bipyridine on defected Au(111), offline fixed-batch replays on saved saturation pools show that probability-of-improvement acquisition identifies the first committed motif much faster than random sampling. Transfer from earlier coverage steps also accelerates later searches, with a trust gate that can fall back to a cold model if the prior fails current-step validation. For CO/Pt(111), fixed-coverage n-tuplet searches locate all four ordered adlayers reported in the literature. In each case, a few hours of GPU screening produce a compact shortlist for DFT refinement. metalsurfer thus provides a practical route through the combinatorial problem of interface construction.
items.authors: Jorge Gonzalo, Jorge Felez, Julen Munarriz, Ruben Laplaza

items.title: First-principles analysis of the metal-free H2 dissociation mechanism by semiquinone radicals in mitochondrial Complex I and III
items.authors: Toru Ishibashi, Enjuro Harunari

items.title: Group-aware validation sharply reduces the apparent accuracy of extraction-category classification in public cannabis laboratory data
items.abstract: Published models that classify cannabis products from cannabinoid and terpene profiles report near-perfect accuracy: above 95% for resin type, 100% for chemovar class. These figures come from random cross-validation or Kennard-Stone partitioning, which hold out no plant, producer or laboratory. We quantify the cost on a task with explicit group structure. On 33,229 public laboratory-result rows for cannabis concentrates that name a producer, nearly all from Nevada, each with a source-declared extraction category (non-solvent against solvent-based), a gradient-boosted classifier scores 78.5% balanced accuracy and a ROC AUC of 0.89 under random five-fold cross-validation. Holding out the producer leaves 54.0% and 0.62. A signal survives: the pooled held-out AUC is 0.61, with a producer-level bootstrap interval of 0.535 to 0.698. But the reported model's pooled balanced accuracy does not separate from chance (51.6%, interval 47.3 to 56.6); it keeps about 30% of its above-chance AUC, and an unweighted logistic regression 41 to 53%. A designed experiment shows the same direction: with the random split averaged over 200 seeds, 162 HPLC-assayed samples fall from 54.3% to 38.9% under leave-one-variety-out with gradient boosting and from 51.8% to 46.3% with logistic regression, against 33.3% chance. In the market data the same profiles identify the producer at 67.1% against a 14.4% baseline and the laboratory at 92.3% against 40.3%. We conclude that the declared extraction category is only weakly recoverable from these analyte panels for an unseen producer, and that a random split overstates it by 8 to 26 points of balanced accuracy depending on the model and subset. We did not rerun the published studies.
items.authors: Arthur Gonçalves Breguez

items.title: MolSanitizer: An open-source pipeline to prepare small-molecule databases for large-scale virtual screening
items.abstract: Accurate preparation of small-molecule databases for virtual screening is crucial for the success of computer-aided drug discovery. Although numerous free software options are available, they often underperform compared to commercial alternatives. Here, we introduce MolSanitizer, an open-source molecular preparation pipeline built on RDKit and designed for large-scale virtual screening. MolSanitizer extends existing open-source functionality through curated, chemical-environment-aware rules for protonation and tautomerization, systematic stereoisomer enumeration, and a dedicated conformer generator that combines knowledge-based structural preferences with stochastic torsional sampling. Our benchmarking results show that MolSanitizer achieves better performance than several free software alternatives while achieving performance levels comparable to commercial software. MolSanitizer features a modular and open-source design, allowing users to easily customize the tool to meet their specific needs. MolSanitizer also generates output files compatible with several widely used molecular docking programs, thereby facilitating a streamlined workflow for users. MolSanitizer is available for free at https://github.com/carlssonlab/MolSanitizer and via a web server at https://carlssonlabtools.icm.uu.se/molsani.
items.authors: Thua-Phong Lam, Szymon Pach, Philip Ullmann, Hocine El Khaoudi Enyoury, Ruth Brenk, Flavio Ballante

items.title: Structural Convergence of MD simulations on RNA Motifs: A tRNA case study
items.abstract: A detailed understanding of the structural dynamics of diverse RNA architectures is critical for elucidating the chemical basis of cellular function and expanding the use of RNA in medicine and biotechnology. While classical molecular dynamics (MD) simulations can provide this much-needed atomic information, sampling requirements remain poorly characterized for RNA systems. In the present study, we compared the conformational ensemble sampled by five independent 5 μs trajectories and 60 independent 500 ns replicas for unmodified Escherichia coli tRNAPhe under three (monovalent, crystallographic-Mg2+, and 6 Mg2+) environmental conditions, yielding 165 μs of aggregate sampling. Although the global L-shaped tRNA fold was retained across all simulations, structural convergence was strongly motif-dependent. Mean base-pair and base-step descriptors of the rigid acceptor and anticodon stem-loop duplex regions were reproduced with modest replication across metal environments. In contrast, the dynamic anticodon loop exhibited substantial trajectory-to-trajectory heterogeneity. A stacking-based analysis identified diverse loop conformations with counterparts in experimentally determined tRNA structures, showing that ensembles of independent classical MD replicas can sample diverse experimentally observed conformations without enhanced sampling. While fewer long trajectories incompletely sampled the heterogeneous loop conformational space, ensembles of many shorter replicas are key to exploring the conformational dynamics of RNA motifs like hairpins. Inclusion of Mg2+ also shifted the sampled conformational ensemble, underscoring the importance of mimicking the experimentally-relevant ionic environment. Overall, our findings offer practical guidelines for MD simulation setup, including trajectory length, replica number, and divalent ion conditions, for studies of RNA systems featuring similar tertiary architectures.
items.authors: Austin Pounder, Mark J. Lea, Umer Yaqoob, Zaki Olvis, Cynthia Fonderson, Ute Kothe

items.title: Automated Extraction and FAIRification of Chemical Structures from Scientific Publications
items.abstract: Chemical structures are published predominantly as images, which makes them inaccessible for database indexing, structure-based search and computational reuse. While Optical Chemical Structure Recognition and PDF-extraction tools attempt post-publication recovery, they cannot restore the information lost during image rendering. To address this, we present BChemXtract, an open-source Java library that extracts chemical structures directly from the CDX and CDXML files that authors already submit with their manuscripts. BChemXtract parses the CDX object hierarchy to isolate chemical fragments from graphical annotations and expands abbreviations using a community-curated lookup table. The structures are then converted via the Chemistry Development Kit into standard machine-readable formats. BChemXtract is integrated into the production workflow of the Beilstein Journals, where extracted structures are manually validated before being embedded in article metadata as Schema.org JSON-LD, deposited in PubChem and offered for download. Applied to the 2993 ChemDraw figures and schemes of volume 20 of the Beilstein Journal of Organic Chemistry, it yielded 23,320 structures with InChIs in under two minutes. On a 225-file benchmark corpus, it generated valid InChIs for 98.2% of extracted unique substances, compared with 14.2% for Open Babel, at comparable per-file speed. BChemXtract makes published chemistry FAIR at the point of publication without altering author workflows. It is available under the MIT license together with a web application and the benchmark corpus.
items.authors: Felix Bänsch, Kohulan Rajan, Markus Nietfeld

items.title: Indium-Catalyzed Deaminative Coupling of Propargylamines with Terminal Alkynes: A Mild Approach to Conjugated 1,3-Dienones
items.abstract: A mild and efficient indium-catalyzed coupling of propargylamines with terminal alkynes has been developed, affording a diverse array of conjugated 1,3-dienones in good to excellent yields. The reaction proceeds via in situ hydrolysis of propargylamines to generate the corresponding enones, followed by an indium(III)-promoted syn-selective alkyne insertion. Using InCl3 as the catalyst and DBU as the base, the protocol features broad functional-group tolerance and operates under mild conditions. Mechanistic investigations indicate that indium activation is crucial for facilitating the addition of alkynes to enones, enabling selective construction of conjugated 1,3-dienones frameworks. This transformation represents a rare example of indium-catalyzed C–C bond formation and provides a practical and versatile approach to structurally diverse 1,3-dienones from readily available propargylamine precursors.
items.authors: Yujuan Xie, Liliang Huang, Huangdi Feng, Erik V. Van der Eycken

items.title: VISION-BASED DRY-MATERIAL INVENTORY ESTIMATION IN AUTONOMOUS LABORATORIES: RGB SEGMENTATION VERSUS RGB-D SURFACE RECONSTRUCTION
items.abstract: Reliable dry-material inventory monitoring is needed for autonomous laboratory operation, but the suitability of a non-contact method depends on material behaviour, optical access, calibration requirements and the quantity to be estimated. We compared two vision-based approaches—material-specific RGB/YOLO level estimation and visible-surface reconstruction from an Intel RealSense D405—across three materials (black polypropylene pellets, wood powder, and microcrystalline cellulose fine powder) in small transparent laboratory tubes representative of common dosing instruments, with the aim of informing a practical, evidence-based framework for choosing between such methods in laboratory automation and similar industrial contexts. Software-coordinated records linked the two camera channels to a nominal mass-fraction inventory reference and a manual-height baseline. Across six runs and 133 paired, reference-eligible material states, D405 achieved lower error than YOLO in every run (mean absolute error of 3.26 vs. 7.14 percentage points), though YOLO offered higher valid-result coverage (97.2% vs. 95.1%). Both methods showed increased error under repeated surface disturbance, with YOLO degrading more sharply than D405. An exploratory correction fitted using the first observation at each mass level substantially improved YOLO but did not surpass D405’s uncorrected accuracy, while a single global correction worsened both methods—indicating that simple corrections do not transfer robustly across conditions. The results support a method-selection framework based on error, availability, viewing geometry, calibration-state representativeness and total resource requirements. Conclusions are limited to the tested materials and setups, and the mass-fraction reference is an operational inventory proxy rather than a direct measurement of true occupied volume.
items.authors: Mostafa Abd Al Kader, Miguel Hernández-del-Valle, Maciej Haranczyk

items.title: Depth-resolved operando grazing-incidence diffraction reveals non-equilibrium Cu-Pt alloy restructuring under glycerol electrooxidation
items.abstract: Alloying Pt with Cu enhances activity towards hydrogen generation and valueadded products during the electrooxidation of glycerol, but the most active alloys typically require electrochemical activation, during which their structure and composition evolve in poorly understood ways. Here we use synchrotron-based operando, angle-dependent grazing incidence X-ray diffraction in a custom dual-chamber electrochemical flow cell to follow, in real time, the depth-resolved structural evolution of Cu-Pt thin-film catalysts under glycerol electrooxidation in alkaline media. Our approach allows us to monitor the temporal evolution of lattice parameter, phase composition and microstrain during cyclic voltammetry and chronoamperometry while varying the X-ray penetration depth from the topmost tens of nanometres into the underlying alloy. For Cu-rich Cu92Pt8 catalysts, we observe substantial restructuring of the near-surface region, including the cyclic formation and reduction of Cu2O, pronounced Cu leaching from depths of several tens of nanometres, and the progressive emergence of a Pt-rich ≈Cu15Pt85 phase that stabilises the surface against further oxidation. These structural changes coincide with a ca. 5-fold increase in current density and a ca. 100 mV increase in onset potential during activation, after which the electrochemical response becomes stable. Pt-richer alloys exhibit markedly reduced restructuring, with compositional changes largely confined to the top ≈20-30 nm of the catalyst. Analysis of peak broadening via Williamson-Hall plots reveals that dealloying and surface oxidation are associated with increased microstrain, which subsequently relaxes as a Pt-rich surface configuration is established. Beyond revealing the non-equilibrium interplay of oxidation, segregation and realloying that governs the performance and durability of Cu-Pt catalysts for glycerol electrooxidation, our methodology and cell design provide a flexible, broadly applicable platform for operando, depth-resolved diffraction studies of electrochemical interfaces in energy and biomass-conversion reactions.
items.authors: Athira Anil, Martin Kapuscinski, Harish Gudla, Prabahar Kuppamuthu, Irina Terekhina, Priyanka Nehla

items.title: Development of A Modeling Framework for Characterizing Protein–Polymer Bioconjugates with Enhanced Sampling Molecular Dynamics Simulations
items.abstract: Protein–polymer bioconjugates represent a class of biomaterials that leverages the molecular specificity of proteins and the tunability of synthetic polymers. Strategic conjugation of polymers to protein surfaces can enhance key biomolecular properties such as structural stability and target affinity while preserving the biological functions of the native protein. The rational design of these hybrid biomolecules demands a detailed understanding of the underlying molecular mechanisms governing protein–polymer interfacial behavior. Critically, strong interfacial interactions can impose substantial energetic barriers that hinder conformational sampling in molecular dynamics (MD) studies of this system. Enhanced sampling methods are highly effective for overcoming such limitations in the simulation of biomolecular interfaces. However, the opportunity to apply enhanced sampling methods toward navigating the complex interfacial landscapes of protein–polymer bioconjugates has yet to be realized by the field. In this study, we showcase the development of a molecular modeling framework that leverages enhanced sampling to extensively characterize protein–polymer bioconjugates. To validate this framework, we constructed two bioconjugate models of hen egg-white lysozyme grafted with activated methoxy polyethylene glycol (mPEG) chains of varying lengths at multiple surface-exposed lysine sites. We then performed all-atom MD simulations of these PEGylated constructs, augmented with well-tempered metadynamics (WTM) to fully explore their conformational landscapes under multi-site polymer conjugation. This approach yielded converged free energy surfaces (FES) characterizing the thermodynamic favorability of grafted mPEG chain conformations at each conjugation site. We also identified key protein contact residues and site-specific non-bonded interactions responsible for bioconjugate stabilization. This study demonstrates a novel application of enhanced sampling methodologies in bioconjugate systems for characterizing site-specific conjugation effects on protein–polymer interfacial energetics and structural dynamics in the context of protein surface chemistry. More broadly, applying this methodological framework across diverse polymer chemistries and protein variants can elucidate molecular design rules for engineering bioconjugates with precise properties and functions for applications spanning biotechnology, energy, and health.
items.authors: Ziyue Dong, Aidan B. Wegner, David Saeb, Matthew M. C. Kwan, Pedro E. Cintrón Baerga, C. Wyatt Shields

items.title: Quantitative Characterization of Pharmaceutical Powder Surface Interactions Using Inverse Gas Chromatography-Derived Surface Energy Profiles
items.abstract: Quantitative characterization of surface and interfacial properties is important for understanding the behavior of pharmaceutical powders, but conventional approaches to powder wettability and surface free energy can be influenced by measurement procedures and sample-specific factors. Inverse gas chromatography (IGC) provides a sensitive approach for characterizing powder surface energetics as a function of fractional surface coverage; however, the reproducibility and interpretation of IGC-derived surface energy profiles require careful evaluation. In this study, the reproducibility of IGC-derived surface energy profiles was examined using pharmaceutical excipients, and the resulting energetic characteristics were compared with wettability measurements obtained using sessile drop and Washburn methods. Surface-energy profiles were further used to calculate thermodynamic work-of-adhesion profiles for powder–water interactions and for drug–excipient systems. Distinct differences in surface-energy profiles were observed among pharmaceutical excipients, including materials with identical nominal chemical compositions but different grades. Drug–excipient work-of-adhesion profiles further demonstrated coverage-dependent differences in calculated interfacial interactions among pharmaceutical materials. The results demonstrate that IGC-derived surface-energy profiles can provide reproducible characterization of pharmaceutical powder surfaces and can be extended to quantitative evaluation of solid–liquid and solid–solid interfacial interactions. These findings support the use of surface-energy profiles as a quantitative framework for characterization of pharmaceutical powders and for comparison of potential interfacial interactions among formulation components.
items.authors: Ken Yoshioka, Kohei Tahara

items.title: Chemically modified hydrogels to improve geothermal reservoir performance by enabling flow control via size-shifting microspheres
items.abstract: Thermal short circuits, where fluids preferentially connect injection and production wells, are a leading cause of premature enthalpy decline in geothermal reservoirs. These pathways accelerate cooling, reduce effective heat transfer area, and limit reservoir lifetime. We propose a temperature-responsive hydrogel microsphere suspension as an “active tracer” that dynamically redirects flow away from cooled short-circuit channels while also tracing fluid flow via fluorescence spectroscopy. Highly idealized reservoir simulations with field-informed permeability distributions indicate that a yieldstress fluid with temperature-responsive behaviors may improve reservoir thermal lifetime by a factor of at least 24 to 59x while maintaining acceptable hydraulic performance. To develop a candidate “active” tracer intended to satisfy the assumptions of the idealized simulations, we synthesized poly(N-isopropylacrylamide) (pNIPA) microgels, characterized their swelling and rheological behavior, and conducted a large-scale laboratory experiment in an analog parallel-plate that demonstrates short-circuited flow behavior. These lab-scale results demonstrate that injected microgels clog cooled short circuits via swelling and diverted flow into hotter regions. This proof-of-concept establishes an attractive pathway for employing engineered materials to actively manage flow and extend geothermal reservoir lifetimes.
items.authors: Aaron M. Baxter, Danni Tang, Bryan H. Abdulaziz, Reeby J. Puthur, Patrick M. Fulton, Sarah Hormozi

items.title: Selective Ligand Replacement Leads to Carbene Complexes as Catalysts in Proteins
items.abstract: Artificial metalloenzymes (ArMs) that incorporate organometallic fragments through direct metal–protein coordination open the door to unlock the full evolutionary potential of the protein scaffold to modulate catalysis. This work builds on our previously published work, in which Ru(II) piano stool complexes bearing bipyridyl ligands were used to deliver [Ru(Arene)]2+ fragments into a naïve protein scaffold, generating a transfer-hydrogenase artificial metalloenzyme. Here we systematically explore Ru(II) piano stool complexes bearing pyridyl–N-heterocyclic carbene (Pyr–NHC) bidentate ligands as active-site precursors for metathases and transfer hydrogenases. In this work we describe the synthesis and characterisation of five novel Ru(II) piano stool complexes bearing a hexamethylbenzene (HMB) arene cap and Pyr–NHC bidentate ligands, in which systematic variation of the NHC wingtip substituent (R′ = Me, Et, iPr, Ph) and the pyridine ring substituent (R = H, F) tunes the steric and electronic properties of the complex. Single-crystal X-ray analysis and electrochemical studies show that the strong σ-donation from the carbene lowers the Ru(II/III) redox potential and elongates the Ru–HMB bond relative to their bipyridyl counterparts. This supports displacement of the arene as opposed to the bidentate ligand in the presence of protein. Systematic comparison between Pyr–NHC and bipyridyl complexes also provided an insight into the influence of the arene and the bidentate ligand on the structural and electrochemical properties of these complexes.
items.authors: Armando Albert Flores, Matthew G. Wheeler, Oskar James Klein, George S. Biggs, Jonathan Shaw, Jonathan Bostock

items.title: Origin of the Difference between Kohn-Sham and ∆SCF Band gaps for Delocalized Electron–Hole Excitations in Hybrid-Functional Supercell Calculations
items.abstract: We examine the relationship between ground-state generalized Kohn–Sham (GKS) band gaps and self-consistent ∆SCF excitation energies for delocalized electron–hole excitations in finite periodic supercells. For a vertical excitation at the undistorted ground-state geometry, these two quantities are expected to coincide when the promoted electron and hole remain Bloch-like. This is mostly true with semilocal functionals, but not with hybrid functionals for which the difference increases linearly with the fraction of exact exchange. The origin of this difference is derived from two equivalent viewpoints: the total-energy change associated with the ∆SCF excitation and the occupation-dependent orbital gap shift arising from the self-consistent potential response. The residual energy arises from the orbital-dependent exact-exchange selfenergy associated with the electron-hole pair and decreases approximately as 1/N
items.authors: Mingxue Fu, Arghya Bhowmik, Juan Maŕıa Garćıa-Lastra

items.title: Earth-abundant 3d metal-catalyzed enantioselective catalysis towards the functionalization of E/Zalkenes mixtures.
items.abstract: Enantioselective catalysis transforming alkenes to chiral molecules have been a breakthrough in the field of organic synthesis. Though a major challenge persists. The “privileged” chiral catalyst capacities depend on the geometry of the olefin substrate which can be either E or Z. Enantioselective catalysis allowing to convert both alkene stereoisomers to a single chiral molecule promises sustainable synthetic routes and novel mechanistic strategies towards chiral molecule synthesis. Enantioselective methods towards the functionalization of E/Z-alkenes, which has largely taken advantages of the recent development of earth-abundant 3d metal catalysis, are covered in this revue. An emphasis on the mechanisms accounting for the observed stereoconvergence and enantioselectivity is proposed.
items.authors: Guillaume Delestras, John Henry Reed, Coralie Duchemin

items.title: Tyr10 Modifications and Peptide Context Rewire GLP-1 Modulation of Amyloid-β42 Assembly
items.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) is best known as a receptor agonist, yet its peptide-level behavior in protein-rich environments remains poorly defined.
