The algorithm employs a fuzzy splitting rule that allows samples to be assigned to both child nodes with certain probabilities, thereby enhancing the model’s fault tolerance. In addition, logistic regression classifiers are incorporated at impure leaf nodes to provide an additional means of separating samples that cannot be perfectly partitioned. Experimental results on two cell line datasets (A375 and A549) demonstrate that the DP-FDT achieves superior performance, particularly in terms of AUC and F1 score, compared with several state-of-the-art oblique decision trees and a deep learning baseline. It also improves recall for minority classes. Ablation studies confirm the positive contributions of its key components. Furthermore, a preliminary bioinformatics analysis provides insights into the biological processes associated with the most influential features identified by the model. Overall, the DP-FDT offers an effective and interpretable approach for analyzing complex drug combination data.
items.authors: Zhenhua Cai, Jin Chen, KunHong Liu

items.title: Climate-Driven Snow Cover Dynamics in the Hindu Kush–Himalayan (HKH) Region and Its Implications for Natural Hazard Modeling Using Multi-Satellite Hydrometeorological Data
items.abstract: Earth’s frozen water reserves are inherently dynamic and play a critical role in the hydrological processes of complex, dynamic river basins. Climate-driven environmental changes have led to a significant decrease in the area and duration of seasonal snow cover, particularly in the high-altitude Asian Water Tower (Himalaya). Snow cover estimates are challenging in the high-altitude Hindu Kush-Himalayan (HKH) region, which is a core contributor to water resources that sustain the environment and diverse downstream ecosystems that support more than half of the Earth’s population. This study quantifies the snow cover area over the period of 1993–2023 across the basins of ten major snow- and rainfall-dominated rivers in the HKH region using Landsat-based Normalized Difference Snow Index (NDSI), SNOMAP, Blue Snow Threshold (BST), and Dozier and Painter methods. Additionally, this study used 178 strategically positioned points across the HKH region to explore the relationship between snow cover dynamics and environmental factors such as temperature, precipitation, and greenhouse gas concentrations. The study observed significant temporal and spatial variations in snow cover, driven by regional climatic conditions and anthropogenic influences. The results revealed declining snow cover trends of 2793.15, 2108.86, 1199.49, 247.51, 230.34, and 169.39 km2/year for the Amu Darya, Indus, Yangtze, Tarim, Mekong, Ganges, and Brahmaputra River basins, respectively. Conversely, the Salween, Yellow, and Irrawaddy River basins showed a slight increase of 1002.66, 147.06, and 20.86 km2/year, respectively. These opposing trends underline the vulnerability of snow mass to water supply and hydropower scheduling, stressing the urgent need for integrated, long-term satellite and ground-based observation platforms, as well as robust hydrological and glaciological modeling. A strategic blend of remotely sensed snow cover data and locally calibrated climate and land-use records will empower decision-makers to predict water security threats and refine reservoir operation guidelines, thereby sustaining both socio-economic and ecosystem services across the principal river corridors.
items.authors: Muhammad Amin, Sikandar Ali, Muhammad Safdar, Taixia Wu, Muhammad Farhan, Moazzam Mushtaq

items.title: Quality Assessment of In-House Prepared Pediatric Oral Suspensions of Bisoprolol and Lisinopril: Assay and Dose Uniformity
items.abstract: Bisoprolol and Lisinopril are among the most frequently used substances in pediatric cardiovascular affections. The medication supply to this age population is limited given the lack of appropriate pharmaceutical forms; therefore, pharmaceutical compounding comes to fill in the gap between pediatric therapy needs and availability of adult-approved formulations. The aim of our study was to obtain and quantify two suspensions of Bisoprolol and Lisinopril in small pediatric dosage. The suspensions were obtained using a commercial suspending vehicle and the active substances. We developed the quality control methods according to the USP. Briefly, both methods were developed and validated using a UHPLC Flexar 10 system (Perkin Elmer) equipped with a Phenomenex Luna C8 column (150 × 4.6 mm, 3 μm) under isocratic conditions at a flow rate of 1 mL/min. For bisoprolol, the mobile phase consisted of water (65:35, v/v) with the specified additives, with detection at 273 nm, while lisinopril was analyzed using 10 mM ammonium formate buffer (pH 5) (96:4, v/v), with detection at 210 nm. The calibration ranges were 30–90 μg/mL for bisoprolol and 20–100 μg/mL for lisinopril. We obtained satisfactory results for method validation, and the method was applied for the assay of two types of suspensions. The obtained results ranged between 80 and 86% of the labeled amounts for Bisoprolol, and 106–108% for Lisinopril. The obtained suspensions reflected some issues related to the sample extraction and potential variability in suspension sampling and dosing consistency, which support the need for continuous optimization and quality control of compounded pediatric formulation.
items.authors: Carmen-Maria Jîtcă, George Jîtcă, Lenard Farczadi, Silvia Imre

items.title: Valorisation of Maclura pomifera Pruning Leaves by Green Crosscurrent Extraction: Process Optimisation, Chemical Profiling, and Preliminary Cytotoxicity Assessment
items.abstract: Urban tree-pruning residues are an underused bioactive resource. This study evaluated a short three-stage crosscurrent process for valorising Maclura pomifera pruning leaves with water and aqueous ethanol. Each stage contacted the preceding residue with fresh solvent and was optimised independently by response surface methodology for temperature, time and, for hydroethanol, ethanol concentration. Responses were total phenolic content (TPC), total flavonoid content (TFC), ABTS radical scavenging, potassium ferricyanide reducing antioxidant power (PFRAP) and silver nanoparticle antioxidant capacity (SNPAC). Extracts from all three optimised stages were pooled per solvent and assessed by UPLC–ESI–MS/MS and for cytotoxicity in four mammalian cell lines. Cumulative TPC reached 21.49 (aqueous) and 23.39 (hydroethanolic) mg gallic acid equivalents/g dry weight, and ABTS reached 52.59 and 49.58 mg ascorbic acid equivalents/g dry weight. Two aqueous stages recovered over 90% of cumulative TPC and ABTS in 15 min. The ethanol-rich third stage contributed 39.2% of cumulative TFC and 28.8% of SNPAC. Hydroethanol favoured flavonoids, whereas water phenolic acids and simple aromatics. Both pooled extracts gave higher IC50 values than ascorbic acid, with the hydroethanolic extract being more cytotoxic. Crosscurrent extraction with water or hydroethanol recovers phenolics rapidly, and staging the ethanol concentration yields compositionally distinct fractions whose suitability for specific applications requires further toxicological evaluation.
items.authors: Mohamed Kherat, Radia Chemlal, Latifa Azzouz, Meriem Moulay-Abdallah, Nabil Mameri

items.title: Deformation Analysis of Rock Mass During the Excavation of a New Tunnel
items.abstract: With the increasing planning and construction of new tunnel routes near existing tunnels, safety hazards and construction problems are receiving increasing attention. To observe the deformation characteristics within the rock mass more intuitively, this paper adopts a transparent rock model test device to carry out the model test of tunnel-proximity excavation. The transparent rock is an artificial transparent material formulated by mixing silica gel powder, n-tridecane, and liquid paraffin. The impacts of the new tunnel on an existing tunnel are investigated, in which the thickness of the intervening rock layer and the excavation footage are the main influencing factors. Results show that when the new tunnel passes over the existing tunnel, heave deformation occurs in the rock mass around the existing tunnel. When it passes under the existing tunnel, the existing tunnel is deformed by settlement. The maximum deformation of the rock mass around the existing tunnel is located at the center of the existing tunnel, and the deformation trough conforms well to a Gaussian distribution curve, with coefficients of determination (R2) of 0.93–0.98. As the excavation footage increases and the thickness of the intervening rock layer decreases, the deformation of the existing tunnel’s rock mass will increase.
items.authors: Qiang Ou, Changlong Yang, Maoyi Liu

items.title: Dynamic Urothelial Remodeling in Diabetic Bladder Dysfunction: Disease-Course Changes, Molecular Mechanisms, and Clinical Implications
items.abstract: Diabetic bladder dysfunction (DBD) includes storage abnormalities and voiding dysfunction, but its clinical and experimental phenotypes do not follow a uniform chronological sequence. The urothelium is a urine barrier and a mechanosensory, paracrine, and inflammatory interface. Early diabetes may cause urothelial shedding, barrier permeability, abnormal ATP release, and altered sensory receptors. With longer disease duration, superficial architecture and some barrier properties may recover, while sensory and paracrine abnormalities persist. In parallel, impaired afferent conduction, reduced detrusor contractility, and extracellular matrix remodeling may become prominent, so local urothelial changes do not necessarily track whole-bladder function. Metabolic and oxidative stress, NLRP3-associated inflammation and pyroptosis, ferroptosis, and epigenetic and post-transcriptional regulation may contribute to urothelial injury, although evidence differs in cell specificity and disease-course localization. This review integrates clinical, animal, and cellular studies to examine urothelial barrier, sensory, paracrine, and cell-fate changes across DBD functional states, appraise the supporting molecular evidence and its limitations, and discuss the clinical relevance of urothelial biomarkers and therapeutic targets.
items.authors: Quan Song, Wanjian Xie, Jing Wang, Yehuan Yuan, Zhi Li, Sisi Sun

items.title: Preparing Future Outstanding Engineers: Multidimensional Structure and Associated Factors of Core Competence
items.abstract: Preparing engineers for rapidly changing sociotechnical environments requires a clear account of the competencies that undergraduate engineering programs should foster. This study used the term future outstanding engineers to refer to engineering undergraduates being prepared for engineering excellence and examined the structure and correlates of their self-reported core competence. Cross-sectional survey data were obtained from 578 engineering undergraduates at a Chinese research university. A reflective–formative higher-order model was estimated using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM); partial least squares multigroup analysis (PLS-MGA) compared grade cohorts; and multiple linear regression examined associations with student background and educational experience. Adaptive, professional, and basic competence formed the higher-order construct, with adaptive competence receiving the largest outer weight. The outer weight of adaptive competence was larger, and that of professional competence smaller, among third-year than first-year students; the outer weight of basic competence did not differ significantly. Selected co-curricular and language-learning experiences were associated with adaptive competence, whereas family background and leadership experience were associated with professional competence. Basic competence was associated with a broader set of student background and engagement variables. These findings support a differentiated, stage-sensitive approach to competence development. Because the data are cross-sectional, self-reported, and drawn from one institution, the results should be interpreted as structural and associational rather than developmental or causal.
items.authors: Jingxuan Wang, Xinqiao Liu

items.title: Formation Mechanisms of Laminae in Continental Shales and Their Controls on Differential Shale Oil Enrichment
items.abstract: Laminae are fundamental structural units of heterogeneity in continental shales and significantly influence organic matter accumulation, hydrocarbon generation and retention, reservoir evolution, fluid redistribution, and fracture propagation. This review critically synthesizes evidence from representative lacustrine shale systems in the Jiyang Depression and Cangdong Sag of the Bohai Bay Basin, as well as the Ordos, Junggar, and Songliao basins, together with selected lacustrine successions worldwide. Lamina development reflects the coupled effects of terrigenous supply, aquatic productivity, authigenic mineral precipitation, hydrodynamic conditions, water-column stratification, and early preservation. Climatic change and astronomical forcing affect these processes indirectly, and their sedimentary expression varies among basins. Depositional heterogeneity is subsequently modified by compaction, cementation, dissolution, mineral transformation, hydrocarbon generation, and fracture development, producing lamina-scale differences in generation, storage, mobility, and mechanical behavior. Available petrographic, geochemical, petrophysical, and experimental evidence indicates that shale oil is dominated by in situ retention, accompanied by conditional short-distance redistribution between adjacent laminae through connected pores, interfaces, and microfractures. However, migration distance, flux, and associated compositional fractionation remain poorly quantified. Accordingly, an evidence-based conceptual framework linking lamina formation, differential hydrocarbon generation, heterogeneous storage, in situ retention and short-distance redistribution, enrichment in favorable units, and fracture connectivity is proposed. This framework integrates processes commonly addressed separately and distinguishes established relationships from basin-specific observations and conceptual interpretations.
items.authors: Yinmei Wang, Shang Xu, Qiyang Gou

items.title: Wire-Guided Percutaneous Drill Osteotomy for Symptomatic Lesser Toe Deformities: A Case Report
items.abstract: Lesser toe malalignment can cause recurrent interdigital skin injury and limit footwear tolerance. We report the clinical course of a 53-year-old man with flexible medial deviation of the left fourth and fifth toes, recurrent pressure lesions, and shoe intolerance despite repeated lesion-directed treatment. Corrective proximal phalangeal osteotomies were performed using a standard orthopaedic drill and fluoroscopy when a dedicated percutaneous burr system was unavailable. A 1.0 mm guidewire was placed from dorsal to plantar, perpendicular to the toe long axis. In both toes, sequential 2.0, 2.7, 3.5, and 4.0 mm drilling was followed by controlled closure around a preserved medial hinge. Retrograde 1.5 mm Kirschner wires maintained correction without metatarsophalangeal joint transfixation and were removed on postoperative day 43. At postoperative day 46, the pressure-related hyperkeratotic lesion had resolved, the reported visual analogue scale pain score was 0, the patient reported tolerating conventional footwear, and alignment was maintained. Radiographs showed interval osseous healing without secondary displacement; no wound, pin-tract, or neurovascular complication was observed. This case documents short-term clinical improvement after an adaptation of available instruments. The brief follow-up and single-patient design preclude conclusions about mature union, durability, overall safety, or comparative effectiveness.
items.authors: Muhammed Yusuf Afacan, Emre Özmen, Oğuzhan Yüksel, Alican Barış
items.category_raw: Journal of the American Podiatric Medical Association

items.title: TMJ Effusion and Anterior Disk Displacement: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
items.abstract: Background: The objective of this study was to assess the association between joint effusion and anterior disk displacement. Specifically, it aimed to determine whether joint effusion is more associated with anterior disk displacement without reduction (ADDWOR) compared with displacement with reduction (ADDWR). Methods: The literature review for this study was conducted using PubMed, Scopus, SciELO, the Virtual Health Library (including LILACS), and The Cochrane Library (Trials and Reviews). Grey literature was also searched, specifically: ClinicalTrials.gov and the International Clinical Trials Registry Platform (ICTRP Search Portal, World Health Organization). The review was conducted according to the PRISMA 2020 statement, and the search strategy followed the PECO (Population, Exposure, Comparison, Outcome) protocol. Study quality was assessed with the Newcastle–Ottawa Scale (cohort studies) and the Joanna Briggs Institute critical appraisal tools (cross-sectional and case–control studies). All raw event counts were independently re-extracted and cross-checked against the original source tables for every included study, and a design-effect sensitivity analysis was performed to explore the potential impact of the non-independence of bilaterally assessed joints. Results: Seventeen studies were included, comprising 4254 temporomandibular joint (TMJ)-level observations (2256 ADDWOR joints, 1998 ADDWR joints) from approximately 2980 patients. The meta-analysis showed a statistically significant association between joint effusion and disc displacement, with a random-effects odds ratio (OR) of 1.70 (95% CI: 1.42–2.03; p 0.0001; I2 = 24.1%), consistent with the common-effect model (OR = 1.72; 95% CI: 1.50–1.97; p 0.0001). The pooled estimate was not materially altered by the omission of any single study; Egger’s test did not detect funnel-plot asymmetry (p = 0.94), although publication or small-study effects cannot be excluded; and an approximate design-effect sensitivity analysis for bilateral joints, under assumed intraclass correlation coefficients of 0–0.8, gave similar estimates. These results indicate an unadjusted joint-level association: joint effusion was more frequently observed in joints with anterior disc displacement without reduction (ADDWOR) than in joints with displacement with reduction (ADDWR). Conclusions: These findings indicate a significant unadjusted joint-level association between joint effusion and disc displacement without reduction. Because in all included studies disc position and effusion were assessed on a single MRI examination, this association should not be interpreted as evidence of causality; further prospective investigation is needed to confirm the association and clarify the underlying mechanisms.
items.authors: Marco Portelli, Ignazio Russo, Angela Mirea Bellocchio, Angela Militi, Riccardo Nucera

items.title: Indoor Air Quality and Nitrogen Oxide Transport in Energy-Efficient Buildings: A Review
items.abstract: Energy codes require envelope airtightness that pushes natural air exchange below 0.30–0.35 h−1, turning the dwelling into a partly closed compartment of the reactive nitrogen cycle. This review synthesizes 82 studies on reactive nitrogen (NO, NO2, HONO) in energy-efficient buildings. The novelty of this review consists of three elements. First, it organizes the evidence around a mass balance for reactive nitrogen rather than around building typologies. Second, it uses the Damköhler number as a single criterion for when indoor transport and chemistry must be solved together. Third, it derives, from published parameters, the ventilation rates a cooking event would require. Emission factors for unvented gas cooking converge on 29.3–42.5 ng NOx J−1 expressed as NO2-equivalent, of which primary NO2 accounts for 7.8–9.1 ng J−1, with NO exceeding NO2 by 1.8–2.7 times. NO penetrates the envelope unimpeded; NO2 penetration is 0.72 ± 0.06 with a humidity-dependent loss rate of 0.27 ± 0.12 h−1. Reactive nitrogen cannot be treated as a passive scalar in quiescent zones of airtight dwellings, where air speeds fall below about 0.03–0.06 m s−1 at 20–40 ppb indoor ozone, whereas the bulk of a mixed room remains in the passive-scalar regime. Using the primary NO2 emission factor, the mass balance shows that keeping the hourly mean below the 1 h guideline during a 30 min cooking event would require 2.9–18.4 h−1, one to two orders of magnitude beyond z ventilation. NO2 removal is governed jointly by ventilation and surface uptake, so carbon dioxide is an unsuitable surrogate for demand-controlled ventilation.
items.authors: Ahmed Adjal, Venera-Stanca Nicolici, Ioana Ionel

items.title: Repeat-Rich Architecture and Gene Duplication Characterize the Expanded Genome of the Chestnut Gall Wasp
items.abstract: Dryocosmus kuriphilus, the chestnut gall wasp, is a globally invasive pest that reproduces by thelytokous parthenogenesis. Despite the absence of conventional sexual recombination, the species has spread widely and persists under diverse environmental conditions, but the genomic features associated with this capacity remain poorly understood. Here, a chromosome-level assembly of D. kuriphilus was compared with seven representative insect genomes, with emphasis on repetitive sequences, orthogroups, and gene-duplication patterns. The 2.28-Gb D. kuriphilus genome contained 79.7% repetitive sequences, including 62.3% transposable elements (TEs), most of which occurred in intergenic regions. OrthoFinder assigned 13,271 D. kuriphilus genes to multi-copy orthogroups, representing 61.5% of the protein-coding gene set. Independent MCScanX analysis classified genes into mutually exclusive dispersed, proximal, tandem, and segmental duplication modes, with segmental and dispersed representing the two largest duplicated-gene classes. D. kuriphilus contained substantially more segmental duplicates than the other species examined. Synonymous-substitution distributions revealed low- and high-Ks components representing different levels of synonymous divergence among duplicated genes, and genes in these components showed distinct functional profiles. Numerous local duplications were found near TEs and included genes involved in host recognition, nutrient utilisation, xenobiotic metabolism, and energy production. Compared with the closely related gall wasp Belonocnema kinseyi, D. kuriphilus has a broader reported distribution and host range and contains higher copy numbers in several gene families associated with chemosensation, detoxification, metabolism, and stress responses. Together, these findings show that the expanded D. kuriphilus genome is characterized by extensive repeat accumulation and increased gene copy number, whereas duplication at multiple scales increased and reshaped the functional gene repertoire. These genomic features identify candidate mechanisms that may contribute to genomic and ecological plasticity, although their adaptive significance requires expression, evolutionary, and functional validation.
items.authors: Ye-Song Ren, An-Kang Lv, Yang Zeng, Dao-Hong Zhu

items.title: Spatiotemporal Differentiation and Influencing Factors of Overseas Chinese Architectural Heritage: A Case Study of Minnan, China
items.abstract: The Minnan region in southern Fujian, China, comprising Quanzhou, Xiamen, and Zhangzhou, is one of China’s major traditional qiaoxiang (overseas Chinese hometown) regions. This study develops a spatial database of 682 Minnan Overseas Chinese Architectural Heritage (MOCAH) sites, divides their formation into four historical periods—Qing Dynasty (pre-1912), Early Republican Period (1912–1936), Wartime Republican Period (1937–1948), and Early PRC Period (1949–late 1970s)—and applies GIS-based spatial and statistical methods to examine their spatiotemporal differentiation and influencing factors. MOCAH formation was concentrated in 1912–1936, declined sharply in 1937–1948, and partially recovered after 1949. MOCAH remained significantly clustered across all periods and exhibited a pronounced coastal orientation. High-density areas expanded along the Xiamen–Quanzhou coast before contracting toward Quanzhou during wartime and subsequently re-emerging as multiple local high-density cores after 1949. Among the selected natural environmental and transport accessibility factors, distance to ports showed the greatest explanatory power, while nonlinear enhancement was observed for its interactions with distance to roads and railways and with distance to rivers. At the county level, MOCAH density was strongly and positively correlated with population density and overseas Chinese remittances, but more weakly correlated with ancestral hall and temple density.
items.authors: Meishan Xu, Shunhe Chen, Hao Liang, Huaqiu Lin, Li Xu

items.title: From Existing to Proposed: Spatial Program Change in School-Facility Pre-Design in Korea
items.abstract: Although user-participatory pre-design has been mandated for school-facility projects in South Korea since the 2021 Green Smart Future School initiative, systematic evidence on how the space program changes between existing (S0) and proposed (S1) conditions remains limited. This study quantified the magnitude and functional composition of S0–S1 change and explored associations with project-level characteristics using a documentary corpus of pre-design reports. Of 118 scope-eligible reports, 111 supported total-area comparison, and 50 additionally supported functional-category analysis. Total-area analysis (N = 111) showed a mean net change rate of 13.41% but a median of 1.12%, indicating a strongly right-skewed distribution. Functional-category analysis (N = 50), using the Functional Reallocation Index (FRI, an application of a compositional-distance measure), showed collaborative learning space increasing by 126.96% and general learning space contracting by 18.20% in pooled functional-area totals; an independent recoding confirmed these directions, but the collaborative-learning magnitude was boundary-sensitive. Holm-adjusted nonparametric tests of school level, regional location, reconstruction inclusion, and comparison scope against net change area, net change rate, and FRI found no association surviving family-wise correction. These findings indicate that total-area growth and functional-composition reallocation are distinct dimensions of space-program change, with implications for project monitoring and stakeholder expectations.
items.authors: Younsook Hwang, Myungsik Lee

items.title: HPV Vaccination Uptake Among Vaccine-Eligible U.S. Adults with and Without a Cancer History: A National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey Analysis, 2011–2023
items.abstract: Background: Human papillomavirus includes more than 200 types, classified by cancer risk. Since 2006, the vaccine has effectively prevented human papillomavirus infection and associated cancers; however, coverage among adults remains low. Furthermore, research examining human papillomavirus vaccination among adults with a cancer history is limited. Objective: To estimate vaccination uptake for human papillomavirus among U.S. adults aged 20–47 and compare uptake by cancer history. Methods: This study used data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey from 2011 to 2023. The final analytic sample included 13,511 adults aged 20–47 with self-reported vaccination status and cancer history. The data were weighted to account for the complex survey design and produce nationally representative estimates. Results: Among eligible adults, 84.7% were unvaccinated, 2.9% were under-vaccinated, and 12.4% had completed the vaccine series. Among eligible adults with a self-reported cancer history, the majority were unvaccinated. Vaccination completion differed by sociodemographic and healthcare-related factors. Conclusions: Human papillomavirus vaccination remained low among eligible U.S. adults, including those with a self-reported cancer history. These findings support efforts to improve adult vaccination coverage and prevent human papillomavirus infections and associated cancers.
items.authors: Jessica Saintibert, Tammie M. Johnson

items.title: Drivers of Enterprise Resilience Under Compound Shocks: A PLS-SEM Analysis of Vietnamese Firms and Cooperatives
items.abstract: Between 2020 and 2022, enterprises in emerging economies faced a succession of overlapping shocks—the COVID-19 pandemic, the supply-chain and energy consequences of the Russia–Ukraine conflict, and a sharp tightening of credit conditions—that tested their capacity to absorb losses, keep operating and adapt. Yet we still know little about which capabilities are associated with resilience, because most studies look at large firms in developed economies and test one capability at a time. This study asks which capabilities are most strongly associated with the resilience of small and medium-sized enterprises and cooperatives facing compound shocks, and through which pathways these associations run. Drawing on the dynamic-capabilities view and the resource-based view, an integrative model of six capabilities—anticipatory preparedness, leadership dynamism, institutional and government support, organizational social capital, human-resource resilience and digital transformation—is tested on survey data from 345 Vietnamese enterprises and cooperatives using PLS-SEM, with mediation analysis, common-method diagnostics and robustness checks. The findings suggest that human-resource resilience is the strongest correlate of perceived resilience, whereas institutional and government support is the only capability also associated with faster outcome-based recovery. Managers should treat workforce development and digital adoption as core resilience investments rather than discretionary costs, and state support programs should pair the financial and administrative assistance firms demand with the skilling and digitalization support that is most strongly associated with resilience in these data.
items.authors: Sang Xuan Le, Trang Mai Tran

items.title: Functionally Characterized Platelet-Rich Plasma Promotes Endothelial Migration and Cutaneous Wound Repair
items.abstract: Platelet-rich plasma (PRP) has been widely investigated as an autologous therapeutic for tissue regeneration; however, its clinical efficacy remains inconsistent, partly due to variability in PRP preparation protocols. In this study, we established an integrated framework for functional characterization of PRP by integrating platelet recovery, functional integrity, growth factor (GF) release, and regenerative outcomes. PRP prepared using a dual-spin centrifugation protocol at 92× g showed significantly higher platelet recovery while preserving functional responsiveness compared to single-spin conditions. PDGF-BB release increased in a time-dependent manner, peaking at 4 h after activation, and was positively correlated with platelet concentration. In an in vitro HUVEC scratch assay, PRP significantly enhanced endothelial cell migration in a platelet concentration-dependent manner. This migratory response was accompanied by increased phosphorylation of ERK and AKT and reduced VE-cadherin expression, indicating modulation of intracellular signaling pathways associated with endothelial cell growth, survival, and migration. In a rat skin wound model, PRP prepared under the selected experimental conditions accelerated wound closure compared with controls. Histological and immunohistochemical analyses revealed enhanced re-epithelialization, increased collagen deposition, increased epithelial cell proliferation, and reduced CD31-positive vascular area, consistent with accelerated vascular remodeling. Taken together, these findings demonstrate that PRP efficacy is governed by multiple interdependent factors. A comprehensive strategy integrating platelet recovery, functional preservation, GF release kinetics, and in vivo and in vitro outcomes provides a rational framework for functional characterization of PRP and may serve as a basis for subsequent translational validation.
items.authors: Sanggu Kim, Seongmo Yang, Soochong Kim

items.title: Nutraceutical Periodization for eXercise (NPX): Matching Bioactives to Training Load, Recovery Demand, and Adaptation Windows
items.abstract: Nutraceuticals are evaluated as though efficacy were a stable ingredient property, although net value may vary with exercise stimulus, exposure schedule, recovery pressure, athlete state, and prioritized outcome. This structured narrative review integrates exercise-adaptation biology, periodized sports nutrition, training-load and recovery models, precision nutrition, and human evidence for sport-relevant interventions. Searches of PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, and Scopus were updated through August 2026 and supplemented by citation tracking. General efficacy was separated from direct evidence of timing, context, or state modification. Nutraceutical Periodization for eXercise (NPX) is an allocation layer applied only after safety, legality, product quality, and plausible efficacy are established. It defines four non-sequential functional windows—performance exploitation, adaptation-permissive signaling, restoration, and resilience—and separates intervention strategy, training context, athlete state, and outcome hierarchy. Four falsifiable propositions test context modification, temporal allocation, bottleneck/state dependence, and whole-policy utility. None of the allocation claims in the present evidence map met the criterion for direct NPX allocation evidence. NPX therefore formalizes hypothetical allocation rules rather than an established supplementation policy; proposed improvements in athlete-centered outcomes or equivalent outcomes with less exposure, burden, or harm remain to be prospectively tested against an explicitly defined active evidence-based comparator. Interaction and policy trials are needed to establish the value and boundaries of these rules.
items.authors: Dan Cristian Mănescu, Cristina Casals, Anna Kurkiewicz-Piotrowska, Tayana Silva de Carvalho, Costin Petcu, Cristian Băltărețu

items.title: Agarose-Encapsulated Multifunctional Microspheres with High Drug Payload and Multimodal Imaging Capability for Arterial Embolization–Associated Hyperthermia Therapy
items.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) represents a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, and transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) remains the standard first-line locoregional therapy for intermediate-stage HCC. Nevertheless, conventional TACE frequently yields suboptimal therapeutic efficacy in advanced or heterogeneous tumors, necessitating combined therapeutic strategies. Herein, we report a one-step emulsion fabrication strategy to develop agarose-encapsulated multifunctional microspheres (AEMMs) using low-cost, biocompatible agarose as the scaffold matrix. AEMMs co-encapsulate PSS for electrostatic drug binding, iodixanol as a dual-contrast agent for CT and DSA, and superparamagnetic Fe3O4 nanoparticles that serve as both MRI contrast agent and NIR photothermal converter. In vitro evaluation demonstrates that AEMMs achieve ultrahigh drug loading capacities of 89.87 ± 1.78 mg/mL for DOX or 90.60 ± 0.84 mg/mL for Irinotecan, which are comparable to commercial CalliSpheres® and nearly twofold higher than DC Beads®. Photothermal evaluation confirms that AEMMs induce rapid temperature elevation above 50 °C within 3 min under 808 nm laser irradiation, with excellent thermal stability and reproducibility over repeated on–off cycles. Furthermore, AEMMs provide excellent complementary contrast for CT, DSA, and T2-weighted MRI, enabling real-time embolization monitoring and postoperative assessment. Blank AEMMs exhibit negligible cytotoxicity against HepG2 cells even at high concentrations, verifying favorable biocompatibility. Collectively, AEMMs integrate mechanical embolization, localized sustained chemotherapy, on-demand photothermal ablation, and multimodal imaging guidance into a single platform, offering a rational and promising integrated strategy to overcome the key limitations of conventional TACE for advanced HCC management.
items.authors: Yuqing Zhang, Shuo Huang, Quanming Kou, Yindong Xu, Yizhou Xu, Lei Chen

items.title: LiDAR-Assisted Survey Locates Unregistered Rock Shelters in the Blue Mountains, Australia
items.abstract: Rock shelters are important cultural and archaeological sites in Australia, often containing evidence of Aboriginal occupation and symbolic expression. While rock shelters have been investigated across Australia, locating them in rugged environments through pedestrian surveys remains challenging. This research contributes a methodology which integrates remote sensing, GIS analyses, and archaeological survey to locate rock shelters in the Blue Mountains. We produced models in ArcGIS Pro that analyse high-resolution, UAV-based LiDAR datasets and publicly available, low-resolution, aircraft-based LiDAR datasets from the New South Wales government. Our models yield locations of potential rock shelters, which can be visually evaluated in 3D LiDAR point clouds and ground-truthed through archaeological survey. Ground-truthing confirmed the successful detection of six known rock shelters on UAV and NSW LiDAR datasets, producing more accurate coordinates than the ones listed in online databases. Significantly, we identified three previously unregistered rock shelters that preserve rock art and lithics. These promising results indicate capacity to improve the spatial accuracy of legacy site records and locate unregistered archaeological rock shelters within, and potentially beyond, Australia. Our methodology promotes targeted and efficient survey of rock shelters that can produce regional datasets benefitting local communities, archaeology, and cultural heritage management.
items.authors: Jacob L. Bongers, Wayne Brennan, Erin Wilkins, Lauren Roach, Emily Nutman, Joseph W. Lehner

items.title: Continual Adaptation Under Missing Propagation Structure: Mechanisms and Limits of a Gated Semantic-Topological Network for Rumour and Harmful-Content Detection
items.abstract: We study sequential adaptation from rumor detection on PHEME, where reply structure is observed, to harmful-content flagging on USE24-XD, a 2024–2025 corpus released without propagation structure. A gated network fuses a BERTweet representation of the source post with a graph representation of the reply cascade, and Elastic Weight Consolidation (EWC) limits forgetting during fine-tuning. With a fixed split, 20 initialization seeds, matched training protocols and validation-only selection of λ, the gated model is no better on PHEME than a model of the source post alone, and neither reply structure nor learned gating improves on fixed fusion; under leave-one-event-out evaluation, however, the graph model generalizes best. Naive fine-tuning reduces PHEME balanced accuracy to below chance (0.481), whereas EWC retains 0.561 (+0.080, 95% CI [0.063,0.098], all 20 seeds): about a fifth of the pre-adaptation margin over chance, at a cost of 0.017 on the new task. Uniform anchoring of equal strength retains as much but prevents adaptation. EWC, not the new data, shifts the gate towards the graph branch, which on edgeless graphs is exactly a multilayer perceptron: the penalty freezes the semantic projection while the graph branch adapts.
items.authors: Emiliano Felicissimo, Marco Parrillo, Luigi Laura

items.title: Hydrogel-Gated Organic Electrochemical Transistors for Wearable and Portable Direct Detection of Aerosol-Borne Viral Antigens
items.abstract: Direct detection of viral antigens in respiratory aerosols is challenging because affinity-based organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) typically rely on liquid samples. Here, a non-flowing agarose hydrogel replaced the liquid electrolyte to capture aerosols, conduct ions, and support target transport. Before OECT readout, a separate 1-min ring-electrode field-assistance step was applied to facilitate target delivery to the aptamer-functionalized gate. Under the optimized conditions, the device achieved a solution-phase concentration-based limit of detection (LoD) of 1.27 fM and a sample-to-result time of 17 min. The approach was implemented in face-mask and handheld formats with a portable wireless readout system. In nebulization-based tests using SARS-CoV-2 spike protein, the LoDs expressed in terms of the concentrations of the nebulizer source solutions were 6.89 pM and 1.19 pM for the face-mask and handheld configurations, respectively. These results demonstrate that hydrogel-mediated aerosol capture and ionic coupling, ring-electrode field assistance, and OECT transduction can be integrated to enable direct electrical detection of aerosol-borne viral antigens, supporting further development of wearable and portable respiratory screening systems.
items.authors: Haiyang Yu, Yuhan Lu, Bihan Guo, Jiameng Wang, Ya Zhang, Bingfang Wang

items.title: Efficacy and Safety of Lythrum salicaria Extract on Body Fat Reduction in Adults with a BMI of 23–30 kg/m2: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Trial
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: Plant-derived ingredients have attracted interest as adjuncts for reducing body fat, but clinical evidence for Lythrum salicaria extract alone remains limited. We evaluated its effects on body fat and its safety in adults with a body mass index (BMI) of 23–30 kg/m2. Methods: Ninety adults aged 19–75 years participated in a single-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial. Participants received either 500 mg/day of L. salicaria extract powder (corresponding to approximately 400 mg/day of plant-derived extract solids) or placebo for 12 weeks. The primary endpoint was the change in body fat mass from baseline to day 84, assessed by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA). Efficacy was evaluated primarily in the per-protocol (PP) population, with supporting intention-to-treat (ITT) analyses. Anthropometric measures, other DXA outcomes, and blood markers were assessed as secondary endpoints. Results: The PP population included 84 participants. Baseline-adjusted differences in body fat mass change, expressed as extract minus placebo, were −2.01 kg (95% confidence interval [CI], −2.51 to −1.52; p 0.001) in the PP population and −2.04 kg (95% CI, −2.66 to −1.42; p 0.001) in the ITT population. Exploratory secondary analyses favored the extract for BMI, body weight, body fat percentage, and adiponectin. No serious adverse events occurred. Conclusions: Supplementation with L. salicaria extract powder for 12 weeks was associated with a reduction in DXA-measured body fat mass compared with placebo. Larger trials with longer follow-up are needed to confirm the findings and investigate the mechanisms involved.
items.authors: Bong-Jin Shin, Hye-Jin Park, Yea-Jin Park, Hyo-Jin An, Su Shin, Yun-Yeop Cha

items.title: Privacy-Preserving Diffusion Against Identity Inference Attack via Semantic Destruction Recovery and Segmentation
items.abstract: Facial image generation or generative editing using diffusion models presents risks of identity leakage, potentially enabling unauthorized re-identification in forensic and content moderation applications. Diffusion editing is vulnerable to privacy-preserving facial identity obfuscation through diffusion-based semantic transformation, which alters identity-sensitive facial attributes so that an identity inference adversary, such as a recognition or classification model, cannot reliably recover the original identity from the protected image. This work introduces DIFP (Diffusion-based Identity-preserving Facial Privacy Protection), a reversible privacy framework that unifies semantic overwrite and key-based image recovery. DIFP protects identity by intentionally overwriting facial semantics during diffusion using identity-altering prompts and adaptive guidance, while preserving background information through a FAPM that localizes transformations to identity-sensitive regions. To enable authorized recovery, DIFP injects a key derived via SHA-256 into the diffusion latent representation through deterministic, seed-controlled perturbations applied during the scheduler-driven denoising process. Decoding the keyed latent produces a privacy-protected image, whereas removing the same key-dependent perturbation enables key-conditioned image recovery to protect generative recovery alignment. This paper further presents a privacy-aware denoising method that illustrates the generative editing and filling of semantic destruction and authorized recoverability across diffusion steps under varying privacy strengths. Privacy effectiveness is assessed within an identity inference threat model, employing a ResNet-50 classifier as a proxy adversary. At the same time, SSIM (Structural Similarity Index Measure) and Facial IoU (Intersection over Union) are used to quantify the visual fidelity of the recovered image in generative identity editing, along with a privacy score. Experimental results demonstrate consistent identity obfuscation through semantic destruction, while preserving high perceptual quality and enabling reliable, authenticated content recovery for legitimate privacy linkage examination.
items.authors: Shahrzad Sayyafzadeh, Hongmei Chi, Shonda Bernadin

items.title: High-Grade Renal Trauma Due to Blunt Injury: Do All Require Surgical Intervention?
items.abstract: Background: Renal trauma management has increasingly shifted toward non-operative treatment, particularly in hemodynamically stable patients. Advances in imaging, resuscitation, and monitoring have improved the outcomes of conservative management, even in high-grade injuries. Blunt trauma, most commonly from falls, is the leading cause, and renal injuries often occur within the context of polytrauma involving multiple organ systems. Management is primarily guided by hemodynamic stability, overall clinical condition, existing comorbidities, and the severity of injury as determined by the American Association for the Surgery of Trauma (AAST) grading system. This study aimed to describe the management strategies and clinical outcomes of patients with high-grade blunt renal trauma (AAST grades III–V), with particular emphasis on the use of conservative management in selected patients. Methods: This study is a retrospective analysis conducted in our department (Emergency Clinical County Hospital in Brasov, Romania) to identify the data of the patients admitted with high-grade blunt renal trauma from 1 January 2019 to 31 December 2025. Results: A total of 58 patients with blunt renal trauma (grade III or higher) were identified. According to the AAST classification, the most common injuries were grade III (35 patients), followed by grade IV (11 patients) and grade V (12 patients). The majority of cases (68.97%) were treated conservatively, and the overall mortality rate was 8.62%. Conclusions: This study highlights the importance of individualized management in renal trauma, supporting conservative treatment in hemodynamically stable patients. Hemodynamic stability, renal injury grade, and the extent of associated injuries should guide treatment decisions. Further research is needed to refine treatment protocols and assess long-term outcomes.
items.authors: Anda Hogea, Ioan Scarneciu, Marius Moga, Mircea D. Hogea, Florin Lucian Sabou, Adriana Prahoveanu

items.title: Accompanying the Dying: End-of-Life Doulas and the Relational Practice of Good Death in the United States
items.abstract: As death in the United States is increasingly managed within biomedical institutions, end-of-life doulas (EOLDs) have emerged as non-medical practitioners who support dying people and their families through education, advocacy, companionship, ritual, and vigil care. Drawing on 18 semi-structured interviews with practicing EOLDs across the United States, this qualitative study examines how these doulas conceptualize a good death, navigate emotionally intensive care work, and sustain themselves in a largely unregulated field. These interviews suggest that EOLDs challenge dominant biomedical models of dying by organizing care around client autonomy, relational presence, and personalization of treatment rather than cure, intervention, and control. According to the interviews, central to their practices are death-positive worldviews, emotionally intimate approaches to care, and strong peer networks. For these EOLDs, lower reported burnout and compassion fatigue were linked not only to self-care, but to a broader relational framework in which death is understood as a meaningful life passage rather than a professional defeat.
items.authors: Amy J. Shields, Lisa Gezon

items.title: Effects of Coal Gangue–Decomposed Straw Composite Substrates on Soil Properties and Plant Growth for Revegetation of Degraded Open-Pit Mine Slopes
items.abstract: Abandoned open-pit coal mine slopes are compacted, infertile and water-limited, hindering vegetation restoration. This study evaluated the combined use of two waste materials—coal gangue (an alkaline, mineral-rich mining residue) and decomposed straw (a nutrient-rich agricultural residue)—as a composite substrate for restoring degraded slope soil. In a 60-day greenhouse pot experiment, slope soil from the Haizhou Open-Pit Coal Mine (Fuxin, China) was amended with coal gangue (5%, 10% or 15% by dry mass), decomposed straw (1%, 3% or 5%), or their nine full-factorial combinations (16 treatments in total, including an unamended control, each with three replicates), and sown with three herbaceous species (ryegrass, alfalfa and tall fescue). Soil physical and chemical properties and plant growth traits were measured. Relative to the unamended control, the composite substrates improved soil structure and fertility: soil water content and field water-holding capacity were highest under the 10% gangue + 5% straw treatment (25.6% and 25.89%, increases of 28.0% and 29.5%), bulk density was lowest, with the correspondingly highest total porosity, under the 15% gangue + 3% straw treatment (1.35 g/cm3, a 14.9% decrease). Organic matter (9.42 g/kg), total nitrogen (0.71 g/kg, +65.1%), available nitrogen (45.3 mg/kg, +33.0%) and available potassium (106.44 mg/kg, +26.2%) were highest under the 5% gangue + 5% straw treatment, which also gave the best growth of ryegrass and alfalfa (alfalfa aboveground and underground dry weight increased by 221% and 188%, respectively), whereas tall fescue grew best under the 5% gangue + 3% straw treatment. These results indicate that a 5% coal gangue + 5% decomposed straw composite substrate is a promising amendment for revegetating degraded open-pit slopes, although field validation is still required.
items.authors: Yifang Long, Ziling Song, Yu Wen, Zhen Gao, Zekun Li

items.title: Multidimensional Green Space Exposure and Housing Prices in High-Density Urban Areas: Spatial Evidence from 3729 Communities in Guangzhou
items.abstract: Green space in high-density cities is scarce and shared unevenly, and the question of whether its value affects housing prices and whether that effect holds between communitie is still unclear, as most studies measure one exposure dimension or report a single area-wide estimate. In this study, we examine 3729 residential communities in Baiyun District, Guangzhou, linking a composite green space exposure (GSE) index to second-hand listing prices. The GSE index equally weights three normalized indicators—the green coverage ratio, park accessibility index, and green view index—which describe availability, accessibility, and visibility. We fitted ordinary least squares, geographically weighted regression, and multiscale geographically weighted regression in turn, judging spatial variation through residual spatial autocorrelation and corrected local inference. The three dimensions of the index peak in different parts of the district: the composite GSE runs higher along the eastern foothills and in parts of Jinshazhou and lower across the central and southern built-up areas. High-GSE and high-price areas overlap only partially: the greenest communities are not, in general, the most expensive ones. On average, a 0.01 increase in GSE is associated with an estimated 4.1% price difference at the district scale, whereas the typical local association is much smaller (about 0.4 to 0.6% for the same 0.01 difference), and the global model explains only 19.4% of price variation. Positive local coefficients cover 65.8% of communities, with 25.0% remaining significant after correction, while significantly negative ones cover 0.7%. Greener community planning should therefore account for exposure dimensions and local market responses, not district-wide averages.
items.authors: Weian Wang, Xinchen Chester Hong

items.title: Deployable Self-Referenced Features for Cross-Cell Battery State-of-Health Estimation: Randomized Pairing Controls and Benchmarking
items.abstract: Battery health estimation depends on feature references as well as learners. Changing one column’s normalization moves root-mean-square error (RMSE) by up to 108%. We construct a self-referenced lift (SRL) from each cell’s earliest retained record. Under the offline author protocol, learners with the full history stack improve on 9 of 11 units after Holm correction, with none significantly worse and two units per backbone not significantly different. Relative-change medians over all 11 units are −16.8% for the frozen foundation model and −19.1% for gradient boosting, including learner effects. Under a strict online reader excluding target-future and label information, compact SRL instead yields +4.3% for gradient boosting (5 of 11 improve) and +10.4% for the frozen foundation model (3 of 11 improve): no overall online accuracy gain. Legacy offline pairing controls favour self-pairing (p=0.0099, 100 derangements). A companion benchmark with implicit self-comparison improves in 6 of 6 batches with per-batch selection (5 of 6 with a fixed configuration); an unseen-library legacy diagnostic improves by 22–33%. Deployability concerns feature computability, not a strict-online accuracy advantage.
items.authors: Bo Peng, Xiaofen Wang, Ke Zhang

items.title: Research on the Evolution Characteristics and Collaborative Detection Strategies for Bottom Oil-Spill Fires in Oil-Immersed Transformers
items.abstract: Conventional single-type detectors generally face difficulties in achieving both early warning and fire-source localization for rapidly developing bottom oil-spill fires occurring in large oil-immersed transformers. In this study, a 500 kV transformer bottom oil-spill fire model is established to analyze the evolution of temperature field, smoke density, CO and CO2 concentrations, and thermal radiation, and to compare the response characteristics of various detectors. A stable high-temperature zone forms within 30 s after ignition, exhibiting a central temperature of 950–1000 °C and a distinct temperature gradient. CO2 and CO concentrations stabilize at 60,000–90,000 ppm and 600–1300 ppm, respectively, while thermal radiation intensity attenuates sharply with distance. Aspirating smoke detectors achieve early response but suffer from poor positioning and anti-interference performance. Distributed optical fiber detectors realize thermal anomaly identification and fire localization. Infrared and ultraviolet detectors respond within 10 s, and ultraviolet detection is less susceptible to thermal interference. This paper proposes a collaborative detection strategy of fiber temperature sensing and infrared–ultraviolet composite flame detection, forming a hierarchical fire identification framework. The findings inform the optimal design of transformer fire detection systems.
items.authors: Yang He, Jianlin Li, Rui Liu, Yi Guo, Yubiao Huang, Jiaqing Zhang

items.title: Study on the Role of FHL2 in Chicken: Promoting Bone Growth and Inhibiting Fat Formation via Regulating BMSC Differentiation Balance
items.abstract: In this study, the objective was to identify the key regulators of the osteogenic–adipogenic differentiation equilibrium of chicken bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs), with the expectation of developing marker genes that promote skeletal development and inhibit excessive fat deposition. BMSCs were isolated and phenotypically characterized. qRT-PCR showed FHL2 increased during osteogenic differentiation. Transfection with FHL2 overexpression plasmid or siRNAs was done. FHL2 overexpression increased osteogenic marker mRNA (RUNX2, ALP, Osterix, and OCN) levels, reduced lipid deposition-related gene (C/EBPα, C/EBPβ) expression, and increased mineralized area and nodules. FHL2 knockdown had the opposite effect. FHL2 overexpression also reduced apoptosis and proliferation-related transcripts, decreased apoptosis rate, and reduced proliferation-related transcripts and altered cell-cycle distribution. After FHL2 knockdown, RNA sequencing identified 81 differentially expressed genes. Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment showed changes in various processes and pathways. Enrichment analysis indicated that the differentially expressed genes were involved in apoptosis, cytokine–cytokine receptor interaction, Th17 cell differentiation, JAK-STAT signaling, cAMP signaling, steroid hormone biosynthesis, and retinol metabolism. These findings indicate that FHL2 promotes osteogenic differentiation and suppresses adipogenic differentiation in chicken BMSCs in vitro and may act through multiple downstream pathways.

items.title: Detection of Tenacibaculum spp. in Caligus rogercresseyi: Evidence of Potential Pathogen Carriage in Salmon Aquaculture
items.abstract: Sea lice (Caligus rogercresseyi) are major ectoparasites in Chilean salmon aquaculture, causing economic losses and increasing fish susceptibility to secondary infections. Tenacibaculosis has recently emerged as the second leading cause of mortality in farmed salmon. Understanding whether sea lice may harbor or transmit bacterial pathogens is therefore highly relevant. A sea lice survey was conducted at an Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar) farm in the Los Lagos Region, Chile. Twenty adult parasites (10 ovigerous females and 10 males) were analyzed using an integrated approach combining immunohistochemistry (IHC) with specific antibodies and conventional PCR with appropriate controls. IHC revealed positive signals for Tenacibaculum maritimum in the gastrointestinal tract and cuticle, and for Tenacibacuum dicentrarchi in the cuticle and ovigerous sac of C. rogercresseyi. A specific PCR test confirmed the presence of both pathogens, yielding amplification products of 1088 bp for T. maritimum and 284 bp for T. dicentrarchi. This study provides the first dual evidence, by PCR and IHC, of Tenacibaculum species in C. rogercresseyi. These findings suggest that sea lice may play a role in pathogen dynamics in salmon farming, highlighting the need for further research on their contribution to disease transmission within aquaculture systems.
items.authors: Pedro Ilardi, Eugenia Jerez, Sara Valdes, Carlos Sandoval, Jaime Romero, Harold Oliva

items.title: Behavioral Smartphone Orientation Is Associated with Upper Limb Dysfunction Among University Students: A Cross-Sectional Study
items.abstract: Background: Excessive smartphone use has been associated with musculoskeletal disorders; however, the relationship between smartphone orientation and objective measures of upper limb function remains insufficiently explored. The aim of this study was to determine whether smartphone orientation is associated with upper limb disability, grip strength, pain intensity and clinical signs of musculoskeletal dysfunction in university students. Materials and methods: The study involved 84 students including women (n = 74) and men (n = 10), with an age of 21 ± 2.6 years. This cross-sectional study utilized the Smartphone Orientation Scale (SOS) to assess behavioral smartphone orientation. Functional disability was assessed using the QuickDASH questionnaire and the intensity of pain was measured using the Numeric Rating Scale (NRS). Objective assessments included hand grip strength measurements via an electronic dynamometer and clinical evaluation using the Finkelstein test. Because the analyzed variables did not follow a normal distribution, Spearman’s rank correlation analysis was performed to assess the relationship between variables across the study group with statistical significance set at p 0.05. Results: Higher SOS scores were associated with lower left- and right-hand grip strength (ρ = −0.391 and −0.395, respectively; Holm-adjusted p = 0.001 for both) and greater upper-limb disability measured by QuickDASH (ρ = 0.387; Holm-adjusted p = 0.001). SOS score was also associated with a positive right Finkelstein test (ρ = 0.294; Holm-adjusted p = 0.020), but not with the left Finkelstein test. Longer daily smartphone-use duration was associated with lower grip strength and higher SOS and QuickDASH scores after Holm correction. Conclusions: Screening using the Smartphone Orientation Scale may help identify young adults presenting with behavioral patterns associated with upper limb dysfunction. Smartphone orientation may represent a more clinically relevant behavioral marker of early upper limb dysfunction than self-reported daily smartphone use.
items.authors: Iga Szukalska, Agnieszka Kempinska-Podhorodecka, Małgorzata Szczuko

items.title: Zingiberis Rhizoma Ethanol Extract Attenuates Recognition Memory Deficits and Neuroinflammation in a Mouse Model of Bilateral Common Carotid Artery Stenosis
items.abstract: Chronic cerebral hypoperfusion (CCH), a key contributor to vascular dementia (VaD), causes white matter injury and neuroinflammation. We evaluated the neuroprotective effects of 6-gingerol-rich Zingiberis Rhizoma ethanol extract (ZRex) in a mouse bilateral common carotid artery stenosis (BCAS) model. BCAS-operated C57BL/6 mice received oral ZRex (30, 100, or 300 mg/kg, three times weekly). Spatial working memory, recognition memory, glial activation, oligodendrocyte and myelin markers, RNA sequencing (RNA-seq), and 6-gingerol molecular docking were evaluated. ZRex partially restored recognition memory in the novel object recognition test without altering Y-maze spatial working memory. BCAS significantly increased platelet-derived growth factor receptor alpha-positive cell counts, which ZRex restored toward sham levels. ZRex also markedly attenuated cluster of differentiation 68 immunoreactivity. RNA-seq identified 479 BCAS-responsive candidate genes (fold-change-filtered) and demonstrated that ZRex selectively restored downregulated transcripts. Molecular docking revealed the strongest predicted binding of 6-gingerol to Mup19 (Vina score: −9.4 kcal/mol), followed by Serpina3, Saa2, Mup1, and F10. Overall, ZRex attenuated BCAS-induced recognition memory deficits and neuroinflammation by modulating metabolic and inflammatory pathways, potentially mediated by direct 6-gingerol interactions with candidate targets. These findings support ZRex as a promising botanical candidate for VaD.
items.authors: Taeyoung Huh, Chiyeon Lim, Sehyun Lim, Kyung-Min Kim, Suin Cho

items.title: A Controlled Reanalysis of KIDO: Text Variants, Image-Model Configurations, and Cross-Modal Score Discrepancy
items.abstract: KIDO pairs children’s prompted happy and sad drawings with written reflections, creating a multimodal setting in which the text and image channels provide very different evidence for the same labels. We reanalyze KIDO by comparing Turkish, original English, and LLM-generated Turkish-grounded English text; replicating image-model configurations; and measuring text–image score discrepancy on 1630 drawings from 815 children. Turkish-grounded English is numerically higher than original English across emotion, gender, and educational-level classification under the controlled English protocol. For emotion, the respective three-seed macro-F1 scores are 0.9808±0.0004 and 0.9798±0.0034; however, the paired ensemble difference is small, and its 95% child-cluster bootstrap interval includes zero. A blinded, tail-enriched bilingual audit of 120 child-distinct pairs provides source-grounded support for the generated text: 88.3% of ratings receive adequacy scores of 4–5, while major meaning errors occur in 7.5% of ratings and are confined to the deliberately sampled low-similarity tail. Text performance also depends strongly on explicit emotion cues: such cues occur in approximately two-thirds of test reflections, and masking them at evaluation reduces macro-F1 by 0.054–0.073, while performance remains above 0.90. Image-emotion models achieve a substantially lower mean macro-F1, ranging from 0.7683 to 0.7867 across replicated DenseNet121 and ConvNeXt configurations. Cross-modal score differences remain substantial: the Multimodal Discrepancy Index, equivalent to total variation in this binary task, ranges from 0.2300 to 0.2753 across image ensembles. These results show that text preparation, lexical cues, and image-model configuration materially affect conclusions drawn from KIDO and support reporting channel-specific evidence before interpreting multimodal agreement or fusion.
items.authors: Ercan Ezin

items.title: Non-Orthogonal DF Relaying for SWIPT over Fading Channels with Power Adaptation
items.abstract: This paper investigates two-phase non-orthogonal decode-and-forward (DF) relaying for simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT) over fading channels. The source transmits in both phases, while the relay forwards the decoded information in the second phase and the destination employs power splitting in both phases. We jointly optimize the source-power allocation between the two phases and the power-splitting ratios to maximize the ergodic end-to-end achievable rate subject to a minimum average harvested-energy requirement. By exploiting the time-sharing property, the original nonconvex problem is solved using Lagrangian duality. Numerical results under Rayleigh fading show that the proposed adaptive scheme achieves a higher ergodic achievable rate and supports a wider range of feasible harvested-energy requirements than a conventional scheme employing a fixed power-splitting ratio, with the performance advantage becoming more pronounced under stringent harvested-energy requirements.
items.authors: Dong-Woo Lim, Jae-Mo Kang

items.title: Bioinspired Soft Modular Robotic Cubes as Building Blocks for Adaptive Machines
items.abstract: Living organisms exhibit remarkable adaptability through distributed actuation and continuous deformation, thereby inspiring new paradigms in soft robotics. This paper presents a family of bioinspired heterogeneous soft modular robotic cubes designed to reproduce such adaptive mechanisms through coordinated pneumatic actuation. Each module combines elastomeric materials with inextensible fiber patterns that emulate muscular architectures, guiding deformation under pressurization. A hyperelastic Finite Element Analysis (FEA) framework was developed to predict deformation modes and experimentally validated using ultraviolet marker tracking. The modules exhibited diverse motions, including axial expansion, twist, bending, and shear, with close agreement between simulations and experiments. When assembled into a Cartesian soft platform, the modules demonstrated coordinated multi-axis movement. These results highlight the potential of bioinspired modular soft robots as scalable building blocks for robotic systems that bridge natural morphologies with engineered functionality, with the observed secondary couplings suggesting a pathway toward adaptive or reconfigurable behavior in future closed-loop implementations.
