items.title: Miniaturized Dual-Band Bandpass Filter Based on High-Order Mode of Spoof Surface Plasmon Polaritons with Triangular Notch Structure
items.abstract: This paper proposes a novel triangularly notched spoof surface plasmon polariton (SSPP) unit for designing dual-band bandpass filters (DPF). Compared with rectangular SSPP units, the proposed triangularly notched SSPP unit exhibits a superior slow-wave effect and enables the simultaneous excitation of multiple higher-order SSPP modes through a simple structure with compact transverse and longitudinal dimensions. The designed filter optimizes the need for conventional mode-conversion transition structures, significantly reducing the overall size. By adjusting the geometric parameters of the proposed triangularly notched SSPP unit, the upper and lower cutoff frequencies of the passbands can be flexibly tailored with fewer adjusting parameters. The final filter achieves two operating passbands covering 4.85 GHz to 9.3 GHz and 10.4 GHz to 15.3 GHz, with the return loss maintained better than 12 dB within both bands. For validation, the designed filter was fabricated and measured. The measured results show good agreement with the simulations, verifying the effectiveness of the proposed structure and design methodology.
items.authors: Yan Liu, Huarui Zhang, Shige Wei, Cong Chen, Hao Luo, Ke Gong

items.title: Failure Propagation and Reliability Degradation in Maritime Kill Webs with Multi-Domain Heterogeneous Function-Carrying Platforms
items.abstract: Maritime kill webs integrate heterogeneous platforms across air, surface, and underwater domains, with each platform potentially supporting multiple mission functions. Existing reliability models often represent attacks as complete node removals and therefore cannot distinguish overall platform failures from local functional degradation or quantify reliability losses caused by cross-domain coordination. This study develops a two-layer platform–function model and a probabilistic attack-response mechanism that couples platform-level and function-level damage. Multi-domain adaptation coefficients are introduced to modify functional-edge reliability, and system degradation is assessed using functional-node retention, structural closure, effective closure, and mission reliability retention. In a simulation containing 24 platforms, 55 functional nodes, and 15,246 candidate kill chains, targeted attacks caused substantially greater mission degradation than random attacks. At a cumulative attacked-platform ratio of 0.25, mission reliability retention was 0.5340 under random attack, compared with 0.2173 and 0.2184 under degree-based and functional-carrier-prioritized attacks, respectively. Under functional-carrier-prioritized attack, reliability loss was greatest for underwater targets (0.869). Sensitivity and ablation analyses showed that local functional degradation strongly affects retained mission reliability, while multi-domain adaptation mainly affects whether structurally closed chains satisfy the mission-reliability requirement. The proposed framework distinguishes structural disruption from reliability-induced mission interruption in multilayer mission systems.
items.authors: Kecheng Meng, Peng Di, Tong Chen

items.title: Molecular Epidemiology of Pityriasis Versicolor Reveals a Remarkably High Prevalence of Malassezia japonica in Coastal South India
items.abstract: Pityriasis versicolor (PV) is a common superficial mycosis caused by lipophilic yeasts of the genus Malassezia. Despite its high prevalence, comprehensive molecular epidemiological data on Malassezia species associated with PV remain limited in several regions of India. Therefore, our study investigated the molecular epidemiology, demographic characteristics, seasonal variation, clinical manifestations, anatomical distribution, and associated predisposing factors among patients with PV from the coastal region of Karnataka. A total of 147 patients clinically diagnosed with PV were included in this study. Skin scrapings were isolated and cultured on lipid-rich media, and isolates were identified using polymerase chain reaction–restriction fragment length polymorphism (PCR-RFLP) and internal transcribed spacer (ITS) sequencing. Molecular identification was performed for 182 Malassezia isolates. Malassezia furfur was the predominant species at 51.1% (93 isolates), followed by Malassezia japonica at 34.1% (62), Malassezia restricta at 5.5% (10), Malassezia slooffiae at 3.3% (6), Malassezia sympodialis at 2.2% (4), Malassezia arunalokei at 2.2% (4), Malassezia globosa at 1.1% (2), and Malassezia pachydermatis at 0.6% (1). In addition, 20 non-Malassezia yeast isolates were identified, including Candida, Rhodotorula, Meyerozyma, and Trichosporon. The study population had a mean age of 27.8 ± 14.9 years, with a male-to-female ratio of 2.2:1. Most cases occurred among individuals aged 10–39 years, while M. furfur remained the predominant species across all age groups and both genders. Seasonal variation was evident, with the highest number of cases recorded during September. Clinically, hypopigmented macules were the predominant lesion type, and the back was the most frequently affected anatomical site. Underlying medical conditions or potential predisposing factors were identified in 18 patients (12.2%), with alcohol-related disorders and immunosuppressive conditions being the most frequently documented. Analyzing all these data, the present study provides updated molecular epidemiological data on Malassezia species causing PV in the coastal region of Karnataka. The predominance of M. furfur and the unexpectedly high prevalence of M. japonica highlight the importance of molecular identification for accurate species-level characterization.
items.authors: Jayaprakash Sasikumar, Bharati Naik, Manjunath M. Shenoy, Tamalika Manna, Shankar Prasad Das

items.title: Hoof Health in the Parmigiano Reggiano Dairy Production System: A Pilot Epidemiological Study Using Digitally Recorded Hoof-Trimming Data
items.abstract: The aim of this study was to describe the prevalence and distribution of claw lesions in dairy cows from farms producing milk for Parmigiano Reggiano cheese and to evaluate factors associated with their occurrence. Data were collected during hoof-trimming visits performed by four professional hoof trimmers on 25 farms between March 2023 and October 2024 using a specifically developed digital recording application. 4410 visits from 3066 cows were included. At least one lesion was recorded in 53.5% of visits and 44.3% of cows. Sole ulcer was the most common lesion (23.8% of visits), followed by sole haemorrhage (19.3%), wall abscess (18.1%), dermatitis (16.4%), and wall lesions (10.3%). Mechanically related lesions mainly involved the lateral claws of the hind limbs. Parity was strongly associated with lesion occurrence: compared with first-parity cows, odds increased at parity 2 (OR 1.41), parity 3 (OR 2.52), and parity ≥4 (OR 3.14). Because parity and age were highly correlated (r = 0.94), this association should be interpreted as a combined parity/age effect, and their independent effects could not be distinguished. Lactation stage showed weaker associations, and seasonal and farm-level differences were observed. Overall, non-infectious lesions predominated. The marked variation among farms suggests that herd-level factors contribute to claw health. Linking these digitally recorded hoof-trimming data with national breeding and production databases may support large-scale surveillance and future epidemiological and genetic investigations.
items.authors: Maria Virginia Ralletti, Fabio Testori, Luigi Grasselli, Raffaella Finocchiaro, Lorenzo Benzoni, Maurizio Marusi

items.title: Triple Genetic Alterations (EGFR Mutation, ALK Fusion, and MET Polysomy) in Gynecological Metastasis of Lung Adenocarcinoma Patient with Acquired Resistance to Furmonertinib: A Case Report
items.abstract: For advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) mutations, targeted therapy is the standard first-line treatment, but acquired resistance and disease progression are inevitable. Identification of resistance mechanisms is crucial for guiding subsequent anti-tumor therapy. We report a 57-year-old female patient with advanced lung adenocarcinoma harboring an EGFR exon 21 L858R mutation. The patient experienced disease progression with rare gynecological metastasis after 16 months of first-line furmonertinib therapy. Next-generation sequencing (NGS) of the uterine metastatic lesion identified concurrence of EGFR mutation and ALK fusion, while fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) confirmed MET polysomy. The patient exhibited intolerance to the combination therapy of glumetinib plus furmonertinib. Subsequently, the patient received a combination of furmonertinib and the ALK-TKI ensartinib, which was assessed as a partial response (PR) at the first restaging evaluation (1 month after treatment initiation), with favorable safety and tolerability. Secondary ALK fusion may represent a rare but clinically meaningful resistance mechanism in EGFR-mutant NSCLC. Furthermore, while gynecological metastasis from lung cancer is uncommon, clinicians should be alert to this possibility in patients presenting with relevant symptoms, with pelvic examination conducted as needed.
items.authors: Qinglong Jiang, Rui Sun, Haiyan Xu, Yanfeng Wang

items.title: HepDecide: A Standards-Oriented, Explainable Clinical Decision Support Prototype for the Chronic Liver-Disease Spectrum—Design, Guideline-Grounded Reporting, and a Leakage-Controlled Retrospective Evaluation
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: Specialist hepatology capacity is small relative to the population needing assessment, so most decisions about whom to investigate for chronic liver disease fall to non-specialists guided by static laboratory indices reported in isolation. This study presents HepDecide, a standards-oriented decision support prototype consolidating stage-specific risk estimation, explainability and guideline-traceable reporting into one physician-facing service, and reports a leakage-controlled retrospective evaluation of its predictive layer. Methods: HepDecide combines stage-specific tabular classifiers, an explainability layer based on SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) anchored to EASL and AASLD guidelines; outputs are expressed as HL7 FHIR R4 resources, with inputs mapped to LOINC and diseases to ICD-10. Three endpoints were modelled on two publicly available, de-identified cohorts: steatohepatitis versus simple steatosis and histological cirrhosis (F4) in a biopsy-characterised MASLD cohort (n= 605), and one-year survival among patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC; n = 165). Because patient-level predictions from the original development runs were not retained, the primary evaluation is a separate re-analysis with a locked patient-wise test partition, imputation, scaling and resampling fitted within training folds only, 25 classifier–imbalance configurations per endpoint, training-only calibration, and calibration, precision–recall, decision-curve and SHAP analyses. Results: On the locked test partitions, ROC-AUC was 0.67 (95% CI 0.50–0.84) for steatohepatitis (n = 121), 0.81 (0.52–1.00) for cirrhosis (n = 121; five events) and 0.76 (0.56–0.92) for one-year HCC survival (n = 33), with Brier scores of 0.096, 0.028 and 0.199. On the same cirrhosis test partition FIB-4 reached an ROC-AUC of 0.92 (0.82–0.99). The five highest-ranked SHAP features accounted for 58–73% of total attribution. Development-phase estimates of 0.90, 0.98 and 0.92 are reported separately as archived values; the cirrhosis estimate is documented in a retained training output, although its original input tables and individual test probabilities are unavailable. No quantitative evaluation of the language-generation layer is claimed, because the corresponding records were not retained. Conclusions: Under leakage-controlled retrospective conditions the predictive layer showed moderate discrimination with wide confidence intervals and did not outperform FIB-4 for cirrhosis. The value of the prototype lies in its standards-oriented, explainable and guideline-grounded design and in a fully documented, reproducible evaluation pipeline; transportability, the text-generation layer and clinical usefulness remain to be established prospectively. HepDecide is intended as a clinician-supervised triage and reporting prototype, not a clinically ready system.
items.authors: Nazlı Tokatlı

items.title: Numerical Investigation of Crack Driving Force and Ultimate Bearing Capacity of D1,422 mm X80 Pipelines with Composite Groove Girth Weld
items.abstract: Existing prediction models for the ultimate bearing capacity of circumferential welds are primarily limited to manual or combined automatic welding with single V-grooves, failing to address full-automatic welding with composite grooves, and that is a critical technical gap for large-diameter, thick-walled X80 steel pipelines using automatic welding processes. To fill this gap, this study focused on cracked circumferential welds with composite grooves in full-automatic welded X80 pipelines, establishing a nonlinear finite element model that accurately accounts for the composite groove’s geometric characteristics, three material zones, and canoe-type crack simulation. Spider-web mesh refinement was applied at crack tips to ensure precision, and the model was validated using full-scale wide-plate tensile tests. Using J-integral as the crack driving force parameter, this study systematically analyzed the effects of nine key factors: load parameters, material properties, geometric parameters, and crack dimensions. The results revealed that residual stress had negligible impact on bearing capacity, while internal pressure (0→12 MPa) reduced capacity by 44.726%, misalignment (0→3 mm) by 52.982%, and crack depth (1→3 mm) by 47.451%. In contrast, increasing wall thickness (21.4→30.8 mm) enhanced capacity by 101.72%, and raising the weld strength matching coefficient from 0.8 (low-strength matching) to 1.0 (equal-strength matching) improved capacity by 96.234%. Finally, a ResNet18-based prediction model was built using a 10,935-case database from parallel calculations. This model enables rapid prediction of ultimate bearing capacity and provides a technical basis for the design and serviceability evaluation of such welds.
items.authors: Yue Yang, Han Zhang, Dong Zhang, Pengchao Chen, Rui Li, Jian Chen

items.title: The Regular n-Flake Dust in ℝ2 Is Not Minkowski Measurable
items.abstract: The Minkowski measurability of self-similar sets is closely linked to the lattice or non-lattice nature of the contraction ratios of the underlying iterated function system. A long-standing conjecture of Lapidus asserts that under certain conditions a self-similar fractal set is not Minkowski measurable if and only if it is of lattice-type. While the conjecture has been confirmed for self-similar subsets of R, the lattice case remains open in general in higher dimensions. This paper establishes non-Minkowski measurability for a class of regular n-flake dusts in R2. The proof uses hole points to show that the parallel volume fails to be twice differentiable at a critical radius, ruling out constancy of the associated log-periodic normalized volume. These results provide further support for the Lapidus conjecture.
items.authors: Jonas Lippold, Uta Freiberg

items.title: Distinct Cross-Vascular Association Patterns of Carotid Plaque Burden and Vulnerability Features with Coronary Atherosclerotic Burden in Patients Undergoing Carotid Revascularization
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: This study aimed to investigate the associations between preoperative carotid high-resolution magnetic resonance imaging (HR-MRI) plaque features and coronary atherosclerotic burden, and to compare the cross-vascular association patterns of plaque burden-related measures and individual vulnerable plaque features. Methods: This retrospective study included consecutive patients who underwent carotid revascularization and had both preoperative carotid HR-MRI and coronary computed tomography angiography (CTA) between April 2017 and December 2024. Carotid plaque characteristics included calcification, lipid-rich necrotic core (LRNC), intraplaque hemorrhage (IPH), loose matrix (LM), ulceration, maximum wall thickness (MWT), maximum wall area (MWA), and normalized wall index (NWI). Coronary atherosclerotic burden was characterized using coronary artery calcium score (CACS), maximum luminal stenosis, and the number of diseased coronary arteries; the number of coronary arteries with ≥50% stenosis was additionally recorded. Associations between carotid plaque characteristics and coronary atherosclerotic burden were evaluated using correlation analyses and multivariable logistic regression. Results: A total of 162 patients were included (mean age, 66.11 ± 7.54 years; 138 [85.2%] men). CACS ≥ 400 was present in 76 patients (46.9%), obstructive coronary disease (≥50% stenosis in at least one coronary artery) in 96 patients (59.3%), and involvement of ≥3 diseased coronary arteries in 128 patients (79.0%). Greater coronary atherosclerotic burden was consistently associated with higher carotid calcification volume and MWT and NWI (all p 0.05). After adjustment for clinical risk factors and correction for multiple testing, calcification volume, MWT and NWI remained associated with CACS ≥ 400, obstructive coronary disease, and involvement of ≥3 diseased coronary arteries. In contrast, individual vulnerable plaque features, including LRNC, IPH, LM, and ulceration, showed weaker and less consistent associations. Conclusions: In patients undergoing carotid revascularization, preoperative carotid HR-MRI-derived plaque burden-related features showed more consistent associations with coronary atherosclerotic burden than individual vulnerable plaque features. These findings suggest that plaque burden-related and vulnerable plaque features may reflect different aspects of atherosclerosis, with plaque burden-related measures more closely reflecting cumulative systemic atherosclerotic involvement and vulnerable plaque features primarily characterizing local plaque composition and instability.
items.authors: Sunan Xu, Zhenjia Wang, Xinyu Wu, Lu Li, Wei Yu

items.title: Shoulder Muscle Tone, Function, and Factors Associated with Functional Recovery in Patients with Chronic Shoulder Pain: A Non-Randomized Comparative Study of Manual Therapy and Corticosteroid Injection
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: This study aimed to compare the effects of manual therapy (MT) and corticosteroid injection (CI) on shoulder muscle tone, function, and health-related quality of life (HRQOL) in patients with chronic shoulder pain (CSP) and to identify the muscle-tone change most strongly associated with functional recovery. Methods: In this quasi-experimental, non-randomized study, 44 patients with CSP lasting 6 months were allocated to MT (n = 22) or CI (n = 22) according to the treating physician’s judgment. Each group received the assigned intervention for 4 weeks, together with conventional physical therapy and a home-based exercise program. Muscle tone (upper trapezius, anterior deltoid, posterior deltoid, and latissimus dorsi [LD]), the Patient-Specific Functional Scale (PSFS), and HRQOL were assessed at the baseline and at 2 and 4 weeks. Exploratory linear regression analyses examined factors associated with changes in PSFS scores. Results: Both groups showed significant improvements in muscle tone, shoulder function, and HRQOL. Compared with CI, MT produced greater improvements in muscle tone, PSFS scores, and EuroQol Visual Analogue Scale (EQ VAS) scores. All participants achieved the PSFS minimal important change of ≥2 points. The proportion of participants achieving a post hoc exploratory threshold of ≥5 points was higher with MT than with CI (90.9% vs. 13.6%). In separate regression models adjusted for treatment group, changes in LD tone and EQ VAS were each associated with the change in PSFS score. Conclusions: Both groups showed short-term improvements, with greater gains in muscle-tone measures and function in the MT group. These findings do not establish that MT itself is superior to CI, and the exploratory LD association requires confirmation.
items.authors: Yongtae Eom, Youngsook Bae

items.title: Solar Photovoltaic Adoption in Malaysian Upscale and Luxury Hotels: Managerial Barriers and Sustainability Implications
items.abstract: This study investigates solar PV adoption in Malaysia’s upscale and luxury hotel segment, drawing on the Technology Acceptance Model to examine managers’ perceptions of its usefulness and ease of adoption. Using semi-structured interviews with ten managers, comprising a general manager and an engineering manager from each of five upscale and luxury hotels, the study identifies the main opportunities and barriers shaping solar PV adoption in these properties. The interviews were analysed using thematic analysis. The barriers reported include high upfront costs, limited suitable roof and land space, structural constraints, unpredictable weather and perceived insufficiency of institutional support. Although the participating managers generally expressed favourable views towards solar PV, these views did not always lead to implementation. The findings suggest two possible organisational boundary conditions on the application of TAM in this context: implementation feasibility and the separation between managerial evaluation and final decision authority. Favourable managerial evaluations may therefore be insufficient when adoption is financially or physically difficult, or when those evaluating the technology do not hold final approval authority. The findings are exploratory and should be interpreted within the boundaries of the five participating hotels and ten managers.
items.authors: Ningxi Ji, Suresh N. Kannan, Keiwei Chia

items.title: A Lightweight Multi-Sensor Feature-Level Fusion Framework for Noise-Robust Fault Diagnosis of High-Precision Milling Machines
items.abstract: The operational reliability of milling machines is a critical factor affecting manufacturing quality and productivity in modern industrial systems. Although multi-sensor fusion can overcome the limitations of single-sensor monitoring, many existing methods rely on computationally intensive deep learning models, which restrict their applicability in resource-constrained industrial environments. To address this issue, this paper presents a multi-sensor feature-level fusion framework for fault diagnosis in high-precision milling machines. The proposed framework integrates vibration signals from three sensing directions through signal preprocessing, multi-domain feature extraction, random-forest-based feature selection, feature-level fusion, and lightweight neural classification. Within this framework, a lightweight multilayer perceptron (MLP) is adopted as the default classifier to achieve an effective balance between diagnostic performance and computational efficiency for edge-oriented deployment. The experiments consider five machine states, comprising two non-fault operating states (No_Load and Normal) and three abnormal or fault-related states (Eccentricity, Bearing_Housing_Shim_15, and Bearing_Housing_Loose). Experimental results show that the proposed framework substantially outperforms single-sensor approaches, improving diagnostic accuracy from 74.00–86.00% to 96.00%. Comparative analysis across different classifier backbones further demonstrates that the lightweight MLP provides the most favorable efficiency-performance trade-off, while the multi-domain fusion (MDF) mechanism exhibits the strongest robustness under noisy conditions, maintaining 94.38 ± 1.96% accuracy at 0 dB SNR and 88.88 ± 2.53% at −10 dB SNR. These results indicate that accurate, efficient, and noise-robust milling-machine fault diagnosis can be achieved through a coordinated combination of multi-sensor feature fusion, lightweight classification, and robust fusion design, thereby providing a practical solution for intelligent industrial condition monitoring.
items.authors: Zhi Xu, Ningyun Lu, Liguo Jin

items.title: Decoding Biofilm Complexity: Artificial Intelligence, Advanced Imaging, and Multi-Omics for Precision Antibiofilm Strategies
items.abstract: Microbial biofilms are highly structured multicellular communities that exhibit remarkable tolerance to antimicrobial agents and host defenses, contributing to persistent infections, industrial biofouling, food contamination, and environmental challenges. Conventional microbiological approaches have greatly advanced our understanding of biofilm formation but remain insufficient to resolve the spatial, molecular, and functional heterogeneity that underpins biofilm resilience. This review discusses how recent advances in high-resolution imaging, multi-omics technologies, single-cell and spatially resolved analyses, and artificial intelligence (AI) are transforming biofilm research from descriptive observation to precision microbiology. We critically examine state-of-the-art analytical platforms, including confocal and super-resolution microscopy, electron microscopy, Raman-based imaging, genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, and emerging spatial multi-omics approaches, highlighting their complementary roles in deciphering biofilm architecture, regulatory networks, and metabolic specialization. AI/ML approaches are increasingly being applied to image analysis, multimodal data integration, predictive modeling, biomarker identification, and systems-level interpretation of biofilm biology. Furthermore, we discuss how these technological advances are enabling mechanism-based precision antibiofilm strategies, including extracellular polymeric substance-targeting enzymes, quorum-sensing inhibitors, nanotechnology-enabled therapeutics, bacteriophage-based interventions, and synthetic biology approaches. We highlight the major translational challenges, including data standardization, explainable AI, multimodal integration, benchmark datasets, and clinical validation, and outline future directions for developing clinically relevant, data-driven antibiofilm therapies. This review provides an integrated framework connecting advanced analytical technologies with next-generation precision antibiofilm interventions and offers perspectives for accelerating their translation into clinical and industrial applications.
items.authors: Ramandeep Saini, Bishakha Thakur, Ayush Madan, Mantosh Kumar Satapathy

items.title: Physical Characterization of Volcanic Aquifer Systems in the Southwestern Ethiopian Highlands: A Case of the Gilgel Gibe Catchment
items.abstract: Volcanic aquifers are globally important groundwater resources, but their pronounced heterogeneity arising from lava emplacement, volcanic facies, structural features, and differential weathering makes hydrogeological characterization challenging. In many developing regions, limited field data further constrain aquifer characterization, increasing uncertainty in groundwater development and management. This challenge is evident in the Gilgel Gibe Catchment, where increasing groundwater demand and limited hydrogeological information require improved understanding of aquifer properties and productivity. This study characterized the aquifer systems of the Gilgel Gibe catchment primarily through lithological log and pumping test interpretations, supported by spring discharge measurements. A total of 30 deep boreholes were analyzed using pumping test data, including 14 with suitable recovery test data. Lithostratigraphic logs were integrated with diagnostic plots to identify aquifer conditions and select appropriate analytical solutions. The aquifer system is predominantly confined, followed by leaky-confined and locally unconfined conditions, interpreted using the Theis, Hantush-Jacob, and Neuman methods, respectively. Estimated transmissivity ranges from 3.9 × 10−6 to 1.3 × 10−2 m2/s, while spring discharges varied from 0.002 to 5 L/s. The Setema, Upper, Middle, and Lower Basalt, and Trachyte flows form low to moderately productive, fracture-controlled aquifers. The Lower Pyroclastic deposits and stratified tuffs form low-productivity aquifers due to the predominance of tuffs, while rhyolite exhibits low productivity due to the predominance of massive lava layers. Alluvial deposits form shallow aquifers dominated by intergranular porosity, underlain mainly by low-permeability tuffaceous materials. These findings provide a hydrogeological basis for guiding groundwater exploration, supporting well-field development, and informing sustainable groundwater management in volcanic terrains.
items.authors: Fayera Gudu Tufa, Fekadu Fufa Feyessa, Adisu Befekadu Kebede, Wagari Mosisa Kitessa, Seifu Kebede Debela, Alemu Yenehun

items.title: Isolation and Functional Characterization of Heyndrickxia shackletonii and Bacillus subtilis from a Biofertilizer with Strong Antagonistic Activity Against Ganoderma boninense
items.abstract: This study investigated culturable bacteria isolated from the commercial oil palm biofertilizer CRPO for antagonistic activity against Ganoderma boninense and plant growth-promoting traits. Based on 16S rRNA gene sequencing, the isolates were putatively identified as Heyndrickxia shackletonii K3 and Bacillus subtilis K8. These two bacterial isolates exhibited significant antagonistic activity against G. boninense, with percentage inhibition of radial growth exceeding 89.0% and volatile organic compound-mediated percentage inhibition of mycelial growth of 45.2% and 38.1%, respectively. Enzyme screening revealed that isolate K8 produced chitinase, cellulase, and lipase, which may contribute to its significant Ganoderma-inhibitory activity. In terms of plant growth-promoting traits, isolate K3 showed a diverse range of plant growth-promoting characteristics, displaying all seven tested traits, whereas isolate K8 was positive for nitrogen fixation, 1-aminocyclopropane-1-carboxylate deaminase activity, and ammonia production. The in vitro antagonistic activity and plant growth-promoting-associated traits of K3 and K8 warrant greenhouse and field trials to determine whether these isolates can suppress basal stem rot and enhance oil palm growth and resilience.

items.title: Effects of Formulation and Electrode Parameters on the Ignition Performance of Electrically Controlled Solid Propellant
items.abstract: This study investigates the effects of flame-retardant fillers, mesh electrode geometry, electrode material, propellant thickness, and applied voltage on the ignition and combustion performance of a perchlorate-based Electrically Controlled Solid Propellant (ECSP). Resistivity measurements show that phenolic resin (BS) increases resistivity by 82.8% (to 78.33 Ω·m), whereas decabromodiphenyl ether (BW) decreases it by 32.3% (to 29.04 Ω·m), relative to the base formulation (42.9 Ω·m). Finite element simulations reveal that current density concentrates at electrode–propellant contact points and decreases with increasing wire diameter and mesh number, whereas average current density exhibits a non-monotonic trend with mesh number. Thermal stress analysis indicates that pore size affects interfacial stress more significantly than wire diameter, and larger pores increase the risk of debonding. Ignition experiments demonstrate that asymmetric electrode configurations generate current density disparities that override polarity effects in determining the ignition sequence. The influence of electrode material follows the order Ti SS Cu and is independent of polarity. Ignition delay increases with propellant thickness, whereas thicknesses below 3 mm are prone to uncontrolled combustion. Under the present electrode configuration and test method, ignition proceeded very slowly at applied voltages below 60 V, whereas ignition occurred readily above 70 V. These findings provide practical guidance for electrode design and operational optimization in electrically controlled solid propulsion systems.
items.authors: Rongyao Zhi, Zhe Zhang, Xiong Zhou, Yanan Wang, Gang Chen, Guodong Li

items.title: Fuzzy Fault Detection and Band-Conditioned Data Quality Assessment for Sensor Streams: A Continuous Glucose Monitoring Case Study
items.abstract: Sensor faults can propagate beyond raw measurements and distort the aggregates used to interpret a monitored phenomenon. We propose a domain-agnostic, five-layer fuzzy pipeline that characterizes the reliability of a sensor stream jointly over time and value bands and carries it through to every derived aggregate: (L1) fault tagging of each sample against five fuzzy failure primitives; (L2) fuzzy windowing; (L3) band reliability; (L4) routed repair with propagated reconstruction uncertainty; and (L5) veracity aggregation with linguistic protoforms. An end-to-end acquisition architecture is also specified. The pipeline was instantiated for continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) with clinical knowledge of glucose dynamics and applied to a 14-month recording of an adult with type 1 diabetes (FreeStyle Libre 3, 5-min cadence), of which 294 days contained at least 120 readings. Clean reference days remained essentially unchanged (mean sample quality 0.98–0.99). On the most corrupted day, the estimated time below range fell from 16% to 3%, with a veracity of only 0.14. Over the recording, 38% of the days were too unreliable to phenotype and 5% changed phenotype. Joint time- and band-conditioned reliability assessment thus prevents corrupted sensor data from producing falsely precise clinical conclusions.
items.authors: Juan F. Gaitán-Guerrero, Carmen Martínez-Cruz, Macarena Espinilla, José L. López

items.title: Energy Trade and Welfare Effects of the 2025 US–China Tariff Shocks: A Recursively Updated GTAP Analysis
items.abstract: The 2025 tariff escalation between the United States (US) and China generated uneven macroeconomic and energy-trade effects. Using a Global Trade Analysis Project (GTAP) model updated recursively to a common 2023 benchmark, we analyze five independent cumulative-tariff scenarios, a sequential experiment, and five Armington-elasticity settings. Under the peak 145% common-baseline scenario S4, China’s equivalent variation falls by USD 203.59 billion and real GDP by 0.59%, whereas US welfare rises by USD 41.43 billion despite a 0.19% GDP decline. China incurs allocative-efficiency and terms-of-trade losses, while the US terms-of-trade gain exceeds its allocative-efficiency loss. These S4 macroeconomic directions remain robust across the elasticity settings. Energy responses are heterogeneous: China’s natural-gas output falls by 11.21%, US electricity output rises by 17.32%, China’s electricity imports increase by 97.62%, and US coal imports increase by 108.32%. All S4 energy-import responses remain positive across the elasticity settings, although some output and export responses change direction. Third-party energy-trade increases are more frequent than decreases but vary across products and economies. In the sequential S5 experiment, reducing the tariff shock from 145% to 30% raises real GDP in both countries relative to S4 but reverses the welfare pattern: China gains, whereas the US loses. Overall, tariff de-escalation eases output losses without producing symmetric welfare gains.
items.authors: Tingting Wang, Yuqing Jiang

items.title: Influence of Horizontal Bike Lane Curve Geometry on Micromobility Users’ Operational Behaviour: A Test Track Study with Bicycles and E-Scooters
items.abstract: Micromobility requires comfortable and safe cycling infrastructure. However, evidence-based geometric design criteria remain limited, particularly regarding the influence of horizontal curve geometry on cyclists and e-scooter riders. This study investigates the influence of horizontal curve geometry in bike lanes on speed and trajectory under controlled experimental conditions. A closed-circuit test track comprising eight horizontal curves with a constant radius of 5 m and deflection angles from 30° to 105° was used. Cyclists and e-scooter riders performed left- and right-turn manoeuvres under free-flow conditions. Operational data were extracted through video-based image analysis and analysed using descriptive, repeatability, and non-parametric inferential methods. Minimum operating speeds generally decreased with increasing deflection angle, with significant differences mainly between lower- and higher-deflection configurations. Male participants exhibited higher mean minimum speeds, although after correction for multiple comparisons, a significant gender difference remained only at 75°. No systematic gender-related differences in lateral positioning were identified. Trajectory behaviour showed direction-dependent differences, while minimum-speed location and longitudinal speed variation differed across experimental configurations. Overall, the findings provide an experimental basis for developing behaviourally informed geometric design criteria for urban micromobility infrastructure.
items.authors: Mustafa Salah Abdulhussein Al-Hakeem, Alejandra Sofía Fonseca-Cabrera, David Llopis-Castelló, Alfredo García

items.title: Growth and Clinical Outcomes Before and After Implementation of a Donor Human Milk Program in Very Preterm and/or Very-Low-Birth-Weight Infants
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: Mother’s own milk (MOM) is widely recognized as the best source of nutrition for premature infants, with donor human milk (DHM) as the next recommended option. However, it remains controversial whether DHM confers the same benefits as MOM. We aimed to compare growth and clinical outcomes in very-low-birth-weight (VLBW) infants before and after the introduction of DHM in our Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU). Methods: This is a retrospective cohort of VLBW and/or very-low-birth-weight infants born between January 2018 and June 2023. Infants were divided based on birth date into Epoch-1 (pre-DHM, N = 98) and Epoch-2 (post-DHM, N = 138). Feeding groups included exclusive MOM (N = 112), MOM + DHM (N = 71), and MOM + Formula (N = 39). Baseline characteristics were compared between groups. The primary outcome was weight gain; secondary outcomes included incidence of necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC), time to full enteral feeding, and length of hospitalization. Multivariable regression models were used to assess these outcomes while adjusting for relevant confounders. Results: Infants in Epoch-2 were born at a significantly higher gestational age (29.3 vs. 28.2 weeks, p 0.001) and had a higher median birth weight (1350 g vs. 1080 g, p 0.001) compared to Epoch-1. In this before-and-after cohort, the post-DHM implementation epoch was not independently associated with differences in growth or complication rates after adjustment. Time to reach full enteral feeding was significantly shorter in the post-DHM epoch (B = −0.255, p 0.001). Conclusions: DHM had no independent effect on growth or complication rates but was associated with earlier achievement of full enteral feeding. Further studies are needed to evaluate its contribution to neonatal clinical outcomes.

items.title: Pre-Harvest Fresh Biomass Estimation of Lavandula × intermedia from UAV-RGB Images: A Controlled Evaluation of FiLM-Based Visual-Numerical Fusion
items.abstract: Estimating fresh biomass prior to harvest can facilitate the planning of lavender harvesting. This study assessed the integration of UAV-RGB visual and numerical data using 459 original images, representing 287 plant-year units from three distinct field-year campaigns. A fixed grouped partition facilitated 135 runs across five input/fusion groups, nine backbones, and three training seeds. The Model17-FiLM demonstrated a seed-level mean R2 of 0.934 ± 0.010 and an RMSE of 178.2 ± 13.8 g, in contrast to the RGB-only Base model, which showed 0.910 ± 0.021 and 208.4 ± 25.6 g. When predictions were averaged across all nine backbones and three seeds, the RMSE decreased from 196.78 g for the Base model to 166.27 g for Model16 and 163.32 g for Model17-FiLM. Pointwise bootstrap intervals indicated the benefit of incorporating the descriptor branch, although the contribution to harvest timing remained uncertain. FiLM produced lower point-estimate errors compared to concatenation, without consistent multiplicity-adjusted support. The numerical-only RF17 model resulted in an RMSE of 423.52 g. Model21 did not enhance predictive accuracy and included redundant nominal scale inputs. The restriction to persistent plants maintained the principal ranking, while audits of acquisition sessions and markers revealed contextual sensitivity. Expanded Grad-CAM analysis demonstrated a strong dependence on the backbone. These findings endorse the evaluated approach within this dataset, though caution is advised against general deployment without independent validation across different field-years.
items.authors: Fatih Bozkurt, Mustafa Teke, Fecir Duran

items.title: On the Schwartz Distribution Approach to Local Volatility for European Option in a Generalised Jump Model with Stochastic Interest Rate
items.abstract: The Dupire formula is commonly regarded as a convenient analytical tool for the valuation of financial derivatives. In this paper, we continue the analytical treatment developed in our previous papers, deriving the aforementioned formula for the European call option in the space of distributions. We consider asset prices driven by Lévy-type stochastic integrals in a framework that allows flexible jump structures and contains a class of stochastic short-rate models, including the Vasicek model. We prove existence and uniqueness for the underlying SDE and establish the Dupire formula in this general setting. More explicit versions of the Dupire formulas are obtained for two models: Merton’s model with the Vasicek short rate, and a model with time-dependent jump scaling.
items.authors: Piotr Nowak, Dariusz Gatarek

items.title: Exercise-Associated Gut Microbiota Remodeling and Cardiovascular Protection: Potential Mechanisms Involving Inflammatory Regulation
items.abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains a major contributor to global mortality and disease burden and encompasses a range of conditions commonly associated with metabolic disturbances, endothelial dysfunction, and chronic inflammation. Emerging evidence suggests that persistent low-grade inflammation contributes to the development and progression of CVD and represents an important component of its pathophysiology. The gut microbiota (GM) and microbiota-related metabolites are increasingly recognized as important regulators of host metabolism and immune homeostasis. GM dysbiosis may influence cardiovascular inflammation through alterations in microbial metabolites, intestinal barrier function, and inflammatory signaling, including the TLR4/NF-κB/NLRP3 pathway and immunoregulatory mechanisms involving IL-10 and context-dependent TGF-β signaling. Accumulating experimental and clinical evidence suggests that exercise may reshape GM composition and microbial metabolic profiles and may be associated with changes in inflammatory and immunoregulatory responses relevant to cardiovascular health. Evidence from atherosclerosis, hypertension, myocardial infarction, and myocardial ischemia–reperfusion injury further supports disease-specific associations among exercise, GM alterations, inflammatory signaling, and cardiovascular outcomes. Therefore, this review synthesizes current mechanistic, animal, and human evidence on these interconnected processes, with particular emphasis on the TLR4/NF-κB/NLRP3 and IL-10/TGF-β-related signaling pathways. Overall, current evidence supports disease-specific associations and potential mechanistic links among exercise, GM alterations, microbial metabolites, inflammatory regulation, and cardiovascular outcomes; however, the GM has not yet been established as a universal or causal mediator of exercise-related cardiovascular protection.
items.authors: Xinxin Liu, Dandan Jing, Xuan Liu, Shujuan Hu, Xianwang Wang

items.title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Emergency Medical Supply Request Regulation in Healthcare Supply Chains
items.abstract: Public health emergencies place acute pressure on medical supply systems. This study develops Med-iDR-MARL, a hierarchical multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) framework for regulating hospital requests before allocation. Regional incentives influence hospital responses for deferrable (DD) and reducible (RD) demand, while a local scheduler retains non-deferrable (ND) demand and applies hospital-level service bounds. Across 20 simulated 30-day windows, the framework reduced DD/RD requests by 37.71% with mean incentive expenditure of CNY 274,844.23, compared with 31.03% and CNY 350,038.43 for Rule-Adaptive. Independent hospital-agent deep Q-network learning achieved greater reduction, lower expenditure, and better pooled reduction per unit expenditure. The proposed framework also had the highest peak-to-average ratio despite lower absolute peaks than No-DR. In a separate five-seed ablation, removing the minimum-service guard increased the hospital-day violation rate from zero to 58.95%. Local scheduler diagnostics found feasible solutions in 132,000 tested states but material optimality gaps and no consistent runtime advantage over vectorized exact enumeration. The results identify conditional efficiency and service trade-offs. The Shanghai COVID-19 series supplies an external risk trajectory; hospital behavior, clinical outcomes, and operational logistics remain unvalidated.
items.authors: Fengjue Xie, Jie Wang, Jinghui Yang

items.title: Unraveling Vulnerabilities and Pathways Responsible for AITL Malignancy to Improve Patients’ Treatment
items.abstract: Angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma (AITL) is an aggressive subtype of peripheral T-cell lymphoma characterized by poor clinical outcomes following conventional CHOP-based chemotherapy and the lack of effective disease-specific therapeutic options. The disease finds its origin in CD4 follicular helper T (Tfh) cells and is driven by recurrent genetic alterations, including mutations in TET2, RHOA, DNMT3A, and IDH2. Despite the rarity of AITL, preclinical models have been fundamental in elucidating disease pathogenesis, identifying key molecular vulnerabilities and providing platforms for the evaluation of novel therapeutic strategies. These studies have highlighted multiple targetable pathways, including aberrant mTOR, T-cell receptor and NF-κB signaling. Additionally, widespread epigenetic alterations in the neoplastic T-cells were uncovered due to mutations in epigenetic modifiers in AITL. More recently, metabolic reprogramming has emerged as an additional therapeutic vulnerability, revealing a strong dependence of AITL cells on mitochondrial respiration and lipid metabolism, particularly the choline metabolic pathway. Advances in the understanding of AITL biology have also accelerated the development of immunotherapeutic strategies. Monoclonal antibodies, antibody–drug conjugates, bispecific antibodies, immune checkpoint inhibitors and chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapies have shown encouraging preclinical and early clinical activity. Of note, the first preclinical results on an in vivo CAR-T-cell approach for AITL are reported. Here we provide a broad overview of AITL, discussing its biological features, pathogenesis, preclinical models, current treatment landscape, and recent advances in therapeutic approaches.
items.authors: Chiara Martinello, Adrien Krug, Pau Marin-Escudero, Aurélia Pollet, François Lemonnier, Laurent Boyer

items.title: Thermally Tunable Ultra-Broadband Terahertz Metasurface Absorber Based on VO2 Phase Transition
items.abstract: Vanadium dioxide (VO2), owing to its reversible insulator-to-metal phase transition, is a promising material for tunable terahertz (THz) devices. In this work, a compact VO2-based terahertz absorber is numerically proposed to achieve thermally tunable ultra-broadband absorption. The proposed single-layer metasurface employs a fourfold-symmetric integration of cross-shaped, circular-ring, and square-frame elements to induce multiple coupled resonances and their spectral overlap, providing a design strategy for broadening the absorption bandwidth while maintaining polarization-insensitive operation. The optimized structure exhibits five near-perfect absorption resonances at 3.23, 5.27, 7.34, 8.82, and 9.73 THz. At a VO2 conductivity of 2.0 × 105 S/m, the absorber achieves absorptance exceeding 90% from 2.95 to 10.36 THz, corresponding to a bandwidth of 7.41 THz and a relative bandwidth of 111.35%. The absorption mechanism is attributed to the hybridization of multiple resonant modes and effective impedance matching with free space, as confirmed by electromagnetic field and impedance analyses. Furthermore, the absorption response can be dynamically tuned through the phase transition of VO2. The absorber also exhibits polarization-insensitive behavior and maintains high absorptance over a wide range of incident angles. These results demonstrate a compact and thermally reconfigurable platform for terahertz imaging, sensing, spectroscopy, and adaptive electromagnetic stealth.
items.authors: Ahmed Ali, Hamid Sharif, Asrafali Barkathulla, Wazie M. Abdulkawi, Majeed A. S. Alkanhal, Yosef T. Aladadi

items.title: An Emerging Omega-3 Fatty Acid—Octadecapentaenoic Acid (18:5n-3): Biosynthesis, Potential Sources and Applications
items.abstract: Octadecapentaenoic acid (OPA, 18:5n-3) is an emerging and poorly characterized omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acid (PUFA) that is primarily produced by certain marine microalgae. Although it is structurally similar to the well-studied eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA, 20:5n-3) and docosahexaenoic acid (DHA, 22:6n-3), OPA’s specific biological and ecological roles remain largely unknown. The purpose of this review is to comprehensively examine and critically analyze the current knowledge on OPA, including its biosynthesis, natural sources, and metabolic fate in consumers to assess its functional and nutraceutical potential. Current evidence suggests that OPA contributes to membrane structure in primary producers but is rapidly metabolized in consumers, acting more as an energy source or metabolic intermediate rather than a stored end product. While OPA shows the potential for applications in aquaculture and human nutrition, its practical utility is largely inferred from structurally related fatty acids. Many application questions remain unanswered due to its low natural abundance, analytical challenges, and a lack of targeted functional studies. Future research is therefore required for a better understanding its stability, bioactivity and metabolism to determine its true functional importance and practical uses.
items.authors: Kaiwen Sun, Jamie Merilees, Xiao Qiu

items.title: Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion with the Watchman FLX Device: A Single-Centre Retrospective Analysis of Procedural and One-Year Clinical Outcomes
items.abstract: Background: Left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) is an alternative approach to stroke prevention in selected patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation. This single-centre retrospective study describes device implantation, peri-procedural complications and clinical outcomes during the first year after Watchman FLX implantation. Methods: We analysed 100 consecutive patients who underwent LAAO with the Watchman FLX device at Helios Frankenwaldklinik-Hospital, Kronach, Germany, between 2021 and 2024. The primary endpoint was device implantation success, defined as correct device deployment and implantation. The secondary safety endpoint was a composite of major peri-procedural complications within 72 h. Additional clinical outcomes were strokes and mortality at 30 days and one year. Results: The mean age was 70.7 ± 6.5 years, and 47% of patients were female. The mean CHA2DS2-VASc score was 4.9 ± 1.4, and the mean HAS-BLED score was 4.1 ± 1.0. Device implantation was successful in 100% (95% CI 96.4–100%). The reported peri-procedural complication rate was 7% (95% CI 2.9–13.9%), including major bleeding in 6% (95% CI 2.2–12.6%) and pericardial tamponade in 1% (95% CI 0.0–5.4%). Thirty-day mortality was 2% (95% CI 0.2–7.0%), with no reported strokes (0%; 95% CI 0.0–3.6%). One-year mortality was 11% (95% CI 5.6–18.8%), with one reported stroke (1%; 95% CI 0.0–5.4%). Conclusions: Watchman FLX implantation was achieved in all patients in this cohort. Bleeding was the most frequently reported peri-procedural complication. The low observed stroke proportion should be interpreted alongside the 11% one-year mortality and incomplete imaging surveillance. This uncontrolled descriptive study cannot establish comparative efficacy or comprehensive device safety.
items.authors: Wasim Allakkis, Mostafa Salem, Mohamed Salem, Mohamed Elabd, Ali Balakishiyev, Moussab Aboud

items.title: Analytical Guidance for Reentry Vehicles Based on Range–Energy Efficiency
items.abstract: To address the reentry guidance problem of hypersonic glide vehicles under complex constraints and terminal area energy management (TAEM), a nonlinear analytical guidance method based on the concept of range–energy efficiency (REE) is proposed. First, a linear energy dissipation mode is proposed following an analysis of the dynamic relationship between energy and range-to-go. By establishing the REE variable based on this energy dissipation mode, the method transforms the problem of tracking the energy versus range-to-go profile into a time-domain regulation problem of REE. It eliminates the need for optimal design of profile parameters and prediction of range-to-go. Subsequently, a nonlinear guidance model for normalized range-to-go and energy is established. A fixed-time analytical guidance law with filter error compensation is then designed, enabling approximately linear convergence of normalized range-to-go and energy, thereby achieving effective regulation of REE. Finally, numerical simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method exhibits mission adaptability and robustness against uncertainties in aerodynamic coefficients, validating its effectiveness for online guidance applications.
items.authors: Youhan Luo, Nan Yang, Naigang Cui

items.title: Ti3C2Tx MXene-Supported Anisotropic Crystallisation of Solvent-Casted p(VDF-TrFE) Films for Improved Elastic Deformation and Piezoelectric Response
items.abstract: This study investigates the percolation limit of solvent-casted p(VDF-TrFE) film through its processing (thermal treatment) and the addition of 2D Ti3C2Tx MXene, by evaluating their distribution using SEM-EDX and determining the electroactive crystalline phases using FTIR and XRD spectroscopies, while evaluating the film’s dielectric permittivity and piezoelectric response after a mechanical deformation cycle (elongation). The robust interactions of the -CH2/-CF2 groups of copolymer (55/45 mol%) with the terminal groups (-OH/F) of MXene influence their distributions and alignment along the MXene nanosheets, and, consequently, the higher and anisotropically distributed β-phase crystallinity near its percolation limit (0.0015 w/w% of loading). This exhibited a piezoelectric behaviour of d33 ~19 pC/N after e-polishing and ~24 pC/N after 50% of elongation performed at an ambient temperature. Such an interconnected and uniform film achieves a dielectric permittivity of ~22, exhibits intrinsic flexibility (fracture resistance), and facilitates effective load transfer during elastic deformation while maintaining the piezoelectric response, which could not be achieved for a pure p(VDF-TrFE) film.
items.authors: Vanja Kokol, Branko Nečemer, Eugenio Gibertini, Vid Bobnar

items.title: Design and Implementation of Semi-Automatic Image Annotation System Based on You Only Look Once Version 8
items.authors: Ming-Yang Chen, Ching-Min Lee

items.title: Discordance Between Surface Wetting and Soil Salinity Responses and Low Persistence of Soil Salinity Ranks After Autumn and Spring Irrigation
items.abstract: Irrigation is expected to increase soil water and promote salt leaching in salt-affected farmland, yet wetter soil does not necessarily mean lower salinity, and relative salinity positions may shift after irrigation. This observational before-and-after study compared soil conditions around two seasonal irrigation events in the Hetao Irrigation District, Inner Mongolia, using 344 field observations collected before and after autumn and spring irrigation. From these observations, 89 unambiguous co-located pre- and post-irrigation pairs were established, including 37 autumn and 52 spring pairs. Soil moisture (SM) was measured in the 0–10 cm surface layer, whereas EC was determined as EC1:5 by averaging measurements from the three soil layers (0–30 cm). Surface SM increased at all paired sites, but the 0–30 cm mean EC1:5 responses varied markedly. Under an operational classification based on the relative change in EC1:5, a decrease of at least 10% was defined as “effective desalination”; this response occurred at 54.1% and 53.8% of the autumn- and spring-irrigation sites, respectively, whereas EC1:5 increased by at least 10% at 37.8% and 26.9% of the sites. These inverse responses remained evident under alternative relative and absolute thresholds, and the magnitude of soil wetting was not significantly related to the net change in EC1:5. Salinity ranks were also poorly preserved across irrigation events. Same-quartile retention was only 32.4% after autumn irrigation and 23.1% after spring irrigation, while 55.6% and 84.6% of the post-irrigation Q4 sites had not belonged to Q4 before irrigation. These results show that surface wetting and the 0–30 cm mean EC response were not consistently aligned at the sampled locations, while relative salinity ranks showed limited short-term persistence. These point-level findings do not demonstrate reorganization of the continuous district-wide salinity pattern. Whether post-irrigation salinity verification or map updating improves monitoring performance requires validation using spatially representative mapped data.
items.authors: Meichen Liu, Jing Gao, Bo Wang

items.title: Digitalization and Occupational Polarization in Indonesia: Evidence from the Labor Market
items.abstract: Rapid digitalization is reshaping labor markets, yet its effects on occupational polarization remain underexplored in emerging economies. This study investigates how internet use and digital technology adoption influence occupational outcomes across low-, middle-, and high-skilled workers in Indonesia while accounting for generational differences. Using nationally representative microdata from the 2024 Indonesian National Labor Force Survey (SAKERNAS) covering 382,920 working-age individuals, this study employs a multinomial logit model with average marginal effects to estimate occupational attainment. The results reveal a clear occupational hollowing-out pattern: digitalization reduces the likelihood of low- and middle-skilled employment while increasing the probability of high-skilled occupations. These effects are more pronounced among Millennials and Generation Z, indicating greater adaptability to digital transformation than older generations. Education, work experience, and job training further promote occupational upgrading, whereas gender disparities and spatial inequalities continue to constrain labor market opportunities. By providing micro-level evidence from an emerging economy, this study extends the literature on digitalization and occupational polarization and highlights the importance of inclusive policies that strengthen digital skills, lifelong learning, and equitable access to opportunities in the digital labor market.
items.authors: Purmini, Ririn Nopiah, Eka Dewi Anggraini

items.title: Near-Real-Time Wildfire Segmentation and Brightness Temperature Estimation from Geostationary Satellite Imagery Using Deep Learning
items.abstract: Near-real-time wildfire monitoring is essential for situational awareness and emergency response. The Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellite (GOES) observes at 2 km every 5 min, whereas the Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS) observes at 375 m twice daily, leaving neither sensor able to track rapidly evolving fires in fine spatial detail. This study introduces a two-step deep learning approach that statistically infers VIIRS-like sub-pixel fire segmentation and brightness temperature (BT) from GOES imagery. The dataset comprises 257 U.S. wildfires within preselected regions of interest, pairing multi-spectral GOES imagery with VIIRS-derived references in four classes (Non-Fire, Small, Medium, and Large) defined by the number of fire pixels. Against an autoencoder-based baseline, the proposed method raises average precision from 0.105 to 0.368 and reduces the fire region BT root mean square error by 72.1% from 81.33 K to 22.69 K. Omission error rates fall from 9.41% to 1.96% for Medium fires and remain at zero for Large fires, whereas Small fires, 37% of the test set, remain at 39.91%. The false positive rate on Non-Fire images falls from 66.86% to 8.48%, near the operational GOES product’s 6.36% with lower omission (31.40% versus 40.35%). Inference completes within 5 min of observation for a monitored region.
items.authors: Ryota Yagi, Mukul Badhan, Majid Bavandpour, Kasra Shamsaei, Dani Or, George Bebis

items.title: Spin Spiral vs. Spin Stripe in La2−xBaxCuO4 (x = 18): Analysis of μSR Data
items.abstract: There are two models that explain the incommensurate elastic neutron scattering from La2−xBaxCuO4 (x=18), (i) spin spiral and (ii) collinear spin stripe. I show that available μSR data taken with a polycrystalline sample is consistent with the generic (arbitrary parameters) coplanar spin spiral. On the other hand for consistency with the collinear spin stripe one needs fine tuning of the parameters of the model. I also propose a further μSR experiment with a single crystal aimed specifically at the window of parameters where the spin stripe model is still consistent with the data. In the proposed experiment, the expected signals for these two models are dramatically different. Such an experiment would finally reject one of the models.
items.authors: Oleg P. Sushkov

items.title: The Informal Care Burden of Older Adults with Disability, Dementia, and Concurrent Cardiometabolic Multimorbidity: A Qualitative Study Based on Social Ecosystem Theory
items.abstract: Background: The co-occurrence of disability, dementia, and cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM) creates a highly complex home-care context requiring informal caregivers to simultaneously provide daily living assistance, cognitive and behavioral support, and management of multiple chronic conditions, yet the multidimensional burden these caregivers bear remains poorly understood. Objective: To explore the caregiving burden and associated factors among primary informal caregivers of older adults with disability, dementia, and concurrent CMM, and to interpret them from a social–ecological systems perspective. Methods: A descriptive qualitative study was conducted. Purposive sampling recruited 26 primary informal caregivers from urban and surrounding rural areas of Shihezi, Xinjiang, for semi-structured interviews. All care recipients had impaired functional ability, clinically confirmed dementia, and at least two cardiometabolic diseases. Data were analyzed inductively with Colaizzi’s seven-step method, followed by interpretive mapping based on social–ecological systems theory. Results: At the micro level, burden mainly involved accumulated complex caregiving tasks, decision-making uncertainty, and physical and psychological exhaustion. At the mezzo level, caregiving responsibility was concentrated in individual family members, and community support was inadequately tailored to these families’ needs. At the macro level, caregivers’ use of external support was shaped by institutional accessibility, geographic distribution of care resources, and sociocultural expectations. Factors across levels interacted and jointly determined overall burden. Conclusions: The burden of informal caregivers of older adults with disability, dementia, and concurrent CMM is multidimensional and multilevel. Nursing and long-term care support should promote family sharing of caregiving responsibility, continuous professional support, and better family–external resource coordination to enhance the sustainability of home-based care.
items.authors: Yuting Yang, Reyisaimu Wumaierjiang, Lin Xia, Xiaolong Wang, Yulong Ma, Mingxia Jing

items.title: Glucocorticoid Receptor Alpha as an Integrative Regulator of Host Defense: A Systems-Level Review and Framework for Immune Regulation and Homeostatic Correction
items.abstract: Current concepts recognize that effective host defense depends on coordinated interactions among innate and adaptive immunity, inflammatory signaling, immunometabolic regulation, and multiple complementary adaptive biological processes. However, far less attention has focused on the regulatory systems that integrate these diverse responses across the evolving phases of the host response. This Review proposes that glucocorticoid receptor alpha (GRα) functions as a systems-level integrative regulator that may contribute to the integration of immune signaling, antimicrobial competence, mitochondrial bioenergetics, inflammatory regulation, and other adaptive processes across partially overlapping adaptive phases of homeostatic correction. A central premise is that these phase-specific actions are shaped by dynamic changes in chromatin accessibility and transcription-factor interactions, providing a molecular basis for differential GRα regulation throughout the adaptive response. Rather than functioning solely as a transcriptional regulator of inflammation, GRα influences biological processes involved in pathogen sensing, NF-κB/AP-1 signaling, immunometabolic adaptation, innate and adaptive immune responses, endothelial and epithelial barrier integrity, lymphatic function, tissue repair, and the transition from early host defense to inflammatory resolution and restoration of physiological homeostasis. These integrated biological processes are organized within the proposed Priming, Modulatory, and Restorative phases of homeostatic correction. By synthesizing evidence across multiple physiological systems, this Review provides a biologically plausible model for understanding how GRα-associated regulatory mechanisms may contribute to immune effectiveness, disease tolerance, host-defense outcomes, and adaptive recovery during infection and critical illness. The proposed model generates testable hypotheses to guide future mechanistic investigation and the development of precision therapeutic strategies.
items.authors: Gianfranco Umberto Meduri

items.title: Effect of Dendrobium officinale Leaf Extract on the Growth and Metabolism of Streptococcus thermophilus, a Most Commonly Used Bacterium in Yogurt Production
items.abstract: Dendrobium officinale leaf contains a variety of bioactive compounds, and has the potential to be used for functional yogurt production. However, the compounds in D. officinale leaf may affect the growth and metabolism of lactic acid bacteria. In this work, extracts from different dosages of D. officinale leaves were added into the media of Streptococcus thermophilus (one of the most commonly used lactic acid bacteria in yogurt production), and the biomass, lactic acid content, glucose uptake capacity, and cellular metabolic/reducing activity were analyzed. Simultaneously, the changes in biomass, lactic acid production capacity, and key enzyme activities were determined during the 24 h fermentation. Furthermore, transcriptomics analysis was performed to explore the molecular mechanisms. Results showed that D. officinale leaf extract can promote the growth, cellular metabolic/reducing activity, glucose uptake, lactic acid production, and β-galactosidase, glucokinase, pyruvate decarboxylase and lactic dehydrogenase activities of S. thermophilus at the appropriate dosage, and the extract from 4% (w/v) leaves is optimal. Further transcriptomic analysis revealed that D. officinale leaf extract enhances the growth and metabolism of S. thermophilus by up-regulating the expression of genes related to amino acid metabolism, translation, membrane transport, carbohydrate metabolism, energy metabolism, and nucleotide metabolism. These findings will provide a theoretical basis for the utilization of D. officinale leaves to fortify the health function of yogurt.
items.authors: Junchao Lu, Lingyu Li, Hang Qu, Bo Chen, Hailong Yang

items.title: Nanoclay-Stabilized Hybrid Pigments from Plant and Biowaste Extracts for Cotton Printing: Color and Fastness Performance
items.abstract: Selected low-impact extracts from red cabbage, spent coffee grounds, Pisolithus sp., orange peel, Iris germanica petals, dragon fruit peel and pine bark were immobilized on halloysite (HA), hydrotalcite (HT) and laponite (LAP) and evaluated as hybrid pigments for cotton printing. A four-run 2(3−1) fractional factorial screening design examined acidification, surfactant and silane additions. Diffuse reflectance, CIELAB coordinates and K/Smax within 400–700 nm characterized powders and prints; HA and LAP formulations with the most useful colors were additionally evaluated for light, washing and rubbing fastness. The clay host strongly influenced the optical response. LAP generally produced the darkest powders and highest color strength, whereas HT gave paler, more yellow and less saturated prints and was not advanced to the fastness stage. HA offered the best balance between color development and durability. HA-based coffee, red cabbage and Pisolithus prints reached light-fastness ratings of 5–7, washing ratings around 4–5 and dry/wet rubbing ratings up to 5/4–5. The combined HCl/surfactant/silane formulation (run 4) consistently provided the best fastness among tested HA and LAP systems. The results extend a companion extraction-screening study and demonstrate a mostly aqueous route from plant and biowaste residues to printable hybrid pigments with potential for sustainable and multifunctional textile coloration.
items.authors: Belén Lema-Amores, Antonio Belda, Daniel López-Rodríguez, Jorge Jordán-Núñez, Álvaro-Francisco Morote, Bàrbara Micó-Vicent

items.title: Multibeam Laser Telemetry for Head Protection of Visually Impaired Individuals
items.abstract: For individuals with visual impairment, traditional long canes provide insufficient protection against hazards at torso or head height. While various Electronic Travel Aids (ETAs) have been developed as complementary tools, a fully reliable solution for head protection remains elusive. Existing technologies do not yet provide a reliable and robust sensing solution suitable for all environments and all obstacle types. To address these limitations, this study presents the design and preliminary validation of a proof-of-concept multibeam laser triangulation architecture intended for head-level obstacle detection. The device uses a near-infrared (850 nm) laser source, split into three beams via a holographic grating, and a CMOS camera equipped with interference filters for signal acquisition. The hardware architecture integrates an FPGA and a low-RAM microcontroller to minimize power consumption, facilitating its use as a portable embedded device. Preliminary controlled laboratory experiments were conducted to validate the performance of the detector under varied environmental conditions and during conventional white cane use. The objective is to evaluate the feasibility of this sensing strategy, how it can enhance user safety and identify the remaining challenges toward an operational device.
items.authors: Lucas Bogaert, Issa Berthe, Liam Jordan, Julien Donnez, René Farcy, Clément Favey

items.title: Walking Distance and Interlimb Gait Differences Across 51 kg of Weight Loss After Total Knee Arthroplasty: A Three-Session Wearable Sensor Case Report
items.abstract: Background and Clinical Significance: Longitudinal observations that combine major postoperative weight loss with limb-specific gait assessment after total knee arthroplasty (TKA) are uncommon. This case report describes three single-trial instrumented assessments in one patient and is intended as a descriptive observation; it does not establish causality, measurement stability, mechanical loading, or a clinically meaningful persistent deficit; Case Presentation: A man in his early sixties at the first assessment had undergone left TKA for end-stage osteoarthritis and subsequently underwent Roux-en-Y gastric bypass. Three assessments were available from approximately 31 to 67 months after TKA. Body mass was 120, 88, and 69 kg (body mass index 43.03, 31.55, and 24.74 kg/m2), while two-minute walk distance (2MWT) was 67.8, 105.1, and 118.1 m. The third walk test was launched in the software’s six-minute module and stopped at 1 min 58 s, so 118.1 m is the distance accumulated over 118 s and was neither adjusted nor extrapolated to 120 s. The operated limb showed longer stance duration than the non-operated limb by 3.04, 5.28, and 2.05 percentage points, and a proprietary propulsion index was lower on the operated side by 18.18%, 17.95%, and 14.06%; the direction of both differences was the same at every session but the magnitude was not, and the index has no published calculation or post-TKA interpretive threshold. Each session comprised one trial, and the third-session gait means were based on only five operated-limb and four non-operated-limb steps. Valid Timed Up and Go (TUG) totals were available for sessions 1 and 2 (13.41 and 14.95 s); the available source documentation did not contain a valid session-3 TUG result. Vendor-derived walk-test speed was excluded from primary interpretation because its calculation could not be reconciled with distance divided by test duration; Conclusions: Across these three observations, 2MWT distance increased while side-to-side differences in stance duration and the exploratory propulsion index were present at each session. These co-occurring changes cannot be attributed to weight loss specifically, because time since arthroplasty, rehabilitation exposure and repeated testing varied together with body mass. The findings are descriptive and hypothesis-generating; confirmation requires prospective studies with repeated trials per session, an adequate number of analysed steps, and validated kinetic or limb-specific outcomes.
items.authors: Andrei Machado Viegas da Trindade, Leonardo Pinheiro Rezende, Junichiro Sado Junior, Marcos Henrique Alves Resende, Claudia Santos Oliveira

items.title: Study of Snow Cover Characteristics According to the Data of Meteorological Stations of Western Kazakhstan in the Context of Global Climate Change
items.abstract: In the Republic of Kazakhstan, runoff in lowland rivers is 90% determined by snowmelt. Therefore, assessing snow reserves in a changing climate is of great scientific and applied importance. This work aims to assess how global climate change affects snow cover characteristics in Western Kazakhstan in the Caspian Sea basin. For the first time, we conducted a comprehensive assessment of snow cover depth, water equivalent, and snow cover duration in the drainage basin. We used statistical analysis of data from 50 meteorological stations for the period 1950–2024. Only data from 14 meteorological stations in the Mugalzhar lowlands (north of the Aktobe region) and on the Podural plateau (north of the West Kazakhstan region), where errors did not exceed 2–4%, were suitable for climate studies. The results showed an increase in average snow height by 3 cm, a decrease in maximum height by 4 cm, and a 17-day reduction in the duration of stable snow cover. However, these trends are not statistically significant (the coefficient of determination is 0.02–0.24), and their values fall within the statistical error. The calculated Pearson and Spearman indicators confirm a statistical relationship between individual global and regional climate indicators (correlation coefficients of 0.23–0.40 at the significance level p = 0.03). However, most snow cover indicators show no statistical dependence: correlation coefficients range from −0.02 to 0.20, with p = 0.30–0.90. The results obtained indicate a random, stochastic nature of the long-term dynamics of depth, water equivalent, and duration of snow cover in the region under study.
items.authors: Akhmetkal Medeu, Vitaliy Zhdanov, Viktor Blagovechshenskiy, Nina Pimankina

items.title: Cauliflower Mushroom (Sparassis spp.): Basic Biology and Industrialization Progress in China
items.abstract: Sparassis species, commonly known as cauliflower mushrooms, are precious wood-rotting edible and medicinal fungi with high nutritional value and diverse bioactivities. Among them, Sparassis latifolia is the dominant artificially cultivated species in China, while Sparassis crispa is widely distributed in Europe and North America. This review systematically elaborates the basic biological characteristics of Sparassis spp., domestication history, key cultivation technologies, phased development of the industrial chain, and current production status of S. latifolia in China. Meanwhile, major bottlenecks restricting industrial development, such as long cultivation cycle, strain degeneration, imperfect standard system and insufficient high-value processing capacity, are analyzed. Finally, targeted prospects for basic research, variety improvement, technological innovation and industrial upgrading are proposed. This work aims to provide a comprehensive reference for both fundamental research and sustainable industrial development of S. latifolia and related Sparassis species worldwide.
items.authors: Chi Yang, Zhi Lin, Jie Huang, Donglai Xiao, Xiaoling Jiang, Hui Lin

items.title: Fibonacci–Lucas Recurrence-Indexed Quaternionic Unitaries: Channel Convergence, Clifford Proximity, and Controlled Entanglement
items.abstract: We investigate the normalized operator geometry of the mixed Fibonacci–Lucas quaternion Qn = Fn + Lni + Fn+1j + Ln+1k. Standard quaternion representations associate this sequence with single-qubit unitary channels. We first establish a convergence theorem for quaternion sequences with two distinct real characteristic roots and a strictly dominant positive root. It gives an exact average gate infidelity to the limit and sharp projective-step asymptotics, including the degenerate constant-channel case. For the Fibonacci–Lucas assignment, orthogonal Binet coefficient vectors yield exact finite-index formulas with projective steps of order φ−2n and average gate infidelities of order φ−4n. Strict comparison of the five projective Clifford rotation classes proves that the limiting unitary has a unique nearest projective Clifford, the cyclic Pauli-axis permutation, with average gate fidelity 115+5/90≈0.884408. For the controlled family, product-input maximization gives concurrence 1−an2, while independent Haar averaging gives linear-entropy entangling power 21−an2/9. Both admit explicit algebraic limits. Reproducible matrix and high-precision scalar calculations verify these results.
