The analysis supplies exact convergence, finite-group, and entanglement benchmarks for a recurrence-indexed family without assuming Hamiltonian dynamics.
items.authors: Zafer Ünal, Can Doğan Vurdu

items.title: Risk-Adaptive Masking for Privacy–Utility Balance in OCR-Based Document De-Identification
items.abstract: OCR-based document de-identification must protect personally identifiable information (PII) while preserving information needed for document analysis. Uniform masking may insufficiently protect high-risk PII or unnecessarily remove useful low-risk context. This study proposes a risk-adaptive masking framework that selects treatment based on PII type, identification risk, document-use environment, and analytical necessity. Eighteen PII types were organized into three risk-treatment groups, and processing environments were classified as controlled internal use, controlled third-party provision, or uncontrolled external use. The framework was evaluated using XFUND-PII, CORD-PII, SROIE-PII, and DocVQA-PII, constructed by injecting synthetic PII into the corresponding public datasets. Weak, Moderate, Strong, and Risk-adaptive masking were compared in terms of privacy protection, downstream-task utility, and masking cost. First, for privacy protection, Risk-adaptive and Strong achieved identical mean PII-region coverage on XFUND-PII, CORD-PII, and DocVQA-PII. On SROIE-PII, Risk-adaptive coverage was 4.09 percentage points lower than Strong; the prespecified coverage criterion was not statistically confirmed. Second, Risk-adaptive satisfied the prespecified downstream-utility criterion across all datasets. Third, compared with Strong masking, Risk-adaptive masking reduced masked page area by up to 25.03%, depending on the dataset. Overall, Risk-adaptive maintained comparable document-analysis performance while achieving similar PII-region coverage and less masking on most datasets.
items.authors: Soonseok Kim

items.title: Evaluation of Machine Vision-Based Automated Detection of Freeway Incidents
items.abstract: Automatic incident detection (AID) can significantly decrease the time to detect incidents and better identify incident locations to allow faster response. The deployment of traffic surveillance cameras has motivated transportation agencies to investigate computer vision technologies for AID using live video streams from these cameras. This paper evaluated three commercially available computer vision-based AID systems. The evaluated AID systems were able to use video streams from six existing Pan–Tilt–Zoom (PTZ) surveillance cameras for incident detection when these cameras were on predefined presets. The three systems with the selected settings performed differently. For example, the system with the highest number of true stopped vehicle incident detections also had a relatively high number of false alerts. The AID system accuracy also varied by study site, likely due to traffic patterns, roadway geometry, and camera angles. Two major factors contributed to false alerts: stop-and-go traffic during non-incident conditions and other highway objects, including light reflection and glare, that were falsely detected as incidents. The three systems also detected additional incidents not reported in existing incident management databases, but these were mainly shoulder incidents and work zone vehicles.
items.authors: Chonlachart Jeenprasom, Tanchanok Sirikanchittavon, Mohammed Hadi, Zhenyu Wang

items.title: Melatonin Supplementation During Middle Gestation Alleviates Intrauterine Growth Restriction in Piglets and Is Associated with Alterations in Placental DNA Methylation
items.abstract: Intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR) has a negative impact on reproductive performance in domestic animals. In this study, we attempt to explore the etiology of IUGR in sows and test the potential beneficial effects and underlying molecular mechanisms of melatonin on IUGR. The results indicated that there was a negative correlation between the concentration of melatonin in the peripheral blood of pregnant sows and the ratio of IUGR, and the concentration of melatonin in the umbilical cord blood of IUGR piglets was abnormally decreased. Supplementing sows with an appropriate dose of melatonin can increase the average birth weight of piglets and reduce the proportion of IUGR piglets. Reduced representation bisulfite sequencing revealed a direct association between abnormal DNA methylation in the placenta of sows and IUGR piglets. The increased DNA methylations of key genes responsible for placenta functions downregulated their expressions. Gene downregulation caused placenta dysfunction and IUGR. Melatonin significantly reduced DNA methylation of genes related to placental function. We identified that melatonin supplementation during mid-gestation stages specifically targeted the CGI, CGI shore, exon, intron, and 3′ untranslated regions of placental genes. The results provide novel information to target the high incidence of IUGR in pigs as well as other species.
items.authors: Likai Wang, Huigang Han, Zhenhua Xue, Laiqing Yan, Zixia Shen, Jiarui Gao

items.title: Fewer Crashes but a Smaller Decline in Fatality Risk: Rethinking Road Safety Indicators for Shrinking Regions in Korea
items.abstract: Population decline can undermine access to essential services and safe mobility. Korea designated 89 municipalities as depopulating areas in 2021 and launched the Local Extinction Response Fund in 2022. We examined whether road safety outcomes improved more in designated than in non-designated municipalities using a balanced 2015–2025 panel based on crash and population data, supplemented by cause-of-death statistics for age standardization and cross-validation. Poisson pseudo-maximum-likelihood difference-in-differences models compared 2015–2020 with 2022–2025. Population-based crash frequency declined 9.0% more in designated areas (incidence rate ratio (IRR) = 0.910, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.863–0.960), whereas age-standardized fatality risk declined less (IRR = 1.086, 95% CI 1.020–1.156). Because the relative crash decline began in 2021, before Fund implementation, and because the fatality estimate was sensitive to alternative exposure definitions and to allowing a differential pre-existing trend, these findings are interpreted as comparative pre-to-post changes rather than as causal effects of the Fund. The fatality gap was larger in municipalities where depopulation designation overlapped with emergency-care underserved status, but similar differences appeared for crashes and serious injuries, while deaths per 100 crashes showed no clear interaction. Road safety evaluation in depopulating areas should consider crash frequency, serious injuries, and fatalities together, alongside broader regional vulnerabilities. These findings can support future multidimensional road safety monitoring and help prioritize safety and emergency-care interventions in shrinking regions.
items.authors: Jung-Ah Ha, Sung-Han Lim

items.title: Whole-Genome Resequencing Reveals Genomic Signatures Underlying High-Altitude Adaptation in Ethiopian Indigenous Cattle
items.abstract: High-altitude environments impose severe physiological challenges on mammals, yet the genetic basis of adaptation in Ethiopian indigenous cattle remains poorly understood. Here, we analyzed whole-genome resequencing data from 70 Ethiopian indigenous cattle representing seven breeds (Abigar, Barka, Boran, Felata, Fogera, Gojjam-Highland, and Horro) distributed across elevations ranging from 523 to 3410 m, obtained from the NCBI Sequence Read Archive. After alignment to the ARS-UCD2.0 reference genome, we identified 49,196,624 high-confidence SNPs and performed population genomic analyses (PCA, phylogenetic reconstruction, and ADMIXTURE), along with genome-wide selection scans using FST and nucleotide diversity (θπ), and in silico virtual knockout of candidate genes in bovine lung single-cell transcriptomics. Population structure analyses revealed marked genetic differentiation between low- and mid-to-high-altitude populations, with substantial genetic connectivity and shared ancestry among high-altitude groups. We identified 398 candidate selective regions showing concordant FST and θπ signals, encompassing 1816 candidate genes, significantly enriched in hypoxia-related and vascular remodeling pathways (phospholipase D, Ras, ErbB, Wnt, Hedgehog). Two hub candidate genes, PIK3CA and RHOA, were prioritized; virtual perturbation of PIK3CA altered extracellular matrix, focal adhesion, and integrin networks, whereas RHOA perturbation activated immune and inflammatory programs (NF-κB, phagocytosis, chemokine pathways) with upregulation of TYROBP, IL1B, TLR4, and NLRP3. Our findings indicate that Ethiopian cattle have evolved distinct genomic signatures associated with adaptation to chronic high-altitude environments, in which PIK3CA and RHOA may represent candidate regulators associated with extracellular matrix organization and immune-related transcriptional regulation, respectively, thereby providing new insights into mammalian adaptation to extreme environments.
items.authors: Ruoshan Ma, Dongfang Li, Ying Lu, Bo Wang, Weidong Deng, Zhendong Gao

items.title: Associations of Serum Niacin and Nicotinamide with Child Behavior: A Longitudinal Study in China
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: Nicotinic acid (NA; niacin) and nicotinamide (NAM) participate in nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide metabolism, but pediatric evidence relating serum concentrations of these vitamers to behavioral-problem scores is limited. Methods: We conducted an exploratory analysis of children assessed in Yiwu, Zhejiang Province, China, with serum NA and NAM concentrations recorded in 2021 and 2025 and caregiver-reported Child Behavior Checklist (CBCL) outcomes in 2025. Vitamin B3 was measured by high-performance liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry (HPLC–MS/MS). Internalizing, externalizing, and total-problem raw scores were the broadband outcomes; seven common raw subscales were exploratory outcomes. Multivariable linear models and three-knot restricted cubic splines (RCSs) were conducted to assess the associations between vitamin B3 and CBCL scores. Benjamini–Hochberg correction and exposure-by-sex interaction tests were used. Results: Pooled associations were compatible with the null after correction. Per interquartile-range (IQR) increase in 2021 NA, boys’ adjusted contrasts were −2.18 (95% CI, −4.22 to −0.13) for internalizing, −3.04 (−5.05 to −1.04) for externalizing, and −5.33 (−9.18 to −1.47) for total problems. In sex-stratified RCS analyses, 2021 NA was associated with externalizing (q-overall = 0.040) and total problems (q-overall = 0.023) in boys, whereas 2025 NA was associated with these outcomes in girls (both q-overall = 0.042). Sex-stratified two-degree-of-freedom RCS models had limited sensitivity for small-to-modest associations. Conclusions: The sex-interaction and sex-stratified RCS patterns for NA are hypothesis-generating and require independent, prespecified replication.
items.authors: Xinhan Zhang, Kuiqing Huang, Chen Liu, Yi Wang, Jinghan Jiang, Zhijian Chen

items.title: From Data to Decisions: Mathematical and Computational Frameworks in Marketing—A Systematic Review and Bibliometric Analysis
items.abstract: The increasing availability of large-scale consumer data and advances in computational technologies have transformed marketing into a data-driven discipline. Mathematical and computational frameworks play a critical role in supporting decision-making processes by enabling organizations to analyze complex market dynamics, predict consumer behavior, optimize resource allocation, and improve strategic planning. This study has four objectives: to characterize the intellectual structure of the field, to classify the mathematical and computational methods employed and the marketing functions to which they are applied, to examine emerging technological developments, and to identify research and methodological gaps. A systematic literature review was conducted, reported in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 guidelines and organized through the Literature Review based on Systematic Bibliometry (LRSB) protocol. A single, fully documented query executed in Scopus returned 56 records, of which 45 met the eligibility criteria and were retained for both bibliometric science mapping and qualitative synthesis. The corpus spans 1992–2025. The review examines the integration of mathematical modeling, optimization techniques, machine learning algorithms, simulation methods, and data analytics within contemporary marketing practices. Drawing on the interdisciplinary convergence of marketing, engineering, mathematics, and computer science, the paper examines how computational approaches enhance market segmentation, customer engagement, demand forecasting, pricing strategies, advertising performance, and customer relationship management. The analysis highlights the growing relevance of predictive and prescriptive analytics in converting raw data into actionable insights that support evidence-based managerial decisions. Furthermore, the study discusses emerging trends, including artificial intelligence, real-time analytics, and intelligent decision support systems, that are reshaping the marketing landscape. The review also documents families of decision-support methods that are well established in the wider literature but almost absent from the retrieved corpus—multi-criteria decision making, mathematical programming beyond the linear case, metaheuristic optimization and Bayesian decision models—and treats this absence as a substantive research gap. Challenges related to data quality, model interpretability, computational complexity, and ethical considerations are also addressed. The findings suggest that the effective integration of mathematical and computational frameworks can significantly improve organizational competitiveness by increasing decision accuracy, operational efficiency, and responsiveness to market changes. This research contributes to a broader understanding of how advanced analytical methods support the transition from data collection to strategic decision-making in modern marketing environments.
items.authors: Albérico Travassos Rosário, Joaquim A. Casaca, Rui Nunes Cruz

items.title: Electrospun Carbon Nanofiber–TiN Composite Interlayers for Improved Cycling Stability and Rate Capability of Lithium–Sulfur Batteries
items.abstract: Lithium–sulfur (Li-S) batteries offer a high theoretical energy density of 2600 Wh·kg−1 and a theoretical specific capacity of 1675 mAh·g−1; however, their practical application is severely hindered by the shuttle effect of soluble lithium polysulfides, the intrinsic electronic insulating nature of sulfur and Li2S, and the substantial volume variation during charge/discharge processes. In this study, titanium nitride (TiN) powder was first prepared, and a carbon nanofiber/titanium nitride (CNF@TiN) composite nanofiber membrane was subsequently fabricated by electrospinning followed by pre-oxidation/carbonization treatment and employed as a functional interlayer between the separator and sulfur cathode. X-ray diffraction (XRD) and high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) showed that the obtained TiN possessed a well-crystallized face-centered cubic structure. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM), transmission electron microscopy (TEM), and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) revealed that TiN particles were relatively uniformly dispersed and anchored within the three-dimensional interconnected CNF network. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) analyses of the composite and the TiN powder confirmed the presence of Ti–N bonding, revealed N/O-containing functional groups on the carbon scaffold, and indicated only a thin oxidized layer on the TiN particle surface. Nitrogen adsorption–desorption analysis confirmed the porous character of the fibrous interlayers. Electrochemical tests showed that the cell equipped with the CNF@TiN interlayer delivered an initial discharge specific capacity of 1205 mAh·g−1 at 0.1 C and retained a reversible capacity of approximately 1010 mAh·g−1 after 100 cycles. At 0.2 C, the initial discharge specific capacity was approximately 1065 mAh·g−1, and approximately 875 mAh·g−1 was retained after 300 cycles, corresponding to a capacity retention of 82.2% and an average capacity decay of approximately 0.059% per cycle. Rate capability, cyclic voltammetry (CV), electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), and galvanostatic charge–discharge measurements indicated that the CNF@TiN interlayer favors reversible sulfur-species conversion and improved interfacial reaction kinetics. The enhanced performance can be attributed to the physical confinement, electron-transport, and structural-support functions of the CNF network, together with the polar TiN interface, whose presence is consistent with restricted polysulfide migration and facilitated interfacial conversion. This work provides a feasible strategy for designing multifunctional interlayers integrating electrical conductivity, physical confinement, and interfacial regulation for Li-S batteries.
items.authors: Chaoqun Niu, Huan Liu, Zisheng Chao

items.title: Surrogate Modeling of Methane Yield in Anaerobic Digestion Under Heterogeneous Feedstock Conditions
items.abstract: Predicting methane and biogas yields from heterogeneous feedstocks requires distinguishing performance within an available dataset from transfer to unrepresented substrate labels. This study compares artificial neural network (ANN), Gaussian process regression (GP), and proper orthogonal decomposition combined with radial basis function (POD–RBF) using 83 laboratory observations and five measured descriptors. The two measured fresh-mass yields are the primary endpoints; four DM/ODM-normalized yields are secondary. Shared five-fold cross-validation (CV) and 30-label leave-one-substrate-out (LOSO) validation exclude substrate identity from the predictors and fit preprocessing and POD exclusively on training data. For the primary endpoints, POD–RBF has the lowest mean CV root mean square error (23.84 m3/Mg fresh mass), whereas GP has the lowest mean CV symmetric mean absolute percentage error (sMAPE; 29.71%). Mean group-wise LOSO sMAPE is 46.35%, 46.78%, and 45.09% for ANN, GP, and POD–RBF, respectively. Mean coverage of conditional nominal 95% GP observation intervals decreases from 93.37% in CV to 77.11% in LOSO. Three full-data POD modes retain 99.16% of centered output energy, partly reflecting deterministic relationships among mass-normalized yields. Model rankings depend on the metric and validation setting, and the single CV partition leaves split dependence unquantified. Large errors for some excluded labels and GP under-coverage limit claims of reliable prediction for unseen feedstocks or industrial application.
items.authors: Kamil Witaszek, Nikolay Kiktev, Volodymyr Reshetiuk, Tomasz Garbowski

items.title: Production Efficiency in Pig Farming in Thailand: A Copula-Based Frontier Model
items.abstract: This study evaluates the technical efficiency of pig production in Nakhon Si Thammarat Province, Thailand, using a copula-based stochastic frontier framework that relaxes the conventional assumption of independence between stochastic noise and technical inefficiency. Farm-level data from 280 pig-farming households were analyzed, with the Gaussian copula selected as the preferred dependence specification based on model-selection criteria. The results indicate a mean technical efficiency of 0.5207, suggesting substantial scope for improving production performance under existing input conditions. Breeder pigs, labor, medicines and veterinary inputs, feed, utilities, and farm size are positively and significantly associated with pig output, whereas housing investment is not statistically significant. The estimated input elasticities sum to 1.5592, and a Wald test rejects the null hypothesis of constant returns to scale, providing evidence of increasing returns to scale. In the second-stage analysis, household income, farming experience, and participation in Good Agricultural Practices (GAP) are significantly associated with lower technical inefficiency. These associations remain broadly consistent under a fractional logit specification with bootstrapped standard errors. Additional robustness checks using alternative stochastic frontier distributions, treatment of extreme observations, and a Translog production specification indicate that the main results are broadly stable across alternative specifications. The findings indicate that technical-efficiency estimates are sensitive to model specification and are consistent with the emphasis on GAP and improved farm management in Thailand’s Swine Action Plan 2023–2027.
items.authors: Siraprapa Yosthongngam, Roengchai Tansuchat

items.title: Physiological Basis of Skeletal Muscle Electrical Stimulation in Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction: Established Mechanisms, Extrapolated Mechanisms and Translational Priorities
items.abstract: Skeletal muscle electrical stimulation, delivered as neuromuscular electrical stimulation (NMES) or functional electrical stimulation (FES), is one of very few interventions in heart failure that produces sustained contractile work in the periphery without volitional effort and, in low-frequency configurations, without a measurable rise in cardiac output. Three decades of clinical evaluation have produced consistent signals of improved muscle strength, walking distance and quality of life. The physiological rationale that underpins these observations has advanced much less. This review separates what has been demonstrated in human skeletal muscle in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) from what has been extrapolated from healthy volunteers, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, critical illness and ageing muscle. We frame stimulation within the muscle hypothesis of chronic heart failure, in which peripheral myopathy drives ergoreflex overactivity, sympathetic excitation and exertional symptoms, and we show that the decisive mechanistic question, whether a programme of stimulation attenuates ergoreflex sensitivity, has never been tested, although two sham-controlled microneurographic studies indicate that stimulation acutely lowers muscle sympathetic nerve activity. Four further gaps are identified: a single biopsy-controlled randomised dataset in advanced heart failure, a single in vivo spectroscopic study in which muscle energetics did not change, absence of contemporary molecular phenotyping of anabolic and proteolytic signalling in stimulated HFrEF muscle, and drift of the recent evidence base towards decompensated, frail and older populations with mixed ejection fraction. Against the background of the 2026 European Society of Cardiology guidelines, which recommend exercise-based cardiac rehabilitation for all stable patients and mention electrical muscle stimulation only as an option for very weak patients, we propose a research agenda in which stimulation dose is reported as a biological variable and muscle afferent physiology becomes the primary mechanistic endpoint.
items.authors: Damian Sendrowski, Dariusz Kozłowski

items.title: Insecticidal Activity and Mechanism of 7-Methylcoumarin Against Diaphorina citri Reveal the Role of Chemosensory Genes in Defense Response
items.abstract: The Asian citrus psyllid (Diaphorina citri) is a major vector of Huanglongbing (HLB), a devastating citrus disease worldwide. In addition to vectoring HLB, D. citri is a significant economic pest in its own right, causing direct damage to citrus by feeding on tender shoots, leading to leaf distortion, shoot dieback, and sooty mold infestation. Chemical control remains the primary strategy for managing D. citri populations, but heavy reliance on insecticides has led to insecticide resistance. Coumarin and its derivatives, as a natural product, are widely recognized for their insecticidal activities against various agricultural pests. In this study, the insecticidal activity of 11 coumarin compounds against D. citri nymphs was evaluated by bioassay, among which 7-methylcoumarin exhibited the most substantial efficacy. Moreover, the insecticidal mechanism of 7-methylcoumarin was assessed by a comparative transcriptome analysis, and 294 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were identified, including 165 up-regulated and 129 down-regulated genes. GO enrichment analysis showed that DEGs were mainly involved in extracellular region/space, (chitin-based) cuticle development, and structural constituent of (chitin-based) cuticle terms, especially down-regulated genes related to cuticle proteins, chemosensory proteins and odorant-binding proteins, which were further verified by qPCR. Among chemosensory genes, only DcCSP2 was significantly up-regulated, indicating its potential involvement in the defense response of D. citri. Suppression of DcCSP2 via RNAi significantly increased susceptibility to 7-methylcoumarin in D. citri nymphs. Molecular docking revealed that 7-methylcoumarin binds within the internal hydrophobic cavity of DcCSP2. This finding provided a potential molecular mechanism underlying the action of coumarin compounds against pest insects and may contribute to facilitating the development of new strategies for managing insecticide resistance.
items.authors: Ao Fang, Xue-Yan Wang, Zheng-Hui Zou, Tong Yang, Wei Chen, Hai-Zhong Yu

items.title: Do AI and Lexicon-Based ESG Scores Converge? Evidence from IPO Prospectuses in an Emerging Market
items.abstract: The growing use of artificial intelligence (AI) to evaluate Environmental, Social, Governance (ESG) scoring from corporate disclosures raises questions about alignment with conventional lexicon-based scores. Such alignment can be problematic as a lexicon-based approach quantifies the textual density using an ESG dictionary, while LLM-based scores are able to assess the thematic coverage of ESG themes. It remains unclear whether the two approaches produce comparable or distinct results when applied to the same corporate information. This paper examines the construct alignment between LLM-generated and lexicon-based ESG scores using 625 Indian IPO prospectuses issued between 2018 and 2024. A rebalanced dictionary of 630 terms measures disclosure intensity, while contextual scores are obtained by prompting a generative AI model. Both sets of scores are harmonised into quantile categories and compared using confusion matrices, correlation analysis, and chance-corrected agreement. The methods converge for the environmental dimension (EMR = 46.1%; weighted κ = 0.56) but diverge for social (28.2%) and governance (23.0%) disclosure, with only limited alignment overall (31.7%). The findings suggest the two approaches operationalise ESG differently, with implications for construct validity and transparency in ESG analytics.
items.authors: Manpriya Singh, Navjit Singh, Vikas Sharma, Ramona Rupeika-Apoga
items.category_raw: Journal of Risk and Financial Management

items.title: Topological Reconfiguration in Sheared Granular Assemblies: Non-Dissipative Mechanism and Its Irreversible Characteristics
items.abstract: Granular materials exhibit pronounced macroscopic irreversible deformations during shearing, which mainly contributes to frictional sliding dissipation in the conventional thermodynamic frameworks. This study aims to investigate the non-dissipative microscopic mechanisms governing macroscopic irreversibility of granular materials. Using DEM, a series of biaxial shear and reverse loading simulations are conducted on dense granular assemblies with different friction coefficients. The results show that continuous topological reconfiguration occurs through the transformation from lower-order to higher-order meso-loops, eventually reaching a statistical steady state at the critical state. Accompanying this topological evolution, elastic energy at contact level is continuously stored and released, providing a persistent non-dissipative energy exchange that sustains continuous shear alongside primary frictional dissipation. Based on the reverse loading analysis, topological reconfiguration is intrinsically irrecoverable, causing part of the free energy to remain locked within the reconfigured contact network as irrecoverable free energy. Meanwhile, another portion of the recoverable free energy is irreversibly dissipated through friction during unloading. Together, these two components constitute the irreversible free energy. The evolution of irreversible free energy with interparticle friction is consistent with those of the critical frictional dissipation and macroscopic volumetric strain, indicating that the macroscopic irreversible deformation of granular assemblies is governed not only by frictional dissipation but also by the irreversible evolution of free energy.
items.authors: Xiaoxiao Wang, Peng Li, Pengqiang Yu, Yang Liu

items.title: A Quantum Mechanism-Centered Review of Carbon Dot-Based Theranostics
items.abstract: Despite advances in drug discovery, effective delivery and precise imaging still pose significant obstacles. Scientists have turned to zero-dimensional nanomaterials like carbon dots (CDs) to enable precision drug delivery. Due to their multidisciplinary appeal, there is extensive research on both the physical properties and biological applications of CDs, yet the fields rarely complement each other. This review applies a quantum-mechanistic framework to better understand CDs and unify the relationship between electronic structure, photophysical behavior, and theranostic performance. We first highlight the theranostic advantages of CDs over quantum dots, then discuss the quantum mechanisms behind a CD’s imaging capabilities, including surface states, excitation-dependent photoluminescence, and the electronic origins of photostability. Through this physical lens, we then evaluate the effect of different precursors and doping strategies during synthesis on electronic structure and how dots are engineered to load, release, and track therapeutic cargo. Photodynamic therapy and surface functionalization strategies are also evaluated. Finally, we address the significance of renal clearance and translational bottlenecks such as heterogeneity.
items.authors: Ian Ke Cheng, Gregory P. Contreras, Ting-Yu Yeh

items.title: The Contributions of Social Factors to Lifespan Disparity: Multi-Factor Analysis and a Four-Way Case Study of U.S. Lifespan
items.abstract: Lifespan varies among individuals, and this variation arises both from heterogeneity (e.g., in sex or race) and from unavoidable individual stochasticity. Treating a heterogeneous population as a mixture of groups, each experiencing different rates, makes it possible to partition lifespan variance into a between-group component due to heterogeneity and a within-group component due to chance. Until now, such studies could only treat factors one at a time. This paper presents an analysis that applies to multi-factor studies and quantifies the contribution of multiple factors and their interactions to variance in lifespan. As a case study it is applied to life table data from a four-factor (sex, marital status, education, and race) study of longevity in the U.S. population, 2015–2019. Even accounting for four main factors, six two-way interactions, four three-way interactions, and one four-way interaction, between-group heterogeneity accounts for only 7% to 10% of lifespan variance. Education and its interactions make the largest contribution. Main effects make the largest contributions; those of two-way, three-way, and four-way interactions are orders of magnitude smaller.
items.authors: Hal Caswell

items.title: Energy Generation Policy Strategies for Low CO2 Emission in Rwanda Using LEAP Model-Based Analysis
items.abstract: This article used the Long-range Energy Alternative Planning and scenario-based analysis to investigate Rwanda’s future energy supply, the energy consumption and emitted GHGs from 2023 to 2053. Impacts of various energy policies are analyzed considering different scenarios such as low CO2 moderate, low CO2 advance, reference and green optimistic. It was found that by 2053 the demand will be 3075 PJ under reference scenario with a GHG emission increase of 201.3 Mt Co2 due to the consideration of aggressive strategies and energy policies from low CO2 moderate to low CO2 advance, as well as aggressive alternatives in green optimistic scenario. More aggressive policy intervention by government, as in green optimistic scenario, would result in a reduction in GHGs (124.4 Mt Co2e) and energy demand (2249 PJ) in 2053. This work also conducted the energy system and cost–benefit analyses.
items.authors: Emile Niringiyimana, Li Jiqing, Zhang Ping, Wang Kedong, Chen Huiwei

items.title: Green Initiatives and Financial Performance: ESG Associations and Corporate Life-Cycle Contingencies in China’s Heavily Polluting Industries
items.abstract: This study examines how green initiatives are associated with financial performance through a statistical indirect pathway involving environmental, social, and governance (ESG) assessment and whether that pathway varies across life-cycle stages. Using an unbalanced panel of 6579 firm-year observations from 1114 Chinese A-share firms in heavily polluting industries during 2015–2024, the analysis compares green investment, green innovation, green subsidy, and ISO 14001 certification within a common framework. Firm and year fixed-effects models with firm-clustered inference are combined with 5000 firm-cluster bootstrap replications and Benjamini–Hochberg false-discovery-rate adjustment. All four initiatives are positively associated with Huazheng ESG ratings. ESG ratings are positively associated with ROA and ROE, whereas a positive association with Tobin’s Q is not established. Each initiative exhibits a positive statistical indirect association with ROA through ESG, although total financial associations remain heterogeneous; green subsidy shows a negative contemporaneous total association with ROA. The mediated effects are economically modest: a one within-firm standard-deviation increase in each initiative corresponds to about 0.20–0.34% of a within-firm standard deviation of ROA through ESG. By contrast, a one within-firm standard-deviation increase in green subsidy is associated with a −0.133 percentage-point total ROA association. Corporate life cycle selectively conditions the pathway: ESG-mediated associations of green investment and green subsidy are significantly stronger in growth-stage firms than in mature or declining firms, while comparable stage differences are not established for green innovation or certification. The evidence distinguishes external sustainability assessment from immediate profitability and locates life-cycle dependence in resource-deployment-intensive green actions.
items.authors: Tian Yang, Teh Boon Heng, Kwan Jing Hui
items.category_raw: Journal of Risk and Financial Management

items.title: Ecological Consequences of Sand Nourishment: Sediment Dynamics and Meiofauna Community Shifts Revealed by Metabarcoding
items.abstract: Beach nourishment is a widely used coastal protection measure that affects beach morphology, sedimentology, and ecology. In Ahrenshoop (Baltic Sea), sand nourishments are applied approximately every five years to widen a 4 km stretch of the tourist beach. From September 2021 to March 2023, we monitored changes in beach width, sediment composition, and the reaction of meiofauna communities. To assess the impact of nourishment, we determined water line shifts, analysed sediment grain size and shape, and used DNA metabarcoding to characterise the meiofauna communities at the beach–water line. Following the nourishment, the sediment composition had shifted towards finer sand, but it returned to the coarser pre-impact state one year later. By this time, the artificial widening of the beach had almost eroded. Meiofauna communities collected before and after the nourishment differed significantly and were associated with fine and coarse sand, respectively. Grain shape parameters correlated with shifts in meiofauna communities, albeit to a lesser extent than grain size. The differences in community composition were primarily driven by operational taxonomic units belonging to Acari, Annelida, and Platyhelminthes. We recommend the establishment of curated genetic reference barcode libraries for future beach nourishment monitoring studies.
items.authors: Iryna Kapshyna, Sahar Khodami, Leon Hoffman, Christian Winter, Pedro Martínez Arbizu, Gritta Veit-Köhler

items.title: Research on the Intervention of Bile Stasis-Induced Pruritus Using Small Molecules Targeting MRGPRX4 Through High-Throughput Screening
items.abstract: MRGPRX4, which is mainly expressed in human sensory neurons, is a key mediator of cholestatic pruritus, but clinically available small-molecule inhibitors targeting it remain very scarce; thus, this study aims to screen out novel active inhibitors targeting MRGPRX4. In this work, we performed high-throughput virtual screening of the small-molecule compound library with Schrodinger software targeting MRGPRX4, and selected the top five commercially available compounds with the highest scores from 13,144 candidate compounds. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulation were used for virtual validation, and the results confirmed that all five compounds could bind to MRGPRX4, among which 6′-O-malonyldaidzin showed the most favorable binding free energy and a compact binding pocket with the lowest SASA value. We further verified the effect of these compounds on Ca2+ influx in 50 μM concentration in HEK293 cells overexpressing MRGPRX4, and confirmed the inhibitory activity of 6′-O-malonyldaidzin, whose binding interaction with MRGPRX4 was additionally verified by CETSA. In conclusion, this study identified 6′-O-malonyldaidzin as a promising lead compound for further pharmacological characterization and lead optimization, with potential for development as a targeted intervention for cholestatic pruritus.
items.authors: Qi Liang, Jiahao Kuang, Liangchen Wang, Hanghang Gou, Dandan Tang, Wei Peng

items.title: Multisensor Analysis of Mediterranean Convective Case Studies Using EarthCARE and Meteosat Rapid Scan Observations
items.abstract: Convection plays a key role in the Earth’s energy balance and is responsible for severe weather phenomena such as hailstorms, which cause significant damage to infrastructure and agriculture. This study investigates convective events over the Mediterranean Basin between September 2024 and September 2025 using a synergistic combination of active and passive satellite observations from geostationary (GEO) and low Earth orbit (LEO) platforms. Convective evolution is analyzed using EUMETSAT Satellite Application Facility on Support to Nowcasting and Very Short Range Forecasting products derived from Meteosat Rapid Scan Service imagery and the Multi-sensor Approach for Satellite Hail Advection (MASHA), which combines passive microwave hail probability retrievals from the Global Precipitation Measurement constellation with high-temporal-resolution Meteosat infrared observations to monitor hail-producing storms in near real time. The analysis is further enhanced with EarthCARE Cloud Profiling Radar reflectivity and Doppler velocity measurements, whose spatial variability provides a proxy for identifying convective cores and storm intensity. For selected events, observations from the Meteosat Third Generation Lightning Imager are also examined, highlighting the close relationship between intense lightning activity and strong convective updrafts. The results demonstrate the potential of combining complementary satellite observations to improve the detection and characterization of severe convection and hail-producing storms and identify the key roadblocks and pathways towards the effective integration of LEO and GEO observations.
items.authors: Aida Galfione, Elsa Cattani, Giulio Monte, Federico Vermi, Blanka Piskala Gvoždíková, Pavlos Kollias

items.title: Korean Buddhist Temple Food: A Traditional Plant-Based Dietary Pattern Linking Gut Microbiota, Metabolic Health, and Mindful Living
items.abstract: Korean Buddhist temple food represents a traditional plant-based dietary practice rooted in Korean Buddhist monastic traditions and characterized by an emphasis on seasonal and minimally processed plant foods. Traditional temple-food practices generally exclude pungent vegetables—such as garlic, green onion, chives, wild garlic, and asafoetida—and incorporate a variety of plant-based ingredients and fermented foods, such as fermented soybean paste (doenjang), soy sauce (ganjang), fermented red chili paste (gochujang), fermented soybean paste (cheonggukjang), and fermented vegetables (kimchi). This dietary pattern provides dietary fiber and diverse plant-based phytochemicals, while fermented foods may contain fermentation-associated microorganisms depending on their ingredients, production processes, and storage conditions. These characteristics distinguish Korean Buddhist temple food from dietary patterns dominated by ultra-processed foods (UPFs). This narrative review synthesizes evidence regarding the nutritional characteristics of Korean Buddhist temple food, its potential relevance to gut microbiome ecology and microbial metabolism, and the cultural and contemplative practices associated with its consumption, including ritual communal eating (baru gongyang), seated meditation (chamseon), and walking meditation (pohaeng). Available evidence indicates that several features of temple food, including high intake of plant-based foods, dietary fiber, and fermented foods, provide biologically plausible pathways through which the dietary pattern may influence gut microbial composition and host metabolism. However, direct human evidence linking long-term adherence to Korean Buddhist temple food with gut microbiome composition, microbial function, or microbiota–gut–brain outcomes remains limited. Therefore, the potential health implications of Korean Buddhist temple food should be interpreted in the context of heterogeneous dietary practices and the distinction between direct human evidence and indirect or mechanistic evidence. Further longitudinal and controlled studies are needed to clarify the relationships among temple-food consumption, gut microbiota, microbial metabolites, host physiology, and associated lifestyle practices.
items.authors: Hae-Ji Kang, Young Hoon Jung, Jungwoo Yang, Yun Jeon Lim

items.title: Influences of Test Parameters on the Meso-Mechanical Characteristics of Coal Rock in the Longtan Formation, Sichuan Basin
items.abstract: As a typical heterogeneous, porous, organic–inorganic composite rock, the microscopic mechanical properties of coal rock significantly impact wellbore stability during drilling in deep fractured formations. Traditional macro-mechanical experiments struggle to reveal the mechanical behavior of its microscopic fabric. This study investigates the local indentation response of Longtan Formation coal rock from the Sichuan Basin under different peak loads, dwell times, and loading/unloading durations. Elastic modulus and hardness are evaluated by contact analysis, together with an apparent indentation fracture index derived from an empirical energy partition model. The plotted responses exhibit protocol-dependent variation and local scatter, without establishing a common optimum for all measured quantities. The observations are discussed in relation to contact-area uncertainty, microstructural sampling, and time-dependent penetration during unloading. These explanations remain conditional because phase-correlated damage observations and independent fracture validation are not reported. The study clarifies the need to distinguish local measurement sensitivity from intrinsic rock properties and provides a basis for designing subsequent correlative and multiscale experiments. Application to wellbore-scale behavior requires independent validation and explicit consideration of rock mass discontinuities and in situ conditions.
items.authors: Haidong Liu, Xiangsen Gao, Min Wang

items.title: Degradation Mechanisms for Automotive PEMFCs Under Dynamic Operation and Mitigation Strategies for Start-Up/Shut-Down: A Comprehensive Review
items.abstract: Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cells (PEMFCs) offer a compelling solution for heavy-duty and light-duty vehicle electrification due to their high efficiency and zero-emission operation. Despite these advantages, limited operational durability remains a critical barrier to widespread commercial adoption. In automotive applications, frequent power transients and Stop–Start events create aggressive electrochemical environments that accelerate stack aging. This review provides a systematic analysis of the fundamental degradation mechanisms occurring during these critical transitions. We focus on coupled degradation processes within the Membrane Electrode Assembly (MEA), detailing platinum catalyst dissolution, carbon support corrosion, and membrane thinning. By bridging fundamental interfacial science with realistic automotive duty cycles, this work identifies current research gaps and evaluates the technical feasibility of existing mitigation strategies. Ultimately, this review provides a comprehensive technical overview that can help guide efforts to extend PEMFC lifetime and support the transition to fuel-cell-based mobility.
items.authors: Wafa Hafsa Saidouni, Marielle Marchand, David Gérard, Samir Jemei, David Bouquain

items.title: A Dual-Medium Model-Based Method for Rapid Thermal Performance Analysis of TPMS Porous Heat Exchange Structures
items.abstract: The triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) structure demonstrates significant potential in the field of active heat transfer. This is due to its high specific surface area and controllable pore connectivity. However, its intricate geometric features result in notable computational costs during RANS-based CFD simulation, greatly limiting the efficiency of its design and optimization processes. Although existing equivalent approaches (e.g., the volume averaging method and the porous media model) have reduced the computational burden to some extent, they still suffer from limitations. Theseinclude insufficient sensitivity to microstructural features and low accuracy in characterizing convective heat transfer. In order to address the temperature-field prediction biases caused by the above limitations when filling TPMS on a large scale, this paper proposes a rapid analytical method based on a dual-medium model. The core idea of this method is to idealize the TPMS structure as a continuous solid thermal conductive medium and to homogenize its internal flow channels into a coexistent Darcy–Forchheimer fluid medium. The thermal conductivity tensor of the equivalent solid is accurately calculated via the homogenization method, whereas convective heat transfer in the fluid medium is characterized using empirical correlation equations. Ultimately, a rapid analytical model coupling solid heat conduction and fluid convection is developed at the macroscopic scale. Numerical examples show that, compared with traditional computational fluid dynamics (CFD) methods, this method improves computational efficiency by approximately 22 times while retaining high accuracy, thus providing an effective tool for the rapid design and performance assessment of TPMS-based active heat transfer structures.
items.authors: Yuxin Hu, Yu Tian, Shutian Liu

items.title: Lubrication and Grinding Characteristics of Electrostatically Charged Cutting Fluid Aerosol
items.abstract: In grinding, the airflow barrier generated by high-speed rotating grinding wheels restricts lubricant access to the grinding zone. Despite its high fluid throughput, flood lubrication suffers from poor penetration caused by this barrier, together with excessive resource consumption and environmental pollution. Conventional minimum quantity lubrication (MQL), assisted by compressed air, can partially overcome the airflow barrier and offers environmental benefits; however, its inherently inadequate droplet wetting and penetration still lead to insufficient cooling and lubrication, resulting in workpiece burn and low machining accuracy, particularly for difficult-to-cut materials. This study investigated electrostatic minimum quantity lubrication (EMQL), which integrates MQL with electrostatic spraying to improve droplet wetting, penetration, and grindability. An EMQL grinding system was constructed for machining GCr15 die steel, and the surface tension and contact angle of droplets were measured at different charging voltages. The effects of voltage polarity and magnitude on workpiece surface characteristics and overall grinding performance were then investigated. The results showed that increasing the absolute charging voltage reduced the surface tension and contact angle of the charged droplets and improved their penetration capability. Under the optimal condition of +8 kV, the surface microhardness decreased by up to 16.86%. Compared with conventional MQL, EMQL reduced the tangential and normal grinding forces, the grinding temperature, and the surface roughness by 58.52%, 37.54%, 22.22%, and 30.58%, respectively, and increased the grinding ratio by 31.36%. EMQL improves lubrication and heat transfer by enhancing droplet wetting and penetration, and the positive electrostatic field further optimizes grinding performance by regulating the surface microstructure and reducing microhardness.
items.authors: Tao Lv, Aibing Yu, Dongmei Wang

items.title: Monthly Peak-Shaving Control Strategies and Economic Analysis of an Ice-Storage Air-Conditioning System for Metro Stations
items.abstract: The energy consumption and electricity cost of air-conditioning systems in metro stations keep rising with the expansion of rail transit. Ice thermal-energy storage (ITES) shifts cooling load to off-peak hours, yet existing studies mostly optimize ice-storage operation on a daily scale and rarely address multi-chiller load distribution, the coordination of the large and small systems of a station, or monthly peak shaving adapted to the two-part electricity tariff. For a standard metro station with platform screen doors in Wuxi, China, the annual hourly cooling loads of the large and small systems are simulated with DeST 2.0, and energy-consumption models of the chillers, multi-split units, and pumps are established. A two-layer monthly peak-shaving framework is then proposed: for the large system, a balanced load-distribution strategy and three stored-cooling allocation schemes (base-load chiller priority, cold-storage priority, and peak shaving) integrated via a monthly load-baseline switching model; for the small system, three annual regulation strategies. The balanced load-distribution strategy saves 0.49–14.90% of energy compared with full-load operation; the combined cold-storage-priority and peak-shaving strategy reduces the monthly demand charge by 15.69% and the annual electricity cost by 2.32% versus the single cold-storage-priority strategy; the ice-storage scheme cuts the annual energy cost by 23.02% versus the conventional system, with peak-shifting and valley-utilization ratios of 56.89% and 39.75%; and the energy-efficiency-priority strategy lowers the small-system energy consumption, operating cost and carbon emission by 8.19% and 16.90%. As these strategies are derived from the load profile and tariff structure of the case station, their applicability to stations with different conditions requires further validation.
items.authors: Xianggan Zhao, Xiangui Shang, Junjie Jiang, Mingyang Gao, Mingyu Deng, Jing Chen

items.title: Dynamic Partner Retention, Network Dominance, and SME Productivity: A Statistical Modeling Approach
items.abstract: Static concentration measures cannot show whether economically important trading relationships persist over time. This study constructs transaction-value-weighted measures of supplier and customer retention and incorporates them into a network-augmented model of firm productivity. Chinese value-added tax invoices and matched firm records from 2019 to 2025 yield an unbalanced panel of 443,506 firm–year observations. Supplier stability is the share of current purchases from suppliers retained from the preceding year, while customer stability is defined analogously using sales. Annual directed, weighted transaction networks are reconstructed from invoice flows, and DomiRank measures firms’ structural dominance. Total factor productivity is estimated using the Levinsohn–Petrin method. Firm and year fixed-effects estimates show negative relationships between both stability dimensions and productivity. Two-stage least-squares estimates using leave-one-out same-industry peer stability as instruments remain negative. Positive interactions with DomiRank indicate that stronger network positions attenuate these relationships. Potential operating-channel analyses associate stable ties with higher gross margins and asset turnover, but also with greater expenses, weaker operating profitability, slower inventory turnover, and longer operating cycles. Results are robust to alternative measures, matching, high-dimensional fixed effects, outlier treatment, lagged specifications, and industry–year stratified permutation tests. The findings show how longitudinal transaction statistics and network position jointly explain productivity heterogeneity among SMEs.
items.authors: Hengyuan Zhang, Ke Peng

items.title: The 11th International Conference on Plasma Medicine (ICPM11) and the 10th International Workshop on Plasmas for Cancer Treatment (IWPCT10)
items.abstract: The 11th International Conference on Plasma Medicine (ICPM11), held jointly with the 10th International Workshop on Plasmas for Cancer Treatment (IWPCT10), took place from 31 May to 5 June 2026 in Gifu, Japan. The meeting brought together 225 scientists from 23 countries across four continents, reflecting the continued growth and interdisciplinary nature of plasma medicine. The scientific program included 24 invited lectures, 51 contributed oral presentations, and 133 poster presentations, covering advances in plasma–biological interactions, plasma-based cancer therapy, wound healing, antimicrobial applications, plasma-activated liquids, sterilization, and emerging biomedical and agricultural applications. This conference report provides an overview of ICPM11 and summarizes the scientific contributions presented during the meeting. The breadth of topics highlights the rapid progress of plasma medicine from fundamental research toward clinical and technological applications, emphasizing the importance of international collaboration in advancing the field.
items.authors: Sander Bekeschus, Hiromasa Tanaka, Vandana Miller

items.title: Research and Experiment on the Vibration Drag-Reducing Soil-Engaging Mechanism of a Full-Feed Topsoil Residual Film Recovery Machine for Xinjiang Cotton Fields
items.abstract: Long-term plastic mulching has caused severe residual film pollution in southern Xinjiang cotton fields, while conventional blade reclaimers face high operating resistance and soil accumulation in moist cohesive soil. This study developed a bionic vibration soil-engaging mechanism based on mole cricket claws to address this issue. The dual drag-reduction scheme works synergistically: the crank–rocker-driven movable blade generates periodic vibration (peak acceleration 150 m/s2) to fracture compacted soil and reduce adhesion ahead of the shovel, while the bionic tooth with an optimized wedge angle (30°) derived from mole cricket claw contours penetrates the pre-loosened soil with minimized geometric resistance. Mole cricket claw contours were extracted to optimize shovel geometry; optimal parameters were determined via EDEM–RecurDyn co-simulation and orthogonal tests, followed by field validation. At 1150 r/min vibration frequency,15 mm amplitude, and 0.5 m/s forward speed, eccentric shaft torque reached 12.72 N·m, with 9.33%and 13.29% drag reduction for bottom and side blades. The 2 m-wide mechanism cut soil accumulation height to 30.5 cm and achieved 16.46% maximum traction drag reduction, verified by field tests. This work provides technical support for residual film control in cohesive southern Xinjiang cotton fields.
items.authors: Qingyu Wu, Qizhi Yang, Lei Liu, Zhengliang Li, Ruoyu Zhang, Aiping Shi

items.title: Unlocking User-Generated Content for Academic Library Service Quality Assessment: A Multidimensional Text Analytics Framework
items.abstract: While traditional metrics and survey-based models such as LibQUAL+ grant valuable foundations for evaluating academic library service quality, they may not fully capture the immediacy and nuance of evolving patron experiences. As libraries increasingly become interactive community hubs, User-Generated Content, including Google reviews, provides a rich, authentic source of unfiltered feedback. Recognizing both the scalability obstacles of manual coding and the semantic limitations of conventional probabilistic models, this study puts forward a multidimensional text analytics framework designed to bridge these gaps with precision and sensitivity to user voices. Examining 8542 multilingual Google reviews from 88 academic libraries across a broad, multinational sample, this approach adopts a Zero-Shot Classification pipeline for theoretically anchored thematic categories with a rating-fortified VADER sentiment analysis to capture delicate emotional dimensions. Findings highlight a clear distribution of thematic feedback. While physical spaces and community events generate the highest satisfaction, digital infrastructure and staff interactions are identified as primary operational challenges. Finally, this data-driven framework seeks to transform unstructured UGC into actionable intelligence, supporting library administrators in making dynamic, evidence-based decisions that respond to the genuine needs and lived experiences of their communities.
items.authors: Ioannis C. Drivas, Eftichia Vraimaki, Nikolaos Lazaridis

items.title: Isolated Thyroid Metastasis from High-Grade Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma After Radical Nephrectomy: A Case Report
items.abstract: Background and Clinical Significance: Thyroid metastasis from clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) is uncommon and may occur after radical nephrectomy despite no evidence of residual or metastatic disease at that time. Diagnosis can be challenging because imaging and fine-needle aspiration (FNA) may mimic benign or primary thyroid lesions. Case Presentation: A 55-year-old man underwent left radical nephrectomy for WHO/ISUP grade 3 ccRCC with focal grade 4 differentiation. Two years later, surveillance ultrasonography detected a suspicious lesion involving the thyroid isthmus and left lobe. FNA was interpreted as Bethesda II (benign), but metastatic ccRCC was subsequently confirmed after total thyroidectomy. Histopathology showed focal vascular and capsular invasion. Tumor reached the margin of the main thyroid specimen, whereas separately submitted perithyroidal soft tissue had tumor-free margins, resulting in a final R0 resection. The tumor was positive for CK8/18, PAX8, EMA, vimentin, and CD10 and negative for TTF-1, thyroglobulin, calcitonin, and CD5. Postoperative 18F-FDG PET/CT showed no additional metastatic disease. Conclusions: Benign thyroid cytology should be interpreted cautiously in patients with previous ccRCC when clinical or imaging findings remain suspicious. Diagnosis requires integration of oncological history, imaging, histopathology, and immunohistochemistry. Surgical resection may provide local disease control in selected patients, with surveillance.
items.authors: Constantinos Papadopoulos, Konstantina Dinaki, Rafail Ioannidis, Ioanna Gravalidou, Anna Zisi

items.title: What Is Observed in Peer Review of Teaching? Quality Standards for Summative Peer Review of Teaching
items.abstract: Peer review of teaching is a relatively recent addition to the quality assurance processes of higher education. Formative peer review has a developmental focus, while summative peer review has an evaluative focus, making judgements against standards. These standards are at the core of the Summative Peer Review of Teaching (SPRoT) process. The SPRoT review project, which forms the focus of this paper, identified three key challenges associated with current standards at an Australian university, highlighting the need to critically re-examine and revitalise the standards. The subsequent review adopted an Action Research methodology underpinned by reflective practice theory to investigate these quality standards for peer review of teaching. Four cycles of Action Research are outlined in relation to the embedded single case study of a large metropolitan university. The outcome was six quality teaching standards for use with summative peer review of teaching. The standards are presented with the scholarly evidence-base that underpins each, together with observable indicators for each standard, that is, identifying what is observed in peer review of teaching.
items.authors: Anna D. Rowe, Marina Harvey, Christa Jacenyik-Trawoger

items.title: Integrated Turboshaft FADEC Architecture and the Effect of Governor Implementation on Protection-Layer Loading
items.abstract: Comparative studies of turboshaft fuel controllers commonly report performance advantages without holding the loop bandwidth or anti-windup implementation constant across the compared configurations. This paper asks what survives such a comparison. An integrated FADEC architecture for a GE T700-class turboshaft is developed on a nonlinear T-MATS model, combining a power turbine speed governor, a two-dimensional variable guide vane schedule, actuator and sensor dynamics with transport delays, and a seven-channel min–max protection layer. Three governors (gain-scheduled PI, fixed-gain PI and integral sliding-mode) are evaluated with identical anti-windup implementations, with their loop bandwidths matched by construction at the hover operating point used for the load-disturbance tests. Transient performance is closely comparable, with overshoot during scheduled transitions differing by at most 0.25 percentage points; however, protection-layer loading is not, as the sliding-mode governor holds the limiters active for 9.2% longer than the baseline under load disturbance. Removing the anti-windup tracking path changes cumulative limiter engagement by 6.6 times the difference attributable to the control law; the ordering survives both sensor noise and a ±20% perturbation of the power turbine inertia. Within the tested architecture, the dominant coupling between speed governance and engine protection is associated with the anti-windup implementation rather than the control law. Automatic code generation yields 37% less algorithm code for the sliding-mode configuration, with software-in-the-loop verification at a fixed 5 ms step.
items.authors: Masoud Norouzi, Ismail Bayezit, Mahmut Reyhanoglu

items.title: Small-Molecule Inhibitors Targeting Bacterial Antioxidants Potentiate Bactericidal Efficacy of Cold Atmospheric Plasma Against Staphylococcus aureus
items.abstract: Antibiotic-resistant Staphylococcus aureus infections pose a formidable clinical challenge. Cold atmospheric plasma (CAP) has emerged as a promising disinfection technology; however, the underlying bacterial response mechanisms and potential resistance to CAP remain incompletely elucidated. Here, we validated the broad-spectrum and efficient bactericidal activity of CAP against both drug-sensitive and drug-resistant clinical isolates of S. aureus. Mechanistically, CAP primarily eliminated bacteria by inducing oxidative damage to proteins and lipids, thereby disrupting internal cellular structures. The addition of exogenous free radical scavengers significantly attenuated CAP-mediated oxidative killing. Transcriptomic analysis and RT-qPCR validation further revealed upregulation of redox-related genes in S. aureus following CAP exposure. Deletion of key antioxidant genes, particularly ahpC and mrgA, markedly enhanced bacterial susceptibility to CAP. Virtual screening and surface plasmon resonance analysis identified two small-molecular inhibitors, C4515 and A8226, which specifically target AhpC and MrgA, respectively, and potentiated CAP bactericidal efficacy. Collectively, this study delineates the molecular interactions between CAP and S. aureus, and underscores the potential of CAP-based strategies for combating drug-resistant bacterial infections.
items.authors: Ruolan Ding, Li Tan, Xitong Zuo, Xiaonan Huang, Qishen Liang, Zhen Hu

items.title: Optimization Method for Measuring and Evaluating Hole-Group Position Under the Combined Effects of Datum Shift and Maximum Material Condition
items.abstract: This paper investigates the combined effects of the Maximum Material Condition (MMC) modifier and datum feature shift on hole-group positional tolerance evaluation. The formulation follows ASME Y14.5-2018 as the primary normative framework, with ISO GPS terminology as a supplementary comparative reference. A constrained minimum-zone virtual-gauge method is proposed for the virtual inspection of planar hole patterns. Virtual gauge is constructed according to virtual condition boundary definitions, and optimized by rigid rotation and translation under non-interference constraints and datum shift limits, to verify compliance of the measured hole group with position tolerance specifications. The experiments show that the proposed method achieves a relative error of 0.13% with respect to the near-global reference solution, while reducing the interference rate from 17% (unconstrained least-squares) to 0%. The method provides a computationally efficient virtual-gauge evaluation tool for quality control of planar hole groups under MMC and datum feature shift in engineering field.
items.authors: Hui Wang, Hanyun Zhang, Xinru Sheng, Ming Li, Qingyue Wei

items.title: Fear of Disease Progression in Patients with Alveolar Echinococcosis: Associations with Psychological, Psychosocial, and Medical Factors
items.abstract: Introduction: Alveolar echinococcosis is a chronic and potentially severe parasitic disease that often requires long-term treatment and is associated with considerable uncertainty regarding prognosis. These characteristics may contribute to significant psychological burden in affected individuals. The aim of this study was to assess the intensity of fear of disease progression among patients diagnosed with echinococcosis treated with different therapeutic approaches and to identify medical and psychosocial factors associated with higher levels of this fear. Method: A total of 35 patients with a diagnosis of alveolar echinococcosis participated in the study. Self-report questionnaires were used to measure anxiety, stress, and knowledge about the disease. Additional data were collected regarding the course of treatment and the nature of social responses after disclosure of the diagnosis. Results: A high level of fear of progression was reported by many patients—seven individuals rated their fear as maximal or near-maximal (9–10 on a 0–10 scale). Statistical analysis showed no significant associations between fear levels and medical variables such as treatment type, drug importation, or presence of side effects. However, a significant relationship was found between the intensity of fear and social reactions. Patients who experienced non-supportive or stigmatizing responses (e.g., shock, distancing, inappropriate comments) reported significantly higher levels of fear of progression compared to those who received support and understanding. Conclusions: Fear of disease progression may constitute a substantial psychological burden in patients with alveolar echinococcosis. In this sample, FoP was significantly associated with psychological and psychosocial variables, including negative social reactions, whereas no statistically significant associations were detected with the evaluated medical and treatment-related variables. These findings highlight the importance of considering the psychosocial context of AE and support the integration of psychological assessment and support into the clinical care of affected patients.
items.authors: Małgorzata Sulima, Agata Zdun-Ryżewska, Magdalena Błażek, Katarzyna Sikorska

items.title: Design of a Novel Hybrid Switched-Inductor/Switched-Capacitor DC-DC Step-Up Converter
items.abstract: In this paper, a new topology of a step-up DC converter is presented for renewable energy applications, yielding a high step-up conversion ratio and reduced voltage stress across the switches. The proposed converter uses a hybrid switched-inductor and switched-capacitor cell to achieve the high voltage gain. Additionally, the capacitors in the switched cell also perform the function of clamping the voltage across switches. The proposed converter utilizes only a single controlled switch and operates in only two modes of conduction. The steady-state analysis and operating principle of the proposed hybrid step-up converter are discussed in detail and various mathematical equations have been derived. The analysis shows numerous improvements over the traditional DC-DC converters. Simulation was carried out in MATLAB Simulink 2021b on a 55% duty cycle and simulation results are compared with theoretical analysis. From simulation results, it is clear the proposed converter exhibits better performance compared to conventional boost and other traditional step-up converters with the same design parameters. Finally, a 31.5-watt hardware prototype was constructed and tested in the laboratory to experimentally validate the theoretical and simulation results.
items.authors: Muhammad Uzair Shah, Zakir Ullah, Mohammed Alqarni, Muhammad I. Masud, Ajmal Farooq, Mian Muhammad Amir Ayaz

items.title: Seasonal Prior-Guided Dynamic Forecasting of Nonstationary Gridded PM2.5 Concentrations in China
items.abstract: Accurate and timely short-term forecasting of gridded PM2.5 concentrations is essential for air-quality management and public health protection, especially for the growing elderly population who are particularly vulnerable to air pollution. Advances in multi-source environmental data and deep learning have substantially improved the spatiotemporal prediction of PM2.5 concentrations. However, existing studies have mainly focused on developing increasingly sophisticated model architectures and optimization strategies while insufficiently considering the temporal nonstationarity of PM2.5 pollution and the recurrent characteristics associated with similar seasonal environmental regimes. Changes in natural environmental conditions and anthropogenic emissions can continuously alter the relationships governing PM2.5 concentrations, challenging the stability of continuous short-term forecasting; meanwhile, historically recurring seasonal pollution characteristics provide potentially valuable prior information for model adaptation. To address this problem, we propose a Seasonal Prior-guided Elastic Weight Consolidation (Seasonal EWC) framework for dynamic forecasting of nonstationary gridded PM2.5 concentrations in China. The framework derives season-specific parameter anchors and Fisher-based parameter importance from historical seasonal conditions and uses this prior knowledge to guide parameter updates during continuous short-term forecasting. Experiments with four representative spatiotemporal forecasting models showed that Seasonal EWC produced architecture-dependent changes in forecasting performance, reducing the annual mean MAE and RMSE by 30.3% and 31.7% for U-Net and by 10.9% and 7.6% for Earthformer, with only small improvements for IAM4VP and mixed changes for ConvLSTM. Parameter analysis revealed that Seasonal EWC reduced parameter-update magnitudes by approximately 27–32% and substantially limited long-term parameter deviation, indicating more stable adaptation during continuous forecasting. These findings demonstrate that seasonal prior knowledge can effectively guide dynamic model adaptation under evolving PM2.5 conditions, providing a promising approach for continuous short-term air-quality forecasting.
items.authors: Haoze Shi, Fuling Wen, Guiliang Zhong, Yang Jiang, Liangkun Deng, Shihan Shan

items.title: Weighted Analysis of Corrosion-Inducing Impurities in Supercritical CO2 Transportation System
items.abstract: The degradation of carbon steels in supercritical carbon dioxide is significantly influenced by impurities, yet a comprehensive understanding of the corrosion mechanism and unified industry standards remains lacking. In response to this challenge, an impact factor weight analysis of 27 published articles, comprising 149 observations, was performed to evaluate the response of the general corrosion rate of carbon steels to impurities such as oxygen, sulfur dioxide, hydrogen sulfide, and nitrogen oxides, as well as their mixtures. The findings indicate that the impurities have distinct effects on steel degradation in concentration- and exposure-time-dependent manners. Notably, sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides demonstrate a significant impact, oxygen plays a moderate role, while hydrogen sulfide exerts a profound influence on the corrosion rate of carbon steels. Hydrogen sulfide and oxygen exhibit a synergistic effect that accelerates degradation in supercritical carbon dioxide, whereas no pronounced synergistic effect is observed for sulfur dioxide and oxygen. This study provides a quantitative ranking of impurity impacts and demonstrates the impact level of the synergistic effects of oxygen, sulfur dioxide, and hydrogen sulfide, offering a scientific basis for developing pipeline integrity management strategies in supercritical carbon dioxide environments.
items.authors: Chao Zhang, Tong Gao

items.title: Scoring-Rule Dependence and Sign Instability in Vision–Language Covariate-Shift Monitoring for Camera Sensors
items.abstract: Camera-distribution monitoring and semantic out-of-distribution detection assign different meanings to weather and illumination changes. We evaluate specified departures from a camera reference distribution and distinguish the image representation from its scoring rule. Frozen CLIP ViT-B/32 gives AUROC 0.504 on a fixed PUG covariate-shift sample with content-prompt maximum cosine, but an ID-fitted Mahalanobis readout of the same encoder reaches 0.809. On BDD100K night, a text-free CLIP KNN readout reaches 0.913 versus 0.534 for maximum cosine. Prompt/scoring controls further demonstrate readout dependence and the effect of named-condition prior knowledge. On Boreas, the baseline ranks winter and evening shifts in opposite directions (AUROC 0.823 and 0.249). One threshold fitted on 500 separate summer calibration frames misses 44.8% of winter and 99.6% of evening frames, with 5.8% false alarms on held-out summer frames. Scene and position controls partly address acquisition confounding. A preprocessing audit overturns the original adversarial-training benefit; corrected checkpoint results and a separate five-seed study replace that conclusion. These results support evaluating complete encoder–score–prompt–calibration pipelines, with explicit sampling and operational limits.
items.authors: Loránt Szabó, Zoltán Weltsch

items.title: Performance Evaluation of WPA2 and WPA3 Security Protocols in Private Wi-Fi 6 Environments
items.authors: Bekzat Kabyshke, Assel Mukasheva, Dinargul Mukhammejanova, Bakyt Tulegenova, Almagul Bizhanova
items.category_raw: The International Conference on Electronics, Engineering Physics and Earth Science (EEPES2026)

items.title: AI Calibracy: A Future-Ready Competency Framework in AI-Supported Professional Judgment and Decision Making
items.abstract: AI Calibracy is a developmental competency that is defined in this entry as a learner’s or practitioner’s capacity to examine, coordinate, and progressively improve their judgment, external fresh evidence, computational models or simulations, and artificial intelligence (AI) within a specific decision context. What can be progressively improved is categorized into four bases of reliance, named as SEMA: Self, Evidence, Model or Simulation, and AI, and discussed in the paper. AI Calibracy is not supposed to prescribe a fixed hierarchy, numerical weighting, or a universal division of authority among these contributors. Instead, it identifies the capabilities required to recognize their relevance, limitations, assumptions, disagreements, and implications for professional judgment. The competency is introduced and also developed through the reliance calibration and regulation cycle (RCRC), as a process in which learners form an initial judgment, inspect evidence, test models, interrogate AI outputs, compare findings, identify uncertainty, revise their judgment and confidence, and reflect on outcomes across repeated tasks. In this concept, AI includes not only generative AI but also various functions such as predictive, diagnostic, recommendation, optimization, computer-vision, decision-support, and autonomous or semi-autonomous systems. AI Calibracy provides a definition for leadership, educators, curriculum design, pedagogy, professional development, assessment, and research into the capabilities required for responsible, as task-specific warrant and context-sensitive practice in AI-enabled environments.
items.authors: Samad M. E. Sepasgozar

items.title: Sensitive and Rapid Determination of Long-Chain Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances in Milk Using Fe3O4-PSA-Based Magnetic Solid-Phase Extraction Coupled with LC-MS/MS
items.abstract: A sensitive and time-saving method was developed for the determination of 11 long-chain per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFASs) in milk using magnetic solid phase extraction (MSPE) coupled with liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS). A primary–secondary amine-modified Fe3O4 (Fe3O4-PSA) sorbent was used for the extraction and enrichment of PFASs from milk. The adsorption behavior of PFASs on Fe3O4-PSA was investigated, and the experimental results suggest the involvement of electrostatic and hydrophobic interactions. Effects of sample solution pH, adsorbent amount, adsorption time, eluting solvent type, and elution time on the recovery of PFASs were investigated, and the optimal conditions were determined. The results show that the method exhibited good linearity (R2 0.9972) in the range of 0.005–20 μg/kg. The limit of detection (LOD) ranged from 0.008–0.062 μg/kg, and the limit of quantitation (LOQ) ranged from 0.0260–0.206 μg/kg. Recoveries of the 11 PFASs in spiked milk samples (0.5, 5, and 20 μg/kg) ranged from 79.4% to 118% with RSDs below 17%. Therefore, the developed method demonstrated potential for the determination of PFASs in milk samples.
items.authors: Tiantian Niu, Nannan Wu, Ranran Shi, Zhenzhen Liu, Siying Che, Xinquan Wang

items.title: Integrating Segment Anything Model 2 and Multimodal Generative Models for a Lightweight Projection Mapping Framework
items.authors: Fang-Yi Chao, Kuo-Yu Liu

items.title: Diagnostic Contribution of Histopathology in Medicolegal Autopsy: A Denominator-Specific Systematic Review
