items.abstract: Background/Objectives: Published estimates of histopathological examination (HPE) contribution in medicolegal autopsy use different denominators and outcome definitions. We examined what these estimates measure and their implications for practice. Methods: PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched from inception to 31 May 2026 (PROSPERO CRD420261401909). Eligible studies reported denominator-specific HPE contribution. Cause of death (COD) provision and change were distinguished from manner change, confirmation, refinement, and targeted forensic interpretation. JBI checklists supported item-level appraisal. Findings were synthesized narratively without pooling. Results: Twenty-one studies were included from 2287 identified records. Strict COD change was reported in 0/100 uncomplicated hanging suicides and 1/189 gross-clear medicolegal autopsies. A broad systematic-histology cohort reported histology-only COD provision in 36/428 cases. In separate unresolved-COD populations, studies reported COD provision in 49/203 and 40/71 cases. These results address different diagnostic questions and do not establish a relationship between uncertainty and yield. Selected denominators, composite outcomes, and incomplete separation from other investigations limited interpretation. Confirmation, injury assessment, and organ-specific findings represented additional functions. Conclusions: There is no single transferable HPE yield: the pre-HPE diagnosis, denominator, outcome definition, and contribution of other investigations must accompany each estimate. The review supports clearer reporting and interpretation of HPE contribution; low rates of COD change do not establish when histology can safely be omitted.
items.authors: Mohammed Sait, Fawaz Almutairi

items.title: We (Nosotras) the People: Women, Equality, and Parity in Latin American and Caribbean Constitutionalism
items.abstract: Constitutions do more than distribute public powers: they identify the political community, define the subjects of rights, and entrench the principles that legitimate public action. This article examines how twenty constitutional jurisdictions in Latin America and the Caribbean incorporate equality between women and men. It applies a qualitative comparative legal method to constitutional texts in force at the study cutoff date and codes six dimensions: constitutional language; equality as a foundational value or interpretive principle; formal equality; anti-discrimination guarantees; substantive equality and affirmative action; and parity or balanced representation. The findings reveal a layered but uneven process of constitutionalization. All texts recognize formal equality, but only ten expressly formulate equality between women and men, fifteen expressly include sex or gender within constitutional anti-discrimination protection, and six constitutionalize parity or balanced participation in public decision-making. Inclusive constitutional language and substantive-equality mandates are concentrated in a smaller group of texts. The article argues that constitutional equality should be assessed through four cumulative layers of constitutional depth: symbolic inclusion, status equality, transformative equality, and power-sharing equality. Latin American constitutionalism has generated notable innovations, particularly in parity democracy, yet constitutional design remains insufficient without enforceable duties, effective institutions, electoral safeguards, resources, and protection against political violence.
items.authors: Lara Martínez de Aragón López, Laura Nuño Gómez

items.title: Root-Based Phytostabilization of Thorium and Uranium in Rare Earth Element-Rich Soils
items.abstract: The expansion of rare earth element (REE) mining has raised concerns about the environmental risks associated with radioactive elements, particularly thorium (Th) and uranium (U), which commonly occur alongside REE-bearing minerals. We investigated the uptake and distribution of Th and U in Pseudoroegneria spicata and Phalaris arundinacea, two grass species previously shown to accumulate REEs effectively. Seven varieties of each species were grown under climate-controlled greenhouse conditions in REE-rich soil collected from the Diamond Creek district near Salmon, ID, USA. Plants were arranged in a randomized complete block design, and Th and U concentrations were analyzed separately in root and shoot tissues. The bioaccumulation factor and translocation factor were calculated to characterize radionuclide uptake and distribution within the plants. Our results showed that P. arundinacea accumulated slightly more Th and U; however, variance due to species was not significant. Tissue type (root vs. shoot) significantly impacted plant Th and U concentrations, with roots accumulating more than shoots for both species. Their limited shoot translocation and preferential root retention indicate potential for phytostabilization, although neither species met hyperaccumulation criteria for Th or U. The life cycle assessment and techno-economic assessment conducted at the greenhouse scale identified electricity consumption as the primary environmental and economic constraint, with a global warming potential of approximately 126 kg CO2-eq and an operating cost of $10,920 per metric ton of soil treated. These findings indicate the potential of P. spicata and P. arundinacea for root-based phytostabilization of Th and U in REE-rich soils.
items.authors: Sneha Pradhananga, Kathryn Richardson, Amin Mirkouei

items.title: Fruit Quality Classification Through Feature Fusion and Deep Learning
items.abstract: Fruit quality assessment is an integral part of food safety, loss reduction after harvest and consumer satisfaction. In modern agricultural production systems, where quality control is essential for ensuring both domestic and export markets, it continues to play a vital role. Manual grading, which is widely used, is poorly time-efficient, imprecise, and prone to human error, and is reliant upon the human eye and human skill. Such limiting practices can result in variability and, in large-scale production, high operating expenses. In this paper, we propose a hybrid classification model using deep learning features extracted from ResNet50V2 along with traditional handcrafted features such as Histogram of Gradients (HOG), Local Binary Patterns (LBP), and color, texture and shape descriptors. The purpose of this study is to develop a model to combine high-level and low-level feature representation to gain a comprehensive understanding of fruit quality characteristics. The proposed preprocessing technique will be followed by data augmentation, ANOVA-based feature selection, and classification using K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Random Forest (RF) and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost). This multi-stage course of action is specifically designed so that the extracted features are appropriate, relevant and discriminative for correct classification. For experimentation, standard datasets were chosen as FruitNet and tomato. There are six fruit types included in the FruitNet dataset with three different quality classes, and another tomato dataset with three ripeness-based classes. XGBoost always outperforms other classifiers on the FruitNet dataset with an accuracy of 97.3% and on the tomato dataset with an accuracy of 92%. The findings validate the validity of the proposed model and its use in all crops under all grading systems.
items.authors: Shajia Nafees, Muhammad Javed Iqbal, Iftikhar Ahmad, Madini O. Alassafi, Neelum Noreen

items.title: Comparison of Treatment Zone Decentration Between VISUMAX 500 and VISUMAX 800 Keratorefractive Lenticule Extraction Using Anterior Segment Optical Coherence Tomography
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: To compare treatment-zone decentration after small-incision lenticule extraction (SMILE) performed with VISUMAX 500 and VISUMAX 800 using corneal thickness difference maps derived from anterior segment optical coherence tomography. Methods: This retrospective comparative study included 44 eyes of 22 participants who underwent SMILE with VISUMAX 500 or VISUMAX 800 by a single surgeon and had preoperative and 3-month postoperative CASIA2 examinations. Treatment-zone centers were primarily identified manually relative to the corneal vertex. Between-platform differences were analyzed using generalized estimating equations (GEE) accounting for inter-eye correlation, with additional adjustment for preoperative cylinder. Participant-level analyses and semi-automated radial color-symmetry localization were performed as sensitivity analyses. Results: Twenty-two eyes of 11 participants were included in each group. Mean radial decentration was 0.219 ± 0.134 mm with VISUMAX 500 and 0.225 ± 0.171 mm with VISUMAX 800. The mean between-group difference was 0.006 mm (95% confidence interval [CI], −0.074 to 0.085; p = 0.890), and remained similar after adjustment for preoperative cylinder (0.006 mm; 95% CI, −0.082 to 0.094; p = 0.888). Participant-level analysis likewise showed no evidence of a between-group difference (mean difference, 0.0056 mm; 95% CI, −0.083 to 0.094; exact permutation p = 0.907). Reanalysis using semi-automated localization yielded a similarly small between-platform difference (0.0114 mm; 95% CI, −0.063 to 0.086; p = 0.763). Conclusions: In this small single-surgeon cohort, treatment-zone decentration did not differ significantly between VISUMAX 500 and VISUMAX 800. The findings were consistent across participant-level and semi-automated sensitivity analyses. Because the study was not designed as an equivalence or noninferiority trial, these results should be interpreted as an absence of evidence for a between-platform difference rather than evidence of equivalent centration performance.
items.authors: Tae Keun Yoo, Si-Hoon Park, Sang-Mok Lee

items.title: Perturbation Stability in Evaluating Modified Stieltjes Continued Fractions for Modern Applications
items.abstract: Due to the demands of modern applications, such as forecasting using ordinal continued fraction regression models in economics, the study of structural stability to data perturbations has become an urgent need. While continued fractions demonstrate superior effectiveness over traditional polynomial models due to their inherent structural stability, their sensitivity to coefficient perturbations can lead to accuracy loss under finite-precision machine arithmetic. This paper investigates the stability to perturbations of the coefficients of modified Stieltjes continued fractions (modified S-fractions). We develop a rigorous theoretical framework based on a fundamental recursive formula for the relative error of the nth approximant, expressing error propagation directly in terms of coefficient perturbations. Using this geometric and analytical approach, we establish three distinct uniform stability sets in the complex plane: the half-plane ΩC, the angular set Ωα,C under weaker geometric conditions, and the exterior of the disk ΩR, which extends verified stability directly to points on and near the imaginary axis. Furthermore, we derive explicit, a priori error bounds for each stability set and prove pointwise stability on a significantly expanded domain, demonstrating that the modified S-fraction remains stable on R∖{0} for any bounded coefficients. These findings establish explicit boundaries for safe computation using standard double-precision arithmetic, providing a mathematical guarantee of algorithmic stability for high-demand contemporary applied models.
items.authors: Roman Dmytryshyn, Volodymyr Hladun

items.title: Dried Urine Spots for Quantification of C0 (Free) Carnitine Excretion: A Validated Method for Follow-Up and Confirmatory Testing of Primary Carnitine Deficiency
items.abstract: Primary carnitine deficiency (PCD), caused by Organic Cation Transporter Novel 2 (OCTN2) deficiency, is detected by newborn screening (NBS) through low blood free carnitine (C0) concentrations. Confirmation of the diagnosis may be supported by demonstrating increased urinary C0 excretion, but urine collection in newborns is technically challenging. We developed and validated a dried urine spot (DUS) method for quantifying urinary C0 excretion as a practical, non-invasive alternative to conventional liquid urine sampling. This approach has the potential to allow parents to obtain urine at home by placing filter paper cards between the baby’s skin and a dry diaper, simplifying sample collection. C0 carnitine and creatinine were quantified in 6 mm DUS punches by flow injection analysis–tandem mass spectrometry (FIA–MS/MS) following butylation. The method was analytically validated for sensitivity, precision, stability, and agreement with liquid urine measurements. The method demonstrated excellent analytical performance, with lower limits of detection (LLOD)/lower limits of quantification (LLOQ) values of 0.02/0.07 µmol/L for C0 and 0.01/0.04 mmol/L for creatinine. Normalization of C0 to creatinine reduced variability related to sampling and punch location. Both analytes remained stable in DUS for at least 10 days at room temperature and after 11 freeze–thaw cycles. C0/creatinine obtained from DUS showed excellent agreement with liquid urine (R2 0.9967), although concentrations were consistently lower, requiring a correction factor of 1.27 to estimate concentrations equivalent to liquid urine. DUS provides a reliable and accurate alternative to liquid urine for measuring C0 excretion in newborns. This simple, home-based sampling approach facilitates non-invasive urine collection and has the potential to support follow-up and confirmatory testing of PCD.
items.authors: Maria van der Ham, Sacha Ferdinandusse, Mirjam Langeveld, Sabine A. Fuchs, Monique G. M. de Sain van der Velden,

items.title: Pilot-Efficient Channel Estimation with FortiTran for Underwater Wireless Optical OFDM Systems
items.abstract: In underwater wireless optical communication (UWOC) systems with orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM), water absorption, scattering, and transceiver misalignment increase the difficulty of accurate channel estimation. Estimation accuracy generally improves with pilot density, but a higher pilot density reduces the resources available for data transmission. This work adapts Fortified Transformer (FortiTran) to sparse pilot UWOC OFDM channel estimation. FortiTran captures both local correlations and broader time frequency variations in UWOC channels through its local and global modeling capabilities. For each pilot density, a separate model is trained and evaluated in both simulation and experiment to compare the normalized mean square error (NMSE), bit error ratio (BER), and pilot overhead across the tested pilot configurations. FortiTran achieves lower NMSE and BER than ChannelNet across the evaluated pilot densities in both simulation and experiment. At an experimental pilot density of 9.52%, FortiTran achieves a BER of 3.69×10−3, compared with 5.24×10−3 for ChannelNet, corresponding to a reduction of 29.56%. For the matched BER comparison, ChannelNet at a pilot density of 25% provides the reference BER, and the corresponding interpolated pilot overhead reductions of FortiTran are 60.10% in simulation and 49.26% in the experiment.
items.authors: Jingyi Jia, Zixiong Wang, Shiyu Zhang, Hao Luo, Shiying Han, Changyuan Yu

items.title: Explicit Feature Extraction and Soft Sensing Application for Chemical Processes Based on Dynamic Symbolic Regression Network
items.abstract: Quality indicators are critical for process monitoring and safety assessment in industrial chemical processes, yet their online measurement remains difficult or cost-prohibitive. This work presents a transparent and accurate soft sensor development framework termed the Dynamic Symbolic Regression Network (DSRN), which explicitly reconstructs symbolic relationships between easy-to-measure process variables and target quality indicators. Unlike mainstream black-box deep learning approaches, the proposed method leverages symbolic regression techniques to derive interpretable mathematical expressions. A genetic algorithm is employed to search for multi-layer optimal symbolic structures, while time-lag terms are incorporated to capture dynamic features, thereby revealing interpretable data-driven relationships within the chemical process. Furthermore, a fully objective feature selection strategy is introduced to determine the optimal subset of auxiliary variables by evaluating the uncertainty of the quality indicator via information entropy, which reduces the dimensionality of the DSRN input space and focuses the symbolic search on informative process variables. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is first demonstrated on a numerical example, where it accurately recovers the true variable relationships and achieves superior prediction performance. A case study on the Dow data challenge problem further validates that DSRN attains competitive prediction accuracy compared with advanced deep learning models, while offering explicit mathematical equations that provide valuable interpretability for operators. These results highlight the great potential of DSRN for practical process monitoring and control applications.
items.authors: Cheng Ji, Chi Zhai, Jingzhi Rao, Jingde Wang, Xiaozhong Chu, Wei Sun

items.title: Consumer Valuation of AR-Enabled Indoor Navigation in Shopping Malls: A Choice-Based Conjoint Analysis
items.abstract: Augmented reality (AR) indoor navigation can combine wayfinding, information, gamification, and promotions in shopping malls, but how consumers value these features is unclear. In a choice-based conjoint experiment, 295 South Korean adults aged 20–49 from an online panel chose among hypothetical service profiles varying in Navigation Mode, Information Layering, Interactive Character Feature, Reward Type, Reward Acquisition Mode, and monthly fee; a conditional logit model estimated utilities, relative importance, and marginal willingness to pay (MWTP). Within the levels and ranges tested, price showed the highest range-based relative importance (52.2%), followed by Navigation Mode (14.1%) and Information Layering (12.7%). Within the experimental choice sets, conditional MWTP relative to the reference levels was KRW 540 per month (95% CI: 377–702) for Map + AR Guidance and KRW 488 (95% CI: 326–649) for Route + Facility Information + Discount Information. Instant Discount Coupons were preferred to Reward Points and Prize Draw Entry, and Visit-Based acquisition was preferred to Social-Interaction-Based acquisition. The Interactive Character Feature had no significant average effect, but its utility was higher among respondents with greater context-specific gamification-feature affinity. These stated-preference findings suggest a layered design for the proposed service, with guidance and contextual information as the functional core and gamified features as optional.
items.authors: Hyojae Kim, Kangu Lee, Merve Sultan Demirkaya, Changjun Lee
items.category_raw: Journal of Theoretical and Applied Electronic Commerce Research

items.title: Stable Image Regression via Adaptive Aggregation of Noisy Predictions and Input-Gradient-Regularized Fine-Tuning
items.abstract: Image regression models may exhibit substantial output variation under small input perturbations, which can reduce their reliability in applications requiring continuous predictions. This study investigates whether adaptive aggregation of noise-perturbed predictions, combined with explicit control of model sensitivity, can jointly improve local stability and predictive accuracy. The proposed method fine-tunes a base regressor using input-gradient regularization and learns a permutation-invariant, data-dependent aggregation operator. The aggregator uses a smooth quantile-like parameterization that adapts to the distribution of noisy predictions. A first-order decomposition defines the score B(x), which is used as a practical diagnostic rather than a formal robustness certificate. Its numerical value depends on the initialization and number of ascent steps used for its estimation. The method is evaluated on three image regression tasks: image quality assessment, facial age estimation, and crowd counting. Compared with fixed mean, trimmed-mean, and median aggregation, the proposed approach provides a more favorable accuracy–stability trade-off across the evaluated tasks and perturbation settings. Ablation and transfer analyses further distinguish the effects of learned aggregation and model fine-tuning and examine their dependence on smoothing parameters, tasks, and architectures. The results indicate that adaptive aggregation and sensitivity-controlled fine-tuning constitute a practical approach for improving the empirical local stability of image regression systems.
items.authors: Ekaterina Shumitskaya, Dmitriy Vatolin, Anastasia Antsiferova

items.title: Impact of Low-Carbon City Policies on Carbon Emissions: A Case Study of Central China
items.abstract: Against the backdrop of China’s “dual-carbon” goals, the low-carbon city pilot (LCCP) program has become an important policy instrument for promoting urban green and low-carbon transformation. Using panel data from cities in Central China over the period 2011–2023, this study employs a multi-period difference-in-differences (DID) model to examine the impact of the LCCP program on urban carbon emissions and its underlying mechanisms. The results show that the LCCP program significantly reduces urban carbon emissions, and this finding remains robust to a series of robustness checks. Mechanism analysis indicates that the LCCP program significantly increases technological innovation, although the corresponding indirect effect on carbon emissions is not statistically significant. By contrast, energy intensity and fiscal autonomy exhibit significant competitive mediation effects, suggesting that the policy’s direct emission reduction effect interacts with indirect transmission channels associated with energy efficiency and local fiscal resource allocation. Furthermore, the emission reduction effect of the LCCP program is more pronounced in non-resource-based cities and small- and medium-sized cities, while no statistically significant effect is observed in resource-based or large cities. Spatial econometric analysis reveals significant spatial dependence in urban carbon emissions. Although the LCCP policy generates a significant local emission reduction effect, no robust evidence of cross-city policy spillovers is identified. These findings provide empirical evidence for understanding the effectiveness and transmission mechanisms of low-carbon policies and offer useful insights for advancing differentiated and coordinated low-carbon development in Central China.
items.authors: Qiang Wang, Xuerong Kong, Wenchao Li

items.title: Ionic-Liquid-Catalyzed Depolymerization of PET: BHET Recovery and Re-Polymerization
items.abstract: The accumulation of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) waste presents significant environmental challenges due to its extensive usage and low global recycling rates. Among the available recycling routes, chemical depolymerization by glycolysis offers a promising way to recover high-value monomers. In this study, six ionic liquids (ILs) were tested as homogeneous catalysts for the glycolysis of post-consumer PET bottles in ethylene glycol (EG) at 200 °C for 3 h, alongside an uncatalyzed control. 1-Butyl-3-methylimidazolium acetate ([BMIM][OAc]) and trihexyltetradecylphosphonium decanoate ([P6,6,6,14][Dec]) gave complete PET conversion with isolated bis(2-hydroxyethyl) terephthalate (BHET) yields of 33.6% and 72.4%, respectively. Moreover, trihexyltetradecylphosphonium bis(2,4,4-trimethylpentyl)phosphinate ([P6,6,6,14][TMPP]) reached 56% conversion with no separable product; however, the other three chloride-based ILs and the control reaction demonstrated negligible conversion at the given process parameters. The recovered BHET was characterized by FT-IR, 1H and 13C NMR and GC-MS, and further, was re-polymerized by melt polycondensation at 270 °C. The FT-IR fingerprint, thermogravimetric decomposition profile and solid-state 13C NMR spectrum indicated that the properties of the recycled PET compete with those of the bottlegrade PET. Their melting peak lay 7.7 °C below the reference on first heating (240.6 vs. 248.3 °C) but rose to 248.5 °C on second heating, 3.3 °C above the reference, suggesting that the initial difference arises mainly from crystal perfection and thermal history rather than from an altered chain structure.
items.authors: Akmuhammet Karayev, Farrukh Shehzad, Hassam Mazhar, Mamdouh A. Al-Harthi

items.title: TMAO at the Crossroads of the Gut–Brain Axis: Emerging Mechanisms Linking Microbiota-Derived Metabolites to Neuroinflammation and Cognitive Dysfunction
items.abstract: Trimethylamine-N-oxide (TMAO) is a gut microbiota-derived metabolite produced through the hepatic oxidation of trimethylamine. Although TMAO has been widely investigated as a therapeutic target in multiple cardiovascular and metabolic diseases, growing evidence suggests it may play a critical role in the neuroinflammation and cognitive dysfunction associated with the gut–brain axis. This narrative review summarizes the current literature to synthesize evidence on the mechanisms linking TMAO with neurological disorders; it discusses potential mechanisms contributing to this association, with particular focus on neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, and activation of inflammatory pathways. Overall, this review also suggests the potential use of TMAO and its precursors as therapeutic targets for multiple neurodegenerative disorders. However, it emphasizes the need for conducting large, adequately powered randomized clinical studies to determine its therapeutic relevance.
items.authors: Aseel Y. Altahrawi, Fatimah Sofi, Zara Kanjwal, Zahoor A. Shah

items.title: The Legacy of Mrs. H.S. Ball’s Chutney: A Psychobiography of Amelia Adkins from Familial Identity to Multicultural Nationality
items.abstract: Identity and nationality develop around shared symbols, traditions and cultural practices. Chutney, as a condiment and culinary tradition, embodies South African multicultural heritage, which include narratives surrounding British settler, Indian and Malaysian influences. Amelia Adkins, associated with the development and commercialisation of Mrs. H.S. Ball’s Chutney, occupies an iconized position in South African food culture. The aim and purpose of this psychobiography was to uncover and illuminate the psychosocial development; personality traits, and identity within the sociocultural context of Amelia’s life to elucidate her transformation from a familial identity into that of a shared symbol of multicultural nationality. Amelia was selected as subject via purposive sampling. Data sources included publicly available biographical and historical material. Alexander’s nine thematic indicators were used for the extraction of salient data, which were analysed via Erikson’s psychosocial theory, Costa and McCrae’s personality analysis, and Mayer, Paul J. P. Fouché and Van Niekerk’s perspective of identity within sociocultural context. Inferred findings and conclusions suggest that Amelia’s life reflected psychosocial dimensions and personality traits of self-determination, entrepreneurship, generativity, industriousness, conscientiousness, and an identity that symbolizes multicultural nationality. Mrs. H.S. Ball’s symbolises a cultural artifact through which many South Africans continue to express shared identity, memories, stories, heritage and national belonging.
items.authors: Paul J. P. Fouché

items.title: The Integration of AI in CRM and Its Impact on Online Sales Services Profitability: A Systematic Literature Review
items.abstract: The rise of e-commerce is leading companies to rethink their customer relationship management (CRM), particularly through the integration of artificial intelligence (AI). AI opens up opportunities for personalization, automation, and optimization of customer interactions, potentially improving sales performance and the profitability of online sales services. This article examines, through a systematic literature review (SLR), the impact of AI integration in CRM on the profitability of online sales services. Following a rigorous selection process using the Scopus and Web of Science databases, and covering the period 2016–2026, 51 studies were selected for analysis. The results show that the integration of AI technologies into CRM functionalities has positive associations or perceived improvements, but causal evidence for profitability remains thin in all the selected studies, regardless of the geographical context, the technologies used, or the performance indicators considered. The limitations identified in the existing literature open several avenues for future research, including a more rigorous measurement of online sales profitability and improved geographical contextualization of studies.
items.authors: Khaoula Fath El Khair, Ahmad El Oualfi, Mustapha El Hamzaoui, Miloudi Kobiyh
items.category_raw: Journal of Theoretical and Applied Electronic Commerce Research

items.title: Bringing the 6 F-Words into Primary School: Development and Validation of the ‘I Know Myself Well’ Questionnaire
items.abstract: The F-Words framework introduces a holistic view of child development. This study evaluated the preliminary development and psychometric properties of the ‘I Know Myself Well’ questionnaire, a new self-report measure based on this framework. Participants included 209 primary school students in Northern Italy. Using a cross-validation framework, exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses revealed a robust two-factor structure (EFA = 90; CFA = 119): Relational Self-Awareness and Agentic Self-Projection. The scale demonstrated satisfactory fit indices and acceptable overall internal consistency. This brief tool provides a psychometrically sound, child-centered instrument to support inclusive educational planning and early career development.
items.authors: Aida Faraji, Lea Ferrari

items.title: Effects of Immersive Virtual Reality and Relaxation Video on Symptom Severity, Distress, and Quality of Life in Lung Cancer Patients During Initial Chemotherapy Cycles: A Three-Arm Randomised Controlled Trial
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: To examine the effects of immersive virtual reality (VR) and a theme-matched relaxation video (RV) on symptom severity, distress, and quality of life in lung cancer patients. Methods: In this open-label, three-arm, parallel-group randomised controlled trial, 315 patients were allocated (1:1:1) to the VR (n = 106), RV (n = 104), or control (CG; n = 105) group. During the first two chemotherapy cycles, the VR and RV groups were assigned two 20 min sessions of immersive nature-themed VR or theme-matched RV, while the CG received routine care alone. The primary outcome domain was symptom severity, assessed through within-session changes in ten individual Edmonton Symptom Assessment Scale (ESAS) symptom scores; distress and quality of life were secondary outcomes. Data were analysed with linear mixed models, and between-group differences are reported with Bonferroni-adjusted 95% confidence intervals (CI). Results: Compared with the CG, the within-session improvement was greater for eight of the ten ESAS symptoms with VR and for five with RV; the largest differences were for well-being (VR 1.26 points, 95% CI 0.98 to 1.53; RV 0.76, 0.49 to 1.03), with smaller differences for tiredness, depression, and anxiety. Distress also decreased more with VR (1.04, 0.73 to 1.34) and RV (0.73, 0.42 to 1.03) than in the CG. VR improved more than RV for well-being (0.50, 0.22 to 0.77), tiredness (0.47, 0.16 to 0.79), and distress (0.31, 0.002 to 0.62). No intervention-specific effect emerged for nausea, lack of appetite, or quality of life. Conclusions: Compared with routine care, two sessions of VR or RV improved acute symptoms, mainly well-being, tiredness, depression, and anxiety, and reduced distress, with no intervention-specific effect on quality of life. The additional benefit of VR was small and, for the ESAS symptoms, below the minimal clinically important difference, so RV may be a practical and accessible option. Study registration: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06863623.
items.authors: Kadir Baysoy, Nur Izgu, Leyla Ozdemir, Fatma Alev Turker, Dogan Uncu, Berna Oksuzoglu

items.title: Nitrogen Homeostasis Reveals an Internal Inconsistency in the Energy Balance Model’s Predicted Coincidence of Energy Balance and Body Weight Stability
items.abstract: The Energy Balance Model predicts that energy balance coincides with body weight stability. The present analysis shows that this relationship emerges from the canonical equations of the model rather than from an assumption introduced by the study. Further analytical examination demonstrates that this predicted state corresponds to fat mass and fat-free mass stability and consequently requires nitrogen homeostasis. These conditions lead to a coupled mass- and energy-accounting system. When solved without enforcing nitrogen homeostasis, the equilibrium solution requires persistent carbohydrate accumulation, protein depletion, and negative nitrogen balance, a combination physiologically incompatible with a prolonged steady body weight. Conversely, enforcing the already-derived requirement of zero nitrogen balance eliminates these macronutrient imbalances but requires obligatory non-urinary nitrogen losses to vanish, which is physiologically impossible. Thus, the contradiction arises from the model’s equilibrium structure. By formal analytical reasoning, prolonged body weight stability must therefore coexist with energy imbalance, a conclusion consistent with observations of stable body weight despite apparent energy imbalance and randomized metabolic-ward data in which energy imbalance failed to correctly predict both the direction and magnitude of body weight change. Energy imbalance alone cannot sufficiently describe body weight dynamics because energetic quantities do not uniquely specify material fluxes.
items.authors: Francisco Arencibia-Albite

items.title: Insulin Intensification and Simplification Strategies in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes and Overweight or Obesity: A Scoping Review
items.abstract: Overweight and obesity complicate insulin treatment in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), requiring consideration of glycaemic control, insulin requirements, body weight, and treatment burden. This scoping review mapped insulin treatment modification (ITM) strategies, synthesised their reported outcomes, and identified evidence gaps among insulin-treated adults with T2DM and overweight or obesity. Five electronic databases were searched following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) and updated Joanna Briggs Institute methodological guidance. Thirty-three studies were classified into four ITM domains: add-on therapy to insulin, switching to advanced insulin formulations, simplifying complex insulin regimens with adjunctive therapy, and switching to fixed-ratio combinations. Intensification was generally studied in patients with higher baseline glycated haemoglobin or insulin requirements, whereas simplification was more often evaluated in those receiving complex insulin regimens. Insulin-dominant intensification generally increased total daily insulin dose, while intensification incorporating Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists (GLP-1RAs) or Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter-2 Inhibitors (SGLT2i) commonly reduced insulin requirements and body weight. Simplification generally reduced insulin requirements and/or injection burden while maintaining or improving glycaemic control, with weight reduction frequently reported. Direct comparisons and obesity-specific subgroup analyses were limited. Intensification and simplification should therefore be considered complementary rather than opposing approaches, with outcomes influenced by therapeutic components and patient characteristics.
items.authors: Chew Huey Chua, Wei Lim Chong, Hasniza Zaman Huri

items.title: A Robotic Picking Framework for Autonomous Singulation of Sweetpotato Slips into Chainpots
items.abstract: Labor shortages in agriculture, particularly for tasks requiring high dexterity such as sweetpotato transplanting, have increased the need for robotic automation. Although automated transplanting machines are available, they require manually singulated slips to be loaded into chainpots, making the overall process labor-intensive and costly. To address this limitation, this work investigates the feasibility and challenges of a robotic framework for automating the slip singulation task in chainpots. The proposed framework integrates a general-purpose robotic manipulator, a 3D camera, and a parallel-jaw gripper. The perception system consists of two core modules: (1) a deep learning-based instance segmentation and keypoint detection model for localizing individual slips and estimating their transplanting direction, and (2) a simple analytical grasp-planning algorithm for computing stable and collision-free grasp poses. To overcome the limited availability of annotated training data, a novel data generation pipeline is developed to create a large synthetic annotated dataset from a small collection of real-world images. The proposed pipeline generates photorealistic cluttered scenes by randomly compositing annotated top-down images of individual slips onto a target background while simultaneously applying domain randomization. During real-world experiments conducted under controlled laboratory conditions, the robotic framework achieved a grasp success rate of 72–100% and a transplanting success rate of 75–88%, depending on the degree of slip overlap, occlusion, and leaf entanglement. The proposed framework represents an initial important step toward the development of a fully automated robotic system for sweetpotato slip transplanting.
items.authors: Prem Raj, Weilong He, Alexandria Brown, Yuxi Chen, Azlan Zahid, Lirong Xiang

items.title: Diachronic Register Variation in Saudi Business Journalism: A Multidimensional Analysis of the Vision 2030 Period
items.abstract: This study investigates diachronic register variation in Saudi business journalism across three stages of Vision 2030. Using Biber’s multidimensional framework, the study examines whether English-language business news in Saudi Arabia has changed in terms of informational density, narrative orientation, explicitness, overt persuasion, and abstract or impersonal style. The corpus consists of 571 business news texts collected from Arab News, Saudi Gazette, and the Saudi Press Agency. The texts are divided into three periods: 2016 to 2018, representing the early stage of Vision 2030; 2020 to 2022, representing the middle stage; and 2024 to 2026, representing the recent stage. Each text was prepared as a 400-token analytical sample, tagged for multidimensional features, normalised, and assigned scores on Biber’s five textual dimensions. One-way ANOVA, Levene’s test, Welch and Brown–Forsythe robust tests, and Tukey HSD post hoc comparisons were used to examine period-based differences. The findings show the strongest linguistic change in Dimension 1 and Dimension 4. Saudi business journalism became substantially more informational across the three periods, while overt persuasive and argumentative marking declined significantly. Dimension 2 and Dimension 3 showed more limited and period-specific variation, while Dimension 5 remained broadly stable despite some evidence from robust tests. Overall, the results suggest that Saudi business journalism has moved from a comparatively more persuasive and developmental style in the early Vision 2030 period toward a more informational, institutional, and report-oriented register in the recent period. The study contributes to corpus-based register analysis, Saudi media discourse research, and the linguistic study of economic journalism.
items.authors: Mohammad Rishad Faridi, Sadia Ali

items.title: Flood-Induced Scour Failure Mechanisms and Multi-Level Protection of Riverside Highway Embankments: A Physical Model Study
items.abstract: Scaled flume tests based on Froude similarity (λ = 1:50) were conducted to clarify the internal stress-field evolution and multi-level protection mechanisms during flood scour of riverside highway embankments. An 18-channel miniature earth-pressure system embedded along the slope, with dual-view cameras, provided synchronous acquisition. Six non-replicated tests covered three protection levels (unprotected; semi-protected with gabion and geotextile; fully protected with an additional spur dike) at three flow velocities, yielding approximately 288,000 time-series readings (about 16,000 synchronous time steps). Scour failure followed a unified four-stage evolution: flow establishment and seepage onset, scour expansion and toe instability, progressive collapse and failure surface extension, and scour-hole stabilization with residual transport. Increasing velocity accelerated failure and shifted the mode from progressive toe scour to rapid retrogressive erosion. Protection structures exerted a dual effect, delaying failure at low velocities through weight stabilization and energy dissipation but potentially intensifying local scour at high velocities through flow concentration. Using internal earth pressure and higher-order statistical moments, a preliminary criterion distinguishing surface scour from internal erosion was proposed. The weight-stabilizing effect of the gabion self-weight was quantitatively characterized. AI1-13 was identified as a candidate early-warning sensor, and a dual warning signal (rise-then-fall and skewness reversal) was observed. A tentative three-level early-warning framework is proposed. Owing to the non-replicated, reduced-scale nature of the tests, these quantitative indicators are presented as preliminary bounds rather than validated field thresholds. The findings clarify embankment protection failure mechanisms and highlight the influence of hydraulic intensity and protection configuration on scour resistance.
items.authors: Peifeng Han, Wenrui Gao, Song Gu, Haitao Xu, Shasha Yi, Songbo Ren

items.title: Knowledge Domains and Practice Orientation in Forestry-Related Research
items.abstract: Forestry research produces different kinds of knowledge, including ecological explanations, resource assessments, decision tools, and policy analyses, yet its practical content is usually judged by the recommendations it contains. Drawing on full-text articles, this study examines how these kinds of knowledge are connected to practice and how an article’s practical claims appear in its abstract. Five hundred Web of Science articles from 2020 to 2025 were sampled, 100 in each of five knowledge domains. Their concluding material and abstracts were coded separately for practice orientation as scholarly exposition, general applied relevance, or explicit prescription. The domains differed in form as well as the degree of practical relevance. Explicit prescription was most frequent in economics, policy and governance, and in ecology and conservation. Inventory and assessment concentrated on general applied relevance, stated through measurement and mapping output. When the concluding material prescribed, the abstract kept the prescription in 94 of 183 articles and restated it as general relevance in 75. In every domain, at least a third of these prescriptions were not kept in the abstract. Recommendation counts therefore favor domains that prescribe, and abstract-based screening misses much of what conclusions recommend. Through this paired coding, the study offers a domain-sensitive basis for judging practical relevance and measures how much practical guidance abstracts leave out.
items.authors: Jingjing Wu, Bingxian Chen

items.title: Establishment and Characterization of a Swim Bladder-Derived Cell Line from Chu’s Croaker (Nibea coibor) for Studying Collagen Regulation
items.abstract: Collagen is a major structural component of the extracellular matrix (ECM) and an important component contributing to the quality of fish maw. The collagen-rich swim bladder provides a suitable tissue source for investigating collagen regulation in fish. Therefore, systematic characterization of long-term cultured swim bladder-derived cells is needed to evaluate their utility as an in vitro model for investigating collagen regulation in fish. Here, we systematically characterized a previously established swim bladder-derived cell line from Chu’s croaker (Nibea coibor), designated NCSB, and examined its collagen-related responses to TGF-β1. NCSB cells exhibited fibroblast-like morphology and grew stably in DMEM/F12 medium with 15% FBS at 28 °C for over 40 passages. COI gene sequencing confirmed their species origin as N. coibor, while their fibroblast-like morphology and Vimentin expression were consistent with the mesenchymal-like phenotype. Transient transfection with pEGFP-N1 resulted in detectable GFP expression in NCSB cells. TGF-β1 treatment induced responses consistent with a myofibroblast-like phenotype, including increased α-SMA and collagen-related gene and protein expression, together with increased collagen-associated hydroxyproline in the culture supernatant and Sirius Red staining. Transcriptomic analysis further identified enrichment of the TGF-β signaling and ECM-receptor interaction pathways in TGF-β1-treated NCSB cells. Overall, the systematic characterization and functional evaluation of NCSB may support its utility as an in vitro model for studying collagen regulation in N. coibor.
items.authors: Yuhong Lin, Yuping Wang, Qi Pan, Yuying Yuan, Xiaobo Wen, Fan Lin

items.title: Optimized Endospore Production and Carrier Formulations of Endophytic Bacillus Species to Enhance Field Control of Wheat Blast
items.abstract: Harnessing endophytic bacteria for plant disease management offers a promising sustainable strategy. We previously demonstrated that endophytic Bacillus spp. significantly suppress wheat blast disease under field conditions. Despite their promising biocontrol potential, the successful commercialization of microbial biopesticides depends on economical mass production, high microbial viability, prolonged shelf-life, and consistent field performance. This study optimized fermentation conditions, endospore production and carrier formulations of three endophytic Bacillus strains (B. subtilis BTS-3 and B. velezensis BTS-4 and BTLK6A) for the sustainable management of wheat blast caused by Magnaporthe oryzae pathotype Triticum (MoT). Sugarcane molasses was evaluated as a low-cost alternative to commercial nutrient broth, while supplementation with 500 ppm MnCl2·4H2O enhanced growth and endospore production for Bacillus spp. Talc- and molasses-based liquid formulations were subsequently developed and evaluated for storage stability. A talc formulation containing 1% (w/w) carboxymethyl cellulose and 1.5% (w/w) calcium carbonate (CaCO3) provided the highest survival up to 180 days, maintaining a population density of 1 × 105–106 CFU g−1, whereas liquid formulations exhibited a faster decline in cell viability. Despite these differences, both formulation types significantly reduced blast disease severity by 48.78–75.98% compared to the only MoT- inoculated control in the field. Seed priming consistently outperformed foliar application and enhanced tiller production (9.40–16.62%), thousand-grain weight (13.47–32.41%), and grain yield (up to 321 g/m2), achieving up to 38.58% higher yield than the MoT-inoculated control. Taken together, these findings establish a cost-effective approach for developing stable talc- and molasses-based formulations, thereby enhancing the commercial viability and large-scale deployment of biological control strategies for sustainable wheat blast management.
items.authors: Sharmin Islam, Md Omar Kayees, Dipali Rani Gupta, Lamya Muazzeda Medha, Julfikar Ali, Md. Shahrear Parvaj Sujon

items.title: The Effectiveness of Geographic Information Systems in Social Studies Education: A Mixed-Meta Synthesis of Academic Achievement and Qualitative Learning Outcomes
items.abstract: This study aimed to synthesize quantitative and qualitative evidence regarding the use of Geographic Information Systems (GIS) in social studies education through a mixed-methods meta-analysis that combines meta-analysis and meta-thematic analysis. As part of the quantitative synthesis, seventeen experimental and quasi-experimental studies were thematically analyzed, while seventeen qualitative studies were thematically analyzed as part of the qualitative synthesis. The results of the meta-analysis, which employed a random-effects model, indicated that the use of GIS has a significant positive effect on participants in the intervention groups’ academic achievement (Hedges’ g = 1.021). Moderator analyses revealed that sample size (Q = 0.382, p = .826), grade level (Q = 3.082, p = .214), duration of implementation (Q = 1.309, p = .520), and publication type (Q = 2.977, p = .226) did not result in statistically significant differences in effect sizes. The meta-thematic analysis identified six themes: higher-order thinking and cognitive skills, the learning process and environment, map literacy and spatial skills, awareness, emotional and motivational contributions, and technological and practical challenges. Qualitative findings indicate that, in the studies examined, the use of GIS was associated with positive contributions to participants in the intervention groups’ cognitive processes, spatial thinking and reasoning, learning experiences, awareness, and motivation. However, these qualitative findings were not interpreted as evidence of objective improvement in participant’ cognitive or affective characteristics. Similarly, no direct link or causal mechanism at the study level was tested between qualitative themes and quantitative effect sizes related to academic achievement. Therefore, the findings suggest that quantitative evidence of the positive impact of GIS use on academic achievement and the learning experiences and perceived benefits reported in qualitative studies provide complementary, yet non-causally linked, evidence.
items.authors: Ahmet Akif Erbaş, Nagihan Evci, Ceylan Akcan, Emrullah Akcan, Erkan Yeşiltaş

items.title: Synovial SLC1A5-Associated Amino Acid Metabolic Features in Knee Osteoarthritis: An Integrated Analysis of Synovial Transcriptomics, Fecal Metabolomics, and Gut Microbiota
items.abstract: Background: This exploratory study aimed to characterize amino acid related features in osteoarthritis (OA). Methods: We analyzed independent public synovial transcriptomic datasets and paired fecal metabolomics and 16S ribosomal RNA profiles from 20 patients with knee OA and 14 controls. Metabolite-sensing genes were intersected with nominally differential genes and prioritized using elastic net, support vector machine recursive feature elimination, and extreme gradient boosting. Results:SLC1A5 (solute carrier family 1 member 5) expression was lower in the discovery cohort GSE89408 (log2 fold change = −0.532, p = 0.0159), but did not meet the false discovery rate (FDR) threshold of 0.05 (FDR = 0.0697). GSE55235 showed a concordant decrease (log2 fold change = −0.695, p = 0.00536; area under the receiver operating characteristic curve = 0.830). Single-cell computational predictions from three OA donors suggested endothelial, smooth muscle, and mast-cell contexts. Tissue-level SLC1A5 expression correlated with inferred M2 macrophage proportions after group adjustment (r = −0.575, FDR = 0.002). Six features with Level 3 putative glutamine-, asparagine-, or glutamate-containing tripeptide annotations differed between groups (q = 0.00245 to 0.00948), whereas the corresponding free amino acids did not reach FDR significance. Bacteroides showed a lower centered log-ratio value in OA (q = 0.00273); none of its six tripeptide correlations remained significant after group adjustment. Conclusions: These observations generate a hypothesis about intestinal amino acid-related features and synovial SLC1A5 expression; they do not establish a direct gut-joint relationship, peptide identity, or a metabolic mechanism.
items.authors: Xingzong Zhu, Hongrui Du, Bin Li, Hangyuan He, Yang Tan

items.title: Multi-Dimensional Characterization of Tetraspanins Reveals TSPAN6 as a Candidate Prognostic Hub in Kidney Renal Clear Cell Carcinoma
items.abstract: Kidney renal clear cell carcinoma (KIRC) is a major subtype of renal cell carcinoma with substantial molecular heterogeneity and variable clinical outcomes. Tetraspanins (TSPANs) are membrane proteins involved in cell adhesion, signaling, migration, tumor progression, and interactions with the tumor microenvironment (TME); however, their collective significance in KIRC remains insufficiently characterized. The expression profile of the TSPAN gene family was evaluated in the TCGA-KIRC cohort using GEPIA2. Differentially expressed TSPANs were further investigated through protein–protein interaction network (PPIN) and univariate survival analyses. Prognostically significant TSPANs were assessed for genomic alterations, promoter methylation, and associations with tumor-infiltrating immune cells. Feed-forward-loop (FFL) was constructed and visualized using Cytoscape. Thereafter, the findings were evaluated in an independent KIRC dataset. Several TSPANs displayed significant differential expression between KIRC and normal renal tissues. TSPAN1 and TSPAN6 were significantly associated with overall survival (OS), with higher expression corresponding to more favorable outcomes. Notably, higher TSPAN6 expression was associated with improved OS but a higher estimated risk of relapse indicating an endpoint-dependent and potentially complex prognostic relationship. Promoter methylation of TSPAN1 and TSPAN6 showed associations with selected clinicopathological characteristics, while both genes demonstrated significant relationships with specific immune-cell populations. Network analysis identified a ZNF260–miR-6794-5p–TSPAN6 FFL subnetwork motif, prioritizing TSPAN6 as the hub TSPAN. TSPAN6 was additionally detected among differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in an independent GEO cohort. This study identifies TSPAN6 as a promising candidate biomarker in KIRC and provides a multi-dimensional framework linking TSPAN dysregulation with prognosis, epigenetic regulation, immune infiltration, and regulatory networks. Experimental and clinical validation is warranted.
items.authors: Hajed Obaid A. Alharbi, Tarique Sarwar, Arshad Husain Rahmani

items.title: A SAM2 and VLM-Based Automatic Radiological Reporting System for Pneumothorax Detection
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: Pneumothorax, caused by air accumulation in the pleural space, can lead to lung collapse and, if diagnosis is delayed, respiratory or cardiovascular deterioration. Most deep-learning studies on pneumothorax address classification or segmentation alone. This study proposes a holistic automatic radiological reporting system combining U-Net-based segmentation, Segment Anything Model 2 (SAM2)-based boundary refinement, and a Vision-Language Model (VLM)-based reporting module for pneumothorax detection on computed tomography (CT) images. Methods: A MobileNetV2-encoder U-Net was trained on 224×224 CT patches from 171 patients (15,555 patches). A frozen, zero-shot SAM2 module, guided by a box prompt derived from the U-Net mask, was combined with U-Net via an Intersection over Union (IoU)-agreement rule. The refined mask and rule-based geometric features were passed to a frozen VLM (Qwen2-VL-2B-Instruct) to generate structured reports with a combined confidence coefficient. Performance was evaluated with Accuracy, Dice, IoU, and Loss, over all patches and over pneumothorax-positive patches only. Results: U-Net achieved 93.09/92.09/99.71% (Dice/IoU/Accuracy) on validation and 93.68/92.79/99.79% on the test set; these largely reflect correct empty-mask prediction on negative patches. On positive patches only, Dice was 0.6295 (validation) and 0.6215 (test), with patch-level sensitivity of 82.2% (validation) and 79.9% (test) and specificity above 97%. SAM2 refinement achieved 92.44% Dice and 91.29% IoU on a random test subsample (n ≈ 300), close to but not exceeding U-Net alone; an ablation analysis confirmed no consistent Dice/IoU or 95th-percentile Hausdorff distance (HD95) gain from SAM2. BLEU/ROUGE and Likert evaluation frameworks for the VLM reports were defined but not yet scored against reference reports. Conclusions: U-Net-based segmentation reliably identifies pneumothorax-containing patches with moderate boundary accuracy, while frozen SAM2 refinement adds limited value. The rule-based reporting layer is reproducible and shows triage-support potential, whereas the VLM free-text layer carries a documented hallucination risk and requires radiologist verification before clinical use.
items.authors: Savaş Tunçer, Mustafa Yıldırım, Özal Yıldırım

items.title: Biodegradable Plastics in Anaerobic Digestion Systems: Compatibility and Engineering Strategies for Circular Agriculture
items.abstract: Anaerobic digestion (AD) offers a potential route for integrating biodegradable plastics (BDPs) into circular agricultural waste management, but suitability depends on conversion of the complete material under practical digestion conditions. This review evaluates BDP compatibility with AD and engineering strategies to improve treatment. BDP conversion in AD generally requires depolymerization and hydrolysis to soluble products, initiated by surface microbial or enzymatic attack for some polymers, followed by microbial conversion to methane. The rate and extent of conversion depend on polymer chemistry and structure, crystallinity, chain mobility, hydrophilicity, material form and formulation, digestion temperature, and anaerobic microbial activity. Poly(hydroxybutyrate) (PHB) and poly(hydroxybutyrate-co-hydroxyvalerate) (PHBV) show high compatibility, while thermoplastic starch (TPS) and accessible cellulose-based materials undergo substantial conversion. Poly(lactic acid) (PLA) is strongly hydrolysis-limited under mesophilic conditions, whereas poly(caprolactone) (PCL) shows pronounced temperature-dependent conversion, with thermophilic conditions generally improving degradation. Poly(butylene succinate-co-adipate) (PBSA) converts more readily than poly(butylene succinate) (PBS) but remains incomplete without pretreatment. PBS and poly(butylene adipate-co-terephthalate) (PBAT) are poorly compatible. Polymer blends are often limited by their least-degradable major fractions. Fragmentation or mass loss does not indicate complete conversion, and polymer persistence does not necessarily indicate process instability. Reactor configuration and treatment should therefore target polymer-specific limitations through controlled co-digestion and loading, optimized particle size, targeted pretreatment, microbial acclimation or enrichment, appropriate temperature and staging, and AD-oriented material formulation.
items.authors: Oluwatunmise Israel Dada, Babashola Dapo Odugbose, Teshan Udayanga Habarakada Liyanage, Kenita Dahal, Ting Chi, Liang Yu

items.title: Experimental Investigation of the Enrichment Characteristics and Governing Patterns of Microscopic Residual Oil During Chemical Flooding
items.abstract: Understanding the enrichment mechanisms of residual oil in the high water-cut stage is essential to achieve highly efficient regulation of chemical flooding. By establishing a one-dimensional (1D) real-digital-core model, this study systematically investigates the regulatory mechanisms of various chemical systems on residual oil mobilization, migration, and enrichment post-waterflooding. The results show that the length of microscopic residual oil is inversely linear with the displacement capillary number. The key requirement for the spatial enrichment of residual oil is the synergistic matching between high initial residual oil content and strong displacement driving force. Single polymer flooding exhibits a syringe-like pattern, in which the pressure jump induced by the high viscosity at the displacement front overcomes capillary resistance and forms a banded enrichment zone. In contrast, single surfactant flooding can greatly reduce the interfacial tension and thus promote microscopic stripping and emulsification. However, its limited mobility control makes large-scale enrichment difficult. The surfactant–polymer (SP) binary compound flooding can reconstruct microscopically dispersed oil droplets into macroscopic oil clusters and form a highly continuous enrichment zone at the displacement front. BPPG-assisted heterogeneous flooding further establishes a synergistic mechanism of viscoelastic action and profile control, thereby achieving full-field reconfiguration of the pore-scale flow field. On this basis, a dimensionless residual-oil scale was introduced to construct a limit chart for the mobilization and enrichment of microscopic residual oil under different chemical flooding modes. This study provides a theoretical basis for the design of enhanced oil recovery schemes in complex reservoirs.
items.authors: Min Zhang, Zhigang Sun, Shirui Guo, Ting Chen, Hongxin Zhang, Fulai Han

items.title: The Evolution of Middle-Level Preservice Teacher Identity
items.abstract: Teachers of middle school students (young adolescents) view students positively, build relationships, design curriculum, and create learning environments for them. As a college student transitions to a student teacher (or preservice teacher) in the classroom, the student teacher’s identity is being formed and developed while working with adolescents who are forming and exploring their own identities. Developing a middle level student teacher identity is a complex negotiation between the student teacher’s history and identity as a learner. In addition, they must adhere to university and school district policies and procedures while in middle schools. The transition to student teaching is the catalyst for professional identity development, prompting students to reflect on who they were and who they want to become as middle school teachers and professionals. The term preservice teacher is broadly defined as a university student enrolled in a teacher preparation program, actively seeking certification, and engaged in learning the craft of teaching through field-based learning. Preservice teachers or student teachers are developing the professional knowledge, skills, and abilities needed before officially entering the profession. Preservice teacher development typically progresses through three stages: early candidacy, mid-candidacy, and late candidacy, moving from acquiring foundational theories to advancing pedagogical skills, engaging in authentic classroom practice, and designing standards-based lesson plans. In this manuscript, preservice teacher and student teacher are used interchangeably and refer specifically to the late candidacy stage. This Encyclopedia entry will highlight the complex development of middle level preservice teachers’ identity as they learn to bridge their personal and (pre) professional selves, using the terms student teacher, preservice teacher, or middle level preservice teacher (MLPST), which will be used interchangeably.
items.authors: Toni M. Williams

items.title: Vision-Based Facial Analysis for Screening and Symptom Estimation of Mental Health Conditions: A Critical Narrative Review
items.abstract: Facial video provides behavioural measurements and camera-derived physiological signals that may complement mental health assessment. Their clinical interpretation, however, depends on the acquisition conditions, reference labels, population, and evaluation protocol. This critical narrative review examines facial analysis for mental health screening and symptom estimation, distinguishing depression, anxiety symptoms, experimentally elicited stress, and other condition-specific assessment tasks. We distinguish questionnaire-defined screening labels, symptom severity, experimentally elicited affect or stress, and clinician-established diagnoses. We review image acquisition and preprocessing, facial action units and movement, remote photoplethysmography (rPPG), temporal architectures, and multimodal fusion. Dataset resources are separated by evidential purpose, and representative quantitative results are accompanied by their targets, modalities, and validation conditions rather than presented as a cross-study ranking. The synthesis identifies three recurring limitations: few independent participants despite many video frames, limited validation across populations and recording domains, and a gap between benchmark prediction and clinical utility. Accurate average pulse rate estimation does not establish reliable beat-to-beat variability or disorder-specific validity. We therefore emphasise participant-level evaluation, probability calibration, prevalence-dependent predictive values, acquisition quality, consent, and prospective clinical assessment. Foundation models and longitudinal monitoring remain research directions whose incremental value must be established against appropriate baselines. Current evidence supports investigation of complementary screening and decision support tools, rather than autonomous diagnosis or a demonstrated ability to predict disease onset.
items.authors: Yaohua Guan, Guangqiang Yin

items.title: AI-Generated Text Detection via Structural and Semantic Entropy Optimization with Adversarial Learning
items.abstract: AI-generated text detectors often achieve high in-domain accuracy but remain sensitive to changes in domain, generator, and writing style. This limitation partly arises because conventional detectors rely predominantly on latent language-model representations and fixed decision boundaries, without explicitly characterizing sample-level structural and semantic variation. We introduce S2E-AL, an end-to-end score-aware structure–semantic entropy adversarial learning framework for AI-generated text detection. S2E-AL encodes local dependency, global contextual, and semantic entropy features into a structure–semantic representation. A gradient-reversal source classifier discourages this representation from retaining source-specific information, while a score-aware threshold estimator conditions on both the entropy representation and a detached base-detector logit to produce a sample-specific logit adjustment. The adjusted logit is used to estimate the final probability that a text is AI-generated. Across HC3, HC3_Plus, LLMTrace, RAID, and XSum, the score-aware model achieved a macro Accuracy of 90.90% and a macro F1-score of 91.42%. Its performance remained lower on XSum, indicating that substantial domain and stylistic shifts remain challenging. These results suggest that jointly modeling structure–semantic variation and detector confidence can improve the overall performance–stability trade-off of AI-generated text detection across heterogeneous test distributions.
items.authors: Yue Teng, Shaomeng Zhang, Gang Ma, Xiaonan Sun, Jikang Zhang, Yi Liu

items.title: Energy Consumer Model Estimation Using Machine Learning
items.abstract: A novel utility model of the daily electricity consumption patterns of any residential unit is proposed. The model is semi-parametric—its internal parameters are tractable to straightforward interpretations from the standpoints of microeconomics as well as game theory. The model considers fixed and shiftable loads. A modified Cobb–Douglas preference function is applied to incorporate utility tradeoffs in operating shiftable loads at different hours of the day based on the consumer’s intrinsic preference and time-of-use pricing. Model parameter estimation is formulated as a quadratic optimization problem with inequality constraints. The existence of a global optimum that is unique except under a very specific circumstance is theoretically established. A dual-gradient-ascent learning algorithm was developed to train the parameters that best fit real time-series load data. For units with single-point monitoring, an optional unsupervised learning algorithm for partial load disaggregation was developed. As a case study, the proposed model was trained with load profiles of two real-world residential units. The trained model is able to faithfully reproduce typical electricity consumption characteristics. Model interpretability was demonstrated by numerically evaluating the utility and cost functions with varying loads. These results illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed methodology.
items.authors: Sanjoy Das, A. Khaled Zarabie

items.title: Associations Between an Individualized Heart Rate-Based Training Index and Mood States in Elite Female Kendo Athletes: An Exploratory Field Study
items.abstract: Athlete monitoring commonly includes subjective questionnaires such as the Profile of Mood States, which may be influenced by individual perceptions and situational factors. This one-week exploratory field study examined associations between Persist, an individualized wearable-derived behavioral–physiological measure, and mood states in seven elite female kendo athletes. Before the monitoring period, the heart rate corresponding to the point at which each athlete perceived exercise intensity as “somewhat hard” was individually determined using the rating of perceived exertion. Heart rate and training duration were recorded during kendo training sessions over one week using a wrist-worn wearable device. Mood states were assessed using the Profile of Mood States 2nd Edition (POMS 2). Persist showed a negative association with Fatigue–Inertia in the unadjusted analysis (rs = −0.847, p = 0.016), but this association did not remain statistically significant after Holm correction for multiple comparisons (adjusted p = 0.162). These preliminary findings indicate a possible association between Persist and fatigue-related mood states; however, larger repeated-measures studies are required to evaluate its validity and potential utility for athlete monitoring.
items.authors: Akari Kitahara, Shinsuke Tamai, Shoko Nomura, Rina Kagawa, Hideo Suzuki, Hideo Tsurushima

items.title: Learning-Enhanced Belief Rule Base for Sensor-Based Bearing Health Condition Assessment
items.abstract: The Belief Rule Base (BRB) provides explainable reasoning and uncertainty modeling capabilities, offering significant advantages in complex system modeling. However, the scope of its knowledge base is constrained by expert prior knowledge, rendering it incapable of encompassing fault categories that appear in the training data but lack expert-defined rules, thereby preventing post-construction expansion in line with data evolution. To this end, this paper proposes a learning-enhanced BRB model (LE-BRB), achieving a verifiable extension of the rule conclusion space within the BRB framework. First, association rules are introduced to mine classes with missing expert rules and generate candidate rules; secondly, a quality verification module is constructed through Pareto-based filtering, and rule fusion is implemented based on antecedent similarity and conclusion conflict degree; Finally, evidential reasoning is employed to achieve traceable diagnosis. Experiments on the CWRU local bearing fault dataset show that, while preserving the original interpretability of the BRB, LE-BRB completes the missing rolling element fault (Ball) rules in the knowledge base, achieving an average accuracy of 91.02%. Experiments on the MAFAULDA bearing dataset show that, while preserving the original interpretability of the BRB, LE-BRB completes the missing rotor unbalance fault in the knowledge base. This fills the coverage gap of the original BRB for this fault category, improving the diagnostic accuracy from 43.69% to 94.17%. Compared with models such as neural networks and decision trees, it achieves comparable or superior accuracy while exhibiting relatively higher stability.
items.authors: Xinrong Li, Yan Li, Shiming Li, Yuhe Wang

items.title: An Explainable Cyber Range-to-MATLAB Co-Simulation Framework for Attack-Chain and Power-Service Impact Analysis in Electric Power Networks
items.abstract: Complex cyberattacks on electric power networks traverse communication links, control objects and power-service processes, making it difficult to explain how network evidence propagates to operational impact. This paper proposes an explainable cyber range-to-MATLAB co-simulation framework that couples traffic-oriented security emulation with power service simulation. The cyber range generates security events, traffic records, alarms and asset topology evidence, while MATLAB models calculate distribution network states, line power flows, switching states, energy-storage PCS states and service-impact indicators. A unified clock, event-mapping function, asset topology and evidence graph connect cyber events with business disturbances and observable power outputs. Mathematical descriptions are developed for event sets, service-state vectors, coupling functions, attack intensity, service-impact score, synchronization error, evidence completeness and metric improvement. Validation focuses on distribution network and energy storage scenarios. At the mapped switching disturbance at t = 180 s, 23 of 33 nodes are de-energized, and 2.235 MW (60.16% of feeder load) is unsupplied. Five repeated trials with plus or minus 3% load perturbations give a mean load loss of 2.243 plus or minus 0.008 MW. Integrated defensive retesting reduces attack intensity from 0.60 to 0.08, alarm latency from 12.4 s to 2.8 s, and recovery time from 240 s to 60 s. The framework, therefore, links cyber-range evidence to direct, auditable power-service quantities for attack-chain interpretation and defensive assessment.
items.authors: Yuantao Wang, Hao Zhang, Xin Liu, Lianghua Gong, Guohua Gao

items.title: Wound Ballistics of Craniocerebral Firearm Injuries
items.abstract: Craniocerebral firearm injuries are associated with high mortality rates as a result of the kinetic energy deposition during the projectile–tissue interaction and its consequences, causing immediate and delayed brain damage. Ballistic factors that contribute to brain injury from bullets are related to the behavior of the projectile (whether it yaws, tumbles, mushrooms or disintegrates following skull penetration) and the creation of bone fragments from the entry site. Pressure waves generated intracranially associated with the temporary cavitation are the hallmark of bullet penetration of the head. Because of the absence of any compensatory mechanism to absorb the transient pressure loading, the largely incompressible brain tissue is subjected directly to its effects. The sudden increase in intracranial pressure and the resultant deformation of the brain during cavitation contributes to the development of brain edema and may affect the cardiac and respiratory centers of the brainstem, even if not transected by the bullet trajectory. Shotgun injuries to the head at close range cause extensive destruction of the brain, usually with catastrophic results, because the pellets enter the cranial cavity bunched together, thus acting as a single projectile of large diameter and kinetic energy. Injuries from fragments present with multiple, more or less circular wounds of various depths, depending on the kinetic energy of the fragments. This review includes a conceptual temporal organization of factors that have a prognostic significance, including those related to projectile and energy transfer characteristics and their consequences.
items.authors: Panagiotis K. Stefanopoulos, Konstantina Sotiropoulou, Alexandra S. Nikita, Apostolos I. Samelis, Georgios F. Hadjigeorgiou, Christos Bissias

items.title: An Experimental Study on the Analysis of Factors Influencing Explosive Spalling of Concrete Under Fire
items.abstract: Explosive spalling is the most serious fire-induced deterioration mechanism of high-strength concrete (HSC), yet the influence of the two principal variables—compressive strength and internal moisture content—has not been quantified experimentally over a wide strength range. In this study, 144 cylindrical specimens (ø100 × 200 mm) were produced from four concrete strength grades (21, 50, 80 and 100 MPa) and three curing conditions (air, sealed and high-temperature water curing) together with an oven-drying treatment so as to obtain a controlled variation of moisture content, and were heated for 15 and 30 min following the KS F 2257-1 (ISO 834-1) standard fire curve. The spalling appearance, cracking characteristics, residual compressive strength and pore structure were measured. Normal-strength concrete (NSC) of 21 MPa did not spall under any combination of heating time, curing method and moisture content, whereas every 100 MPa-grade specimen spalled severely, and they were in some cases completely destroyed. For 50–80 MPa HSC, the occurrence of spalling showed no consistent correlation with strength or with moisture content, which indicates that initial imperfections of the material dominate the onset of spalling. The spalling of HSC occurred mainly within the first 15 min of heating and its severity increased with compressive strength and heating time, while the influence of moisture content was threshold-like rather than monotonic. Threshold moisture contents for spalling-free behaviour were estimated as about 3% for 50–80 MPa and about 1% for 100 MPa and above, although these provisional thresholds require confirmation by tests at intermediate moisture contents. The residual compressive strength ratio after 15 min of heating averaged about 88% for the 21 MPa NSC and about 87% and 80% for the 50 and 80 MPa HSC, respectively, but after 30 min it decreased to about 64% for 21 MPa, 53% for 50 MPa, 43% for 80 MPa and 39% for 100 MPa.
items.authors: Dong-Joon Kim

items.title: Composition, Physicomechanical, and Clinical Behaviour of Nanohybrid Resin Composites: A Narrative Review
items.abstract: Nanohybrid resin composites are the dominant class of direct restorative materials, yet evidence on individual products is dispersed and difficult to compare. This narrative review appraises the composition, physicomechanical, chemical, optical, and clinical behaviour of Filtek™ Z550 (introduced in 2012), an extensively tested nanohybrid, and places its profile in the context of its class. Methods: A structured search of PubMed and the Cochrane Library with manual reference screening was performed; no formal risk-of-bias or certainty-of-evidence assessment was undertaken. Original in vitro and clinical studies were screened against predefined PICO-oriented criteria and synthesised qualitatively. Results: Twenty-seven studies were included, twenty-six in vitro and one clinical. The material was consistently described as a multicomponent dimethacrylate matrix reinforced with a bimodal zirconia and silica filler system at approximately 82 percent by weight, a configuration linked to high early flexural strength, elevated surface hardness, and favourable polishability.
