Artificial ageing reduced microhardness by roughly 16 to 24 percent and increased wear, three-point flexural strength fell below the ISO 4049 minimum after thirty days of ageing in artificial saliva, and low-pH and oxidative challenges degraded gloss and colour. Clinical data were limited to a single eighteen-month trial reporting high retention with more frequent transient postoperative sensitivity. Conclusions: The laboratory evidence indicates favourable early physicomechanical and esthetic behaviour that is sensitive to hydrolytic ageing and to polymerisation quality; clinical evidence rests on one short-term trial, so statements about clinical suitability are preliminary.
items.authors: Alexia-Ecaterina Cârstea, Ioana-Irina Anton, Lucian-Toma Ciocan, Vlad-Gabriel Vasilescu, Marina Imre, Andreea-Cristiana Didilescu

items.title: Groundwater–Stream Connectivity Under Climate Change: Implications for the Ecology, Conservation and Sustainability of Urban Streams
items.abstract: Freshwater systems, including urban streams and groundwater, are increasingly affected by climate change through altered precipitation, rising temperatures, droughts, floods, and changing water demand. This narrative review synthesizes evidence on how these pressures modify groundwater–stream connectivity and the resulting ecological, conservation, and sustainability implications in urban environments. The literature shows that groundwater supports baseflow, thermal buffering, hyporheic exchange, and habitat persistence, but that urbanization can simultaneously reduce natural recharge and create new anthropogenic recharge pathways. Studies of urban streams document flashier hydrographs and ecological degradation under conventional urbanization, whereas infiltration-focused low-impact development has been shown in some catchments to increase baseflow and reduce seasonal variability. Climate change adds further pressure: global modelling projects substantial warming of shallow groundwater by 2100, while long-term stream studies show taxon-specific community responses to warming and extreme events. Major knowledge gaps include limited long-term paired groundwater–stream observations, scale mismatches among hydrology, ecology, and governance, and underrepresentation of arid, semi-arid, tropical, and Global South cities. Addressing these gaps requires coupled hydrological–ecological research, functional indicators, and context-specific nature-based and hybrid management strategies that maintain or restore groundwater–stream connectivity as a component of urban freshwater resilience.
items.authors: Augustine Ovie Edegbene, Sara El Yaagoubi, Martin Schletterer, Yakubu Manbe Mohammed, Otorme Sarah Okolodo, Tega Treasure Edegbene Ovie

items.title: Separation Laws for Flip Bifurcations and Endogenous Switching Boundaries in Gradient Maps
items.abstract: Gradient clipping is widely used to control large updates in optimization, while finite-step gradient descent develops period-two oscillations near the edge of linear stability. Recent work has analysed these oscillations via smooth flip bifurcation theory and higher-order stability criteria, whereas piecewise-smooth bifurcation theory describes generic interactions between period-doubling and switching boundaries. It remains unclear how a smooth gradient-descent oscillation first interacts with the switching surface generated endogenously by radial gradient clipping, and what dynamical structure emerges after this contact. For the finite-dimensional clipped gradient map \(F_{\eta,c}(x) = x - \eta \, C_c(\nabla V(x))\), we analyse this transition near a nondegenerate strict local minimum with a simple maximal Hessian eigenvalue. Clipping is locally inactive near the minimum, so the fixed-point stability threshold and the local flip bifurcation coincide with those of ordinary gradient descent. Under a supercritical flip condition, the stable period-two branch reaches the clipping boundary at \(\eta_{\mathrm{sc}}(c) = \eta_f + K c^2 + O(c^4)\) with \(\eta_f = 2/\lambda_*\), where \(K = \Gamma/(3\lambda_*^4 \|v_*\|^2)\) is determined explicitly by derivatives of the potential up to fourth order and by the clipping norm. Beyond the separation law, the gradient structure yields rigidity absent from generic switching maps: the two points of every smooth period-two orbit have opposite gradients and hence reach a radial clipping boundary simultaneously; mixed smooth--clipped period-two itineraries with one strictly smooth and one strictly clipped point are impossible; and every strictly fully clipped period-two orbit has an exact unit Floquet multiplier and is therefore nonhyperbolic. A solvable planar model realizes the full transition from a stable smooth two-cycle to a neutral family of fully clipped period-two cycles.
items.authors: Zisong Yuan, Xiao Wen

items.title: Virological Events During Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor Therapy: A Multi-Source Evaluation
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: Virological findings during immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy may represent viral loss of control, pre-existing infection, tumour biomarkers, or infection after immune-related adverse event (irAE)-directed immunosuppression. Distinguishing these possibilities is important for treatment and diagnostic decisions. We evaluated virus-specific patterns across complementary data sources. Methods: We evaluated HBV, HCV, HIV, EBV, CMV, HSV, and VZV using FAERS disproportionality analysis (2011Q1–2026Q1), PubMed evidence mapping and appraisal, EBV endpoint verification, and review of ClinicalTrials.gov protocols by start era. Findings were interpreted in relation to prevention, monitoring, endpoint interpretation, and infectious mimic evaluation. Results: Among 200,699 primary suspect ICI reports, only HBV reactivation met the prespecified reporting criterion (226 reports; reporting odds ratio 1.20, 95% CI 1.06–1.37); this estimate did not persist with an oncology-restricted comparator (0.81, 0.71–0.94). Same report overlap of HBV with hepatic events and CMV with enterocolitis or pneumonitis identified diagnostically ambiguous settings without establishing event sequence. EBV DNA reflected viral inflammatory activity in some conditions but tumour burden in EBV-associated cancers. The evidence map included 198 publications, with design-specific appraisal of 84. Among 164 trials, conditional viral eligibility appeared in 49.0–57.1% across start eras, whereas longitudinal monitoring appeared in 8.2–19.6%. Conclusions: Reporting patterns were virus-specific and comparator-sensitive. The findings support HBV prevention, confirmation of HCV and HIV control, disease-specific interpretation of EBV markers, and CMV evaluation when inflammation or irAE-directed immunosuppression raises concern for infection. Context-specific assessment may help avoid unnecessary ICI interruption while identifying viral loss of control and infectious mimics.
items.authors: Yue Cao, Zenghui Zhang, Yanying Liang, Chenxi Zhao, Xvrong Li, Qingluan Yang

items.title: Quinones as Optical Signal Transducers: Emerging Roles in Spectroscopic Sensing, Carbon Dots, and Enzyme-Free Immunoassays
items.abstract: Quinones have emerged as versatile optical signal transducers in spectroscopic analytical chemistry because of their unique redox activity, electron-transfer capability, reactive oxygen species generation, and tunable photophysical properties. Beyond their traditional roles as biologically active molecules and electrochemical mediators, quinones now function as derivatization reagents, fluorescence-modulating probes, recyclable chemiluminescent and colorimetric signal amplifiers, functional nanomaterial components, and stable labels for enzyme-free immunoassays. This review presents a unified analytical framework that organizes these diverse applications according to their mechanistic roles in molecular recognition, optical signal generation, redox amplification, and nanomaterial-assisted sensing. The molecular principles governing quinone redox cycling, photoinduced electron transfer, fluorescence quenching and recovery, reactive oxygen species-mediated amplification, and nanoparticle coupling are critically discussed to explain analytical performance and guide rational platform design. Recent advances in quinone-derived and quinone-functionalized carbon dots, chemiluminescent and colorimetric amplification systems, fluorogenic derivatization, and quinone-based enzyme-free immunoassays are comprehensively evaluated with emphasis on sensitivity, selectivity, stability, portability, and practical applicability. Current limitations, including matrix interference, mechanistic validation, aqueous compatibility, and reproducibility, are critically assessed, and future opportunities for biomedical diagnostics, food analysis, environmental monitoring, and point-of-care testing are highlighted. Collectively, this review establishes quinones as multifunctional analytical building blocks for next-generation optical sensing platform development.
items.authors: Mahmoud El-Maghrabey, Rania El-Shaheny, Ali Abdel-Hakim, Helal F. Hetta, Naoya Kishikawa

items.title: Evaluating Analytical Performance of Commercial Screen-Printed Electrodes for Point-of-Care Uric Acid Sensing: A Comparative Study
items.abstract: Uric acid (UA), a key purine metabolite associated with metabolic, cardiovascular, and renal disorders, has been extensively investigated using electrochemical sensors. Increasing efforts now focus on translating these technologies into commercial point-of-care (POC) platforms for rapid, decentralized detection. Commercial screen-printed electrodes (SPEs) are widely employed as substrates for such platforms, typically after surface modification with nanomaterials or recognition elements; however, their inherent, unmodified analytical capabilities remain largely uncharacterized. This gap is significant, as the baseline performance of the underlying electrode ultimately constrains or enables the benefits of any subsequent modification. Here, we systematically compare two commercially available SPEs, DRP-110 and DRP-150, for UA detection using differential pulse voltammetry under standardized conditions. Both electrodes exhibited two distinct UA oxidation peaks. The first peak gave linear calibration over 0.02–0.5 µM (R2 = 0.9863 DRP-110, 0.9928 DRP-150), with validated LOD/LOQ of 0.076/0.230 µM (DRP-110) and 0.055/0.166 µM (DRP-150); the second peak extended the linear working range to 1–1000 µM (DRP-110, R2 = 0.9833) and 1–2000 µM (DRP-150, R2 = 0.9928), with LOD/LOQ of 3.37/10.20 µM and 2.23/6.77 µM, respectively, derived from its low-concentration segment. DRP-150 demonstrated superior sensitivity at both peaks. However, both electrodes showed low selectivity toward ascorbic acid. Spike recovery testing in modified artificial urine gave recoveries of 68.0–98.49%, supporting preliminary feasibility in a defined urine-like matrix.
items.authors: Ligia Chelmea, Mihaela Badea, Sehrish Bilal, Davide Calin Mereu, Andrea Elena Neculau, Radu Dan Necula

items.title: Hospitality as Living Heritage: Migrant Heritage-Making, Belonging, and the Cultural Politics of Welcome
items.abstract: This article conceptualizes hospitality as a form of living heritage through which migrants and refugees preserve cultural practices, negotiate belonging, and reshape relations of welcome in receiving societies. Drawing on Walker and Avant’s concept analysis approach, literature from heritage studies, migration studies, hospitality, tourism, sociology, and intercultural inclusion was reviewed and thematically synthesized. The analysis identified four core dimensions of hospitality as living heritage: cultural rootedness and heritage transmission, relational care and reciprocity, adaptation and negotiation across contexts, and intercultural connection and belonging. These dimensions are shaped by migration and displacement, collective memory, experiences of exclusion, and opportunities for intercultural encounter. The findings position migrants not only as guests or recipients of support, but as active hosts, heritage makers, and contributors to social cohesion. By linking hospitality, living heritage, and the cultural politics of welcome, this article offers a conceptual framework for understanding how everyday practices of care, sharing, and reciprocity sustain cultural continuity and foster belonging in migration contexts.
items.authors: Areej Al-Hamad, Yasin M. Yasin, Lujain Yasin, Talha Khan, Harshet Tohan

items.title: Effects of Unilateral Leg Training Using Elastic and Inelastic Barbells on Dynamic Balance and Muscle Activation: A Randomized Controlled Trial
items.abstract: Background: Elastic barbells generate continuous, unpredictable perturbations through elastic deformation of the bar, delivering a top-down instability stimulus that transfers from the upper to the lower limbs. Whether repeated exposure produces training-related changes in muscle activation, and whether any postural control gains transfer to an untrained movement condition, remains unknown. Methods: Twenty-eight resistance-trained men (mean age 22.8 ± 1.6 years; experimental group (EG) 23.4 ± 1.4, control group (CG) 22.3 ± 1.7) were randomly assigned to train with an elastic barbell (EG, n = 14) or an inelastic barbell (CG, n = 14). Both completed an identical progressive unilateral leg training program twice weekly for 12 weeks (20–40% of one-repetition maximum). Pre- and post-intervention measures were the Y-Balance Test (YBT), centre of pressure (COP) displacement during single-leg deadlift (SLDL), and surface electromyography (%RVC) of seven trunk and lower-limb muscles across three lifting speeds. Data were analyzed with mixed-design ANOVA (α = 0.05). Results: The EG showed greater gains in dynamic balance; the post-intervention YBT composite score was significantly higher in the EG (102.55 ± 6.22%) than in the CG (90.65 ± 12.95%; Group × Time F(1, 26) = 7.25, p = 0.012). A significant Group × Time interaction for COP under the untrained inelastic barbell task (anterior–posterior F(1, 26) = 8.86, p = 0.006; medial–lateral F(1, 26) = 5.61, p = 0.026) indicated task-specific transfer of postural control. The semitendinosus was the only muscle with a significant Group × Time interaction in both barbell tasks, with activation decreasing in the EG and increasing in the CG. Conclusions: Elastic barbell training improved dynamic balance and altered lower-limb muscle activation more than inelastic barbell training, and the postural control benefit transferred to the same task performed with an untrained barbell. Because injury outcomes and motor-unit behaviour were not assessed, injury outcomes were not assessed; any application to injury prevention remains a hypothesis for future investigation.
items.authors: Jihwan Jeong, Jayeon Lee, Chaekwan Lee, Shuho Kang, Ilbong Park

items.title: Associations Between Playful Study Design and Multidimensional Well-Being: The Indirect Role of Student Engagement Among Italian University Students
items.abstract: University students face sustained academic demands that can compromise engagement and positive mental health, underscoring the need to identify modifiable everyday strategies that support health promotion in higher education. Drawing on Study Demands–Resources theory and proactive motivational perspectives, this cross-sectional study examined the direct and indirect associations among playful study design (PSD)—students’ self-initiated efforts to make study activities more enjoyable (designing fun) and more challenging (designing competition)—student engagement, and emotional, social, and psychological well-being. A sample of 511 Italian university students completed validated measures of PSD, student engagement, and positive mental health. The hypothesized indirect-association model was tested using structural equation modeling (SEM) with bootstrapped confidence intervals. PSD was positively associated with student engagement and with all three dimensions of well-being. Significant indirect associations between PSD and emotional, social, and psychological well-being through student engagement were observed. After accounting for student engagement, none of the direct associations between PSD and the three well-being dimensions were statistically significant in the primary ML analysis. The model showed a mixed pattern of fit: RMSEA and SRMR indicated acceptable fit, whereas CFI and TLI remained below conventional thresholds. These findings extend emerging PSD research by identifying student engagement as having an indirect role in the associations between the playful redesign of study activities and multidimensional positive mental health. Given the cross-sectional design, the results do not establish temporal precedence or causal mediation. The findings provide a preliminary rationale for further longitudinal and intervention research, but do not establish the effectiveness or practical feasibility of PSD-based initiatives.
items.authors: Flavio Urbini, Antonino Callea, Tommaso Pompili, Emanuela Caracuzzo

items.title: Network-Based Walk-Access Coverage of an Integrated Metro–Bus System: Measurement Sensitivity and Distributional Outcomes in Riyadh
items.abstract: Walk access determines the effective catchment of a transit system, yet coverage statistics are still commonly derived from straight-line buffers, and no network-based estimate exists for Riyadh’s newly integrated metro and bus system. This study quantifies walk-access service coverage for the Riyadh urban center along the pedestrian network, tests its sensitivity to measurement choices, and examines who is served. Using open data, network access distances were computed by shortest-path search; coverage was evaluated across network scenarios and thresholds; the pedestrian route directness ratio isolated the effect of street layout; and Lorenz curves, Gini coefficients and spatial econometric models characterized the distribution of supply. Under conventional thresholds, 24.2% of residents live within walking distance of an operational stop or station—or 19.6–30.4%, depending on the definition of the operating bus network—against 42.7% from straight-line buffers. The metro alone serves 7.8%; most coverage comes from feeder and community bus routes. More than three-quarters of residents cannot reach any line, while supply among those served is comparatively even. Coverage rises with building height, residential density and proximity to arterial corridors, is robust to spatial error and lag models, and is not detectably associated with district land price. Coverage gains are therefore expected from feeder routes and pedestrian permeability rather than trunk expansion, al-though these measures were not modeled. The results give planners a baseline for tracking route openings and support reproducible monitoring of Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) indicator 11.2.1 in Riyadh and comparable cities.
items.authors: Fayez Alanazi

items.title: Residual Performance of MWCNT-Modified Geopolymer-Based SIFCON Subjected to Elevated Temperature
items.abstract: This study experimentally investigates the residual performance of geopolymer-based slurry-infiltrated fibrous concrete (SIFCON) incorporating multi-walled carbon nanotubes (MWCNT) after exposure to elevated temperatures. Two SIFCON mixtures were examined: a reference geopolymer-based SIFCON (G-SIFCON) and an MWCNT-modified mixture (NM-G-SIFCON) containing 0.12% MWCNT by mass of the precursor materials. A total of five exposure conditions were considered, including the unheated condition and exposure for 30, 60, 90, and 120 min in accordance with the ISO 834 standard fire curve, corresponding to nominal furnace temperatures of approximately 821, 925, 986, and 1029 °C, respectively. The specimens were evaluated in terms of density, water-related change in mass, thermal change in mass, and residual compressive strength. The corrected mass-loss results showed an exposure-duration-dependent response, with NM-G-SIFCON exhibiting lower change in mass than G-SIFCON at 30, 60, and 120 min, but slightly greater change in mass at 90 min. The unheated compressive strengths of G-SIFCON and NM-G-SIFCON were 93 and 97 MPa, respectively. Following 120 min of fire exposure, the residual compressive strengths decreased to 23.7 MPa for G-SIFCON and 49.13 MPa for NM-G-SIFCON, corresponding to strength retention of 25.5% and 50.6%, respectively. The results demonstrate that MWCNT incorporation does not produce a uniform improvement in mass stability at all exposure durations; however, the NM-G-SIFCON mixture exhibited greater residual compressive-strength retention at prolonged fire exposure. The findings highlight the potential of MWCNT-modified geopolymer SIFCON for improving post-fire compressive performance, while further investigation of microstructural and tensile/flexural responses is required to establish the underlying mechanisms.
items.authors: Balamurali Kanagaraj, Aman Kumar, Nammalvar Anand, Daniel Paul Thanaraj

items.title: Alert360: A Low-Cost, Interpretable Browser-Based Motion Awareness for Multi-Camera Monitoring
items.abstract: This paper presents Alert360, a low-cost and intrinsically interpretable browser-based multi-camera motion awareness system for local monitoring in security, retail, education, laboratory, and workplace settings, designed to run on commodity cameras and consumer-grade browser-capable computers without dedicated GPUs. Existing video analytics platforms are often cloud-dependent, costly, or designed for complex surveillance tasks that exceed the needs of small sites. Alert360 addresses a narrower but practically important problem: lightweight operational motion awareness using commodity cameras and modern web browsers. Alert360 provides lightweight, rule-based, and privacy-conscious motion awareness using commodity cameras and modern web browsers. The system performs camera capture, frame processing, motion estimation, alerting, and event review entirely on the client side. Its motion pipeline includes frame down-scaling, grayscale conversion, smoothing, adaptive background differencing, temporal differencing, mask refinement, and blob-based activity estimation. The interface supports concurrent camera streams, configurable frame rates, adjustable sensitivity, movement focus, off-screen guidance, optional acoustic alerts, and local snapshot retention. A controlled benchmark across seven multi-camera scenarios showed a mean processing time of 10.62 ms per frame, zero late frames, and a maximum estimated processing duty cycle of 24.43%. An illustrative office-area deployment using a 1080p 360-degree webcam showed that all thirty scripted human-movement scenarios activated the expected motion-triggered recording workflow. These results demonstrate that motion awareness can be delivered through browser-native local processing on consumer-grade computers under the evaluated multi-camera configurations.
items.authors: Minh Nguyen, Trung Nguyen, Xinyu Hu, Bingjie Xiao

items.title: An Integrated PS-InSAR and K-Means Clustering Framework for Roadbed Deformation Susceptibility Assessment Supporting Sustainable Urban Road Management in Daegu, South Korea
items.abstract: Long-term deformation of urban road networks can compromise infrastructure performance and requires spatially continuous methods for identifying segments that warrant targeted monitoring. This study integrates Persistent Scatterer Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (PS-InSAR), geotechnical data, multivariate k-means clustering, and GIS road-network analysis to evaluate roadbed deformation susceptibility in Daegu, South Korea. A total of 184 ascending Sentinel-1 SLC images acquired between June 2018 and December 2025 yielded 32,590 roadbed persistent scatterers (PS) and 247,734 surrounding-ground PS. Because a single ascending geometry was used, all measurements represent relative line-of-sight (LOS) motion rather than absolute vertical displacement. Roadbed relative LOS velocities ranged from −8.63 to + 4.87 mm/yr. Roadbed and surrounding-ground velocities correlated moderately within a 200 m neighborhood (r = 0.59), while percentile- and exceedance-based comparisons showed slightly heavier deformation tails on the roadbed. Susceptibility was assessed by clustering relative LOS velocity, SPT-derived VS30, and effective soil depth for 31,263 PS with complete data. The three resulting classes were defined by combinations of deformation and subsurface conditions rather than by velocity thresholds. The critical class exhibited the most negative mean relative LOS velocity (−0.60 mm/yr), lower mean VS30 (382 m/s), and relatively deep soil conditions, whereas the concern and stable classes had similar mean LOS velocities but were differentiated primarily by their subsurface profiles. Of the approximately 883.7 km major road network, 668.8 km was classified, comprising 161.8 km (24.2%) critical, 284.1 km (42.5%) concern, and 222.8 km (33.3%) stable roads, while 215.0 km remained unclassified because of insufficient PS coverage. Comparison with 19 documented ground-subsidence incidents yielded critical-class enrichment ratios of 0.34–0.49, but the limited sample was insufficient to either confirm or reject the susceptibility classification; 14 of the 19 incidents were associated with abrupt underground-utility or construction-related failures rather than gradual deformation processes. The proposed framework can support targeted monitoring, preventive maintenance, and sustainable urban road management.
items.authors: Moon-Soo Song, Sung-Wook Kim, Seung-Hyuk Choi, Manik Das Adhikari, Sang-Guk Yum

items.title: Estrogen and Alzheimer’s Disease: Neurobiology, Epigenetics, and AI-Driven Therapeutic Design
items.abstract: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder, and women are disproportionately affected. This review examines the evidence that estrogen signaling contributes to this disparity and asks what a molecularly targeted therapeutic would require. We first distinguish prevalence from incidence in the gender-difference literature and review the genetic, epigenetic, and ascertainment factors that structure female-specific risk, noting that the associations localize consistently to tau rather than to amyloid pathology. We then examine estrogen receptor (ER) biology in the brain, reconciling apparently contradictory accounts of ERα and ERβ function by resolving them at the level of downstream pathway and cell type rather than receptor identity, and review evidence that DNA methylation at ER genes predicts cognitive decline and tangle density through mechanisms independent of receptor expression. The consistent failure of systemic hormone therapy in clinical trials is interpreted not as a refutation of this biology but as a constraint defining three design requirements: receptor engagement resolved by subtype, cell type, and tissue compartment; sufficient central nervous system exposure; and delivery timed to the perimenopausal window. Against these requirements we review AI-driven approaches to ER modulator design, spanning diffusion-based backbone generation and protein language models for peptides, and virtual screening and generative frameworks for small molecules. We argue that the principal barrier is data rather than model architecture: ERβ-selective binding data and peptide blood–brain barrier permeability data are both scarce, and no AI-designed ER modulator has been evaluated in an AD model. We conclude by identifying the epigenetic layer as a target class that current design pipelines do not address, and for which the necessary editing tools are technically available but validated against the wrong readout.
items.authors: Tianhua Zhai, Risa Garg, Peiming Li, Zixuan Wen, Yijing Su, Li Shen

items.title: Influence of Carbon Addition Amount on the Strength and Reduction Performance of Pellet Ore Under Blast Furnace Lump Zone Reaction Conditions
items.abstract: Increasing the proportion of pellets in blast furnace (BF) burdens raises the raw material iron grade and reduces slag volume, thereby lowering fuel consumption. However, due to their dense microstructure, pellets typically exhibit low degrees of reduction. Controlled carbon additions may improve pellet porosity and subsequent reducibility. This study investigates the effects of varying carbon addition ratios on pellet pore structure, compressive strength, and metallurgical properties, including reducibility, reduction swelling, and reduction disintegration after the reduction program. The results show that increasing carbon additions increase porosity in both acidic and basic pellets but reduce compressive strength. For basic pellets, reducibility peaks at 1.5% carbon addition before declining, whereas acidic pellets show progressively lower reducibility with higher carbon ratios, suggesting that excessive carbon adversely impacts reduction kinetics. The reduction swelling index of basic pellets increases with carbon addition, reaching 21.7% at 2% carbon. Conversely, acidic pellets exhibit a maximum swelling index of 14.7% at 1.5% carbon, followed by a decline. These findings provide important theoretical and practical insights for optimizing carbon addition in pellet production.

items.title: Preparation of Polyurethane Solid–Solid Phase-Change Material with Soft Segment for Application on Temperature-Regulating Fabrics
items.abstract: The emergence of water-borne polyurethane solid–solid phase-change materials (PCMs) has overcome the problems of core material leakage in solid–liquid phase-change materials. However, water-borne polyurethane solid–solid phase-change materials also have issues such as poor heat storage performance and limited temperature regulation range. This study used polycaprolactone diol (PCL-diol) and poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG) as the composite soft segments, and selected dicyclohexylmethane-4,4′-diisocyanate (HMDI) and glycerol (GL) as the hard segments, to prepare a PEG-PCL-HMDI PCM. By adjusting the ratio of the composite soft and hard segments, the content of the soft segment, and the molar ratio of the monomers, the phase-change temperature was precisely controlled and the heat storage performance was synergistically improved. After the PEG-PCL-HMDI PCM had finished being applied onto the surface of cotton fabric, the temperature-regulating fabric exhibited a significant temperature-buffering effect in the 25–35 °C human activity temperature range, with the heating rate reduced and the cooling rate delayed. This study provides a new material system and process scheme for the development of intelligent textiles with both efficient energy storage and precise temperature regulation functions.
items.authors: Xiran Qiao, Shaofeng Lu, Qiancheng Yang, Songcong Lin, Mingqiang Wang, Wenzhao Shi

items.title: Echo-Driven Doppler Parameter Estimation for High-Resolution Squinted Spaceborne Sliding Spotlight SAR
items.abstract: High-resolution squinted spaceborne sliding spotlight synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging requires accurate Doppler parameters. In conventional SAR processing, Doppler parameters are generally derived from prior ancillary information or estimated from the received echoes. However, Doppler parameters derived from prior information are sensitive to ancillary-measurement errors, while existing echo-based methods remain insufficient for ambiguity-resolved Doppler-centroid estimation and Doppler frequency modulation (FM)-rate refinement in high-resolution squinted sliding spotlight SAR. To reduce the reliance on prior ancillary information for Doppler-parameter determination, this paper proposes an echo-driven Doppler-parameter estimation (ED-DPE) method. The proposed method first estimates the baseband Doppler centroid using adjacent-echo cross-correlation and then resolves the Doppler ambiguity number based on the range-migration slope, thereby obtaining the absolute Doppler centroid fd. The estimated absolute Doppler centroid is subsequently used as a physical constraint on an attitude-equivalent observation geometry, which is refined through contrast-based full-aperture image formation to obtain the Doppler FM rate fr and the imaging parameters. Point-target simulations and real spaceborne SAR experiments demonstrate that the proposed ED-DPE method supports accurate focusing of 0.25-m-resolution squinted sliding spotlight SAR.
items.authors: Zelin Wang, Zhirong Men, Kangxin Xiong, Pengbo Wang, Bing Sun, Jie Chen

items.title: A Survey of Smart Contract Vulnerability Detection Based on Tree Representation
items.abstract: Smart contracts, characterized by automation, transparency, and decentralization, can establish efficient, secure, and reliable blockchain fund management and data processing mechanisms, playing a crucial supporting role in blockchain application scenarios. However, security issues in smart contracts are increasingly prominent, making vulnerability detection a critical research focus; detection methods based on tree representation have emerged as a promising direction in this field. A comprehensive review of tree representation-based smart contract vulnerability detection methods is provided in this paper, aiming to offer new insights and theoretical support for smart contract security. First, a three-level vulnerability taxonomy covering 18 common smart contract vulnerability types is presented, categorized by the specific stage of the smart contract life cycle where the vulnerability originates: the Solidity code layer, the EVM execution layer, and the blockchain system layer. Second, four traditional detection paradigms—formal verification, symbolic execution, fuzz testing, and static analysis—are characterized by their core mechanisms and compared across multiple performance dimensions. Third, following the PRISMA systematic review guidelines, 23 primary studies on tree representation-based methods are selected and organized under a novel three-category taxonomy: pure AST sequentialization/traversal, tree-structured neural networks, and AST-to-graph transformations. The technical and application-level challenges of these methods are synthesized, and corresponding open research questions and improvement directions are discussed to inform future work.
items.authors: Gongming Wang, Junsong Zhou, Bingsen Li, Haiying Li

items.title: Yield and Agronomic Traits of Grain Legumes in Organic and Conventional Cultivar-Testing Networks in Poland
items.abstract: Grain legumes are important in organic cropping systems because biological nitrogen fixation reduces dependence on external N inputs. We analysed 2022–2025 data from two separate Polish COBORU cultivar-testing networks conducted at 52 distinct experimental stations/trial sites across the main agricultural regions of Poland: an organic network (approximately five soybean and 7–8 field pea and narrow-leaved lupin locations annually) and a conventional post-registration network (27–33 locations per species). Trial soils spanned agricultural values of 52–94 points, pH 4.6–7.5, available P 40–190 mg kg−1 and K 60–240 mg kg−1; soybean and pea were tested mainly on wheat/wheat–rye complexes, whereas lupin was concentrated on lighter rye complexes. Because the networks were spatially independent, all comparisons are network-level and descriptive rather than causal. Mean soybean yield was 3.77 t ha−1 in the organic network and 3.50 t ha−1 in the conventional network (+7.7%), but the annual difference changed from +13.2% in 2022 and +22.8% in 2023 to approximately 0% in 2024 and −8.0% in 2025. Organic-network mean yields of field pea and narrow-leaved lupin were 21.6% and 11.6% lower than the corresponding conventional-network means, respectively. For soybean, very early/early, medium-early/medium-late and late/very late groups yielded 3.28 vs. 3.11, 4.04 vs. 3.64 and 3.93 vs. 3.83 t ha−1, respectively; the medium-early/medium-late group showed the largest positive network difference (+11.0%) and therefore merits further common-site validation. Field pea showed less lodging in the organic network (6.63 vs. 5.70; 9 = no/minimal lodging). Precipitation–yield relationships were non-monotonic, indicating that annual totals alone did not explain yield variation. Conventional fertilizer ranges were 16–36 kg N, 34–45 kg P2O5 and 59–80 kg K2O ha−1; permitted mineral P and K inputs in organic trials averaged only 1–3 kg P2O5 and 3–9 kg K2O ha−1. Synthetic herbicides were prohibited in organic trials, whereas harmonized herbicide-use intensity in the conventional network could not be reconstructed from the annual summaries. Indicative 2025 gross-margin scenarios were EUR 1424 vs. 407 ha−1 for soybean, EUR 264 vs. −59 ha−1 for pea and EUR −20 vs. −449 ha−1 for lupin (organic vs. conventional), with strong sensitivity to assumed organic price premiums.
items.authors: Marek Cieśliński, Jan Žukovskis, Dariusz Gozdowski

items.title: GeCoM: Joint Generative and Interactive Contrastive Self-Supervised Learning for Few-Shot Classification of Multi-Source Remote Sensing Imagery
items.abstract: Accurate image classification under extreme label scarcity remains a critical challenge in remote sensing, where hyperspectral imagery offers rich spectral signatures but suffers from coarse spatial resolution limitations. Although integrating complementary panchromatic and multispectral data can alleviate this spatial bottleneck, existing methods struggle to fully exploit their deep spatial–spectral features without dense annotations. We propose GeCoM, a joint generative and interactive contrastive self-supervised learning framework for few-shot multi-source image classification. GeCoM employs modality-specific Transformer encoders with a multi-scale masking strategy to reconstruct fine spatial–spectral patterns. Simultaneously, an interactive contrastive optimization module is introduced to align heterogeneous multi-source features within a unified latent space. Experiments on the Houston 2018 benchmark and two regional scenes from Gaofen-14 satellite demonstrate that GeCoM achieves superior Overall Accuracies of 74.66%, 92.36%, and 94.02% with only 15 labeled samples per class, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines. This study provides a robust, label-efficient spatial–spectral representation solution for multi-sensor earth observation.
items.authors: Jinchun Qin, Hui Gong, Xiuce Yang, Mingyu Zhao, Yongqiang Wei

items.title: Direct Determination of Readily Accessible Quercetin-Reactive Aluminum and Ascorbate-Reducible, Ferrozine-Reactive Iron in Cosmetic Emulsions
items.abstract: Aluminum in antiperspirants is relevant to formulation control and compliance, whereas reactive iron can promote oxidative instability in emulsions. We developed smartphone-based colorimetric assays relying on metal–reagent complexation directly in oil-in-water (O/W) emulsions, without digestion or extraction. The aluminum assay measures quercetin-reactive aluminum from aluminum chlorohydrate (ACH). Calibration data were fitted by linear regression (R2 ≥ 0.971). Acceptable accuracy (relative bias within ± 8.5%) and intermediate precision (CV ≤ 9.4%) were obtained upon quality control (QC) analysis (above the LLOQ). Relative bias in commercial antiperspirants and corresponding in-house preparations was within ± 15.2%. The iron assay measures ascorbate-reducible, ferrozine-reactive iron. Its calibration data were also fitted by linear regression (R2 ≥ 0.981), while QC analysis showed acceptable accuracy (relative bias within ± 13.7%) and intermediate precision (CV ≤ 12.6%). Comparison with portable energy-dispersive X-ray fluorescence (EDXRF) yielded a regression slope of 1.14 and an intercept of 0.40 μg/g, suggesting a proportional difference and a possible constant component. Common chelators and certain metals interfered with both assays. The effect of interferents in commercially relevant concentration was, however, minimal (relative bias within ± 15.2% for Al and at 4.5% for a Co/Cu/Fe-fortified model emulsion) after matrix matching or dilution. Although mostly inferior in terms of technical characteristics compared to established instrumental methods, this methodology is sufficiently accurate, precise and selective under the defined conditions.
items.authors: Georgia Eleni Tsotsou, Dimitra Dremetsika, Georgia Bakara, Mirofora Pilakouta

items.title: Organellar Genome Analysis of the Red Alga Acrosorium flabellatum (Rhodophyta, Ceramiales, Delesseriaceae): Evidence of Gene Duplication and Group II Intron in cox1 Gene
items.abstract: Mitochondrial genomes (mitogenome) offer important information about evolutionary history, genomic diversity, and structural dynamics of Rhodophytes. The complete mitochondrial genome of Acrosorium flabellatum Yamada, 1930 (Delesseriaceae, Ceramiales), is reported in this study. The circular mitogenome spans 31,818 bp and has a biased A+T (78.8%) composition. The mitogenome contains 61 genes, including two rRNAs, 33 tRNAs, 24 protein-coding genes (PCGs), and two open reading frames (ORFs). Notably, the mitogenome contains several duplicated genes (nad6, sdh3, sdh2) and a Group II intron within the cox1 gene, suggesting continued intron mobility and structural expansion within Delesseriaceae. Codon usage indicated a strong preference for AT-rich codons, and intergenic regions were compact. A majority of PCGs showed positive GC skewness and negative AT skewness, reflecting conserved nucleotide bias across Ceramiales. Comparative analysis within the Ceramiales revealed lineage-specific differences in genome size, gene arrangement, gene content, with A. flabellatum revealing clear features of duplication and gene loss (sdh4, rps3). Several structural rearrangements, including gene order, presence of the Group II intron and ORFs, further support dynamic mitogenome evolution within Delesseriaceae. Phylogenetic analysis based on 23 conserved PCGs strongly supported the monophyly of Ceramiales and placed A. flabellatum within the Delesseriaceae clade with high bootstrap support. Overall, this study enriches the genomic resources of red algae, and sheds light on the comparative patterns of mitogenome structure within the Ceramiales. The mitogenome of A. flabellatum shows both conserved and dynamic features within this diverse red algal lineage.
items.authors: Maheshkumar Prakash Patil, Jeong Gyu Kim, Young-Ryun Kim, Kyeongmin Kim, Pradip Vitthal Hirapure, Jong-Oh Kim
